Phainon was… curious. That was all.

His best friend since high-school had a secret, one he had let him in on once but seemed to keep to himself otherwise. It wasn’t an accident when he had confessed, nor was it coerced out of him in any way. Mydei simply said it over the phone as if it were a casual fact about him, like he didn’t care if he knew even if he didn't ever talk about it.

“Well, I haven’t had a boyfriend, but I did have a submissive. He wasn’t difficult to talk to.”

He hadn’t understood what that meant or why he felt the need to differentiate between the two.

Was it similar to the ‘square is a rectangle’ kind of logic? A boyfriend could be a submissive kind of partner, but a submissive wasn’t always a boyfriend?

How did that even work? With nothing but casual sex between them? Were there no romantic feelings involved?

From what he knew, his best friend wasn’t a playboy. Mydei didn’t casually flirt with guys in an attempt to take them home, and he didn’t seem to like other people most of the time too. That stoic expression of his didn’t exactly give off the impression he enjoyed company, and his way of speaking came off more callous than anything.

If he thought long enough, he wasn’t even sure if Mydei ever mentioned the guys he found attractive or wanted to potentially ask out. The only reason he knew he was interested in guys to begin with was because of a singular enamel pin that once lived in the strap of his high-school book bag.

They had never really spoken about the topic either, just accepted the other wordlessly as they shared details about themselves over time. Coincidentally, that was how most of their friendship went—silent acceptance of uncomfortable topics and full-blown, back-and-forth banter over others.

Phainon had wanted to ask about this particular thing when it happened, however, but over the phone after a failed attempt at picking someone up felt like a terrible setting to have the conversation. He didn't have it in him.

Now, he wished he did.

Mydei’s slip of the tongue had quietly bothered him since the moment he heard it, and he talked himself into believing it was because his own sex life was bone dry. It has been years of just him and his steadily growing collection of toys. Part of him assumed it was that way for his best friend too since he never brought up partners, dates, or feelings. As ambitious as he was, he thought the other man was just too focused on climbing the corporate ladder of his father's company.

Yet that one sentence proved Mydei wasn’t going through the same thing as him. That one line told him that while he was single, bored, and feeling a little left out of the romance scene, Mydei was secretly seeing God-knows-who and having the time of his life.

On one hand, good for him. On the other hand, it was just a little bit annoying.

Though he knew he could try to find someone at a bar or club too, strangers never seemed to hit the mark he needed them to. Pretty girls approaching him didn’t excite him as much as they should’ve when all they wanted to do was dance on top of him. Handsome men offering to buy him a drink only made him think too much about going to a place he’s never been to with someone he’s never met to do things while he was too drunk to remember his own name. There were hardly any moments to just… talk, to get to know each other better before moving on to physical things, and there were too many potential risks in sleeping around. His brain never let him enjoy it.

On top of that, his heart couldn’t take just being someone’s sexual object for a night when he wanted a connection closer than that. It didn't make sense how someone could open themselves up without trusting them first.

That was why he confronted Mydei.

With two shots of liquid courage in his system before the man showed up, as they sat around his apartment casually chatting about the newest thriller movie they were watching, Phainon just had to know. It ate away at his psyche, begging to be acknowledged.

“Hey, De? H… How did you even find a submissive?”

Mydei hummed, the sound low and rumbling as he contemplated his answer for a moment. “I met my last one on a dating app,” he answered simply, cleanly.

Dating apps somehow felt worse than bars or clubs. They felt emptier than talking face to face, and he heard stories of catfishing and uncomfortable sexting from his other friends who have them.

Mydei never seemed like he would take part in the online-dating group of people, but he guessed these were the intimate details that wouldn’t typically be shared in a conversation. Those habits weren’t just casual day-talking conversations. Especially since his style of dating wasn’t, well, dating. It was darker. Dirtier.

“Why do you want to know?” Mydei wondered after.

“You sound a little defensive. Is there a reason why?” Phainon shot back as amber eyes bore right into his cerulean ones.

Mydei’s lips pursed. The rim of a sleek glass touched his bottom one, then tilted back for a drink of the rich, caramel-tinted liquor.

“No.” Alcohol burned his vocals into a rasp. “But why ask such a question so suddenly?”

“How’d you even get into it?” He asked him instead, too tangled within his curiosity and confusion to entertain him with a response. “It’s some pretty violent stuff.”

“Pardon?”

Thick, golden eyebrows furrowed together into a pinch as his gaze hardened. More than a purse, his lips then tilted downwards into the makings of a frown.

Phainon swallowed over the brooding expression. “What?”

BDSM was violent. Dominance of his kind was aggressive in nature, and submission was the fear in response to it. Rules and punishments, permissions and denial, those kinds of things weren’t common in a relationship. They weren’t something someone should adhere to in a place where comfort, trust, and acceptance were meant to be. It was arbitrary.

In addition to not being a playboy, his best friend wasn’t necessarily a violent person either. He had his moments of anger, but so did everyone else when pushed far enough. Which was what made this even more surprising.

When did he grow to crave such all-consuming power over someone?

“It’s not something violent if you don’t want it to be,” Mydei argued, pulling him from his thoughts.

His glass clinked to the coffee table, and the movie they were watching was paused with a singular button. Everything they had been doing was put on halt, stopped so they could have this conversation.

“I am not violent with my partner.”

“You’re not, but isn’t that what BDSM is, Mydei? Sexual violence?” He reasoned, unable to accept that it was different from what he read about online. “Someone pushes something on to someone else, and they’re too afraid of punishment to deny that demand. Sadism is right in the title, and sadism is, by definition, getting off on hurting people. It’s… violent.”

Mydei’s voice cut like a knife as he retorted, “Why are you suddenly so interested in things you clearly don’t like?”

Phainon paused, aware that he was upset with his viewpoint and poking at a lion poised to strike. But he also knew that he wouldn’t try to interject more than necessary because he valued his privacy greatly. Trying to prove him wrong would mean having to admit the gritty details of his affairs, and he wasn’t the kind of guy to just spill his guts for anything.

“It doesn't make sense,” he told him. “Why are they considered your submissives and not your boyfriends?”

“Why are you so fixated on my personal affairs, Phainon?”

This time, it was him who turned to face the other man better. With his knee bent on top of the couch cushion and his hands on his calf, he gave Mydei his complete attention back.

“Why won’t you answer my questions? Is it because you know I’m right?” He bit, trying to imagine his best friend in the shoes of some of the videos he saw while searching for answers.

The man throwing someone’s smaller body around as he pleased despite their cries for mercy; the man tying someone up with rope, hitting their delicate skin while in such a defenseless state, and finding enjoyment in their pain; the man resting his heavy, dirty boots on top of someone's bruised, naked body while casually watching television—that was Mydei. That was his best friend.

The same guy who bent down to pet stray cats on the street and gifted his friends meticulously wrapped, homemade desserts was a person who got off on dehumanizing his partner.

Phainon wasn’t sure how that sat inside of his stomach as he looked at him, at the face he almost didn’t know if he recognized.

A shadow had been cast over him, replacing the golden light that once cascaded over him. How was he meant to see him as that same person knowing what he enjoyed doing to someone else?

Silence followed.

The tension between both men was chokingly thick and heating with each passing moment. All of the oxygen in the room dissipated, replaced with something that could be sliced with a knife, something not so easily taken into the lungs.

Mydei’s glare over him was hot. Piercing, even, like it shot right through his body in an attempt to find an explanation himself since he refused to answer his questions too.

“You’ll look me in my eyes and accuse me of being an abusive person?” He asked incredulously.

This was his best friend. They had grown up with each other for over ten years now, visiting each other’s houses as often as their parents would allow them to and begging to spend the night after. When he had football games in high school, Mydei was there in the stands to support him, win or lose. During the days Mydei was too drained with his family problems to make it to his college courses, he took extra time to help him study the notes he had written down for him in their shared classes.

Mydei wasn’t a bad person. He knew that. His heart knew that.

Phainon’s shoulders sunk in on themselves, and he looked away as the accusation hung heavy in the air.

“That’s not what I…” He tried to defend himself, just to sigh heavily. “Forget I said anything, De. It’s not like I think you’re a bad person.”

His best friend scoffed bitterly. “Clearly you do, Phainon.”

Guilt weighed over him as he winced from the sound, not used to hearing so much venom within his voice. Especially when it was directed at him.

“No, it’s not like that,” he protested weakly. “I’m just… I-I guess I’m confused on how it works.”

“The internet is in your pocket.”

“The internet is why I think the way I do!” Phainon raised his voice.

As their eyes met again, Mydei’s glare softened.

I found people w-with bruises over their bodies, and people being treated like sexual objects, and people talking about how their ‘masters’ control every aspect of their life from when they wake up to what they eat! Isn’t that just a little bit crazy?” He begged him to understand, voice pitched louder with disbelief. “Is that… your life? Do you do that?”

Deep down, he was begging to hear him say ‘no’.

No matter his interests and no matter his past, even if it was just a little white lie, all he needed to tell him was that he got it all wrong. None of that was his thing. He didn’t enjoy a single aspect of anything he just listed. It was crazy. Who could live like that?

But another beat passed them, and that hope plummeted faster and faster with each second of silence.

Then Mydei answered, his voice much more gentle than it had been previously.

“Yes.”

Phainon’s breathing hitched over the response he knew was coming, and he leaned away from him as he gave the man a once over.

“Does that upset you, Phainon?” He asked honestly, still holding on to that same gentle tone. “Knowing what I do in my own time, does that make you feel uncomfortable around me?”

“I look for people whose interests align with mine.”

“Because!” His voice raised for a moment, then dragged on into a quieter sound as he gripped the leg of his sweatpants helplessly. “Because it’s… different… from anything I know, okay? It’s weird, and it makes me feel so differently about… things.”

Mydei sucked in a sharp breath, and a few seconds later, he exhaled as if those words had physically hurt him.

“I see…”

It hurt in his stomach the longer he thought about it.

Instead of answering, Phainon chose to grab his forgotten glass and throw back the last of his forgotten drink. It burned lightly going down, warming his throat and chest in the process.

“Phainon, are you deaf?” Mydei grumbled loudly, not hearing as he coughed from the alcohol. “If you’re still hungry, I’ll make you something real quick. What’s in your fridge?”

“Don’t be stupid,” Mydei brushed him off, then placed his phone on the couch beside him. “No more alcohol without food tonight, lightweight. You’ll get sick.”

He never noticed it, but Mydei was always in charge of the things around them. They butted heads because of it, fiery personalities colliding to start a blaze sometimes, but he always tried hard to take care of what, or who, was closest to him. From buying him things without any warning to scolding him when he wasn’t careful with himself, it was as if his best friend was taking responsibility for him.

Was this how he treated his partner—his submissive—in the past?

Did Mydei buy that man things if he couldn’t afford it, ensure he ate enough throughout the day, and take care of his wellbeing if he didn’t care to? Would he reward him with the freshly baked desserts he handed servings out to his friends?

That soft, spongy fruitcake he gave to him, Cyrene, Cassie, and Cifera a few weeks ago on a whim, was that a piece of his ex’s reward?

The thought was amusing and uncomfortable.

“Free trial run,” he snickered to himself as Mydei sat down on the couch beside him again.

“Hm?”

“I was thinkin’—”

“Oh no,” Mydei cringed, and he gasped in offense as the other hung his head. “Now what?”

“—if you act like this to your sub’, then I’m technically the first you ever had,” he teased him, and Mydei was silent as his face scrunched up momentarily in confusion. “All the things you did for me as your friend, was that how you got into these kinds of things? Was I the free trial before you decided you wanted a premium plan?”

“Stop thinking. It doesn’t suit you,” he deadpanned, not bothering to look at him. “Every time you open your mouth something senseless comes out.”

“C’mon.” Phainon pushed his shoulder lightly, smiling at the way he allowed himself to sway from his touch. “You know I’m right."

“‘Trial run’,” he repeated under his breath, then scoffed. “At this point, my commitment as your best friend will be the longest one I’ll ever have. These so-called ‘premium plans’ don’t last me even a fraction of how long I’ve known you.”

“Don’t jinx our friendship! Knock on wood!” He cried.

“Okay, and where is the wood?” Mydei asked, splaying his hands in front of him as if to tell him to look around them. “Your carpeted floors, your glass coffee table, or your leather couch? Do you have a brain?”

Well, he had a point.

“Smart ass,” he huffed, pushing him again.

“You would give me such a migraine as a submissive,” Mydei sighed, then grabbed the television remote from between them. “‘Trial run’…”

“If you can’t handle me, maybe you should get better at being a dominant. I’m not even doing anything,” he told him, earning a snort.

Mydei’s arm hugged the back of the couch as he raised an eyebrow at him.

“Are you serious? Phainon, you didn’t even know what it meant to be one about ten minutes ago,” he reminded him, sounding both offended and amused by the jab. “You have as much knowledge about BDSM as a house-dog does of the outside world.”

“I am not a dog!”

“You sure bark like one,” he shot back.

“What? Are you gonna muzzle me if I’m barking too much for your taste? Will you punish me for using my free will?” Phainon scoffed, unsure where in his chest it was coming from but feeling as each word climbed his vocal cords and fell from his mouth.

Mydei’s eyes rolled. “With how much you keep bringing this topic up, I’m starting to believe you might want me to.”

“As if I’d want that!” He protested, but the thought brought a sickening tingle throughout his body. It chilled around his chest and inched into the pit of his stomach.

There was no immediate response, but Mydei watched him for a moment as he squirmed within his spot. Amber eyes darted from the way he held on to his own arms, hoping to subtly soothe the prickle of his skin, and then back up to his face where heat had pooled inside of both cheeks. Whether it was the alcohol in his system or not, he didn’t really know, but they were warm. Maybe rosy.

And of course Mydei noticed.

“Are you sure?” He egged him on. “You might enjoy it.”

“Of course I’m sure,” Phainon hissed sharply, looking away from the eyes that always saw right through someone. “I’m not some… some pathetic, subservient mutt. I don’t want someone to dictate my life for me.”

“Don’t lie,” Mydei warned him. “Look at me, and think about it, Phainon. Why are you so interested in it? Why do you keep bringing it up? Why is my style more important than anything online when I told you it’s almost the same?”

“Be—”

“You and I both know it’s not because we’re friends,” he cut him off before he could even get the word out. “Are you interested in this? Do you want a proper trial run of this?”

He was quiet, too busy biting the inside of his lip and trying to push that bubble of confusion, curiosity, and disbelief aside. They mingled together into a tangled knot, one that made his stomach cramp uncomfortably the longer he mulled the question over.

Did he want that?

No… There was no way. He didn’t want to be told what to do with this time or how to behave by someone with a power trip. It didn’t excite him to imagine someone sticking their nose up at him and expecting him to obey.

But this was Mydei. His best friend, Mydei. Would sooner run his bank account dry than let someone struggle in front of him, Mydei.

Mydei wasn’t just someone, and he wasn’t some faceless, nameless ‘dominant’ who didn’t give a damn about how people felt.

“Phainon.”

He looked back at him.

“It’s alright.” Mydei came in closer to steal the space between them. He could feel his presence coming nearer and the warmth radiating off his body. “If you’re curious, it’s best to be honest with me. Don’t joke around with it, and don’t run away from me.”

A shaky breath fell from his lips.

He could feel his heartbeat picking up. Each pound slammed against his ribcage, threatening to break through the bone with each passing moment.

“You can trust me.”

He knew that. He did.

There was only one other person he trusted as much as he did Mydei, but she was currently taking a trip back to her parents’ house. She wasn’t here to ask what to do, and she wouldn’t be for awhile. Texts weren’t the same, and the service was always so bad out there in the countryside that calls felt like pulling teeth with a pair of pliars.

He couldn’t rely on her advice for this, just his own judgement.

“I’m not someone who can let my guard down easily,” he reminded him. “I mean… I haven’t had a relationship since I was a teenager, and no matter how hard I try, I can’t even want someone enough to participate in things like that freely.”

“You’re thinking too much about it.”

“You—!”

When looking back at him, his breathing hitched. The tension in his brows that he didn’t even realize was there smoothed out, and his lips sealed shut before he could even finish his sentence. All the words he wanted to say had been stolen within seconds.

Mydei was there. Right there.

Leaned closer to his height, one hand on his knee and the other on the back of the couch, he was only inches away. Liquor fell from his breath. Crackled leather from his coat and warm amber stained his burgundy collar where a few buttons had been undone. Sunset bangs were swept over the crooked bridge of his nose, kissing his golden cheeks but splitting to reveal his expectant gaze.

“Don’t say ‘someone’ if you mean me,” Mydei instructed him, speaking quieter since he was so close. “You don’t care about them. You said you only cared about me.”

“M-Mydei…”

“You need to be honest with me, Phainon. What do you want out of tonight?” He asked him seriously. “Did you really only call me over to have a few drinks and watch movies?”

Phainon gulped, and as his lips parted for a response, a knock sounded at the door.

Before Mydei could speak, before he could force him to ignore the presence and respond, he bounced on to his feet and rushed over. Stumbling, he used the doorknob and wall to keep himself upright.

The door was pulled open, and he looked at the paper bags left on the floor before glancing to the driver already walking down the steps. Four bags were in front of him, each packed full with things Mydei had picked out for him. From what he could see, there were fresh vegetables and produce, even a few peeking labels of pasta boxes and packed bread.

“I bet the bread and eggs are at the bottom,” Mydei commented from behind him, and he jumped from the proximity. “Here, let me help you put these away.”

Without waiting for a response, he lightly batted him aside to carefully pick up three of the four bags. By chance, or maybe by his design, the last happened to be the least full of them all.

“Thank you again for this, Mydei.”

“What are friends for?”

Phainon locked the door behind him, and as he cradled the brown bag in arms, he watched as Mydei began unpacking them.

“This is a lot for a few days…” He trailed off.

“Three nutritious meals a day, snacks in between, and a little bit of sweets to keep you happy. Doesn’t seem like a lot to me,” he reasoned with him. “You need to eat properly. You’ll lose muscle and weight if you don’t.”

“It wouldn't be that noticeable.”

Mydei stood his ground. “It never is until it is,” he insisted.

The bag in his hands was set beside the others, and as Mydei tucked a bottle of juice away, his shaking fingers grasped the sleeve folded up by his elbow. They curled into the soft fabric, grabbing his attention almost immediately.

“Mydei, look. I’m not really… good at being open about my feelings,” he confessed, staring at his heavy forearm as he was unable to meet his eyes. “To be honest, I-I don’t know why it bothered me so much to know you’re so much more successful in dating than I am…”

A soft hum of encouragement followed, coaxing him to continue speaking his mind.

“Usually we’re so neck-and-neck, but it’s like you’ve got this whole thing figured out while I… don’t.” The awkward, forced laugh that bubbled past his own lips made Phainon cringe on himself lightly. “On top of that, the things you want are so… out there. I needed to understand how you could manage it but I just… can’t.”

“Heh…”

Mydei’s opposite hand planted itself on top of his head, and he grunted quietly over the weight of it.

“Stupid,” he mocked him playfully. “We aren’t competing on who has a better love life. I may have had more partners, but yours have lasted much longer than mine.”

Phainon’s eyes followed a folded sleeve up to the bulge of Mydei’s bicep, then brought his attention towards his face. To his surprise, the other man was ready for it. He met his eyes swiftly, holding on to his gaze.

“And for the record, if it was you, I-I think I could trust you.”

“Could you?” He asked as if he was interested in that statement. “So, if I were to tell you to bring me our dishes from the living room, sit at the bar to keep me company, and let me fix you a small meal, would you listen to me?”

His heart skipped. His stomach knotted.

Exhaling shakily, he gave a singular nod of his head.

“I mean, it’s the same as just straight up asking me as a friend, right?” He laughed nervously, trying not to see it as a test but a simple request. “I wouldn’t… say no… That’s my mess out there too…”

Mydei nodded in the direction of the living room. “Then go,” he said simply, casually, like it wasn’t a thinly veiled command.

“S… Seriously?" He double-checked, and Mydei nodded curtly. “That’s an actual… demand? You want me to—”

“Phainon, please just go,” he repeated himself, softer this time. “Bring me our dishes and that bottle, then come sit down for me.”

His hand let go of him, and he turned to the living room slowly.

“I’m only doing this because I have to clean up my own mess anyway,” he tried to convince him before walking back to the living room. As he did, paper bags crinkled with movement once again.

It felt so odd to hear his best friend talk like that to him. His tone of voice and clear-cut instructions made his stomach tight, but he still wasn’t sure if it was out of disgust or interest. Both feelings grew around one another like roots mingling too close together, using the soil of his insides as a place to mature as one singular flower. A horribly confusing flower that blossomed suddenly, violently, when he thought of BDSM and its complicated nature.

All at once, this was embarrassing and thrilling.

He was upset at himself for rolling over to listen, yet his body was alive in ways he never was before from doing a simple, meaningless task.

Phainon’s fingers shook as they stretched to pick up their twin glasses. The cups rattled from his unsteady hold, glass clinking and echoing a pitched chime. His other hand grasped the neck of their almost-empty bottle of whiskey, eyeing the caramel liquor that was giving him all his strength.

Without it, he probably would have caved in on himself and never called Mydei over in the first place. But three small drinks and he was obeying the other man like some kind of butler…

He almost wanted to throw the last of the bottle back in hopes he could forget tonight entirely come tomorrow morning. It whispered his name, beckoning his lips to meet the opened rim, to reignite that phantom burn down his throat. Maybe it could kill that flower inside of him, burn it from the roots before it could bud.

“Phainon, what’s taking you so long?”

He snapped his attention in the direction of his kitchen, breathless, and carried all three glasses back to Mydei.

What was wrong with him?

“Here,” he offered him, thrusting them all across the counter roughly. “Finish it before I do.”

“I said no more for you tonight.” Mydei took the bottle before removing it from his arm’s reach. “Here. You can have water.”

The words echoed within his head.

‘You can have water.’

This was his apartment. He paid the rent every month for it. This was his kitchen. He bought the bottle Mydei had grabbed from the refrigerator on his last run to the grocery store.

But he could have it. It was his water, but Mydei was giving him permission to drink it instead of the alcohol eyeballing him from across the room. The alcohol he wasn’t allowed to have even if he bought that too.

Phainon stared at the cold bottle, then at his best friend’s back when he turned to chop some lettuce that he definitely didn’t have in his fridge ten minutes ago.

“I can have water,” he repeated to himself quietly, bringing the drink closer. “What else can I have inside of my own place, De?”

“For now, just sit.”

“Yes, master,” he mouthed back.

His knife drove harder into the cutting board, thumping sharply through the otherwise silent room and rattling the couple of spoons left in a dish rack.

“What?” He continued, amused by his still figure and silence. “Gonna keep bossing me around in my own place? Is it getting you off to tell me where I can sit, what I can drink, and decide what I get to eat, De?”

“Phainon…”

“Tell me where to put my bottle when I’m done with it, or when I can head to bed for the night,” he tagged on, warmed by the heat within his cramping stomach.

Mydei’s voice lowered as he set the knife down. “Phainon, stop,” he warned.

“Should I sleep on the left side or the right side of my mattress, master?” He bit back, not caring to listen. “Can I wear a shirt as I sleep, or do I have to be shirtless for your viewing pleasure, master?”

“Phainon, I said that’s enough!”

He flinched back from the strength of his voice, and Mydei looked over his shoulder to stare back at him with a fierce glare.

“Stop acting like a petulant little brat by throwing this tantrum, and stop calling me by that title,” he demanded of him. “I’m no one’s master because I don’t have a partner.”

Gulping, Phainon cracked the seal on his bottle with trembling hands. He threw it back quickly, hoping it could wash away the full-body chill Mydei’s outburst gave him and keep his mouth busy for long enough.

“If you hate this so much, you can say it. You can ask me to stop, and I will.”

He kept drinking, swallowing loudly and slowly.

“Or, we can keep playing this cat-and-mouse game until you make up your mind on how you feel about it,” he allowed. “Either way, if you’re going to be mouthy and disrespectful, I’ll find a way to make you quiet.”

A moment of quiet passed, allowing his threat to hang heavily in the air. Then the chopping sounds continued, proving that he was done speaking and ready to move on.

As Phainon’s bottle lowered, he watched him grab a plump, ripe tomato from the sink before slicing it in half.

“How?” He whispered between the rhythmic clicks of his chopping, and Mydei was still for another second. Nothing but the consistent hum of the refrigerator and crinkle of plastic filled between them.

“How what?”

He felt it, the bud in his stomach peeking in sick, twisted interest to see what comes next.

“How will you make me?”

Mydei brought the knife down and turned around to face him. With a quarter of the produce in one hand, he walked up to him and raised the opposite to grip his chin. His index finger brushed his bottom lip, and his thumbprint pressed firmly to the bone. They held him there steadily, not pulling him closer, pushing him away, or prying to make him drop his jaw.

“Open,” he said firmly.

Sparks popped through his body once more. They tingled in his chest and beneath his belly, buzzing through every nerve like a live current.

When he didn’t part his lips, Mydei stood taller in front of his seated figure. Those deep, honey-gold eyes stared down at him, gluing him into his spot within their syrupy gaze even as his leg bounced rapidly and fists tightened.

Another crinkle filled between them.

“Open your mouth,” he repeated himself, and Phainon slowly lowered his jaw for him. “If you eat it, that tells me you don’t want this.”

The tomato was placed on his tongue, and he made a move to sink his teeth into its flesh just to show Mydei the flex of his jaw, to show him he could just chew it up and swallow it down.

He could end this now. Right now. That was his free will, and it was something Mydei had no control over.

“I’m going to finish this sandwich, and you’re going to sit here quietly until you can eat it,” Mydei said slowly, ignoring his glare and the push back against his authority.

Part of him wanted to spit the thing back at him. How dare he think he could talk to him like that? So what if he did buy him this meal and decide to make it for him? They were friends, not partners. He didn’t owe him submission, and this game was starting to feel less like a game the longer it went on.

But a bigger part of him simply wanted to swallow its sweet juice on his tongue and leave it to fill his mouth. Where would this take them if he committed to this bit they set up? What would it mean for them both if he actually listened and kept it between his teeth?

Did he even want to know?

Phainon sat there silently as Mydei went back to fixing his food, both ashamed by his curiosity and intrigued by the possibilities.

It couldn’t have been that long, maybe even just a few minutes, but the wait felt like forever.

The stretch of his jaw wasn’t uncomfortable. Neither was the weight sitting on his tongue. But what it symbolized made him squirm, itching inside of his seat for this to end. Even without Mydei so much as glancing at him and his fully clothed body, he felt stripped bare for the other man.

A plate was set in front of him soon enough, and he looked down at the cold sandwich before flicking his attention upwards. Silent.

“Did you eat it yet?”

The right side of his lip curled upwards, revealing the bright red tomato still clutched between his teeth. Mydei watched him bite right through it this time, but Phainon decided to close his mouth while chewing.

Then, he swallowed loudly.

“Now I did,” he mouthed off, unsure what that meant for them both moving forward.

Had he completed that punishment? Was he meant to wait for an instruction to swallow?

“You’re going to give me one hell of a headache, Phainon, but if you can be open-minded, then I can be patient,” he told him, hinting at what he was both afraid of and curious about. “Do you want to start a trial run of this dynamic? If you don’t like it, you can cancel at any point in time.”

“Do you offer all your friends a chance to be your submissive, or is it just me?” Phainon found it within himself to joke, laughter being the best cure for confusion and awkwardness.

“You can sleep on it,” he brushed off. “Take the rest of the week to think about it.”

He was… serious about that? If they did this, then what did that mean for them as friends?

“Friends don’t just do things like that together,” he reminded him, wondering how he could be so casual about this all.

“Everyone deserves a safe and comfortable place to explore,” Mydei reasoned. “If I can be that for you, I will. The last thing I want is for you to look elsewhere and get hurt in the process.”

Phainon nodded, taking the dish from him and admiring its clean cut halves and impressive height. Packed full of vegetables and meat, it seemed Mydei was determined to make sure he ate enough before he went to bed for the night.

“You know, you’d make a good boyfriend if you actually dated instead of playing king or something.”

He huffed, acting annoyed for the sake of his joke. “You could make for a good submissive, if you aren’t scared of a spanking every now and then."

Everything inside of him lit up at the thought of possibly being spanked by his best friend’s heavy hand. Red flashed violently inside of his head from the sirens that screamed, ‘do you really want to be hit’. Sparks the size of fireworks bursted within his veins, each booming loudly as if to drown out those cries of reason.

“I don’t really…” Phainon cut himself off, trying to wrack his hazy mind of what he wanted to say rather than whatever was instinctual. “No. I never actually thought about having sex with you before.”

His best friend was an attractive man—that was an undeniable fact. Anyone with eyes could see how he meticulously upkept his appearance and his health, always making sure to fit a workout into even the busiest of schedules and dressing himself luxuriously. Being friends since childhood meant he had seen him in various states of undress, and his body was that of the gods chiseled from old, marble slabs.

But just because Mydei was attractive, that didn’t mean he ever considered having sex with him until his brain was infected by things like sadism and bondage.

Mydei shrugged in response. “We don’t have to have sex,” he reassured him.

Was BDSM not inherently sexual? Was pulling someone’s pants down and smacking their bare ass repeatedly not considered a sexual act?

Phainon lowered his eyes to the hands in front of him, to the thick fingers drumming over the counter, their trimmed nails, and the golden ring glistening on his pinky. He tried imagining them on his body. He tried to envision the heat of his palm when he cocked his hand back to swing it against his bottom, the strength of his grip as he grabbed on to his body in pleasure, and the stretch of them possibly buried inside of him like the toy tucked into his bedside dresser. The hands that pushed him when he got annoying and held him when falling apart, how would they feel trying to please him?

A blank card was drawn.

He had never gotten that far with a man, and he couldn’t quite picture what it’d be like to have his hands on him.

Mydei’s arm lifted, and his focus followed until it reached to tuck a strand of sunset gold hair behind his ear. There, he looked back at his eyes.

“That is a subject we can talk about if you agree to continue. I have nothing else to say on that as of now,” he brushed off. “Please eat.”

“If I agree, will that ruin our friendship?” He asked quietly. “How could we go back to being the way we were if we…”

Phainon didn’t need to finish his sentence. The sincere expression on Mydei’s face said all he needed to know.

A twitch pulled on his lip, and he sighed before picking at the corner of his sandwich.

“Do you promise?”

Losing him would be the worst outcome of all. Forget the bruises that may happen. Forget giving up his autonomy. Forget being seen as a perverted freak for agreeing to try. If he lost his best friend because of this, what would be the point of anything after?

“Our friendship will not change, Phainon.”

Nervous laughter bubbled from his lips as he realized he was seriously contemplating agreeing, and his clean hand pushed the other man away when he took a few steps closer. It was instinctual. His body just moved to do the first thing he could think of, and it just felt right to do.

Though Mydei swayed, he didn’t move from his spot beside him at the bar. And though he only meant to push, his hand didn’t move away from the plush muscle of his bicep.

It was comforting to feel him there, especially since this was uncharted territory he was blindly waltzing into. His only guide through the maze, and his only support in this secret endeavor, was him. He had to hold him.

Who knew where he’d end up if he didn’t.

“Let’s talk about it some other time,” Phainon suggested, overwhelmed by everything they had talked about. “I would love to eat, then get ready for bed. If I’m lucky, I’ll forget this in the morning.”

“You didn’t drink nearly enough for that. Don’t delude yourself,” he chuckled back at him, allowing himself to be held.

He almost wished he drank more. Things would be so much easier if he woke up with nothing but a headache and magic groceries in his refrigerator.

As many times as Phainon had woken up in the middle of the night to change sleeping positions, the dreams of being his best friend’s submissive partner didn’t leave. And unfortunately for him, they weren’t even one long, cohesive dream that he could slip right back into. That would have been too easy. It would have been too kind.

Instead, his imagination ran wild with whatever scenario it could think up, but he remembered only one when he woke up.

He recalled the scene where he was on his knees and looking up at Mydei’s dimly lit figure with unwavering clarity. He could remember every detail in the outfit his best friend wore, a black-colored button down shirt with his tie loosened beneath its undone buttons and dark, fitted jeans that hugged his thighs nicely. A gold and navy pin attached to his tie glittered despite the poor lighting, and it matched the heavy, dangling earring beneath his ear.

There weren’t any words telling him what to do, just the weight of silent yet deafening authority gazing down on him. But he wasn’t able to speak either. His mouth had been free, and his lips could move to formulate the shape of words, but the sound of his voice was stolen. It didn’t want to come out.

All he could do was sit there and rely on the other man to just… know. He had to trust him to make sense of, and follow through with, the things he couldn’t communicate.

It left Phainon on edge the whole day, and he mentally blamed Mydei for it completely.

Had he never mentioned his ex-submissive so casually, he never would have gone searching online for all things BDSM-related that night. And had he never gone online to see the violent depictions of sex and domination, then he never would have felt the need to ensure his best friend wasn’t secretly a terrible person. And had they never had that conversation last night, then he never would have had a dream so chilling and intrusive.

That image of Mydei mixed with his authoritative voice last night was all Phainon could think about at work.

His hands shook while tapping on the screen of his tablet to take orders, sometimes clicking the wrong option and having to make his tables wait longer than they should so he could fix it. The painted smile on his lips when serving their dishes was just a ploy to mask the sinking, dirty feeling in his stomach for being so distracted. Each pitched word that came from his mouth was rushed and overly excited, leading to a few weird looks and awkward smiles, but he just didn’t want them to hear what it sounded like shaking.

Then, as he listened to the chefs shouting at one another and chopping things at record speed in the kitchen, all it reminded him of was Mydei gripping him by the face and telling him not to speak. Those fingerprints stained the skin of his chin and jaw, phantoms pressing into them when he found himself still for too long.

He had looked so… in control, so in his element as he stood above him and told him what to do. It was as if he somehow knew how far to push and when to give him his space.

But was he seriously going to agree to that proposition? Was he going to just hand over everything to Mydei and follow behind him like a dog on a leash?

How long would this thing between them last? Did Mydei have an end in mind for it, or was it just until he decided he either liked it or hated it?

“Damn,” a huff pulled himself out of his thoughts, and he looked over to his co-worker as she peeked down at her phone. “My stupid month trial is up…”

His lips wobbled into a shaky grin. Then, he laughed quietly to himself and hoped that was just a freak coincidence.

Logic told him that people couldn’t read minds. They couldn’t hear thoughts either. No matter how rampant and loud the words became or how long strangers looked at him and stood by him, these thoughts and feelings were his alone. The only other person who knew of them was Mydei, and he was on the other side of the city in his office at this point in time. He doubted the man was thinking about him as he took phone calls, sent out reports, and read his emails.

But even if he knew that, it felt as if his shame was printed across his skin for all to see. To him, he might as well have the word ‘pervert’ tattooed over his forehead in big, bold letters.

—

After work, he decided to just swallow down what was left of his pride and text Mydei. He wanted to see if he could swing by his condo to hang out for a little bit, as it would make him feel a little bit better to have company around. Though, the most important part of this was having company he could confide in. Otherwise, he had other friends who he knew weren’t doing anything tonight.

And as he always did, his best friend gave him a time to show up.

While at his kitchen bar, he almost wanted to ask for a drink stronger than his simple ice water, but he wasn’t necessarily a drinker. Not like Mydei, who was fixing himself a glass of something strong just to take the edge off after a long day. Or maybe to give himself the confidence to have another emotionally charged conversation too.

Should he ask?

“Have you eaten?” Mydei spoke before he could.

“More than I should’ve probably,” he joked, watching as his best friend leaned back into his refrigerator comfortably. “I visited my mom to pass the time before I came over, and she cooked up this whole feast.”

“Did she really?” He encouraged him to keep speaking. “How has she and your father been?”

“Mm… She spent most of the time telling me how much she misses our hometown. One of these days, I need to get her out of the city and bring her back to that old, rickety house,” he signed wistfully, thinking of his childhood home. “The smell of the ocean and the fields would be so much better than all this pollution.”

“You should,” Mydei rasped out, powering through the burn of his liquor. “Your father works hard too… All of you should take a trip back and recharge.”

“It’s just hard with all of our busy schedules,” he brushed off. “When I save up enough and have some days off, I’ll mention it to them… Hey, maybe I can kidnap you and show you where I used to live before we met.”

“‘Good morning’ and ‘good night’.”

His attention lifted, finding Mydei was already looking at him with his arms crossed over his chest. The food he had worried about was still sitting in a bowl beside him, cold and untouched, since he found himself busy with him instead.

“You want me to tell you that every day and night?” He clarified, just a little bit confused. “You’ll make fun of me when you see how late I go to bed… especially on nights I don’t work the next day. I can already hear you scolding my sleeping schedule.”

“I enjoy having a present submissive. One that updates me on their lives and includes me even if I’m not around,” he explained. “I won’t make you. But if you’re seriously considering this, then that’s one thing I’ll expect out of you.”

If he was being honest, two text messages didn’t seem like a lot to ask out of someone. Wanting the person he’s seeing to think of him so often and keep him informed of their day seemed like the most normal thing of all this.

He hasn’t dated in awhile, but he would do that without being told if he was in a relationship.

“I can. I’ll text you more.”

“I keep my phone silenced at work, but I check it periodically. You may text me as much as you’d like for whatever you’d like,” he allowed like that wasn’t already a channel open for him.

“If I see really fat cats when I’m out running, do you want me to send them to you?” He joked, trying to push their previous topic out completely.

Mydei stifled a chuckle, his eyes pinching from the lift of his amused grin. “Yes, Phainon. Please send me videos of the fat stray cats around your apartment complex. Update me as much as you can.”

“I can do that since you’re going out of your way to make this as comfortable as possible for me. Is there anything else you might want, master?” He teased, the word a little less daunting to say the more he used it.

His eyes rolled over the title. “You can also compile a list of the things you like for me. I know some off the top of my head, but a document would help.”

Phainon’s head tilted in confusion. “That’s weird. Why would I do that?”

“I want you to,” was his response. “If you want a specific pair of boots or a certain bottle of cologne, link it in that document and send the file to me. With it, I want to know the sizing too if necessary.”

A quiet laugh left his lips, now aware of why he wanted to know so much about him. It wasn’t rocket science to put two and two together.

“I’m not letting you—”

“Good behavior should be rewarded. If homemade desserts and meals won’t motivate you, allow me to spice up the reward pool,” Mydei cut him off, standing firm on his request. “You don’t need to ‘let me’.”

Phainon covered his face as heat began to burn underneath his skin from his stern tone and the nature of his request.

He thought about his best friend essentially spoiling him in gifts, and it brought a bittersweet knot to his stomach. It was one thing to force groceries at his doorstep, or maybe cover a meal every now and then when they shared one, but things like colognes and shoes would be too much. As kind of a gesture as it was, he couldn’t possibly let him pour money into him. This was meant to be a temporary arrangement, after all.

This wasn’t real. It was an experiment between someone who was experienced and someone playing with the idea of kinks and fetishes. A trial run to see if he liked it or not.

He couldn’t accept gifts like that. It’d be like taking advantage of him, and Phainon did not want to do that.

“Mydei, that’s not necessary,” he promised him. “I won’t be doing that one.”

“Does it upset you? Why?”

He shrugged. “I just don’t need that.”

“Yes, that’s why I said ‘want’, Phainon,” he mused. “You don’t need these things, but everyone has wants. For instance, I want to give them to you. It’s the same as if—”

“I just can’t accept gifts for nothing, okay?” He rushed to say. “Cologne, shoes, and things like that get expensive. I can’t let you spend that much money on me for whatever this is. You should use it on yourself or tuck it away for a rainy day.”

“I want to,” he repeated himself with a little bit more force. “Phainon, you are trying very hard for me. The things I’ve been asking of you are far from your comfort zone, but you’re pushing past it anyways to learn and understand. That is not ‘nothing’. Your efforts deserve to be rewarded.”

Phainon’s lip wobbled, and he shook his head while planting both elbows on the counter. He hid himself further, unable to let the other man see a single bit of his face.

“You just… Why’d you have to go and say that?” He asked him, already feeling the crack in his resolve. “Why’d you have to be so… supportive? You’re talking me up as if I’m doing something ground breaking when I’m just… trying out some sex stuff.”

“It’s not ‘sex stuff’. We haven’t had sex, but here we are still exercising this loose dynamic of you entrusting in me and me guiding you. That’s dominance. That’s submission,” Mydei explained, and Phainon’s shoulders shook with a silent chuckle.

He hated him.

Oh, Phainon hated that Mydei was so passionate about wanting to reward him because he knew he meant it. That was just the kind of guy he was, supportive until the grave. Even then, he would probably tag along as a ghost and continue egging him on to keep being better, to keep pushing himself to overcome his worries and fears.

“Fine,” he caved, glaring at the other man through his spread fingers. “Fine, I’ll do it! I’ll make that dumb list, and you can just play sugar daddy!”

“Thank you,” he said in return, earnest. “And I’m not a ‘sugar daddy’. I provide more than just sex and money to someone, so watch it.”

“I know. I know. I’m just talking shit. God, I feel like such a mess…” He grumbled, rolling his head to the side before sighing. “Mydei, I’m exhausted.”

“You’re welcome to stay the night, but I have a meeting to attend early in the morning. I then promised Cassie I would help her bake a cake for someone,” he informed him, tone slightly solemn as if apologetic.

Speaking of cake…

One arm dropped, and he picked up the fork beside him before bringing a bite of his forgotten treat to his mouth. Sugar and the light tang of lemon filled his tastebuds, and he sighed dreamily to himself over it.

It was making him feel a little bit better after the emotional rollercoaster he just went on, like the lollipops doctors gave him after getting shots as a kid.

“What will you do with the rest of that?” He asked curiously, pointing to the baking dish still on the counter. “That’s a lot for one person.”

“Perhaps one of our friends would enjoy it.”

He nodded, swallowed, and then pointed his fork to where Mydei was standing instead.

“Now, I need to ask this so be honest, De. Have you ever fed us things you baked for your other submissives?” He narrowed his eyes on him. “Did you feed us leftovers of their reward treats?”

“Hm…” His lips were pulled between his teeth, and he drummed his fingers over his arms before nodding his head slowly. “A few times I made something for them, but because they misbehaved, I packaged it up and gave it to you guys.”

“We ate someone’s punishment dessert…” He mumbled to himself, taking another bite while wondering what gifts were of the heart and what were simply disposed on to him.

“The cinnamon rolls Cyrene gobbled up with her coffee—”

“Oh! Those were good too. Thank whoever that guy was for whatever he did to upset you. I promise that tray did not go to waste,” Phainon grinned happily at the memory. “You have to make those for us again.”

“Say please.”

Their eyes met, and a light flutter filled his stomach over the stern tilt to his voice and expression.

Fork to his lip, he flashed a smile back at the man. “Please make those again for us,” he obeyed.

“I’ll keep in mind that you liked them. If you continue to behave well, I will continue to give you things you want,” he promised him, nodding with approval. “If you become a spoiled brat, I’ll have to refrain from giving you anything at all.”

“Yes, master,” he joked.

“You like that title a lot, don’t you?” Mydei taunted him. “If you keep that up, I’m going to slap a collar around your neck.”

The hand not holding his fork reached for the leather band he wore daily in his neck, and he pulled it a few times before letting go.

“Can’t. I already have my choker, and I don’t take it off. There’s no space for a collar here,” he mouthed off, not taking him seriously.

“You want to bet?”

Now he was taking him seriously.

“H-Huh?”

“No, not yet. I have rules, you have limits, and we need to agree on them.” Mydei looked away, rubbing his jaw as he exhaled. “That’s… a conversation for another time. Forgive me, I got carried away.”

“Bring them over this weekend,” he allowed. “Your rules… you have them written somewhere, right? Surely it’s not just in your head. Knowing you, there’s definitely some kind of folder.”

“Yes. Of course.” He nodded. “I’ll bring my list, and we’ll discuss them at your place. If we move forward with this, then I will be able to collar you. You won’t take that one off either.”

He gulped, holding the base of his throat gingerly as he imagined some kind of thick, leather collar squeezing it. Maybe it would be the ones with a heavy metal ring in the middle, the kinds people wore casually for an edgy fashion sense. Though he doubted Mydei wanted him in a collar for fashion’s sake when he mentioned chains looked best when attached to them.

Was he seriously meant to wear two leather chokers on top of each other every single day? That would look ridiculous to other people and feel uncomfortable for everyone.

But maybe he’d get a say in it.

Knowing Mydei and how he’s been with him, maybe they’ll be able to talk about it then too. They could make it as comfortable as possible, and they could decide together about when and where he was meant to wear it. His best friend wouldn’t jeopardize his life by making him walk around in some kind of dog collar at work or at home. He believed in that. He trusted him with that.

His fingers lowered, leaving his neck to lay against the counter.

Yeah, it would be okay.

some bratty little touch-starved phainon getting, well, touched in this too. and mydei being his soft-ish dom self

Sunday morning, Phainon started his day off with his face smashed into his pillow, one eye cracked open, and his nearly-dead phone balanced beneath his hand. The edge was pinned to his bed, holding it in place as his thumb lazily dragged against his blurry keyboard. Every so often it slipped and clicked the wrong key, and while trying to delete it, he nearly dozed back off into a longer sleep.

> [Phainon: Goof Morbingg Myfei]

> [Phainon: Good Morning Mydei*]

Within seconds—maybe, he had nodded off again while staring at his text messages—his phone buzzed in his hand. The sudden vibration jerked him awake, causing his eyes to snap open and his phone to fall screen down into his bed.

Groaning, he lifted it back up and then looked at the screen, eyes squinted to read the response.

> [Mydei: What morning? It is 11:36am…]

> [Mydei: This is to be expected when you go to bed at 3am. You should have slept earlier.]

> [Mydei: Did you at least sleep well?]

> [Mydei: This idiot fell asleep on his keyboard. No way it takes that long to type something out…]

His eyes rolled. Had he not called it—Mydei bullying him for his sleeping schedule on his days off? It was as if he knew the future.

Phainon quickly tapped against the keyboard again, more awake than he had been when he sent his first few text messages.

> [Phainon: Okay DAD]

> [Phainon: And yeah, I slept great. Out like a light.]

Phainon couldn't remember what his dream was, but he hasn’t had another night where Mydei had an almost ominous aura from above him. His imagination has been nice to him and his rest. If he was in one, it was simply as his best friend—smiling, laughing, and calling him stupid.

He wondered, at the moment, if it was because Mydei was making all of this BDSM stuff out to be less… dark… than he had originally believed.

> [Mydei: Don’t call me that. I’m not on your birth certificate. If I was, you wouldn’t be asleep at 12pm.]

> [Mydei: At least you slept well. Tell me about your dreams if you remember them.]

Phainon hated him. What was he going to do about him sleeping in when they really get this ball rolling? Punish him because he was tired?

> [Phainon: It’s my day off and I’m a grown man. Mind your business.]

> [Phainon: And I didn’t remember this one. Next one, I’ll tell you.]

This time, instead of Mydei sending another text to him, he got an audio message about twelve seconds long. The play button stared back at him until he clicked it, and he cranked the volume up to better hear.

“So long as you’re doing this dance with me, your business will always be my business,” Mydei said to him, leaving no room for doubt or discussion. “And mind your tone when you're texting me, Phainon. Don’t be a brat.”

Underneath his voice was the chime of a store’s door opening, then the muffled greeting of the receptionist to a woman. It wasn’t his mom’s though, as Phainon knew her voice well and it wasn’t that high.

He was saying that in public. Maybe outside of whatever place he was at with his mom, waiting for her and biding his time by texting him. Or, well, talking to him for that instance.

Phainon shivered as he listened to it again, taking note of how his voice lowered in both volume and depth when telling him to behave. Like he was being not only firm to drive his point across but cautious of his surroundings.

Then he listened to it again, specifically that second half, and he hummed to himself as a warmth pooled into his stomach.

Once it finished, he tapped the microphone on his own keyboard and then raised it to his mouth.

“Heh, you never said anything about when I speak to you.” His own words were lowered from their usual pitch from just waking up, and they dripped with attitude. “You should mind what you say in public, master. You could get caught saying something you shouldn’t.”

He sent it, then turned the screen off before dropping the device on to his bed and sighing.

“Do not check that phone until he comes over,” he said to himself as it buzzed, and buzzed, and buzzed.

Mydei might just kill him, but why did that thought make his stomach feel so giddy?

—

Later, he had scrubbed his skin until he swore it was cleaner than ever, brushed his teeth twice just in case something happened there, and tidied up his bedroom since that was where he figured they’d be most of the time. Clothes were put in the wash to get rid of the pile on his chair. His bed was made up to make sure it didn’t look like he slept in until noon. The window was cracked open, curtains pulled open to let a nice breeze in.

It was perfect if Mydei decided he wanted to mess around a little bit. Well, hopefully it was perfect. He hasn’t done that in a while, and it was nerve-wracking to think about.

Phainon was busy agonizing over his hair in his mirror when his phone buzzed again from his back pocket. Seconds later, the doorbell rang.

Oh, was Mydei going to kill him for teasing him in public and then ignoring him for the last few hours?

A mix of nerves, excitement, and shame twisted inside of him, and he pulled just beneath his t-shirt’s collar to gently fan his heated skin off. Each step only made it worse, until he was standing at the door with his hand on the knob. It felt as if he would throw up, but he was trying desperately not to.

His phone buzzed again, causing him to suck in a deep breath before twisting the lock and opening the door.

“Where is your phone?” Was the first thing Mydei asked as he walked into his apartment, though it was clearly him demanding to know why he wasn’t responding to him. “Dead? Charging? Half way across the damn city?”

Phainon shook his head. “In my back pocket,” he answered honestly, unsure why his belly felt so… tingly.

“Then why weren’t you texting me back all afternoon? Did your fingers break while trying to make yourself pretty for me?” He pressed.

His best friend walked around him, making his presence known inside of his apartment before he pushed the front door closed on his own. The force reverberated through the walls and trembled them for a moment, then a steady quiet filled the space between them.

Not even his refrigerator kicked on to hum, as if holding its own breath in the face of his best friend’s wrath.

Mydei leaned over him. The arm that had shoved his door closed bent at the elbow, pushing him in closer.

“W-Woah,” he mumbled, chuckling awkwardly to himself as his eyes raked over his best friend’s face and neck. “Mydei, y-you’re um… close…”

He was in his personal space at this point, but when wasn’t he? Since talking about this, it felt as if the man was always touching him or closing in on him to back him into a corner— metaphorically and physically. There was nowhere to go trapped between his body and the door, then nowhere to hide inside of his small apartment. In his head, there was still only him in all of his thoughts and senses.

It made his heart beat pick up just a little bit.

“Hands,” Mydei demanded, and Phainon lifted both of his hands for him to see the second it left his mouth. “Not a single bandage in sight. Is your phone charged? Let’s find out. Make these useful and hold this for me.”

A deep, wine red folder was handed to him, and he marveled for a moment at how heavy it was inside of his grasp.

This wasn’t what he was expecting at all. Just how many rules did he have for this to feel like some kind of magazine? How many pages lived inside of this plastic sleeve?

“Look at me.”

His eyes lifted, meeting Mydei’s as he raised his phone to his pierced ear. The screen darkened when close enough, but he had seen the contact photo before it did. He knew it was his own since it had been the same for years now—a picture of them at their college graduation.

As the dial tone rang, Phainon’s ring tone began to chime. Each vibration in his back pocket made him sink deeper within himself.

“So, f-funny story,” he smiled sheepishly, clutching the plastic folder tighter as the eyes looking down at him narrowed. Clearly, he wasn’t in the mood for ‘funny stories’. “You see, I was so focused on cleaning up that I forgot to check my phone. I completely zoned out! You know me, I can be a bit of a ditz.”

“Mm…”

Mydei very obviously didn’t believe him, but he also didn’t seem too keen on calling him out on his lie.

“Let’s not ‘forget’ to text me back next time, okay?” Mydei hinted at, eyes travelling down his face and neck before picking back up to his own. “You want to be good, don’t you? You want me to praise you, speak highly of you, and reward you with nice things and delicious treats, right?”

A shaky breath fell from his lips, and though he couldn’t bring himself to nod, he knew it was obvious.

“Then the next time you decide to act like a mouthy little brat while I’m out with my mother, you’re going to take the consequences like a man instead of running off like a child,” he instructed him, speaking slowly to emphasize his seriousness. “Got it?”

He nodded weakly.

“I need to hear you, Phainon.”

“Yeah. Y-Yeah, I got it,” he forced himself to say.

Mydei gave one last look over his flustered expression before pulling away. With it, Phainon bit down on the inside of his lip and pulled the folder to his chest as if the plastic would cool his skin through his shirt.

“How was your morning?” He asked, following behind him as he made his way to the living room. “What’d you guys do?”

“She wanted to get her car detailed, so I took her to the hair salon for an appointment while we waited,” he answered. “I need stationary. Where are your…”

“Pens?”

“You don’t own markers anymore, do you?” He deadpanned, and Phainon shrugged. “When was the last time you saw a highlighter that wasn’t in college?”

“On my paystub when they highlight my cut after taxes.”

“Oh…” Mydei smacked a hand to his forehead. Breathing deep, he then nodded. “I know Cyrene has some kind of pink, purple, blue, or whatever kind of markers in her room. Please grab them.”

“She would kill me if I went into her room while she was gone…” He trailed off, more scared of her than he was of testing Mydei’s authority.

“Don’t get caught.”

His blood would be on Mydei's hands.

Phainon, still holding that folder to his chest, walked towards his roommate’s bedroom and flinched as he opened the door even if he knew she wasn’t there.

There would be no possible way that she knew he was in here unless there was a camera hidden inside of a teddy bear, but that bunny on her bed felt like it was watching him. If it was sending live footage to her phone right now, he wouldn’t be surprised. Since his phone wasn’t ringing and she wasn’t scolding him in fragmented words because of poor cell service, maybe he was just being paranoid.

His fingers pulled her desk drawer open, and he sighed as he picked up a set of adorably packaged highlighters.

“Don’t kill me, ‘rene,” he mumbled.

Once in hand, Phainon rushed out the door, a weight in his chest like she just knew what he was going to do with him. Like she was a fly on the wall and ready to make fun of him.

He set them on his coffee table, and Mydei stifled a chuckle over the cartoon characters printed on each one.

“Those are very cute.”

“Don’t mock them!” He hissed, hitting his best friend in the chest with his own folder. “Why do we need markers anyways? Are we studying this thing?”

“I’m not mocking them. They’re cute,” he repeated, then opened the sleeve up. “And yes, you and I will be discussing and creating our rules.”

“What? You don’t just smack me with the Ten Commandments and I have to oblige like a devout follower?” He grumbled, sitting down on the carpet between his table and couch. “Yes, master, my master. Whatever you wish from me, your darling slave-in-training.”

“That tongue in your mouth will get you in trouble. I advise you to bite it. Now,” he warned him but sat beside him anyway. “Here’s the key for how we’ll revise these pages. Understand this before we do anything else…”

He picked three markers out, then placed a pad of white sticky notes in front of them.

“This… red-ish, pink-ish… color means ‘no’.” As he spoke, he scribbled a box shape down and the word beside it. “This means absolutely not. You will not do that under any circumstances. Reserve this for your hard-limits.”

Phainon pulled his knees to his chest as he nodded, watching him pick up another one from the pack.

“This orange-ish, yellow-ish color means ‘maybe’.” Again, he scribbled in the shape of a box and wrote the word beside it. “This means you’re not happy with this or you’re unsure of it, but you’re willing to do it with a push from me. Your softer and pushable limits will fall here. Understand?”

“Yeah, it makes sense so far.”

“This green-ish, blue-ish color is ‘yes’.” For a third time, he created a final box at the bottom of the notes. “It means yes. You like it, and you want it.”

“I would have never guessed,” he joked, and Mydei shook his head as he peeled the note off. It was placed on top of his folder’s cover, then flattened out for easy access and reading.

Color-coded, like the tupperware in his fridge and the books on his shelves. He knew his best friend liked things neat and organized, but he never imagined him to be this meticulous with order.

“Now, we should have a safeword. Do you know what that is?” He asked, and Phainon hummed as he thought about it.

Safe… word. Safe meaning ‘to protect’, and word being, well, a word.

A word that protects.

“Is it something you say when you're scared?” He answered unsurely, hearing of it when he did his short venture online but never quite getting an explanation of it. “Or maybe a word to use when you don’t feel safe doing something anymore?”

“You’re close. This is a word that stops our play,” he explained to him, tapping the capped tip of a purple pen to the pad of sticky notes. “This word tells me you need a time out, and it tells you that I need a time out. It should be easy to remember and quick to say, and we both need to adhere to it.”

“What does someone say if they can’t speak?” He asked him curiously. “You put that tomato in my mouth to keep me quiet. Had it been something… different, what do I do with something I can’t swallow or remove?”

“See these?” Mydei pointed to the color code, and he nodded. “One finger. Two fingers. Three. I’ll ask you how you’re doing, and you’ll give me one of these signals. You’re at your limit. You’re nearing your limit. You’re good.”

He drew tally marks in each corresponding color, and Phainon looked at his own hand before lifting his fingers accordingly.

“Okay…”

This was both easy to remember yet a lot to swallow down.

“As for a safeword, think of something. What would you not say while doing something… sexual?” He brought the purple marker back, this time with its cap open.

“Can I just say a color if you ask me for one?” He wondered, figuring that would be the easiest solution. Otherwise, he’d be here for a while wondering what word was good enough to be considered a safeword, and that didn’t sound fun at all.

“Final answer?”

He nodded, and Mydei wrote that down before placing it beside his other note.

As he sat there watching him organize his things, Phainon leaned down to his shoulder and rested his cheek against it. The hand with a marker woven between his fingers raised, settling over the top of his head to bring him in closer. For comfort, he leaned back further, slouching just a bit and turning his knees closer to Mydei’s body. If he bumped the coffee table, he only mentioned it with a short, amused breath.

“This isn’t so bad, right?” Mydei smiled softly, and Phainon looked at the crisp pages he was pulling out with his free hand. “Are you okay?”

“Fine,” he brushed off, catching a glimpse of some words printed amongst the bulletpoint list. “Just… really surprised. I’ve known you almost all my life, but this is the first time I’ve ever seen… this. It’s the most shocking part.”

“This was my business,” he said simply, matter-of-factly. “But since you want to do this dance with me, it’s now our business. There's nothing for me to hide from you.”

“You say that to all your submissives to make them feel special?” Phainon teased him, wondering how many people have sat here in his spot and gone over these things with him.

Did they all use the same color systems? Did they all have the same exact rules to follow and lines to learn?

How many times has he done this… ‘dance’?

Mydei chuckled, his shoulder shaking and bouncing his cheek in tandem. “No, they typically know what to expect, which makes a lot of this redundant. A few of them have bossed me around during this phase too, bringing their own rules to me.”

“Mm… But you do this with them all?”

“Yes. My sub will always have a say in what we practice. I’m not God, and they’re not devout followers. But, I’ve never used a… black cat… pen while doing this before,” he commented, looking at the cartoon character before showing it to him. “What is that exactly?”

“Kuromi,” he answered.

“Kur—huh?”

“You don’t know Sanrio characters? What kind of a big, bad dominant are you?” He mocked him, and Mydei blinked a few times as if processing his insult. “The one you used for ‘red’ is My Melody, and ‘yellow’ is Pompompurin.”

“Pompompu—what?” He repeated, and Phainon laughed over his confusion. “What kind of a ridiculous name is that?”

“What kind of a name is Mydei?” He shot back, and the other man rolled his eyes before bringing his arm back down. “I like that one, you know. The yellow one.”

“Do you?”

He nodded, and Mydei picked the highlighter up before rubbing his thumb over the character.

“I suppose it’s cute. This one reminds me of you though,” he said, handing him a pale blue pen from inside the case.

Phainon looked down at it, at the ivory puppy with bright blue eyes. “I look like that?” He asked.

“Yes.”

His fist gripped it tightly, and he hummed to himself as Mydei began preparing his trio-colored pens to mark up some more pages.

“Do you just keep a stack of your rules handy to rinse and repeat this step?”

“A few at least. Feelings always tend to change over time. You may think you hate something, then turn around and feel up for it a month later when things get more comfortable,” he answered. “I’m going to tell you what I expect from you, and you’re going to tell me how you feel about it—red, yellow, or green.”

Phainon nodded, fiddling with the pen in hand as he awaited the list. His thumb pushed and pulled the cap off, adding a click to the ambiance of their comfortable silence. While Mydei stacked the papers neatly on the table and readied them in front of him, he was already reading the text printed on the page.

“If I don’t like it?”

“Then we discuss it and come up with one we both do, or I can just cross it out,” he told him. “This is a mutual agreement we should both benefit from. When we finish, you will tell me your expectations of me too.”

That sounded fair to him, but he wasn’t quite sure what he expected out of him besides to just… lead. Wasn’t that the whole point?

He didn’t know anything about this. It was so uncomfortable, yet for some reason his body kept reacting positively to it—to the praise, silent ownership, and being dragged along. Those tingles deep inside of his gut and the boil of his blood when things felt right were so foreign to him, and he needed help navigating them.

He needed Mydei to show him, teach him what to want and ask for, and cushion the negativity that clawed in his gut.

Why did he need to have any other expectations than just… ‘take control’? What else was there?

The capped butt of a red marker was used to motion to each bullet point statement, and Phainon listened as he read it, explained it, and gave an example.

He expected him to text him ‘good morning’ and ‘good night’ every day. If he didn’t have service for any reason and physically could not, that was fine. Things happened and they couldn’t control that. But, if he simply chose not to do it, then it would be taken as he didn’t care to speak with him. There would be two warnings, and the last would be a punishment. His punishment would be having to physically drive over and apologize in person—tedious to do if he was tired after a busy day and embarrassing to think about.

It would be easier to just text him throughout the day, he agreed.
