The only things Phainon expected to do after he got home from work the next day was to organize his apartment a little bit and prepare an excuse as to why Cyrene’s Cinnamoroll marker had a cracked lid. His apartment was already clean because he pretty much only used it to get dressed for work. The fridge was full because he hadn't been eating at home except for making lunch. Even his bedroom was spotless besides for a half-full basket of clothes that needed to be washed soon.

But two things happened after he started some last minute preparations—the first being Cyrene calling to say she got stuck in traffic since she left too late this morning, and the second being Mydei coming over earlier than he expected with a few bags inside of his arms.

It was as if he rushed over as soon as he got off the clock, not bothering to stay a second longer inside of his second home—his office. Which, he couldn’t blame him, but it also wasn’t really like him to do. Most days he stayed an extra thirty minutes or hour to work late.

“Pour me a glass of whatever you have. I don’t want to open the wine before I start cooking, but if I have to, I will.” That was the first thing Mydei said to him as he walked into his apartment. His eyebrows were pinched in frustration, and a tightness flexed in his jaw briefly. “Then swap her old pack of highlighters out with these.”

“Huh? You found the same pack?”

“Yes. I rushed to pick them up from the store when I got off,” he sighed, and the sound of its plastic pouch touching his countertop followed. “And for the trouble of even messing with her things, I also bought you both one of these. It would appear odd to randomly give her something when we aren’t close, so congratulations on being my scapegoat, Phainon. You get a toy too.”

His back was already turned while Mydei continued to speak, but he heard some of his bags crinkle after. They rustled and crackled as they were dug through and folded away, then his garbage can lid flipped up with more force than anticipated.

“Thank you, but you really didn’t need to buy me anything,” he said back to him, grabbing a full bottle from his pantry as he was told to do. “Cyrene wouldn’t think it's weird, and neither would I. It’s just a kind gesture from a friend to a friend.”

“Wait. Time out. Why do you have a full bottle of that?” Mydei asked suddenly when he twisted the lid off. “Did you start drinking more on your own without telling me?”

Phainon laughed as he carefully began to pour him the drink he asked for. It was amusing to hear his offended tone at the assumption of being left out of his loop, but what was even funnier was the idea of him drinking at all by himself. That was never really his thing.

“I bought this for you.” He turned around to approach him, glass in hand to offer the other man happily. “On the off chance he decides to visit, my master likes a drink to relax. If I wanted a drink for myself, I would ask you. I promised that I would.”

“Huh… Aren’t you cute?” Mydei accepted it from him with the tilt of a smile. “Thank you.”

“Aren’t I good?” He corrected him, an edge of hope to his voice. “You take such good care of me that I wanna be someone comfortable for you to come back to, too.”

“Both,” he said. “You’re very thoughtful, and I find that both cute and admirable. You’re my good boy.”

Phainon perked up, skin tingling and stomach warming over the thought of being good for him, of doing something he could be proud of him for. He liked the way praise felt more and more each time it came.

“How was work?” He asked after, watching him take a drink. “You’re here pretty early. Plus, you made a few stops, so just how much were you rushing to get here?”

Suddenly, their mood shifted. Mydei’s soft expression soured ever-so-slightly. The crease between his eyebrows made its way back to his face.

“Terrible,” he rasped out, voice rough from the burn of liquor and tinged with annoyance. “I left as soon as I could because my father kept ringing my company line carelessly. He doesn’t think. Maybe the reason I don’t pick up my personal cell is because I don't want to answer his fucking…—”

Mydei paused. The gaze that had been on him shifted to the floor beside them, and he took a deep breath before covering his mouth. Fingers curled over his cheek, dragging slowly down his jaw and chin before closing into a fist.

“Forgive me. That was uncalled for,” he apologized swiftly, taking a moment to compose himself. “I only answer his calls if it’s related to work. He doesn’t like that, and he’ll call my office or work phone to get my attention. It frustrates me.”

Phainon watched him finish his glass, then he held his hand out to take it from him.

“You can talk about that,” he coaxed gently, noticing the red tainting his cheeks from trying to hold it in. “He works you hard, and he always has. Don’t you remember all the times I had to let you copy my notes because you were too burnt out to get out of bed?”

“I remember, but it’s not so simple,” he denied the offer while handing him the glass. “There’s nothing immediate that can be done about this, so complaining only breeds more negativity. Being angry around someone who has no part in it is ridiculous of me.”

Was that how he saw his feelings then? A burden for only him to bear? A bed to lie in with his teeth clenched tight?

That didn’t sound right. It didn’t sound fair to him.

“Complaining about things helps you feel better, master,” he hinted, dragging the title out suggestively and playfully in an attempt to lighten the mood. “Bottling things up only makes it worse. We both know I’m prone to my own outbursts and spirals, so… take it from me. It’s a… ‘do as I say, not as I do’ kinda thing.”

Mydei had been there when he crashed, burned, and exploded from his own emotions. The disgust and anxiety wasn’t something that disappeared overnight, and he was learning not to expect it to. Things took time, and things needed to be let out. Breathing easily was difficult with a chest under so much pressure.

And the same could be said about anger, right? If he was angry at his father, that wasn’t something that just fixed itself. It was a problem that needed to be talked about, the smoke aired out of its container so they could assess the damage properly.

For once, he needed to be the open and vulnerable one between them.

“You’ve been doing a very good job at not letting your emotions get to that point,” Mydei praised him casually, and he frowned slightly. “I’m very proud of you, Phainon.”

“Thank you, but this isn't about me,” he tried to explain. “You need to be more open with me about your feelings and thoughts, no matter how violent or heavy handed they are. I don’t need to be protected from you.”

A moment of silence passed between them both. Within it, only the soft trickle of whiskey filling his glass and Mydei’s deep breaths could be heard.

“Fine. It’s wrong of me to expect this kind of transparency from you but not give it back,” he caved, and that sounded much more reasonable to him.

“I’m all ears.”

“I guess I get a little… upset… when my father forces himself into my life like he owns it,” he admitted to him, then sighed agitatedly. “After all, he pushed this life on me. I never asked to be groomed into this corporate trap of his. I know I have to since there’s no one else to accept it, and that I can deal with. I’ve made peace with that. But even the semblance of a care for what I want would have been nice from him. For instance, I want him to leave me alone.”

His chest both hurt and warmed from the confession, saddened that Mydei never felt as if he could talk about this yet glad it was him he was opening up to. Conversations between them alluded to these feelings. Over the years, he learned they weren’t particularly close over the context clues and from behind the closed doors of his family home, but it must have been nice for him to finally say it all out loud for once. Even if it was a slightly coerced confession, the relief of letting it out must have felt nice.

“No, you didn’t ask for this,” Phainon agreed softly, handing him his second glass.

Absent-mindedly, Mydei took it, clutching the drink tightly while glaring at a wall. Then he scoffed in dry amusement and cold frustration. “And yet he tries to talk to me as if we’re friends. He attempts to steal my alone time as if I haven’t given him enough of my life as is. He invites me out on trips with other old, rich bastards as if I want to be there to fuel his ever-burning ego. But we aren’t friends. I’m his trophy son, but he isn’t proud of who I am, just what he made.”

“That’s not fair at all,” he added when his words paused for a break, supporting him in hopes he’d continue.

Mydei always strived to be as perfect as he could be. He knew this. His best friend worked hard back in school and at his job, strived to be as independent as fast and as effectively as possible, and continued to maintain a clean image so as to not embarrass the people around him.

Phainon couldn’t help but feel terrible. He wished he could do something, anything, to help him, but all he could do was listen and hope it was good enough.

“Why would I waste what little free time I have with him when I can use it on things that are actually important to me?” Mydei demanded. “Nearly every day I have to stay late, or take my work home, because he hires the sons and their friends of his friends. But they’re all so damn bottle-fed that they can't even send a proper email! I have to proofread their work like a school teacher before it goes out or it makes us all look stupid! But he doesn’t care because denying these guys ruins his oh-so perfect image. So I have to do my job, then I have to babysit, then I have to give him my free time off the clock, then I can finally think about myself? Fuck that!”

Phainon set a hand on his arm, squeezing his bicep tightly. “Hey, it’s alright,” he hushed him.

“No, it’s not fucking alright, Phainon! I—”

Mydei’s trembling hand suddenly covered his mouth again. This time his fingers dug into his face, silencing himself completely so he could take a couple of deep breaths. As he did so, he shook his head slowly.

It seemed he was done spilling his guts. The horrified expression on his face read that he had come to realize the bloody mess before him, and Mydei hated a mess.

“Just breathe for me,” he said softly, and their eyes met as he exhaled shakily into his hand. “It’s not fair, you're right. You work very hard, try to make yourself available for everyone else with what little time you have to yourself, and it’s not fair for him to exploit you to make himself look better to his friends. You’re more than just a shiny trophy to reflect off of.”

“Phainon, I-I shouldn’t dump this on you. I shouldn’t have yelled at you like that,” he apologized again, voice rough but trying to be compassionate. “You have your own troubles to work through with everything we have going on. I’m complaining and whining like a selfish child, and I’m sorry.”

“Hey, we made an agreement, remember? Signed our names in those Sanrio markers and everything," he reminded him, chuckling softly at the memory. “You told me if I ever felt too ill to take care of myself, you would step in to help me. Well, it goes the same way, right? If you feel too mentally exhausted to do anything, then I have to do more to help you relax. This isn’t some one-sided thing where I get pampered like a prince and you deal with the world on your own. It’s mutual.”

Mydei would have to be stupid to think he’d just stand there and let him suffer on his own. Submissive or not, he was still his best friend, and every word he spoke was coming from the depths of his chest as someone who loved him dearly. Because he did. He loved Mydei, and that meant he wanted to make sure he was okay.

“If you’re exhausted, go rest in my bed while I cook for us all. If you’re overwhelmed, tell me what I can do to lighten the mental load,” he said earnestly. “If this trouble with work and your dad makes you feel powerless, then take what I have. It’s yours."

“Phainon…”

He smiled sweetly up at him. Soft eyes the color of summer’s sky searching the golden ones burning across from him.

“That’s me,” he returned playfully, hoping to ease some of that heat. “C’mon, don’t be like that. All of the things we’ve done together, yet this has you speechless?”

Phainon brushed his fingertips down his sleeved arm, admiring the way his biceps and forearms filled out the fabric before spinning his wrist around. He grabbed his elbow carefully, raising it without a warning, and then popped open the button on his left cuff.

“Let’s start with getting you comfortable,” he suggested. “You look so dressed up that it’s making me feel overwhelmed. These tight cuffs, that belt, and your buttoned collar must be suffocating right now.”

Smooth, dark fabric was folded up to his forearm as he usually saw it after work, revealing sweat-damp skin and still-flexed muscle. Afterwards, he took Mydei’s other arm to do the same thing. He lifted its weight, raised his wrist, and gently folded his sleeve as close as possible to the opposite side.

They hung limp by his best friend’s sides, and he took that moment to hold either in his forearms. Fingers pinched to try and massage them, lining up and down in an attempt to ease their tensed state. As he did so, Phainon’s eyes found the tie still pressed snug to his stiff collar.

Trailing his hands higher, he stretched them open wider to accommodate his upper arms and rubbed gently between his muscles. The pads of his thumbs moved in careful, circular motions, travelling until he found his shoulders. Fingers squeezed around them, pinching around his stiffened body.

“You don’t need to do all of this,” Mydei whispered, taken back by the gentle handling of his body.

Phainon only grinned back at him.

“I don’t need to,” he agreed, speaking much more firmly. “Just as I don’t wanna be an object for you, I don’t want you to sacrifice your well-being to protect me. So, let me.”

His touch lowered, dragging along his collarbones before finding the fabric of his tie. Without being asked and without any warning, Phainon began to unravel its knot slowly.

“You shouldn’t push yourself too much. You’ll burn out,” he was told. “I already made you do more than I should have, and we saw how that went. You freaked out. You felt terrible for days. A mistake made in repetition stops being a mistake and becomes a choice, and I won’t let us choose to put you through that again.”

Phainon bit down on the inside of his lip, chewing it deeply as he remembered the drop he experienced.

He was terrified that all his worries would actualize, that after the kindness and comfort given to him became unexciting, Mydei would be like those cruel men he saw online. The redness in his skin and the tenderness of his chest was so foreign, and the fact Mydei wanted him to feel that way because he enjoyed seeing him like that scared him a little bit. It was too new and too much at once, something he didn’t realize until after all the pleasure subsided and left him sore, dirty, and cold. Never had he felt his head so detached from both his body and reality.

Leaving him to rest by himself and offering to leave him alone made him afraid that he opened himself up to be discarded by the person he cared about most. To brush him off so quickly made him insecure of his place. It made him want to lash out to gather some kind of reaction that proved Mydei cared, that he wasn’t just another person in his bed.

But he didn’t know what it would be like, and Mydei didn’t think he’d drop so hard. Between not knowing each other’s bodies well and pushing the boundaries too far, they had an accident. They made a mistake.

“You couldn’t have known how badly I’d react after all the hormones wore off,” he defended them both. “What we did then was more intense than anything I’ve ever done, but this doesn’t feel scary. This feels like helping my best friend, so don’t deny me this. Don’t deny me a chance to help the person closest to me.”

“Phainon, listen to me,” he slowed his words down and hardened his gaze. “You don’t need to do this.”

“I want to,” he stressed, trying to keep his voice steady and calm despite their disagreement. “You want me to take care of myself, and I understand that. You’re worried about pushing me too far, and I appreciate that. But this feels more natural than anything we’ve done so far.”

Mydei’s jaw tightened as he finished unraveling his tie and balancing out the tails.

“Phainon, I’m serious. Don’t say things like that to me.”

“Mydei, I am too,” he said back. “What kind of a man would I be to stand here watching you hurt but do nothing about it? What kind of a best friend would I be?”

For a moment, it looked as if his best friend wanted to say something back, but he didn’t. There was no witty retort. He had no argument to fight back with.

“Please just… tilt your chin up and allow me to be there for you. I can’t stand seeing you upset,” he requested when the silence stretched on, touching his buttoned collar next.

But Mydei didn’t budge, too busy searching his face for something to use against him.

He hummed, growing just a little bit annoyed by his continued resistance. “Please, master?” He tried again.

That seemed to work.

His head tilted back slightly, giving him enough room to unbutton the shirt he had on. Every night, he had four buttons opened up while in the comfort of his own home, so he counted each one silently while undressing him.

On the first button, he felt Mydei’s eyes continuing to stare down at him, taking in his every movement. They watched his face. They raked over his hair and lips, moving in the outer edges of his focused vision.

On the second button, he heard him breathe in deep and slow like he had earlier. His hands felt the fill and deflate of his chest, and he smelled the bitter alcohol off of his lips.

As he worked the third one open, two hands reached to settle over the smallest part of his waist, holding him tightly beneath the halves of his zip-up hoodie. Not thinking much of it, he pinched the fourth button and eased it from the slit in his shirt. This one had a slight fray in its stitching, and it peeked from the design in its button.

The moment his hands pulled away, a push sent him stumbling back.

Stiff metal smacked into his shoulders and upper back, and a quiet grunt fell from his lips. Discomfort pinched his eyebrows together, and worry immediately bloomed inside of his chest from the rattling behind him. The last thing he wanted was something to spill or break inside of his refrigerator, especially when he was so proud of his entire apartment being spotless.

“What the hell—”

“Silence,” he cut him off sharply. “You can’t say all of that and expect me not to react. Do you have any idea what words and actions like that will do to a guy like me? Do you get what you just said?”

Pawing hands pulled him to his body, jerking it from the surface he just collided with. They circled around his torso, scratching into his black t-shirt and fisting the cotton just before his shoulders blades.

“Mydei, I was just being honest.”

An echoed pounding filled his ears, but he wasn’t quite sure if it was from knocking his head back or the rush of his racing heart. Rhythmic and quick, all signs pointed to the latter.

Phainon let himself be grappled at and wrapped around, accepting the desperate touch silently. Head to the refrigerator, he let Mydei duck into his neck and wrap his arms around his body like he owned every inch of it. One of his own hands pulled him in by the belt loops of his slacks, easing their hips together so their thighs touched as well.

“Don’t call me that. Not right now,” he demanded quietly. “Don’t undress me on your own and offer up all of your control just to call me ‘Mydei’ as if you’re anyone else in the world. You know what you should call me when we’re together, so say it. Call me by the name only I get to have, and show me you meant what you said. Show me that serving me comes naturally to you. After all, that’s exactly what came out of your mouth.”

Nose to choker, his best friend buried himself into his body as if he didn’t want to be seen at all, as if he were ashamed of somehow being looked at. The anger. The frustration. The desperation. He let it show, but he didn’t want to be seen wearing it.

And Phainon understood. It was nerve wracking to feel vulnerable. It felt like being naked even when fully clothed, stripped apart even when standing in one piece, and sitting on your knees even when on your feet.

For that, he pulled his hood up with his opposite hand, tilted his head back, and let the deep purple fabric hang over his eyes. Those fingers then held the back of his head, threading upwards through the long strands to cradle him close.

“Yes, master,” he obeyed. “Take what you need from me. I’m here for you.”

He was held tighter, so tight it felt like his ribs could crack and lungs could pop, but it didn’t hurt. Neither did his back or head after that initial throb of surprise. None of it was scary, and not a single part of him wanted to change a thing in that moment.

Phainon closed his eyes as he let Mydei ground himself within his body, thinking silently to himself.

Was this what it was like when he pulled him in before? The roles were usually reversed. It was his nose buried into Mydei’s collar to breathe in his scent, and it was his emotions laid out between them to be read like a book. He was the emotional one. He was the one struggling to keep up.

It didn‘t necessarily feel good to stand here. There wasn’t much peace in knowing his best friend bottled his things up and struggled with accepting care in return. Phainon didn’t get any rush of power for being the one comforting rather than being the one comforted.

But he felt a little bit understood, like Mydei got a glimpse into the mess it felt like to be so transparent with things he never thought about sharing. After all, it was hard. It was scary.

“I want you to call me by that name until Cyrene shows up," he mumbled into his collar. “I don’t want to hear my name, I want to hear ‘master’.”

“Can you look at me while you say that please?”

Slowly, one of the hands on his body lifted and moved. It planted flat to the refrigerator behind him, forearm angled by his head to lean into his personal space. The rose on his cheeks was prevalent, just like the tear and swell in his lip from chewing on it.

“I need to hear you call me ‘master’,” he said instead, looking directly into his eyes. “I need you to do it until your roommate gets back.”

Before, he said he ‘wanted’ it. Now, he was saying he ‘needed’ it. That made him wonder what the difference was.

“Can you do that? Can you be my good boy?”

But now was probably not the time to ask, was it? That could be a conversation for a later time. Right now, all he wanted to do was help Mydei feel better.

His hand slid from his hair to his cheek as he hummed lightly, cupping his haw. “Yes, master. I’ll be good,” he promised him.

“Good.”

They stayed like that for a moment longer, looking at one another as if the silence would make it easier to gauge what the other person was thinking.

Maybe Mydei could see that he’d do anything if it would cheer him up, from following any order to calling him whatever he preferred. If he asked him to sit and talk, he would take a seat and try to strike an unending conversation. If he wanted him to help him cook, he would wash his hands and start prepping whatever he brought. If he wanted music, a podcast, or some television show for background noise, he’d grab his tablet and prop it up on its stand.

Maybe he could see that Mydei really, really needed this from him to feel better about something. Be it his rough day at work, his sudden outburst, or their minor disagreement, it was clear this was how he wanted to calm down. And that was fine. He could do it.

They pulled apart, and his eyes shifted to look behind Mydei and at the counter.

“What are we doing first, master?” Phainon asked gently, following him a few steps forwards. “What’s the schedule for tonight?”

Mydei pushed his sleeves higher, then surveyed his surroundings. After watching him for so long, he knew his best friend was assessing the space and mapping out what he planned to do. He looked along the cleared out counters, over the stove where a metal pan sat, and then around to him since he was still in front of the refrigerator.

“I’m going to cook pasta for dinner and make a peach cake for dessert. I remember her saying something about peaches, so I brought a couple,” he said clearly, firmly, and Phainon nodded. “You’re going to bring me what I need and help keep this space clean and organized. I don’t want music. I don’t want unnecessary talking. I just want to cook, bake, and focus. If you want to talk, we can do it after.”

“Are we starting the cake first?”

“Yes. I need to prepare the peaches, then it needs time to bake. Dinner won’t take as long as that,” he explained. “Phainon, empty the bags.”

He nodded, slipping between his body and the counter. “Yes, master,” he returned.

“And open the balcony window. It’s going to get hot, and heat makes people easily irritable,” he advised. “Let’s nip that in the bud.”

“Yes, master.”

Mydei breathed in deeply, loudly, then exhaled before nodding. Without a word, he began to grab what he needed to start the dessert. As he did his thing, Phainon looked down at the food in front of him. Though they were taken out of the paper grocery bags, they were still in their plastic wraps and produce bags.

While helping him through the prepwork and cleaning up the messes made, Phainon made sure to ask permission for anything as well. Even if he typically didn’t need to, he asked. If he wanted to check his phone to see if Cyrene texted him, he made sure to ask when the counters were clean and he didn’t need assistance. If he had to use the bathroom, he asked if he could slip away for a minute or two.

Whatever the answer was, he obeyed. No back talk. No teasing. No questions. It wasn’t the time for any of that and he knew it—not that Mydei would deny him the chance to relieve himself. He just felt the urge to give him that ‘choice’.

And if Mydei told him to move out of his way, he stepped aside to a place where he wasn’t headed. When he asked for a clean knife or specific seasoning left out of reach, it was in his hands within seconds.

If Mydei decided to grasp the strings of his hood and pull him into his body for a silent hug every so often, Phainon welcomed him with open arms. He let him stay, cheek to his shoulder, and decompress for a second before he went back to silently cooking.

The scent of chili, garlic, and shrimp soon flooded his kitchen, and while he wasn’t the one to put most of his effort into the dish, he was proud. Watching Mydei smile down at the deep-walled pan and glass cake platter made his heart feel so full that it threatened to spill from the gaps in his ribs.

“Do you want to try the pasta?”

Phainon was so good that he didn’t even try to sneak any bits and pieces, nor did he bother to ask. To be offered a bite made him giddy.

“Yes, master,” he beamed happily, closing the space between them.

Mydei spun a clean fork into a spoon, gathering a bite of pasta for him before forking through one of the shrimp. With it, he carefully raised both utensils towards his mouth.

“It's hot. Blow on it,” he instructed him, and he lightly blew a few times before dropping his jaw. “Tell me if it's under-seasoned or too salty.”

Phainon shook his head quickly, humming positively. “Mm… Mm-mm!”

“Swallow then speak. I can’t understand you,” he mused, watching him chew with a fond tilt of the lip. “You’ve got a little bit of—”

Before he could try to wipe his mouth with the sleeve of his hoodie, Mydei set the utensils down. He pinched his chin between his thumb and index finger after, holding him firmly in place. His gaze was raised and tilted to the bright lights above them for a better look.

The pad of his thumb stretched to swipe where the end of a noodle had touched his bottom lip, cleaning the rosy sauce from his skin. It dragged slowly, gently. Their eyes never left one another’s, not even for a moment.

As of now, he couldn't tell if it was the chili oil he made or the brush of contact that left his mouth tingling and numb.

Mydei raised his thumb to his own mouth, then licked the mess instead of washing it away. With a satisfied hum, he chuckled. “That’s delicious. We make a good team.”

Phainon nodded in agreement, stunned into silence.

‘Team’.

Cooking with Mydei tonight was essentially him doing clean up and fumbling around to find pots, pans, strainers, and lost ingredients, but he let him have that. After all, he’d rather see that pleased look on his face rather than the hurt from earlier. Confidence and comfort looked best on him.

Soon, the sound of keys jingling filled the apartment, and they both turned around as the lock on his front door twisted. Vaguely, he could hear a muffled chant through the wood, the voice nearly begging for something. And when it opened up fully, the words became more coherent.

“Please be my apartment. Please be my—oh! It is!” A happy, pitched voice practically squealed.

Phainon perked up, and he wiped his mouth with his sleeve anyway before rushing to the front door.

“It smelled so good outside, and I’m starving!” His other best friend’s voice cried. “Phainon! I missed your cooking so much!”

A blur of pink and white ran towards him faster than he could even comprehend, closing the gap between them in a blink. As their bodies collided, he groaned softly and grappled on to the wall beside him for stability. His other hand then held between her shoulders, lowered just enough that he touched the back of her tank-top rather than rosy skin.

Cyrene’s arms slipped beneath his hoodie, holding him tightly while rocking back and forth. With her face pushed into his chest, he couldn't help but rest his chin on her head.

“You missed my cooking but not me?” He pouted, and she nodded quickly while laughing. “Because I missed you, ‘rene. If the feeling’s not mutual, then—”

“I was just kidding! Don’t be like that!”

He grinned, eyes closing as their swaying stilled to a stop.

“My parents wanted you to come with me,” she said into his chest, half of the words muffled. “We all missed you, Phainon. That place hasn't changed much since we last visited, and our initials are still carved into that old tree—the one with the swing, remember?”

“I remember,” he sighed softly, thinking about that old rickety swing his mom swore would never break on them. Would it still be able to hold his weight now that he had put on more?

Suddenly, their third party’s voice jumped in, and he snapped his eyes open to look back at the other man. He peeked awkwardly at them both, one hand on the wall and the other settled over his hip.

“Everything is ready if you’d like to come sit down and eat,” Mydei informed her, his voice much more stoic than it had been twenty minutes ago. “Phainon and I prepared a meal for you.”

“You didn’t have to do all that,” Cyrene waved her hand at him. “But thank you very much, Mydei. It smells delicious, and I can’t wait to try it all. Come here. How have you been?”

Her body pulled away from him, and he chuckled as she went to give his other friend a hug as well. Though it wasn’t one nearly as close and intimate, she still gave him a small shake side to side before pulling away.

“Welcome back,” Mydei said to her. “I’m doing alright, and you?”

“I’m good! I might be a little bit tired and my hair feels weird from the salt water, but it’s nothing yummy food and a shower can’t fix,” she mused. “Sorry I look like a mess. I wasn’t expecting people here, just Phainon.”

Phainon rolled his eyes. “Do you know what a ‘surprise’ means…?”

“The girls aren’t hiding around here either, are they? Oh, I missed Cassie and Cipher so much, but I'm not ready for an apartment full of people,” she told them both honestly. “We should go out some Friday night when I am ready for everyone though. All of us.”

“Maybe,” he said just to tease her and watch her pout. “I might have plans without you next. Who knows?”

“Don’t be rude,” Mydei chided, a playful air to voice that masked the demand beneath. “Besides being tiresome, how was your drive otherwise? Tell us all about it.”

“Oh, I never want to drive there again! Everyone was right when they said the plane is cheaper and faster,” she huffed, ignoring the dining table to head straight to the kitchen bar. “But road trips are just so much fun! You don’t get to stop and smell the roses on a plane… just stuffy, stale air and body odor. Ugh. No thank you.”

“Here.” Phainon grasped the head of a pink plushie off of the dining table, then set it in front of her on the counter. “This is for you. Say ‘thank you’ to m… Mydei for being so considerate—a gift and a meal? He really rolled out the red carpet for you.”

Mydei’s eyes shifted to him, and he felt the stare for a moment as the nature of his potential slip up settled between them.

He had to be so, so careful of not exposing them both now. The last thing they needed was Cyrene knowing they were messing around with each other, especially to this degree.

“Oh, Mydei, she’s so cute. How did you know I liked My Melody and plushies?”

“I pay attention,” he said simply, and Phainon stifled his laugh over the real reason he learned about the characters. “I hope you like it.”

“I love it. You have to remind me again why you’re single,” Cyrene sighed dreamily while taking the toy into her hands. “You can cook well, you have a good-paying job, you’re super kind, and you’re handsome. What girl isn’t trying to scoop you up?”

“Keep it in your pants. He’s not a girl, so you’ll be disappointed when his clothes come off,” Phainon joked, but she just harped on about how lucky his future girlfriend would be.

Phainon knew she was right too.

If Mydei dated casually, or if he simply wanted to try a relationship without his series of rules and regulations, he’d be so popular. On top of what Cyrene had said about him, Mydei was also very patient and articulate when he wanted to be. Things were hard to slip past him, and if they did, it was only because he allowed it to. It’d be easy to see that he was someone comforting and safe after his cool exterior melted away.

But the thought of another man genuinely fawning over him and catching his attention made his stomach feel… strange. Thinking about his stagnant love life while they were tangled up in this arrangement made him uneasy, as he must have also been popular in his own respective community. After all, he wasn’t the only submissive he has ever had. There were others—guys he never even met—who had been all over him before.

He could be with any guy he wanted if they weren’t doing this, couldn’t he? Yet he chose to be loyal to him, to this temporary thing they had.

That made him both proud and guilty.

“I don’t have the time for relationships,” Mydei said simply, vaguely, leaving no room for her to suspect anything. He also didn’t bother to correct her ‘girlfriend’ comment—something he let everyone just assume unless they asked him personally for his preference. “I’m very busy.”

“Well, thank you for finding the time to get this for me then,” she gushed, holding the Sanrio toy to her chest while looking at him. “I love her. I’m going to sit her in my bed next to all of the others, and I’ll treasure it forever.”

He nodded curtly. “It reminds me of you—pink.”

“Two pink girls against the world, huh?” She asked the plush toy cutely, then wiggled its arms wildly. “‘Yeah, Cyrene! We’ll be the cutest duo!’”

Mydei rolled his eyes over the childish gesture, and Phainon glanced at the matching white plush meant for him. He had hardly acknowledged it, and Mydei didn’t push him to. All he did was set it down, let him know it was there, then leave it alone.

“De says I look like this guy too,” he brought up, and Cyrene looked over at him as he held the toy by his head.

“Yeah,” she agreed almost immediately, looking between them both. “You’re kinda like a dog, Phainon—in the cutest way possible! I mean, you even walk around collared all the time!”

He laughed, examining the Cinnamoroll plush before petting its soft, fluffy head. “Collared is a bit much. It’s a choker, Cyrene,” he protested.

His collar was much, much heavier than this old thing, not that he could say that. Not that she could know that.

“It could be a dog collar,” she teased. “You look as if Reaver was a human. Are you sure you’re not a big Samoyed disguised as a man? I can even imagine the furry little ears on top of your head—how cute!”

From behind her turned body, he could see where Mydei’s lip was tilted downwards into a frown from the conversation at hand. His eyes were on her, like he wanted to speak out on it but was holding himself back from doing so.

“I’m not a dog,” he denounced, still keeping his voice light. “Sorry, Cyrene. And if I was, you’d have to pay the safety deposit, you know.”

“To keep you? I would,” she played along. “I’d buy you the cutest little blue collar with hearts all over it.”

Mydei’s frown lifted. His lips pursed together before flicking his heavy gaze over to him silently.

If he had to physically hide his distaste, that must have meant this was beginning to stop sounding like a joke, right?

He cringed lightly, chuckling awkwardly over her poking and teasing. “Let’s not do that… I don’t want that, ‘rene.”

After carrying the weight of Mydei’s collar, the idea of anyone else trying to do that to him made his stomach churn and skin crawl. Joke or not, fetish or not, there was no one he could ever imagine showing that side of him.

“What a senseless conversation. Let’s just eat,” Mydei brought up suddenly, and Cyrene nodded in agreement before tucking her plush into her lap. “Would you like a glass of wine to unwind?”

“We have wine?” She gasped, then looked over to the other man. “When did we keep so much alcohol in the house? I’d love a glass, thank you!”

“This was an old gift I kept,” he answered. “I figured it’d serve as a nice surprise for you both, and it pairs well with this meal. Phainon, where are—”

“I got—”

“Sit,” Phainon hushed Cyrene, holding his arm out to keep her in her seat and rushing to help. “You spent all day driving, and I bet you just want to rest. Relax, we’ve got it.”

She eased back into her barstool, watching them both as he grabbed one glass for her from his cabinet.

“Grab two,” Mydei said just loud enough for the two of them to hear.

The intention was so well hidden between the words he spoke, that it took him a moment to realize what he meant by it. At first, he was confused, wondering why Mydei would want both a glass of wine and his whiskey. But that wasn’t the case, right? If it was, he wouldn’t have been so quiet.

Upon realization, his cheeks warmed, and two glasses then filled his hand.

In other words, not only was he allowed to drink with them tonight, but Mydei was telling him to at least try it.

“Okay,” he whispered back. “You’re the culinary genius, so you know best, chef.”

Mydei hummed, swaying when he was gently nudged by his shoulder. “I just enjoy cooking,” he brushed off, then nudged him back with a little more force.

“Anything else you need, chef?”

“Is this how you behave at work?” He shot back, looking over to him knowingly while holding a deep bowl. “Bring the bottle to your table.”

Phainon’s jaw dropped over the reference to his job, and he bumped him with his hip even harder when walking past him.

“Whoops, behind you,” he mouthed off, feeling the lingering glare when he gently placed two glasses at the kitchen bar Cyrene was sitting at. “Your wine, ma’am.”

A singular pink eyebrow raised as he twisted the cap off, and he grinned before flicking his gaze towards Mydei’s stern expression briefly. It was clearly telling him to watch himself, and he was. Because someone else was here, he was trying to be good and playful at the same time.

“If you need anything, be sure to let me know,” he told her. Once he looked away from him, his right eye dropped into a playful wink for the woman in front of him. “This bottle is on the house tonight, courtesy of Chef Mydei.”

Her eyes rolled, and she waved her hand at him before accepting the full glass. “You two are so weird. Do you always need to be so petty?”

“‘Petty’?” He gasped, feigning offence. “I am not ‘petty’! I’m simply doing what I do best— serving.”

“Go ‘serve’ Mydei,” she hushed. “Don’t make our guest do everything all by himself! Where are your manners? Auntie raised you better.”

“I’m fine,” Mydei promised, and Phainon grabbed his best friend’s half-empty glass of whiskey before setting it by the seat.

Three plates were handed out, and their glasses were filled with their respective drinks. As he and Mydei stood side by side, they looked to the empty spot beside Cyrene.

The actual dinner table itself was free, but it was simply not being used except to sit their matching plushies. She was already sitting at the bar, and that was where the two of them usually ate together anyway. It would be a hassle to move everything over when she was already comfortable in her seat, and one single person eating alone would look sad. He didn't want to be him, and he couldn’t stand to see either of his friends feel like a third wheel.

“Go sit.” He nudged Mydei with his elbow, then nodded to the stool beside his drink. “I have a lot of energy, so I’d like to stand.”

“You stood all day,” he argued.

“I’ll be okay,” he brushed his concern off. “Besides, I need a little longer to tell if Cyrene’s red from the wine or from being sunburned… I want to see her face to face. Can you look this way?”

Two hands covered her face immediately, hiding away the rosy flush that warmed her skin ear to ear and across the nose. “The sunscreen wore off on my drive, and I forgot to reapply it, okay? Leave me alone!”

“I guess you don’t need to wear blush when you go out for the next few days. It’s almost natural looking,” he joked, making her cry quietly about how silly she must look. “Go sit down, Chef Mydei. You’re still a guest here, so relax a bit and enjoy the fruits of our labor. I won’t accept any other answer, you know.”

He walked silently, taking the stool for himself without another protest.

“Mydei, I can feel your leg shaking the floor,” Cyrene commented, still hiding her face but turning to his direction. “Are you okay?”

“I’m fine.” The response was short, sweet, and just like him. She didn’t seem to notice.

Maybe it was the hands on her face that hid the glint inside of his eyes from her, or the fact she wasn’t as close to him as he was, but Phainon heard it. He saw it. He felt it.

“We should eat,” Phainon told them both sweetly, and Mydei straightened his posture before grabbing his glass. “Before the alcohol hits an empty stomach.”

“Uh-oh… You’re right,” Cyrene mumbled. “All I’ve eaten is candy and chips…”

“You should take better care of yourself and your body,” Mydei brought up casually. “No one else is going to do it for you.”

“Yeah yeah…” She sighed. “I’m just really forgetful sometimes. And my mom tried feeding me lunch, but I hate driving long distances on a full stomach.”

He shrugged lightly. “That’s no excuse.”

“I know.”

Phainon felt heat creep over his neck as he looked away from them.

That was an interesting thing to hear come from his mouth after coming to terms with the fact Mydei wanted to take care of him. Healthy meals, planned outfits, and glasses of water for him to drink regularly, Mydei personally made sure he had all the things he needed while around. When he was too sleepy to stand, he pushed him to work out. After long showers and hot baths, he reminded him to moisturize and put lotion on to take care of his skin.

Even as friends, he bought him groceries and fixed him a meal if he was hungry. It wasn’t just out of courtesy either. Those gestures were of his own concern for his well-being.

Yet to anyone else around him, it was, ‘no one else is going to do it for you’ and ‘that’s no excuse’.

“Are you feeling alright? You’re red,” Mydei pointed out, looking at him attentively. “Are you suddenly sunburned as well?”

“Shut up,” he mumbled. “It’s really hot in the kitchen.”

Mydei wasn’t convinced, but he had no reason to be. Phainon was a liar, and it was obvious to everyone in the room. Even Cyrene, who glanced at him and giggled over the sight of his rosy face.

“Red’s a nice color on you,” she noticed. “But seriously, why are you red? Do you like watching me get bullied that much?”

“You’re fun to tease.” Her eyes rolled at that. “Now, say ‘thank you’ to—”

“Oh my—zip up his slacks when you're done with it!” She gasped, cutting him off and making his cheeks even redder as he reminded of that. “Thank you for the food, Mydei, but Phainon’s being obnoxious with it.”

“Ignore him.” Mydei rolled his eyes as well over the comments being thrown around. “Tell us about your trip. How is the ocean and the wheat fields this time of year?”

“So nice! I spent so much time just enjoying the docks and feeling like a little girl again. We used to skip so many stones and throw so many bottles into it,” she sighed dreamily. “This vacation gave me all the creative energy to work on some new stories.”

Mydei smiled lightly. “That’s good to hear. What are some ideas you came up with while out? I’d like to hear if you’re willing to share.”

Phainon, unable to stop himself, smiled as he listened to Cyrene begin to ramble on about all the ideas she had. Beside her, his best friend listened intently, completely engaged in the conversation.

It made his chest so unbelievably warm to know Mydei would go out of his way to be there for not just him, but for the people closest to him. Even after a busy day at work, even when he was having a terrible evening, he still made an effort to be kind and give her his full attention.

Him and Cyrene weren’t close. They met only when he was there to bridge them both together, and it was like that all their lives. Yet he came, he brought her gifts, and he treated her like she was one of his own close friends.

But, that was just like him, wasn’t it? He didn’t show up anywhere without an invitation, but if asked to be there, he was never late, always supportive, and ready to give his all. Whether he needed to or not, it didn’t matter. He was always willing to go out of his way if he cared enough.

It was so sweet. Mydei was so sweet.

His heart gave a throb, and he hummed quietly to himself as he took a sip of his wine, waiting for the right moment to jump into their conversation.

—

The first to turn in that night was Cyrene. Between her long day, a belly full of food, and a few too many glasses of wine, she left all her bags and suitcases in the living room before crashing into her bed.

He wasn’t even sure if she took her outside clothes and shoes off, but that would be a problem for morning Cyrene. And maybe him too, as she would probably complain that he should have reminded her—not that she would have listened if he did. When she was tired, there was no way to make her do anything but sleep.

That left him and Mydei alone, and he nervously shut the door to his bedroom after they cleaned up and changed into their pajama clothes. The space suddenly felt smaller, hotter, and much, much more intimate than it ever did while sharing it with him. After all, he wasn’t here often, and his room was much smaller than Mydei’s was. He couldn't just walk off to a walk-in closet or bathroom, just to one end of the room or out the door.

“It’s cold,” Mydei commented, looking around while crossing his arms over his chest. “Sleeping with the window open at night will make you sick.”

“It gets a little warm in here,” he defended himself, trying not to notice the way his arms looked in that borrowed long sleeve. “Do you want me to close it?”

“No, it’ll get hotter sleeping in the same bed,” he said casually. “That is your plan, isn’t it? Bringing me in here, shutting all the lights off out there, and locking your door means you never planned on letting me take the couch. You decided I’d sleep in here with you.”

A sheepish smile tugged on his lips over the accusatory statement, and Phainon took a step back when Mydei took a step forward. With those deep, amber eyes on him like a predator staring down its prey, he felt his palms begin to sweat.

“Maybe…” He dragged out, then gasped when his bed hit the back of his legs. “Mydei, wait. Wait, I’m gonna—!”

They both tumbled on to his bed, and he laughed quietly while looking up at him. Both arms were raised above his head, the lower half of his body was bent off of the bed, and Mydei was hovering over him with one knee between his legs.

“Shh, you’re gonna wake her up,” Mydei grinned back at him, forcing him to nod quickly in return and seal his lips shut. “And call me by the right name since it’s just us two.”

“Master.”

“There you go.” Shivers tickled up his spine from the smooth, encouraging tone. “That’s what I want to hear from you.”

Phainon’s belly tingled while watching him, warmth pooling within it the longer they stayed like this. Their eyes were locked together, personal bubbles merged into one protective shield around them. Two toned hair fell over his face, blocking everything around him out with its sunset veil. It left only Mydei there.

“You smell like whiskey,” he murmured, and Mydei shrugged.

His eyes were the same color too, tinted a warm caramel-color that beckoned him to fall in and drown within them. Half-lidded from exhaustion and a night of catching up, they stared down at him like it gave him energy to stay up.

“I had more than I should have while we all enjoyed ourselves,” he agreed quietly. “Do you have an alarm set for the morning?”

“Six, like always,” he promised, feeling as the hand beside his head raised slowly. Its indent into his mattress proved as much. “Are you excited to see the kitties? I don’t have a view like yours, but it’s a nice neighborhood to lap around and admire. The park nearby has a nice little creek that runs through it, and a pretty pond with a fountain full of ducks.”

“I haven’t seen those cats in awhile. I bet they miss you when you stay the night at my place,” Mydei teased. “Who else takes care of them?”

“I don’t know. Maybe the people in the apartment they stay next to.”

Soon, hot fingertips tickled over the bare flesh of his right arm. They lightly trailed above the elbow and teased the muscle of his forearm, curling around slowly to grasp beneath it. Goosebumps bubbled underneath the touch.

“Master, what a-are you doing?” Phainon’s voice was breathy but quiet, nervous yet excited, all at once.

Mydei’s fingers cupped his wrist firmly. His thumb stretched to nab the second, bringing them side by side before he closed his fist. They were pinned to the mattress as he leaned closer over him, leaving him unable to touch him or push him away.

Phainon exhaled shakily, shifting beneath him as his heartbeat picked up. Even if he could break free, if he knew it was possible to leave his grasp, it still left him with an air of vulnerability.

“I want to thank you for earlier,” he brought up, contradicting the dominating hold he had on his body. “You did something that made me feel better, and you did it all on your own. There was no way for you to know what I needed, but you took a shot in the dark and hit right where you needed to. Whether that was blind luck or an educated guess, I’m not sure, but it doesn’t matter to me.”

Oh. That was what this was about.

Their moment in his kitchen, when he willingly offered for Mydei to take whatever he needed and gave him all the time he wanted to hold him close, had slipped his mind completely over the night. Not that it wasn’t important, just that he wasn’t sure if there was a reason to bring it up again or dwell on it. That topic was sensitive, clearly, and he would rather not upset him.

“Thank you, Phainon,” Mydei said gently. “Thank you for letting me complain for a little while, and thank you for letting me come down with you. I appreciate it.”

“You’re welcome, master,” he returned in that same tone. “I’m here for you too, so come to me if you feel upset. You do so much, and you deserve to have your needs and wants met.”

Phainon wiggled his arms beneath his grasp out of pure instinct rather than to fight it, and he shifted his hips to a more comfortable position.

“Can I… hug you tonight?” He asked suddenly, tightening his grasp on his wrists. “Can I hold you instead of sleeping back to back like we usually do?”

His heart skipped for a second as the words echoed inside of his head. They bounced around for a moment, bringing heat to his face and a flutter inside of his stomach.

Like… cuddle? Mydei wanted to cuddle with him in bed as they slept together?

“Can you?” He teased him in an attempt to combat the rush underneath his skin. “Are you asking for permission?”

There was a sick sense of amusement within him when Mydei’s eyes widened slightly over his mocking tone. They then dropped down to his mouth slowly, watching them grin and move to form his next words.

He didn’t… mind the idea. Besides, his bed was probably too small to comfortably sleep the way they did anyways. They’d risk falling off if they tried to keep any space between their turned backs.

Well, no. Mydei would risk falling off, considering his bed was tucked into a corner in his bedroom. Without a partner, he never needed both ends of his bed for two people to move in and out of freely. That meant Mydei would be the one to fall off, as he preferred sleeping by the wall where he could charge his phone.

“Can you please hold me tonight, master?” Phainon asked him instead, rewording the simple statement. “And can I please sleep by the wall?”

“Yes, I can,” he answered. “And yes, you may.”

He pulled away from him almost immediately. The hold on his hands was raised, and his knee eased away from the mattress. With a flick of a switch, the lights shut off, and Phainon stared at where his best friend had just been standing. Though his eyes hadn’t adjusted yet, it was as if he could feel him staring back.

“Bedtime,” Mydei told him, and he shifted away from his position to meet his pillows. “Come here.”

Springs creaked underneath the added weight, and his bed dipped in when Mydei sat on the edge. The sound of a phone touching his nightstand followed, then the bright light of an illuminated screen flashed. Right beside his own phone, Mydei had plugged his in, and he stared at them both sharing the wooden surface before glancing at him.

The light soon flickered off, and he turned around as the bed creaked again. With an arm under his pillow, he faced the wall, nose ticked by the ivory plush Mydei had gotten him. It smelled like a kid’s store, like most synthetic stuffed toys usually did, but a hint of Mydei’s cologne lingered.

He could imagine Mydei holding it in line, pressing it to his chest and unknowingly rubbing off on it as he waited to pay. Maybe because this character reminded him of him. Maybe because he had his hands busy with other things.

Phainon pulled it closer, draped his arm around its middle, then grinned.

“Grown man with a toy,” he teased himself, then felt a presence behind him as the sheets and blankets were pulled higher.

It wasn’t new. The feeling of Mydei sliding into bed and covering them both wasn’t something ground breaking or abnormal. Neither was the rocking or the bouncing. But the proximity was. His body lined so closely that his breathing hitched sharply and suddenly, caught in his lungs.

Mydei’s arm stretched underneath his own pillow, but it curved towards his own to brush. A faint tickle of breath batted against the back of his neck, telling him his face was close but not that close. Not enough to feel the heat directly or the point of his nose close in on him.

“How does this make you feel?” He asked him, laying his arm down over his waist slowly, lightly, like he was nervous of crushing him.

Phainon was pulled closer. His tailbone pressed firmly to the hips behind him. Eyes still, lips parted for a breath that never came, he laid there inside of Mydei’s hold for a moment. Then, for two.

In the quiet, he wondered if the sound of his pounding heart could somehow echo through the room.

“I’m okay,” he whispered back.

“What about this?”

His arm shifted, easing around his waist loosely while slowly inching higher, and higher, and higher. Fingers dipped between him and his plush, along the divot between the mounds of his pecs, then flattened out against his collarbones. With a push, it forced his back to the other man’s chest next. Like this, their entire torsos were touching, bodies separating only when his legs curled at the knees while Mydei’s stayed relatively relaxed.

“Green,” he murmured, and Mydei hummed softly.

“Lift your chin. Pull your shoulders down and relax,” he was instructed, and Phainon obeyed.

The second be opened himself up, Mydei brought his hand higher, and he gasped over the feeling.

“I got you,” he promised, not squeezing, not gripping, and not pushing. His palm simply laid hot to the bottom of his throat, fingers curled loose around the column. "I want a color.”

They laid like that for a moment, Mydei’s hand gingerly holding his neck and his arm pressed firmly to his chest. He was engulfed fully within him, warmed by his body and the layers of sheets and blankets. Despite being in his own room and using his own bedding, he could smell the familiar comfort of Mydei’s skin.

He willed his body to relax, to sink into his touch and grow accustomed not just to cuddling but to having his neck held.

“Yes, master,” he said back to him. “Green.”

“Very well. Goodnight, my prince. Have sweet dreams,” he mumbled from behind him, and Phainon gulped before pulling his plush closer.

“Goodnight, master,” he returned, eyes focusing on the textured wall across from him. “I’ll see you in the morning.”

There was an intimidating tingle where his best friend’s fingerprints sat on the sides of his throat, one that was both scary and exciting all at once. Both emotions tangled inside of his stomach tightly, twisting and knotting into something too daunting to try and decipher at the hour. His body has learned to get tired at this time, and he could feel it dull the confusion within him.

Did he like Mydei’s hand around his neck? Did he like being held on to so completely?

He didn’t know, but that could be a problem for morning Phainon, not this one.

—

When waking up, they carefully dressed up and slipped out of the apartment, trying not to disturb the girl snoring away next door.

Phainon rubbed his eye sleepily, half of a bagel in his mouth while Mydei had already finished the other half. His feet dragged across the entrance to his apartment, but the other man practically took two steps at once to warm up at the base of the staircase.

It was always like this. He was the tired one from being up at the chilling crack of dawn, and Mydei was always ready as if this was the absolute highlight of his day. Never had he known someone who loved working out and exercising as much as he did. But today he seemed even more energized.

A deep breath filled his lungs, one so crisp and cool that it burned a little bit going down. The sun was still rising, tangerine shades of orange bleeding into the pale blue morning sky. Clouds dusted in sparse, faint puffs. A singular plane flew in the distance, a darkened speck leaving behind the faintest trail behind.

Underneath it all, Mydei’s arms stretched high and tall above his head. Fingers interlocked, he sucked a shaky breath in through his nose, allowing it to fill his body for a few moments before he exhaled. His borrowed shirt had ridden up, exposing the crimson bolts around his hips that stretched to his back and the dimpled base of his spine. Gold and crimson stared back at him hauntingly, the sliver enough to make his heart race despite only climbing down the stairs.

Dragging his gaze higher, he watched his ponytail swing side to side, back and forth. Its lowest lock kissed his shirt’s collar, and on one side, it was braided tightly. Both whipped when he turned around, throwing a look over his shoulder.

“Wake up, sleeping beauty,” he goaded him, a glint sparkling within his amber eyes. “We don’t have all morning. Pick up your feet.”

“Mm…”

Phainon joined him in warming up, half-ass’ing his stretches in favor of finishing his early-morning snack. Only after he wiped his mouth with the navy band around his left wrist did he start to put his all into it.

“What’s your usual route?” Mydei asked, and he looked towards the gate before raising his hand.

“Take a right, cross the street to the neighborhood, then I go around to the park behind,” he explained, pointing as if he could understand. “I’ll do it a few times, then circle around the complex a few times.”

“Before we leave, I want to see them.”

Phainon laughed, and he followed Mydei towards the visitor’s spot he parked at. The lights on his charcoal-colored two-seater flickered, its locks opening up with an echo.

He watched him tear a piece of a cardboard box, then grabbed two metal tins before ripping the lids off.

“You came prepared,” he noticed.

“I always do.”

The makeshift tray was handed to him, and he took it without question to support it. Mydei dumped the food on top carefully. Both cans were cleared out as much as possible, then he grabbed a small paper bowl from a fresh pack sitting inside the same bag. It was filled with water soon after, then carefully set on the floor so it didn't spill.

“I don’t want my car to smell like cat food, so I’m going to tie these up and throw them out at the dumpster before we go,” he said. “Hold this. Don’t go without me.”

“I won’t,” he promised.

Phainon watched him rush towards the dumpster not too far away, each step faster than he would have normally. As he did so, his attention looked down to the bowl. Steady fingers picked it up, holding both the tray and water while waiting patiently.

When Mydei came back, he shot him a wobbled grin. Dark, blond eyebrows furrowed over the look.

“What?” He asked. “Why do you have that look on your face right now?”

“Have I ever told you that you’re a really good person?” He asked out of nowhere, and Mydei went quiet for a moment. “You treating Cyrene like she’s one of your good friends and going out of your way for a bunch of strays around here is… so incredibly kind of you.”

It was cute too, but he didn’t want to say that out loud.

“It’s courtesy,” he defended himself. “She’s someone closest to you, so of course I should be courteous towards her, and you always take care of the people who need it. In this case, homeless cats who are probably starving.”

“It’s all very sweet.”

“Just show me where they are,” he huffed.

Phainon carried the cardboard tray while nodding at him to follow, aware of his rosy face but choosing not to tease him for it.

They walked quietly along the paved sidewalk, then across the street towards a large mailbox. Behind the wall was a long bush, and parked off to the side of it sat an old car with holes in its bumper and sun-faded stickers.

Squatting down, he tapped his fingers against the uplift in the curb while watching, already noticing the leaves rustle. Mydei bent down beside him too, setting the paper bowl down as two peeked from the bush. When another poked its head from beneath the car, he jumped, staring wide eyed at the orange animal looking up at him.

“Oh, hello, little one…” He greeted it, one hand carefully reaching out for the curious animal. “You’re so fat… How did you hide inside of that car? Does Phainon feed you too much when he’s home?”

“Hey,” he pouted, then chuckled as content purring and soft meows filled the morning air. “I’m not responsible for his weight. I’m not the only one here that takes care of them.”

The smallest one clawed at his bar knee, using it to stand up right on its hind legs, and the third went face first towards the food.

“Hi there, did you miss me?” He asked, voice pitched higher as he lightly petted its head. “Oh, you’re so pretty, girl. Look at those eyes… I missed you too.”

“You’re dirty,” Mydei protested, letting his fingers trail from head to back against the chubby animal beside him. Then, he picked it up casually. “Eat.”

He placed it by the other, and Phainon laughed quietly before guiding the kitten beside them both.

“Yeah? You wanna join them too, little girl? C’mon. My master bought all of this for you guys because he’s so sweet and thoughtful,” he coo’ed when it meow’ed loudly, eating happily through the pitched sound. “Nom nom nom, you’re gonna be a chubby little thing just like daddy, huh? Look at you…”

“Phainon.”

“Yes, master?” He hummed, turned to look at his best friend as he stopped petting the cat. “Should we go now? Are we already behind on our schedule?”

Another silent moment passed, and he shook his head before tilting his lip up higher.

“You’re an idiot," he teased him, a gentle glint in his eye from the sunlight catching them. “That baby voice is so stupid sounding. Do you talk like that often?”

He frowned, feigning offense. “Don’t be so mean! What? Do I talk to it the way I talk to you?”

Phainon lightly pushed him while straightening himself out, causing Mydei to stumble in his bent over state as he hadn’t expected the sudden shove. His shoes scraped against the street as he fell, and his hand slammed on to the floor to keep himself from falling.

Watching him made him laugh, especially since his cheeks were even darker from the embarrassment of slipping. “I am so sorry. Th-That was an accident, I swear. I didn’t think you’d be so easy to knock over,” he apologized through the giggles.

“You should run,” Mydei warned him, and that was when Phainon noticed the gate that was squeaking open for a car to pass by. “If I catch you, I’m going to punish you for pushing me into this person’s rust bucket.”

“Oh?” He pressed, leaning forward while offering a hand out for him. “And what will my master do to me?”

“When, not if, I get my hands on you, I’ll cuff your hands behind your back the next time you come over,” he warned him with a hushed voice, and a rush filled his stomach when his hand was pushed away. “You have five seconds to run. One.”

Not wanting to waste a single one, he took a step around his still-crouching figure before dodging the incoming car.

“Two.”

“I’m running left,” he called behind him, finding Mydei was watching him walk away with a grin on his lips.

Clearly, his best friend wasn’t upset, just feeling more playful in nature. Otherwise, he probably would have gotten scolded for being so careless of his surroundings.

“Three!”

Mydei was already standing up, and his eyes widened before he turned back around and began jogging away from him.

“Four!”

The countdown hadn’t hit the last number, but he swore he was already hearing his shoes hit the pavement as he chased after him. Even if it was to catch the closing gate before it sealed him off, how was that fair? The extra seconds of putting in his code wouldn’t have been that big of an advantage.

Phainon laughed, picking up his pace since he saw the sidewalk was completely empty. He didn’t have to worry about running into anyone, and that gave him even more confidence.

The street separated three ways, one with a free crosswalk counting down for pedestrians, the other still orange for cars to pass, and then a simple left turn around his apartment complex to loop around it. His end was coming up fast, and he had maybe five seconds to make a choice.

The first one straight ahead guaranteed his safety, as Mydei would have to wait to cross the street once the timer was up. It also led straight towards a gas station and a few small fast food places, which meant more people could see them. He didn’t want to think about what strangers would think of two grown men running after each other on the sidewalk—even if they were in workout clothes.

The second one towards the right gave Mydei an obvious advantage, leaving him to wait for the light to turn his way and risk getting grabbed in turn. It technically was the right way to go, too, as it led towards another housing community and the accompanying park. That was where they were supposed to go.

The last one left them both in a comfortable spot to chase one another a little while longer because they could follow it around the complex. It would deviate them from the plan, but a run was still a run, wasn’t it? Their hearts were still pumping. Their legs were still moving. This was still a workout.

Phainon stopped, looked in all three directions, then behind him where his best friend was chasing him. Mydei was already gaining on him from his short stop at the light, ponytail swinging and bangs bouncing with every step.

With a smile over his shoulder, he turned left, wanting to continue their little game for a little while longer.

No matter who won in the end, at least this was fun.
