With Cyrene home, it was a little bit harder to find excuses to stay over at Mydei’s place and do what they usually did.

Visiting was one thing. He could go when given a time, see him for a little bit after work like they used to, but now someone was at home wondering where he was, what he was doing, and who he was with. Though he wasn’t obligated to tell her, and he knew it was just for curiosity’s sake rather than to be over-protective, having to think up excuses was difficult. Lying was hard for him to do on its own, adding in the fact she was always honest around him only made it more difficult.

But he couldn’t just tell her their secret. Not only did he promise Mydei to keep his preferred lifestyle quiet, but this was something no one could know about him too. If people were to find out about this part of him, this side that enjoyed being Mydei’s ‘good boy’ and liked being owned like his property, it would be the end of the world. He could never show his face again.

He wanted to see Mydei though. He really, really wanted to keep doing what they were doing.

While on break with one of his co-workers, that was all he could think about. It plagued his thoughts while taking orders, when in the bathroom on his phone to escape the rush, and even now.

How could he hold on to their secret without letting Cyrene grow suspicious?

His back was pressed to the wall of the restaurant as he contemplated, and beside him, a woman he vaguely recognized was squatting down having a cigarette. The scent was chokingly strong, and if he could be bothered to look for somewhere else to stand, he would. But he couldn’t be. He was too deep in thought.

Could he really keep pretending he and Mydei didn’t have something going on? That the only reason he visited so much was because they were just such good friends?

Should he try to pretend that Mydei needed him for personal business? Lying on a man known for his blatant and blunt honesty didn’t seem right though. Not only would he make himself out to look bad, but his best friend would be dragged down by it too. Tarnishing his look wouldn’t be right.

In the midst of his thinking, a monotonous yet quiet voice spoke up, disrupting their silence.

“Your name is Phainon, right?”

His gaze dropped to the only other person out here, surprised that he was being acknowledged right now. “Yeah, that’s me,” he returned, and she looked up at him. “What’s up?”

He never noticed her much. She blended into the background well, simply doing her job and then leaving right away—not that he blamed her for that. From what he knew, she worked at the bar. And while he would grab a drink or two from her for a table, it wasn’t nearly often enough to remember her name, how long she was there, or anything past her general appearance.

But now that he got a chance to really look at her, she was pretty. The kind of pretty that could probably bring someone to their knees.

Her eyes looked like the ocean back at home, comforting and gentle in the way they beckoned someone to take a dive. Dark hair framed her face and hung over her thin eyebrows, but a chunk was tucked back thanks to a few ivory clips. A pearl earring sat beneath her ear on that same side, heavy and bright underneath the setting sun. It swung loosely when she shifted.

“Don’t look at me like that,” she said, holding her cigarette by her face to block it from sight. “Your puppy dog face is making it hard to talk to you.”

“Huh?”

“How old are you, kid?” She asked him suddenly, and his eyebrows furrowed. “You look… young, but you can’t be that young if you’re working here, right?”

‘Kid’? How old was she?

“You’re awfully straightforward,” he chuckled awkwardly, not wanting to tell this stranger his business so quickly. “Isn’t it rude to shamelessly ask someone their age like that?"

“I’m twenty-eight,” she said casually instead as if she didn’t hear him. After, her fingers twitched to flick the ash off of the tip of her cigarette. “Everyone else here is graying or a bit stuck up from the reputation of this place, so… I thought I’d take a chance and ask you.”

Phainon’s head tilted slightly in confusion.

This whole time she had been talking about confronting him for something, but she wasn’t explaining anything to him. The vagueness and suddenness of it all was becoming a little bit unsettling, even if she didn’t look particularly suspicious. What kind of person just approached someone like this?

“For what, exactly? What do you need to ask me?”

They weren’t friends, and they weren’t even coworkers who pretended to be friends while on the clock. What did he have that she needed?

“Tell me you're not fresh out of high school first.”

“I’m not that much younger,” he mused, but she shivered as if the thought of him being a teenager disgusted her. “Would you like to see my ID for proof?”

“I don’t need to know when you turn twenty-one or what height you rounded up to.” Her hand waved him off. “I’m being pushed to do something I don’t usually do. I thought you could help me, but I’d rather not get tangled up with some eighteen year old out of desperation.”

Phainon could scream, laugh, and groan in frustration, but the one thing he couldn’t imagine doing was straight up walking away. Even if he probably should.

“Well, I’ve been twenty-one for a while now, and I am over six-foot,” he promised, just a little bit offended by her accusation. Did he look like someone who lied about something as stupid as his height?

But that seemed to be good enough for her.

The next thing she did was sigh as if resigned, as if she were being forced to have this conversation with him, but he was the one who didn’t even know her name. Not a syllable came to mind.

“My wife thinks I need friends,” she disclosed, not sounding the littlest bit joking. “I’m wondering if you could help me make her happy.”

Phainon had to physically bite his tongue to keep from laughing at her confession. Thankfully, she had her eyes fixated to the ground because one look was all it would take to see how close he was to just letting it out. Had he been any less surprised by the nature of her request, maybe he would have been in stitches by now.

“Wait.” She hesitated for a moment, a rush to her still-monotonous words. “You’re not one of those people who hate like… you know… right? I can talk about my wife?”

“Oh, of course not.”

“Wait. I can’t talk about my…?”

He really, really wanted to laugh at her.

“No, I meant that I’m not one of those people. You can. You can talk about her,” he allowed, and a breath of relief left her lips. “What were you saying about your wife? She uh… She thinks you need friends, and I’m the person you chose to ask?”

A large part of this was amusing because no one had ever admitted that to him before. No one just took a space right next to him out of nowhere, sat in silence for a moment just existing together, and straight up asked to be friends because they had none. Usually people talked about something they had in common, waited until they enjoyed the conversation, then decided from there if they could be friends. It wasn’t just a ‘yes’ or ‘no’ question right off the bat.

But another part of him felt a little bit bad as he watched her shoulders slightly curl inwards from his words. Two fingers played with her pierced ear, rolling the lobe around slowly, and her other hand kept that burnt down cigarette to her lips.

Clearly, this was an uncomfortable conversation for her to have.

Now, he felt bad for wanting to laugh at her at all.

“I’m… kind of new in town…?” She admitted to him. “All I’ve done since we moved here is work, stay in the house, or go out with her. She’s demanding I try to make friends, but it’s… hard as an adult. The only people I see regularly are here at work, otherwise, they’re all just strangers I’ll never meet again. It’s all so confusing. It makes me anxious.”

Phainon’s lip twitched downwards.

Well, now he felt even worse for wanting to laugh at her.

“She says it’s not healthy to only talk to one person, but I can’t find anyone to approach. You seemed like someone nice though,” she complimented him. “Sorry. I’m really not good at this. Is that weird to say to someone you don’t know?”

“It’s okay. I’m glad you think I’m nice! That’s what I’d like for people who don’t know me to think.” She looked back up at him, eyes still gentle but unsure, and he offered her a soft smile while holding out his hand. “Let’s start a friendship the right way. I’m Phainon, and I like just about everything you can think of—sports, superheroes, sleeping, and everything else.”

The fingers playing with her earring paused, and she reached for his hand tentatively before shaking it.

“Hysilens,” she told him. "I like… my wife, and music.”

“Yeah? What’s your favorite genre?” He asked, shaking her hand firmly. “I like all kinds. I’m not the biggest fan of like… death metal and things like that, but I can appreciate a good song if one comes up.”

“I like all kinds of music.” Her lip tilted upwards into a soft smile, becoming more confident in their conversation. “If it has a nice sound, I’ll listen to it or learn it. I rarely find a song I don’t like.”

“Ah, does that mean you can play an instrument?”

Hysilens nodded, and he pulled his hand back to check his watch. “I play the violin the most, but I own much more. I also sing.”

A smoker that sang didn’t sound like a good combination to him, but he wasn’t going to judge her anymore than he already had. She seemed too nice for such cruelty.

“Our break ended a few minutes ago… We should go before we get yelled at,” he chuckled, watching as she then stood up to stomp out her cigarette. “Let’s continue this talk over the phone later. Here, give me your number, and you can go home and tell your wife that you now have a friend from work.”

She nodded excitedly, eyes lighting up at the mention of pleasing her.

“Thank you.”

He shrugged, slipping his phone out of his pocket to hurriedly create a contact for her. She watched from beside him, hands tucked behind her back with her feet rocking back and forth.

“Don’t mention it. I’m happy to help where I can,” he reassured her kindly. “I love making new friends too.”

—

When visiting Mydei that night, the first thing he did was hand the other man his phone because of how often it was lighting up. Texts from Cyrene and Hysilens took up a majority of his notification bar, and it was distracting him. One was rambling that it was good he and Mydei were working on their ‘competitive pettiness’, and the other was filling his messages with music recommendations for him to listen to when he had the time.

Both were kind, and he liked talking to them. Neither of the girls were the person he wanted to focus on right now, though.

The second thing he did was undress as he was told to, then hop into the shower to clean up. Mydei left him with clothes to wear, as he always did to make his evening just a little bit smoother. A pair of black lounging shorts and a white t-shirt were folded on top of the bathroom counter, and beside them both were his collar and a pair of familiar cuffs. But they didn’t have that same lengthy chain connecting them. Instead, his gear was hooked together with one much shorter, leaving very little space in between.

The set was nerve wracking to look at.

Standing in the bathroom, he stared at the bondage equipment laid out before him for a moment. Memories of his own rosy wrists flashed inside of his mind, then the clinking of chains when he had struggled against them futilely. Being locked down to the bed was both thrilling and terrifying, and feeling Mydei’s hands on his vulnerable body was more pleasurable than he anticipated.

Phainon wanted them on. He wanted to try it again to see what it’d feel like now that he was a little bit more comfortable in this all.

But thinking of the handcuffs made him think of the nipple clamps too. Those hurt in a way he had never felt before, and they pinched so much tighter than a pair of fingers ever could. He was right in saying Mydei’s suggestion made him want to try something scary, but Mydei had been well within his rights to assume he would like them too. He did it to himself, and he allowed him to do it too. Why wouldn't he come to that conclusion?

Maybe they would have been okay if they weren’t tightened down or paired with any kind of pulling. Maybe if he wore them for a shorter amount of time, he wouldn’t have felt so sore after. Maybe there would be a time when they could try them again too… just not tonight.

Phainon turned to the bathroom door, a deep breath filling his lungs as he was pulled open.

“Mydei?”

Without a response, he hummed, then gathered the leather equipment into his arms. Each step came with a light bounce while walking down the hall, and a mix of excitement and nerves tangled within his stomach as he got closer.

“Mydei!” He called, just to find the man sitting on the couch with his phone in hand. Upon meeting his eyes, he grinned. “I mean… Hi, master.”

Mydei lifted an eyebrow, then beckoned him closer with a nod.

“Why do you look so happy to be punished?” He mused, setting his phone aside immediately upon seeing him. “You’re not supposed to want it, you know. That takes away the ‘punishment’ part.”

While with him, Phainon learned that there were two different kinds of ‘punishment’ to be dealt.

One was, in fact, a ‘punishment’ for misbehaving and breaking his rules. Those weren't meant to be comfortable or enjoyable. Being forced to kneel with a leash tying him down was the prime example of that. It was meant to hammer in what he did wrong, to make him realize he wasn’t the things he called himself to help him stop feeling that way. And so far, it’s helped.

The second kind was more akin to something mildly inconveniencing or reprimanding, like not getting to call Mydei by his name or getting his phone taken away. It got the message across that he did something wrong, but it was a little bit lighter of a sentence since the wrong-doing wasn’t nearly as bad. They could even be fun.

For getting caught by him in their game of chase, Mydei decided he wanted to put him through the second version of punishment. It was meant to be fun, playful, and just a little bit of a push towards his boundaries.

Mydei knew that. He knew that. The air in the room knew as it carried a gentle comfort and amusement within it.

“Oh no… Please, master. Please don’t do it,”  he feigned terror, earning a low chuckle in return for his dramatic performance. “Please don’t handcuff me and touch my helpless body.”

“I never said I would touch you,” he tsk’ed, taking the trio of leather bands from him. “Sit on my lap. Back to me.”

Phainon bit down on his bottom lip, and he turned around before allowing himself to sit backwards on Mydei’s knees. Both hands held the bones beneath him, drumming over his skin gently.

“You won’t?”

For whatever reason, he expected to be touched in some way, and he had come to want it. Knowing it wouldn’t happen made him just a little bit disappointed.

“If you want me to, you’ll have to ask me,” he said simply, making him squirm from having a choice being thrusted upon him.

It was easier when Mydei just went in and did it because he wanted to. Saying ‘yes’ or ‘green’ was easier than admitting that he wanted more from him, and thinking about having to ask to be touched made him antsy. Both guilt and anxiety made it a difficult task, even if they had dwindled down to a fraction of their size since they started this.

“Phainon…” He hummed, head shaking as he turned to look over his shoulder at Mydei. “Bring your arms behind your back. How can I cuff what isn’t here?”

Oh. Right. They were in the middle of something.

Phainon brought his wrists behind him comfortably, and he straightened his back out while Mydei touched his body gingerly.

“You are going to be handcuffed while we talk about your day, do you understand?” He checked in. “I won’t touch you in any suggestive way unless you ask, properly.”

“We’re just… talking like we usually do?” He repeated quietly, feeling as smooth leather wrapped around one.

“Talking while you’re handcuffed, since you feel the need to put them on me so carelessly,” he hinted at the other morning, and Phainon felt a grin stretch across his face.

“I didn’t mean to,” he swore, even if his humored tone betrayed him. “But it was funny.”

Mydei scoffed, the sound quiet and playful. “My brat is going to sit still and take this like a good boy. Don’t fight your restraints and make sure to stay calm during this. The moment you begin to think yourself into a bad spot, tell me. Got it?”

He nodded in understanding. “Yes, master.”

“We’re going to share a bowl of fresh fruit, and you’re going to tell me all about your day. When we finish talking, then I will uncuff them,” he promised. “If your shoulders get stiff, tell me.”

“I will.”

That sounded a little less intimidating than he anticipated this being.

One by one, Mydei secured the leather handcuffs around his wrists. Fingers slid around his wrists, tucking between the cushion and his skin to make sure it wasn’t too tight. When he pulled experimentally, a light and gentle tap smacked against his arm.

“Ah ah. I said not to pull,” came his scolding.

Phainon took a deep breath. “I’m sorry, master.”

“I don’t want you to say sorry,” he shot down, not accepting it. “Why did you pull after I said not to, Phainon? What’s wrong?”

“I wanted to test them,” he admitted sheepishly. “I wanted to see if I was really stuck again, and I am. There’s nowhere to go.”

“Yes. There’s nowhere for you to run, so stay with me.” Mydei’s voice lowered, his tone rich and silky like the night they spent in his office. “Don’t let yourself slip, and don’t let yourself overthink. Stay here, listen to me, and don’t fight.”

Phainon relaxed his arms, his hands fitting into one another despite the chunky cuffs pressing around his wrists. In doing so, two palms then gently reached for the base of his neck, lightly massaging just beneath with firm pinches.

“Give me a color.”

“Green, master,” he answered softly as his head rolled to the side. “Will you put my collar on?”

“You’ve grown to like it, haven’t you?” He noticed. “Is it comforting to know that when you come to my home, I own you entirely?”

His stomach tingled, and the hands on his neck lifted to gently cup his throat within it. Both thumbs stacked over each other top to bottom, and his fingers gently laced over his Adam’s apple. He didn’t threaten to squeeze, and he didn’t dare attempt to tighten. All he did was hold him, gentle and reassuring, like a collar with life in it, a choker with warmth to give, a necklace no one else in the world could have.

“Yeah,” he breathed out, eyes shutting softly to listen to his voice better. “I-I like my collar a lot, master.”

"Do you wish to have a different style?”

“No. I like the colors, the fit, and the… the ring you can pull on for my attention,” he confessed. “I like that it’s yours.”

“Good boy,” he praised him, then removed his hands slowly by inching them back down to his shoulders. There, he tightened his grasp. “Shoulders back. Eyes straight. Chin up.”

Phainon fixed his posture, straightening his back and opening his eyes to be more alert. From touching his shoulders to feeling nothing, he waited for those hands to come back with a gift. He waited for the kiss of leather around the middle of his throat, the tightened buckle to squeeze lightly, and that gentle click of metal.

He felt the edge rest over the base of his neck, enclosing around him loosely as Mydei chuckled.

“I used to close it right here,” he reminded him as he looped the end into its buckle. “That’s not what you want now, is it?”

“No, master.”

“What about this?” It tightened a little more, raised a little higher, and he gulped. “Is this enough for you?”

“Please…”

Mydei finally brought it to his Adam’s apple, pulled it enough to sit snugly over him, and he twitched from the pressure. A soft, shaky breath filled the room.

“That’s it,” the man behind him purred, feeding the prong through. “You like it right here, don’t you? Nice and tight, it keeps you from dropping your head too low, doesn’t it? That gives you more of a reason to look up… at… me.”

Phainon’s bound fists rolled, squirming underneath the heat of his husky tone and fixed gaze. Even without looking at him, he felt it.

“Stand for me, handsome.”

His knee swung carefully off of his body the moment those words left his lips, and he stabilized himself on one foot. With the help of Mydei’s warm hands, his other leg followed slowly until he didn’t need the assistance. While standing in front of him, he turned, focusing on his best friend completely.

There it was—that hot look of interest in his burning gaze as he looked him up and down. Despite being clothed, despite wearing just a t-shirt and some shorts, Mydei was lining his figure like he could see all of him. Like he wanted to see all of him, bound and collared, obeying his every word.

Phainon watched Mydei then grab a half-full bowl of mixed fruit. There was one fork inside of it for two people.

“Come sit down.”

Phainon carefully planted his knee beside his hip and into the couch cushion, lowering himself over his lap as he wanted. When he swayed too far, one hand pressed to the small of his back. It pulled him closer and steadied his body on top of him.

“I could do whatever I wanted with you right now,” He teased him, and a shiver inched up his spine over the familiar words. “You look handsome like this.”

“Master, keep it in your pants,” he teased him. “I’m not doing anything special.”

“All dressed up in leather cuffs and a collar…” He trailed off. “How would you feel about wearing a harness? A strappy chest piece that… Mm… I’m getting ahead of myself, aren’t I?”

Phainon’s eyes glanced down to Mydei’s chest, then as close to his own as the tall trim of his collar allowed. He tried to imagine himself shirtless, to see black leather straps working around his body in any way that could make sense. Tight, warm, hugging him like his collars and cuffs.

“You’re about the same size as I am. You have so many, surely one might look good on me,” he suggested, and Mydei nodded in agreement. “If… you ask me to in the future, I will. But not tonight.”

“Will you?”

“Yes, master.

“What if I bought you one for yourself?” He asked, and his eyes lifted. “No. Don’t take that as an offer or a suggestion. Will you wear it, yes or no?”

The ring was reminiscent of his home collar, of the submission he promised to give him, and the blue stone simply called out to them.

“Look at me.”

Phainon turned, and he looked at his best friend.

Mydei had already done his hair. The side braid he kept was neatly plaited over one ear, the ends capped in a clean, golden cuff. He smelled of his usual hairspray and deodorant, not having spritzed his cologne on yet since he still needed to finish dressing. His button down was missing. His tie was missing. All he wore was a fitted white tank-top, his usual slacks, and the jewelry he frequented.

While meeting his eyes, he caught the dangle by his ear through the edges of his vision. Gold, like all the things he wore, with a deep-rooted sapphire embedded into the top.

“Can I put it on you?” He asked, and Phainon nodded. “Use your words.”

“Yes, master.”

“Turn around. Don’t move too much.” He instructed him, grabbing the necklace from the box. “There are two keys. One stays in my bedroom and locked in my cabinet at all times. One will sit in my wallet at all times.”

His fingers reached for his glass of juice, and as much as Phainon didn’t see the point in these juices, he raised it to his lips for a drink.

“If it needs to come off, I will unlock it prematurely. Tell me. If an emergency persists and you can’t get a hold of me or make it to my place, well, that isn’t a problem either. You can just cut the lock. I’ll buy a new one,” he explained to him.

“How can I get into your locked house to get a key in your locked cabinet?” He mused, licking his lips of the bitter juice.

“Easy. I’ve written the code in our folder, and I will be giving you a spare key.”

The glass clicked a little harder than he meant for it to, and he stared down at his plate as cold metal kissed the base of his neck. Due to its shorter chain, there was very little space between his collar and the necklace, allowing it to sit directly above his shirt’s collar. It dangled tightly, enough to not be suffocating but enough to remind him it wasn't just for fashion.

“A-A key to your place?”

“If you lose it, you will not get another one.”

Fingers fumbled behind him, and he felt the firm press of metal on the back of his neck.

“But I’ll get one?” He asked for confirmation. “I can just… come over whenever I want? Do I need to ask permission to walk in?”

Did he give one of those to all of his submissives when they put on a day collar?

Mydei chuckled, the sound light and amused. “You should warn me first because that’s common courtesy, Phainon. If you text me before you come over, you are free to stay. Whether I see it or not is my fault for how often I check my personal phone, not yours.”

“I don’t… know what to say,” he admitted to him, a little bit surprised he would be given access to all of his things.

“Then don’t say a thing. Simply accept it.”

The pressure on his neck soon left, and he looked down at his neck to try and see the necklace on himself.

“Here,” Mydei offered. Within seconds, he picked his phone out of his pocket and swiped to access the camera. “Look at it.”

It sat cleanly and prettily on his shirt, the royal blue stone contrasting brightly against the crisp white fabric. The golden chain matched his neck tattoo too, making it not look out of place on his body.

“Is it too obvious?” He asked quietly, lightly tracing a shaking finger over the ring. “What if someone asks about it? What am I meant to say, De?”

“People have much, much busier lives than to scrutinize the necklace of a man they’ll never see again,” he promised him. “If they somehow don’t, you don’t owe them any explanation. It’s your body, and the only person who can tell you what to wear is me.”

His eyes rolled over his possessive words. “Seriously. What do I tell our friends and my family?”

Mydei tilted the camera up, this time to look at him without having him turn around.

“You can tell them it’s just a necklace, that you saw it online and you liked it. If they ask to see it, or if they ask for you to take it off, you can tell them to mind their business,” he said firmly. “If someone gets too pushy, you only need to remind them that you’re entitled to your interests without an explanation.”

That worked for him. Mydei liked his peace and his privacy. Everyone knew that and accepted that.

Between how close he was with Cyrene and his parents, things like that didn’t really fly so easily. They loved questions, and he loved sharing everything with them. How was he meant to blatantly lie to their faces?

“It’ll be okay,” Mydei hushed as if he could hear his thoughts. “You’re okay.”

He nodded, tilting his head back to look up at him instead of the phone screen. In doing so, his neck stretched, making room for Mydei’s hand to lightly cup beneath his chin to hold him there.

“All you need to do is tell them you liked it. No one is going to jump right to you being my submissive from a singular necklace,” he repeated gently. “If it persists, call me, and we can handle it together, okay? I will talk you down, and I will guide you on what to say.”

“What if you’re busy working?”

“Then I will call you as soon as I physically can, and we’ll talk about what you said and where to go from there,” Mydei told him. “For now, just tell them it’s fashion.”

“Yes, master,” he murmured.

One hand reached upwards, and his fingertips lightly brushed his singular earring.

“We’re matching again,” he pointed out. “First, your gear and my play collar are red and gold. Now, your earring and my day collar are blue and gold. What’s next?”

“Do you hate it?”

Phainon smiled, brushing the back of his ear to toy with his earring's butterfly back.

“I love my collars,” he reassured him. “You could have grabbed anything simple, anything in the standard black that you can find in stores, but you didn’t. You could have been so clinical about this whole thing, but you aren’t. These are yours, and seeing you in them makes wearing them less daunting.”

“How could I ever treat you like someone impersonal?” Mydei traced his thumb over his chin as he spoke. “You’re not just some random man I’ve let into my life or an object to push my desires on to. If I’m going to do this for you, of course it needs to be catered to us. If it's not me you see when you close your eyes, then what else would you think of?”

“I… don’t know. I don’t have any feelings for anyone to imagine them touching me,” he chuckled. “Maybe I would see those guys from the videos again…”

“Sex still scares you then, huh?”

“A little bit,” he admitted. “Some of the things we’ve done weren't scary at all, but… I guess the sexual aspect of being dominated is a bit harder to grasp. I… I’ve never been the kind of person to think much of it with someone, so to have it so suddenly is a bit much. This though?”

The hand not touching Mydei’s ear held the wrist beneath his chin, and he smiled when it pressed deeper.

“I like this part,” he told him honestly. “I like this… structure, and I’ve been feeling better as of recently, probably from all the extra sleep, exercising, and healthy meals. My nerves have gotten better too, but that’s because you’re a very comforting person, Mydei.”

“I’ve always been good at supporting someone else,” he agreed. “Maybe after me, you’ll like this so much that you’ll feel confident enough to join online communities and meet new people. You never know, maybe the reason you couldn't find a partner is because you were looking in the wrong areas.”

Phainon shrugged, not caring to think about some nameless, faceless dominant. He couldn’t find it in him to conjure someone else up when all he saw was Mydei there with his red and gold collar in hand.

“Maybe.”

“Maybe I’ll go back and see you getting hounded by all the men and women who want such a handsome and eager to learn sub,” he joked, but the thought of other people wanting him like this made his stomach churn. “Have you ever thought of being dominated by a woman?”

“No.”

Phainon gripped his wrist tighter as he listened to him continue.

“Maybe you'll like it,” his best friend pressed, still holding on to his joke. “What’s so bad about a dominant woman? You can call her ‘mistress’, or ‘mommy’, or—”

“I like my master,” he cut him off, and Mydei quieted down. “I don’t want a ‘mistress’. I don’t want a ‘sir’ either. I want my master.”

The sound of a camera’s shutter went off, and he grinned softly at the thought of him getting so distracted his finger slipped.

“What a possessive little submissive,” Mydei teased him, pulling back his phone to tuck it into his pocket. “You’re the one in a collar, but I’m yours, huh?”

Phainon’s fingers pinched his ear gently, careful of his jewelry, then smiled. “Please eat with me, master. As you get dressed for work, I’ll clean up the kitchen for us so you don’t have to do it.”

“What a good boy,” he said, rubbing his cheek gently. “You’ve got a stubble growing, by the way. It’s scratchy here.”

“What? Do you prefer a man with a clean shave?” He mused, and Mydei’s eyes darted from his face to his lap. “Hey! My eyes are up here!”

“I think your face is cuter when it’s smooth,” he said casually, and Phainon made a mental note to shave when he got home. “Don’t be nearly as heavy handed with a razor anywhere else though.”

“H… Huh?” He choked, and Mydei tapped his cheek again before letting go of him. “What does that mean? Like down there?”

“Continue eating now, Phainon,” he instructed him, ending that conversation. “I’ll eat with you.”

Mydei sat down beside him. Without him standing behind, he eased his neck lower before looking at his own plate. One hand picked his fork up, and just as he was about to rest his arm on the counter, he paused. Then he set it on his lap.

“Good job,” Mydei praised him.

Heat warmed his cheeks, and he took a small bite before glancing at him, noticing that he was already looking.

How was he meant to think of anyone else in his place?

Phainon’s day collar wasn’t as show stopping as he had anticipated. It didn’t draw nearly as much attention as he assumed it would, and no one dug in too deep when they saw it. Like Mydei said, no one really paid that much attention to him.

Cyrene asked the most questions, but she wasn’t particularly pushy on the subject. All she said was jewelry looked odd on him since he never wore it before, and he could accept that. After all, he didn’t wear it often. Not rings. Not earrings. Not necklaces. He had his choker, his friendship bracelet with her, and his watch. That was all he ever needed.

At work, Hysilens complimented it, saying it was as pretty as the depths of the ocean. When visiting his parents, his mother warned him that he needed to be very careful not to lose something so beautiful. His father just told him that it looked good on him while patting his back.

It felt so… freeing. Even if his head told him they knew, no one confronted him like it was some dark, twisted secret to be ashamed of. No one did more than a glance and send a bit of praise his way, too busy or uncaring to do much else.

He could be Mydei’s openly in front of them all, in front of everyone who passed him by, and no one knew any better. He loved it. He loved that freedom of expression and the security of knowing this secret was safe.

Days rolled by in a comfortable routine. Every few nights, he went to Mydei’s place to talk, hang out, and keep up with their dynamics. They watched movies, played games, and tossed their back and forth banter around like they always did. Mydei cooked for them. He cleaned for them. At the end of the day, they’d cuddle in his bed with his hand on his throat to hold him close. At the start, they’d work out as the sun came up over the horizon to discuss their schedules.

Otherwise, he stayed home and did his best to abide by his usual rules by texting him for ideas of what to eat and what to wear. He sent him videos of his meals as he cooked them, snapped pictures of his freshly shaven face when he cleaned up, and took photos of him with the plush toy that sat cutely on his bed. In return, he got Mydei’s audio messages praising him for being so good and pictures of him doing the same mundane things.

Though being there in person was infinitely better, he didn’t mind this if it meant they could hold on to their secret a little while longer. Especially because he could save the photos and videos sent to him, and the messages could be replayed whenever he felt like it.

While he was stressed at work, he could hide in the bathroom with his phone to his ear, and he could listen to his best friend’s voice as he called him a ‘good boy’. It gave him just enough strength to leave the stall, wash his hands and face, then get back out there with a smile on his face. Because if Mydei saw him hiding out instead of working, he’d tell him that he could do it. He’d tell him that there were just a few hours left on the clock, and he was strong enough to get through his shift no matter how rude people could be.

He could be a good boy, right? He could get through just a little bit more, couldn’t he?

Yeah, he could. He would.

He did.

By the end of his shift, he was both exhausted and proud of himself for managing to get through the night. He was ready to go home, to make the easiest dinner he could think of, then head to bed to call Mydei and talk until they fell asleep. Like kids did in those childish romance movies when they had a crush on someone.

Not that Phainon had a crush. He just liked spending time with Mydei, and it was routine to talk about their days at the end of it. Without these personal touches, casual conversations, and sincere interest in one another's personal lives, their arrangement would feel far too strict and detached.

But as he was leaving, he felt someone lightly grab his sleeve. Upon turning to look, he saw Hysilens there with one hand pinching her rosy ear and the other gripping his shirt.

“Are you… uh… busy tonight?” She asked, and he almost wanted to say yes. He almost wanted to tell her that he just wanted to go home and end his day already.

Mydei’s voice popped into his head a second after that thought, telling him she deserved a friend who would be kind to her. Lying wasn’t a ‘kind’ thing to do, and since he had agreed to be friends, neither was dodging her when she asked to hang out.

Would he want someone to do that to him? No, he wouldn’t.

“I’m not busy. Why? What’s up?” He caved to the weight of the memory, torn between cursing his best friend for making sense and himself for feeling selfish.

“I was wondering if you would like to see this local band perform. They’re playing at a bar nearby, a-and my wife got me two tickets in. She told me to ask my new friend to join," Hysilens explained sheepishly. “You don’t have to, but—”

No, he had to. There was no way he could turn her down if the tickets were already purchased. It’d be a waste of money if both weren’t used.

“When?”

“In a few hours, I think. So… that makes it about eight? I can send you the address and we can meet up a bit before it starts,” she said hopefully, and he bit down on the inside of his bottom lip.

It wasn’t necessarily his bedtime. There was nothing in their rules that said he had to be in bed by eight or he’d risk being punished. The reason he found it a routine at all was because Mydei typically was. He was in his bedroom by eight and asleep no later than ten every weekday. And when he visited him, that was something he had to abide by if he wanted to keep waking up at six to work out with him.

While apart, Mydei allowed him to stay up a bit later since he didn’t necessarily need to be up so early, but he still wanted to be in bed. He wanted to talk to him on the phone as they relaxed and prepared to fall asleep.

“I’ll need to check in with someone, but I should be able to make it. I don’t see why not.”

“Is it your girlfriend?” She asked suddenly, making his cheeks warm at the assumption he even had one to report back to. “I don’t want to intrude on your relationship. If you need to be home with her, then—”

His head immediately shook. “No. I don’t have a girlfriend,” he chuckled awkwardly to shoot her down. “I’m single, and flattered you’d think otherwise, though.”

Her eyebrows furrowed as if confused by the revelation, eyes darting down his neck before shooting towards the left. Her lips parted, but not a word left them when she decided to simply nod and meet his eyes again. The hand on his arm let him go, tucking behind her back with the other.

What was she just staring at? His every day choker? His day collar?

Nerves immediately thrummed underneath his skin, aware that she looked at one before trying to make it appear as if she didn’t.

It wasn’t as if they’ve ever talked about anything close to BDSM, just chores they do around the house, the things they enjoy, and her wife. He didn’t make it obvious that his chores were expectations from Mydei when at his house. He didn’t even talk much about him besides occasionally mentioning a ‘protective friend’ of his, one that made sure he was in bed by a specific time. That wasn’t enough to figure him out, right?

Did he make it too obvious by also mentioning that he needed to check in with someone first? Was his ‘necklace’ really about as secret as a room made of glass like he feared?

No. No, it couldn’t be. She couldn’t know that he was tangled up with someone, or that his ‘necklace’ was anything more than simple jewelry.

With the newfound freedom of having his arm back, he pulled his phone out of his back pocket to check the time and break their uncomfortable eye contact. As warm as her gaze was, it felt a lot like she was burning a hole right through his security. But the worst part was he couldn’t even blame her, it was his shame cranking up the heat.

Once he held the device in hand, his thumb rushed to input his passcode, desperate to find a way out.

“I… should get going… I’d like to change out of these clothes and into something more appropriate for a night out,” she brought up, and he agreed with a distracted hum. “I’ll see you in a bit. Hopefully you can make it.”

Did he even want to go anymore and risk being found out by her?

Phainon flicked his gaze back towards the woman, gave her a happy grin with a slight nod, then let her walk away first before he went to tap Mydei’s contact. As the dial tone rang, his hurried feet carried him out of the building and towards his car. While unlocking the vehicle, the ringing ended.

It wasn’t wrong to seek comfort in him right now, was it? After all, Mydei insisted that was what he was there for—support.

“Hello? Phainon?” He heard. Beneath his best friend’s voice was the clacking of a keyboard. “Is everything alright?”

“Hey, De. You’re not still at work are you? I thought you got off already. Don’t… tell me you’re staying late again.” He frowned, worried that he might have disrupted him during something important.

Maybe he should have texted first.

“No, I’m in bed. I’m just browsing online at the moment.” A click sounded as Phainon got into his car. “You’re not disrupting anything, handsome.”

When the door shut, he felt his lip twitch upwards from the privacy, the reassurance, and the gentle pet name. Even if he hadn’t said it out loud, he just knew that was one of his worries. It felt like Mydei knew what to look out for now.

“Oh? And what’s a man in bed alone browsing for?” He joked instead. “Did I call you at a bad time?”

“You’re shameless,” Mydei tsk’ed, but the lightheartedness was easy to discern.

“What? I can’t tease you anymore?” He pouted. “Surely even the oh-so composed Master Mydei has his urges when alone.”

It was meant as a joke, but sometimes he wondered if Mydei actually did look at stuff like that. Since they weren’t particularly deep in the sexual aspect of everything because of his own nerves, where did he get his fix? What did he like to watch in his free time? Who did he think about when he did it?

Porn never did anything for him really. Sometimes a good one popped up, but most of the time he found himself cringing at the acting or the concept.

But what did Mydei use for himself? Was he the kind of person to imagine being with whatever attractive man was on the screen, or did he imagine himself with someone else in that position?

A thought suddenly struck him after that.

Did Mydei imagine him when he touched himself? Or did he imagine someone else he was with before?

“Ha. Ha.” The sarcastic reply brought him back to their conversation. “Don’t get too curious about things like that, Phainon. You know where that nose leads you and where that head can take you.”

He could warn him of that all day and all night, but Phainon wanted to know. He needed to know.

Did Mydei think of him? Did he see his eyes looking up at him as he had his lips wrapped around him? Did he remember the way he looked on his lap, dressed in things he's never worn, as he shook from the pain and pleasure?

Was he the only person he could touch himself to right now? Or did he turn around and think of one of his exes when he left?

“Are you really complaining about my curious nature right now?” He mouthed back, and silence followed the bratty response. “Why are you warning me of it when it’s given you a sub that's as dedicated as I am? Do you not like me anymore?”

Mydei then sighed. “We’ve been through this lesson before, Phainon. I don’t like when you talk poorly of yourself or portray me as someone I’m not.”

“I haven’t said anything depreciating about myself though,” Phainon defended himself. “I’m just asking you a question. Is my curiosity a bad thing now? Should I stop being adventurous and start staying within my comfort zone more?”

“Phainon, this is your third and final warning. Talk to me as you should,” he reprimanded him. “What you're doing is not communication. It’s a one-sided argument that you’re somehow losing.”

“Third warning until what?” He dared.

“The more you run that mouth of yours, the more ways I’m going to imagine shutting it up,” he threatened. “I can get pretty creative. You may or may not like what I come up with.”

Phainon then looked down at his steering wheel.

“And how would you do that?” He retorted one last time, using it as a chance to see if Mydei would talk about what he would do with him. “You’re too busy rubbing one out to some guy online to do anything to me, right?”

Silence took over for a moment, then a deep intake of a breath from the other end disrupted it. Slowly, that breath bled into a chilling chuckle. It taunted him as if asking if he were sure he wanted to have this conversation, as if warning him that he might not like the things he was going to say. He could hear the humor and the interest in each shake of his chest, like it was going to come out whether he liked it or not too.

But Mydei did say he was going to teach him how to please him, and that included pushing his limits again and seeing how much he could bend. In return, he did promise to give him that control over him all the time.

All he had to worry about was asking for what he wanted and telling him when he felt uncomfortable with something. That was it. Otherwise, Mydei was free to act.

What would he do with that power?

“What’s so funny?”

“Do you think I’m stupid, Phainon?” He was still laughing lightly. “If you need reassurances, or if you have something you want from me, you don’t need to be a disrespectful brat to achieve it.”

Phainon didn’t want to admit this though. He didn’t want to bring up the sour feeling that reared its ugly head whenever he thought about Mydei doing these things with him just to imagine another person when he was away. It was embarrassing. There was no real reason to feel that way, but he just… did.

The thought of Mydei thinking about someone else as they went through this together made him uneasy.

“What if… I don’t wanna talk right now?” He hinted, hoping he could just act instead of forcing him to talk. “What if I want you to push me a little bit and get my mind off of something? We can talk about it later.”

“Where are you right now, Phainon?”

His eyes darted over the darkened dashboard and stereo. “In my car. I haven’t turned it on to go home yet,” he answered, curious about where this would go.

“Turn it on and drive yourself over here instead,” Mydei instructed, his voice firm and sending a tingle through his heavy stomach. “You have twenty minutes to be inside my bedroom and ready to accept a punishment for your attitude. Don’t expect me to be as nice as I was.”

He shivered at the thought. What exactly did a ‘not so nice’ version of Mydei entail?

“Oh, but wait. I can’t,” he back tracked, reminded of why he called in the first place when he noticed the building in front of him. “I have somewhere to be later. I was supposed to ask you if I could go, but I got… distracted.”

He had to go home, get dressed, and shake himself of this nasty feeling. Then, he needed to think of a way to throw Hysilens off of his case and convince Cyrene he wasn’t seeing her when she asked what he’s doing later—as he knew she’d tease him. There was so much to think about, so much to do, and—

“You can come earn your permission like a good boy does. Stop talking, and start driving,” he said to him, cutting off his thoughts. “Now.”

The knee-jerk reaction to shakily shove his key into the ignition was almost laughable. With all the time they spent together, his reflexes knew just when to obey, and that tone of voice triggered it every time. Low, husky, and effortlessly dominant, he was weak to it every single time.

“I’ll see you in twenty minutes, brat.”

“Y-Yeah, I’ll be there.”

Their call ended, and he slumped back into his seat before rubbing his hands over his face from a mix of frustration and flustered heat.

The drive from his job to his place was about twenty minutes already, even longer at this hour with all of the traffic. People were still getting off. Everyone was trying to get across town and get back home to relax. He worked in the busiest part of the city, and finding parking around Mydei’s place was a time-consuming task most days. There was no way he’d make it.

Mydei knew that too. He knew this was an impossible task to ask of him, but maybe that was the point. His best friend was too smart not to know how hard he would try to fulfill it, meaning he must have also known how miserably he would end up failing it.

Phainon squirmed, completely untouched yet bothered in a way that made him hot underneath his work clothes. His heart was pounding, beating harder and harder as he thought about the sadistic kick to Mydei’s words.

‘I can get pretty creative.’

‘Don’t expect me to be nice.’

‘Come earn your permission.’

It was scary all over again, but it was Mydei at the end of the day. He could do it if it was him. He could take it if it was him.

He was quick to start his car after taking a moment to just breathe, to drive the route he knew best and beat the clock. It brought a sense of comfort within him to see the familiar shops and lights, even if there were a lot of tail lights around him. Music helped to calm the bubbling nerves that grew stronger as the space between them got smaller.

Between hitting every red light the city had to offer and fighting to find a parking spot, he knew he wasn’t within his time frame. If anything, the trip probably took him nearly twice as long.

Hurried feet carried him quickly through the building, past the receptionist who always gave him a flirty wave and right towards the elevator. His eyes didn’t stray. His lips didn’t twitch for any kind of polite smile back. Not this time. He was a man on a mission, and every second mattered now that he had absolutely blown past his allotted time frame.

Knowing Mydei, he was counting. He was waiting with a timer, ready to tell him just how much time he wasted.

There was a key hanging off his key ring that slotted perfectly into Mydei’s doorknob. The metal was cleaner than the rest of them, making it easy to spot and prove just how new it was in his possession. He could have easily opened the door himself and walked in like he owned the place. Maybe it would have been faster too.

But this time, he didn’t rush. He knocked.

With his keys in one fist and the other balled to meet the wood, he stood there, waiting for Mydei to let him in on his own time. Because this was his space, and how could he ever try to treat it like it was his when Mydei was the one in charge?

Had he not been home or not demanded he visit, yes. Maybe Phainon would have let himself in. Something deep inside told him, however, this was not the time to do it.

Soon, the lock flipped, and its sound immediately made a rush flood through his nerves and upwards to his chest. It was cool and just a little anxious, as he had no idea what to expect when it opened.

Well, Mydei was there. And he expected that. But he didn’t expect to see him like that.

As the front door pulled open, he saw his best friend’s raised eyebrow and knowing smirk looking down at him. One arm was bent at the elbow and pressing against the doorframe beside his head, and in his hand was his phone with a ticking timer on it. The pad of his thumb hovered over the stop button, but even while looking at him, he didn't stop him. It stayed, waiting for the right moment to press.

“I’m here,” he said shakily, watching the numbers run but not knowing what it meant. “M… Master, I’m here.”

“Hello,” he greeted him casually. “You’re here, yes, but what did I say? Where do you need to be?”

Phainon looked at his face, following the bare expanse of his neck and shoulders while trying to wrack his brain for an answer. Words were leaving his lips. Thoughts were escaping his head.
