Her eyes shifted, and she pinched her earring while curling into herself. “Isn’t it kind of like that? You just tolerate me while I talk about myself and my wife? That’s not fun for you to deal with, is it?”

Phainon only laughed in return, the sound light and easygoing. He pulled her closer, away from the crowds of people and on to his opposite side. There was more space for her to walk, less bodies to bump into, and therefore more room for her to breathe. Hopefully, that helped her relax a little bit more around him.

“You know, you really shouldn’t talk so poorly about yourself like that,” he advised her as she linked her arm with his. “I get it’s easy to do, but you deserve better than to feel like someone’s burden. ”

She was quiet, so he continued.

“This isn’t some drag to do. I’m here to have fun and get to know you better, so don’t think you’re forcing me into anything. I’m a grown man. I can say ‘no’.”

Hysilens nodded, but whether she was truly comforted by the statement or not, he had no clue. “Thank you, Phainon,” was all she said in return.

“And, for the record, I like listening to you talk about your wife. It’s cute how much you love her, and it’s obvious she brings you the most comfort,” he noticed. “So… will you tell me more about her over a drink? Preferably something without alcohol.”

That made her perk up.

“I’m not allowed to drink tonight,” she returned, and he thought about that word for a moment—‘allowed’. She wasn’t ‘allowed’ to drink, just as she ‘can’t’ let him pay for her.

His eyebrow lifted. “Why’s that?”

“My wife doesn’t like when I drink without someone she trusts around,” she disclosed. “That’s not a slight on you, but the people who might be here.”

Phainon wasn’t offended at all, and part of him wasn’t surprised to hear that. Something in him expected a response like that.

More than just Mydei and her wife, maybe the two of them had more in common than he thought as he remembered those same words leaving Mydei’s mouth. It wasn’t just about him driving later. It was about him being a lightweight too, and Mydei didn't want him to drink without having him around to look after him. Who knew if someone would try to get in too close with the wrong intentions?

He assumed her wife felt exactly the same. She didn’t know these people, and she couldn’t trust them with her spouse. Hell, he was a stranger to her, so he couldn’t blame her if she didn't see him as trustworthy yet either.

“I hope to become someone your wife can trust so you can have fun around me,” he told her kindly. “Also, my finger’s a little bit itchy tonight. You don’t mind if I take some photos and videos of us, right? For the memories.”

Mydei wanted to see him have fun, and he wanted to share this night with him too even if he wasn’t around.

She held her phone up too, waving it shyly in agreement. “My wife requested I do the same…”

That made him think back to earlier that night, to her eyes on his day collar and the assumption of a girlfriend. Her potentially figuring him out was a terrifying thought, and it made his stomach knot uncomfortably all over again.

But he was being a bit of a hypocrite tonight.

The more she knew about him, the more he wanted to run away and hide it all inside of a locked box. But the more she casually shared with him about her, the more… normal… everything about him began to feel.

She spoke of her own permissions, and it made him think of himself and his own. If it was weird, over-protective, or out of the ordinary to have someone behind him to request this of him, then she was right there with him, right? Or was it wrong to relate his dominant and submissive dynamic with her marriage despite not having any kind of confirmation she was into the same thing?

They had similar rules. They had similar people looking over them. The only difference was the ring on her finger and the comfort she had in expressing it openly to people.

Phainon looked at that ring as he thought about it, then the earring he recalled matched her wife’s necklace.

“I can send you the pictures I take, and you can send me the ones you take, and we’ll have twice the memories of tonight to share,” he suggested, and that made her eyes sparkle. Pink dusted over her pale cheeks, and both were pushed to a plush round from her wide grin.

She was always so pleased and so excited to make her partner happy, and part of him wondered if he looked nearly half as sweet in Mydei’s eyes.

Did he look like that?

When he did something to make Mydei happy, and that made him feel proud of himself, did he have that same look on his face?

Hysilens grabbed his arm and dragged him towards the bar immediately after hearing his proposition, and he couldn’t help but share that excitement. As much as he was here for himself and to have a good night, he wanted to share this with Mydei and let him see the result of his influence.

He liked keeping him updated on his life away from him. A lot.

—

Despite never knowing this place existed, Phainon enjoyed his time there. Drinking mocktails and munching on finger foods as they listened to the live band perform was nice. He took photos of him and Hysilens with their pretty glasses, videos of the band playing on the lit up stage, and quick mirror pictures inside the bathroom with strangers who wanted in on the attention. Men who posed right beside him, smiled brightly as the shutter went off, and laughed before wishing him a fun time.

It made him so glad that he agreed to come in the first place, then beyond grateful that Mydei pushed him to come out when he tried to change his mind.

He learned more about Hysilens and her relationship too, like how she and her wife had been together for nearly ten years. They met in high school, explored what being together would be like, then committed to it before they could go to different colleges. She went to school for music, her wife studied law, and they moved in together after school. They then moved here for her wife’s work, and Hysilens followed because she didn’t care where she was as long as she was beside the other woman.

Though he didn’t say it out loud, that sounded so romantic.

“You do whatever she says then?” He asked casually, hoping it wasn’t too heavy of a question to spring upon her.

“She wants what’s best for me,” she replied, holding a french fry to her mouth before taking a bite. “All I ever need to worry about is having fun and coming home to her.”

“Why do you still work if she pays for everything?”

“My money is put into our savings and used to save for vacations. Her money is spent on everything else,” she answered like it was that simple. “I never need to worry about it because her card always has enough for whatever I need it for.”

Phainon looked down at his drink, taking in the mint garnish and the half-empty glass full of limes before stirring it with his straw.

“You don’t feel the need to… I don’t know… hold on to that part of yourself? Is it hard letting her do it all for you?” He couldn't help but wonder.

“She’s my wife.”

One thing he noticed is Hysilens never used her name. In text messages, in social media posts, in verbal conversations, she never spoke her name when referring to her. She was ‘her wife’, and it felt like that was the only thing that ever needed to be said about the woman.

Why did she do something? Because her wife said so.

And why did she listen so diligently? Because that was her wife.

“Are you not allowed to say her name?”

Hysilens hummed thoughtfully, and when he looked up at her, she shook her head. “I don’t feel the need to say it unless someone asks me specifically what it is. Referring to her as what she is makes the most sense, and she feels the same.”

When she met his eyes, he picked his drink up and took a slow sip, unable to hold on to her gaze for long.

“Can I ask you something, Phainon?”

He nodded while drinking.

“What do you think about relationships where… someone has more power than the other person?” She asked him, speaking carefully but getting right to the point. “Like my wife and I?”

“I… uh…”

What was he supposed to say without giving himself away?

“I don’t… ever see myself having a partner who would want to rely so heavily on me,” he confessed to her, hoping that would suffice. “It’s not for me.”

He couldn’t be like Mydei and her wife. Even if he had the means to support that kind of lifestyle, the stress alone would be too much to handle on a daily basis. Having to worry about himself on top of someone else so closely would make him panic over the right thing to do at every turn. Being a provider for someone else never once crossed his mind, not in the way they did it.

He could work. Being a breadwinner wasn’t the issue if he could bother applying elsewhere out of his comfort zone, and being someone reliable wasn’t what worried him when he knew he was.

But he couldn’t take someone’s life, hold it in his hands, then mold it to their combined image like clay. He didn’t have that in him.

“What about the opposite?” She brought up after, and he gulped quietly to himself. “What about… being someone like me? The one being taken care of?”

“I never considered that possibility,” he lied, attempting to protect his secret.

“Your necklace is very pretty,” Hysilens complimented him suddenly, then tapped a certain spot on her throat. “The lock on the chain needs to be readjusted though.”

His eyes widened over her observation, and he immediately reached for his neck before gripping the chain. Sure enough, the pill sized lock was front and center by his shirt’s collar for all to see. How long had it been like that?

Frantic hands spun the lock towards the back of his neck to hide, and as she looked at it, then at him, he exhaled shakily. Caught. Like a deer in headlights just awaiting the impact.

“I-I’m… I didn’t…”

She knew he was lying to her.

“It’s okay,” Hysilens told him gently. “No one would notice if they didn’t already know what it was.”

But she knew.

It wasn’t speculation anymore. The worry of being found out wasn’t just a worry anymore, it was reality. This was real.

She knew about him wearing a locked collar, and she knew there was someone behind him telling him what to do. She knew he reported back to his dominant to get permission to come out tonight, and she knew he was a filthy liar for saying he didn’t think much of a dynamic with a power imbalance.

“It’s not just a necklace, is it?”

He was quiet, and her fingers brushed over her pierced ear before gently brushing the dangling pearl.

“If it makes you feel better, this isn’t just an earring.”

His eyes watched it swing for a moment, unsure whether he wanted to run from her now or sit in his discomfort to face it head on.

The air around them was thick and heavy, hot from the bodies packed in and stuffy from too many combined scents. It didn’t go down easily. It didn’t taste like anything but fear. Even as he tried hard to swallow it down, his lungs felt as if there wasn't enough of it to go around.

This table they occupied was so public. There were so many people around them. Though no one seemed to care or notice what was happening, he couldn't help but fear that they knew. Somehow, someway, everyone knew, like when he first started this journey and had ‘pervert’ planted over his forehead everywhere he went.

Reason said no one but Hysilens knew. But his nerves didn't listen to reason.

With his collar in hand, Phainon dragged his finger over the golden chain and traced over each slender link. He circled around the ring and slid the attached pendant side to side, toying with it.

If Mydei were here, he'd tell him not to worry. He’d tell him that he didn’t owe her an explanation, and if he didn’t want to share a word about it, he didn’t need to. This was their business. This was their life. Even if she guessed right, or if he was careless enough, he didn't need to open his mouth.

But… he was caught.

Noticing his discomfort, she sighed. “I pierced this ear for my mistress.”

Phainon looked at the backs facing them their way from the people ignoring their presences, then back at her as she smiled lightly. There was a look in her eye that made him wonder if he she cared at all that anyone could see, or potentially hear, her.

Was she really that shameless? Did her wife not care if she told people?

No. Did her ‘mistress’ not care?

“I wear too many chokers, and I have so many necklaces. I didn’t want her ownership to look like just any old necklace,” Hysilens shared with him, and his eyes darted to her neck full of layered accessories. “I pierced my ear, and she gave me this earring—a pearl, because I love the sea and my mistress loves me.”

‘Mistress’. Mydei brought that title up when he tried to poke and tease him, but even thinking about that name when referring to someone whose face he could point out made him uneasy. To him, that was her wife. He didn’t like the title so much as floating around in his head even if Hysilens was quick and comfortable to share it with him.

Phainon liked his master. He liked the thought of Mydei being the only person in his head with any kind of title attached to him. That was his thing. That was reserved only for him.

“Is she your… wife… all the time?” He managed to force himself to ask, and one dark eyebrow lifted over his question. “Is that why you don’t say her name?”

“Yes. She is my wife, nothing less.”

So many questions plagued his head, but Mydei didn’t want anyone to know this side of him. Only his submissive was allowed to know he liked this kind of relationship, and that meant he couldn’t speak a word of anything that could identify him as his dominant. But he was curious. It was eating away at him.

Was this ‘normal’ for her too then? All day and every day, were they practicing it like he and Mydei were? Was she as ashamed as he was when they first started exploring this?

A part of him wanted to know how she handled it, if she could give him tips, and if he came across as obvious. He wanted to know how similar his experience was to her own, and if he was ‘normal’ to be enjoying it as much as he did. Reassurance from someone other than Mydei could be nice, as the shared experiences between them so far have brought him a little bit of comfort in opening up. Could she offer him advice on how to feel better inside—one submissive to another?

But another part wanted to run. He wanted to jump out of his seat, hop into his car, and drive as far as possible from her. The door was so close, and he just needed to move his feet. They could pretend this night and conversation never happened, and he could just… ignore her the next time they saw each other at—

No.

He couldn't do that. That was too cruel to imagine.

She came clean, and she was trying to make him feel better. He wasn’t that kind of person, and Mydei would be so utterly disappointed in him for being a coward like that. He wouldn’t just scold him, he’d punish him, and not the ‘fun’ kind either.

A submissive who just kept misbehaving on purpose and racking up the ‘bad’ kinds of punishments wasn’t a good one, was he? If he suddenly stopped playing the role he agreed to, that would be upsetting to the stability they’ve slowly created together. If he stopped giving him obedience, then why would Mydei keep giving him his guidance?

Phainon exhaled, pulling harder on the necklace as he tried to recall the way Mydei said he was okay. This was okay. He had no reason to be ashamed, and he had nothing to feel dirty about.

He was okay.

Hysilens knew, but she was in the same boat as he was. How could she see him in any kind of way if that reflected on her as well?

If he was dirty, she was dirty. If he was weak, she was weak. If he wasn’t normal for being collared every single day, she wasn’t normal for using ‘wife’ as a secret title for her dominant.

“Phainon?”

“I-I need some air. Please excuse me.”

His chair scraped to the tiled floors, and he winced while heading towards the exit. Bodies bumped into him in his pursuit to leave, and he stumbled over his own boots from his own clumsiness. People scoffed behind him, and some managed to see him barreling through to step out of the way just in time.

When he managed to make it out anyway, he took a slow and deep breath of the cool, crisp air around him. There weren’t many people outside now that the band had left and the night matured, leaving the stench of cigarettes distant. It was refreshing, and it grounded him as he stepped away from the building and pulled his phone out.

Shaky fingers fumbled with it, and there were two things he noticed when turning the screen on—one being it was nearly midnight, and the second being he had about four percent of battery left from all the time he spent recording his night. He kept all his memories, but sacrificed his comfort in this moment as he watched the number drop to three.

Three percent, just enough to open their messages and see that the last text sent was his own unopened string of pictures. They were left on ‘delivered’, and that made him realize Mydei probably fell asleep. It was so late, and he probably tried to stay up, but couldn’t bring himself to.

Oh, was he going to be in trouble anyways?

Maybe not seriously. Knowing Mydei, he’d probably make his punishment something like waking up early despite going to bed so late. That was the natural consequence of being out like this. Or he’d make him sleep earlier the next few nights, meaning no movies, shows, or videos before bed.

He could deal with that. It was boring, and he would prefer to have it, but punishment was punishment.

While thinking, he felt someone stand beside him, and he knew the silhouette in his peripheral vision well.

“We still match,” she told him, and he looked down as she held up her bare arm beside his leather clad one. “You don’t need to talk about it, and you don’t need to worry about me talking about your business. The only person I’m obligated to share information with is my wife.”

That made sense.

“If you don’t want to bring it up, I won’t,” Hysilens promised, and he nodded quickly. “If you need anything, ask. I’m pretty open about this to people I get close to. It’s been my life for almost… six years now, maybe? I think I have some knowledge of it… trials, errors, successes, and all.”

Six years.

Mydei said he had two years under his belt of practicing it, then a few more of researching and being interested in it in silence. She had more than that. She must know even more than he did about this.

“If you don’t feel comfortable talking about it with me, here. You can look at this blog, and you never have to talk to me about it again,” she offered, and he held his hand out as she placed a napkin in it. “I document everything there. It’s my online journal.”

Vaguely, he remembered Mydei saying he stumbled across someone’s journey online when he first got into everything. He didn’t get the violent videos and crude fantasies of fanatics like he did. He found this, blogs and communities of real people doing real things in their day-to-day lives. Nothing fabricated. Nothing exaggerated.

“Are you sure this is okay?” He asked quietly, gripping it tightly. “I… I don’t mean to pry, or be weird about this. I’m just… new to this all. Like really new.”

“Consider it a ‘thank you’. You’ve done your best to make me comfortable, so if I can help, I’d like to as well.” Her sincere expression made it difficult for him to deny her kindness. “We’re friends now, right? Nothing has to change because of what we do in secret on our own time.”

Where did he hear that before?

He looked at the name written on the napkin, then watched her check her phone for the time.

“My wife will be angry at me if I’m not home soon, so I should call it a night.” She sighed to herself after. “And you?”

“Yeah, I should have been back a bit ago,” he admitted, not able to admit he had someone waiting on him too.

“Are you okay to drive? You’re not shaken up or anything, right?” She asked, and he nodded in response. “Yes… you’re shaken up?”

“No,” he laughed, getting a sense of deja vu from this too. “No, I’m okay. Thank you. Really. I… uh… I had a good time, and… thank you, again, for this.”

He held the napkin, and she elbowed him gently. It didn’t hurt, nor was it particularly hard, but he allowed himself to sway from the push.

“Don’t tell anyone,” she requested. “I’m open with you because we’re friends, but I’d like to keep my intimate little journal, well, intimate. It isn’t that popular, and I like it that way. It’s just me, my wife, and a small community of people like us.”

“I don’t even know who I’d tell,” he confessed awkwardly. It wasn’t as if he wanted people to know he looked at stuff like this, let alone practiced it. “Text me when you get home so I know you made it safely.”

“You too,” she returned. “I’ll see you at work—”

“And come out with my friends and I sometime,” he cut her off with a rush. “You should have more than just me and your phone to hang out with. The girls will love you, if you don’t mind Cyrene’s preppiness, Cassie’s timidness, and Cifera’s curiosity.”

“I’d like that,” she said while holding her keys in hand. “I’ll ask my wife. I’m very sure she’ll be happy to let me go. Who knows? Maybe I can convince her to come out and meet the guy she allowed to take me out.”

Phainon liked that idea. He wanted to see how they acted in public too, if it was like him and Mydei or if they knew how to be more discreet. Maybe they could learn from them, as they had so much more experience.

Maybe Mydei could make a friend with her wife too.

“I’d like that too,” he repeated. “Good night, Hysilens.”

“Good night, Phainon.”

He watched her walk towards her car, waving as she started it and laughing when her music boomed louder than it should have been. For extra measure, he waited for her to pull out completely from the parking lot, then his feet carried him towards his own vehicle.

Oh, he couldn’t wait to lay down beside Mydei and finally go to bed. His head was hurting, and he was exhausted from the nerves burning up his energy.

—

It was past midnight by the time he got back to Mydei’s place. His fingers carefully took his borrowed boots off, gently pulling the zipper and setting them on the rack beside him. The borrowed jacket was hung up in a coat closet nearby as well, left so it could be wiped down and cleaned at a later time. All of it was routine the moment he walked into his home.

Phainon’s busy, thought-riddled head didn’t even notice the lights were still on until his fingers pushed gently to the wall and found the switch already flipped. Beneath the refrigerator hum, beneath his own shaky breathing, soft and steady snores filled the open floored kitchen and living room. They were welcoming and familiar in every way, easing his frustrations almost immediately.

He found Mydei right there by the kitchen bar. There was a cold cup of coffee by his sleeping figure, its contents half empty with a beige lip stain on the edge of its white rim. Beside that sat a glass cake dish full of fluffy, gooey cinnamon rolls stacked into an uneven tower due to their differing sizes. They were slathered messily in icing, so much so that it dripped over one another and made a complete mess over the bottom of the dish and its dome.

It looked as if he had fallen asleep while resting his head in his hand, as if he tried to stay up but ultimately ended up succumbing to exhaustion. Hunched over the counter with his face tucked into his inner elbow, the way his arm and wrist hung over the back of his head looked anything but comfortable.

His best friend was waiting for him. He probably went and baked to stay up longer, made some coffee to fight his own internal clock, forced himself to finish the desserts even if he could barely bring himself to care about aesthetics, then passed out trying to wait some more. Not that Phainon could blame him. This was later than he ever stayed up. He slept by ten, but it was past midnight.

Guilt settled in his stomach as he looked at his uncomfortable position, at his crooked arm and slumped over back.

How long was he asleep? His back was going to hate him in the morning.

One hand gently settled over his shoulder, sliding along his cold skin from underneath the cut out of his tank-top. Phainon rubbed him gently, not wanting to shock him or scare him awake.

The action caused Mydei to shiver before curling deeper into himself, fingers twitching and balling into his fist slowly. His next breath was deep and clearly disturbed, before it slowly mellowed out once more.

“De,” he whispered carefully, and the other man hummed just shy of inaudibly. “Let's get you to bed.”

“Mm…”

“You don’t look very comfortable.”

“Mm…?”

Amusement twitched his lip upwards over the confused rumble.

“Master,” he said into his ear lightly, dragging the name out almost teasingly to coax him awake. “Can I take you to bed?”

At the sound of that, Mydei’s arm lowered slowly, stiffly, carefully against the counter until it was flat to the cool surface. Then, he wiped his mouth. One eye cracked open just enough to look at him before he turned to look at his hand on his shoulder.

Phainon couldn’t help but wince when his joints popped and cracked from him sitting up.

“…—is it?”

“What’s that?” He mused, unable to understand the quiet, rumbling sound that left his lips.

Mydei hummed again sleepily, his voice still low and raspy as he slowly let himself wake up. “What… time… is it?”

Phainon sighed quietly, disappointed in himself when a pair of rosy eyes stared back at him, half-lidded and exhausted. “It’s after midnight. I’m sorry, master.”

“Did you have fun?” Mydei asked him while picking his elbows off the counter and straightening himself out in his seat. “Did your friend have fun?”

He was sweet.

Forget his misdemeanor, and forget that he was just woken up in the middle of the night. He wanted to know how he was tonight.

“I had a lot of fun. It was an… interesting night.”

A quiet groan then left his lips, and Phainon laughed quietly while watching him immediately reach to hold his back.

“Shut up…” Mydei grumbled as he pushed his shoulders back. “I should be sleeping in my bed…”

But he fell asleep waiting up on him, he knew. It didn't need to be said out loud to hang heavy in the air.

“Do you want me to rub your back?” He teased him, sliding his hand deeper beneath his tank-top to brush between his shoulder blades. “I’ll put you to bed with a massage.”

A low hum filled the quiet room, pleased by the feeling of him pressing his fingers down and rubbing. His head tilted back, eyes shutting in gentle bliss and drowsiness.

“Did… you eat enough tonight?”

“Yeah, I ate and drank plenty. Hysilens ordered us a ton of food, but I might have had a few more mocktails than I should have. Please don’t punish me for being so careless with my sugar intake,” he joked, and Mydei’s lip curled upwards with his own.

Clearly, he was feeling more playful than anything.

“You’re fine. It’s a single night, and you were out,” he reassured him. “Make sure you drink water before you lay down. Those aren’t hydrating.”

“I will,” he reassured him.

“Did you treat her tonight? Or did you guys split?” He wondered, rolling his head to the side. “I’m… mm… assuming you split…?

“Actually…” Mydei’s eyebrows furrowed upon hearing that. “The tab was on her wife’s card. She said they wanted to treat me, and… I wasn’t going to argue in front of so many people. She basically told me it’s rude to refuse a gift.”

“Oh.”

It was only one word, but Phainon could feel that something was off the moment it was spoken. His body didn’t feel any different as his shoulders weren’t tense and he didn’t notice his jaw flex, but his voice sounded stiff. It sounded displeased by the revelation.

“Is something wrong?”

“Stop touching me,” he murmured after another moment of quiet, and Phainon’s hand stilled mid-rub down his back. “Please take your hand off of me.”

He pulled back, watching as Mydei’s head straightened out and his hand went to wipe his eyes again. A sinking feeling filled his stomach as he watched his eyes open, squinting from the light but focused on him.

“You… let her wife pay for you?” He asked him as if he didn’t believe the words leaving his mouth. “You let another person’s dominant provide something for you that I could have given to you?”

“Did I do something wrong by accepting?”

Mydei was silent for another moment, then his head shook lightly. “No, you didn’t do anything wrong. That just surprised me.”

The stool lightly creaked as he stood up carefully, and Phainon looked down at the counter while chewing on his bottom lip. He thought about his reaction, about his fallen smile and the immediate denial of being touched when he had been previously enjoying it. He repeated his words, thumbing over their confusion and wondering what could possibly—

“Wait, how did you know that…?” He brought up unsurely, watching as Mydei grabbed his coffee cup. “I never told you Hysilens and her wife were…—”

“No, you didn’t,” he agreed. “I follow her blog online, and I was surprised you knew her and worked with her. It’s also why I really wanted you to go out with her tonight. She could be good for you and your confidence, Phainon.”

He didn’t know what to say to that.

Mydei was playing match maker with him, pushing him to be friends with her tonight so he could… what? Confide in her about what they did? He could barely talk to her after she pieced him together and saw the lock on his collar. In fact, he ran out on her and needed to be chased into the parking lot.

It was wishful thinking to hope he could ever confess about the things they did.

“I can reassure you, but maybe another submissive could make you feel more understood than I could,” he tried to explain to him.

Phainon wanted to say he didn’t care about what other people did like he always did, but… that would be lying now. He was curious. He was so curious how her experience was similar to or different from his own, especially in their daily lives.

Mydei’s style of dominance was what he knew, but what did she experience with her wife? Was it just like him—minus the marriage part?

“You were looking out for me in a way you thought was best, and I appreciate that. I had a really nice night because of that push," he settled on, and Mydei looked at him as if he didn’t expect to hear that from him. “But I would have appreciated you telling me that more though, Mydei. You didn’t need to hide that from me.”

“I should have said something to you,” he agreed quietly. “But understand that it wasn’t my business to tell you what she did in her own time. Just as it isn’t your business to tell anyone what you do in yours."

That was reasonable. He could understand why he didn’t tell him as that was how Mydei always was.

“But you still should have given me a head’s up,” he argued. “I tell you everything you need to know. I feel like I deserved to know that.”

“I know. I’m sorry, Phainon.”

A moment of silence passed between them, and Phainon’s hand reached slowly for his arm before leaning into his shoulder. He held him gently, fingers wrapping around his upper elbow as his nose turned in deeper to the cold bicep beside him. As he closed his eyes, another breath interrupted the silence.

“On the topic of sharing things with you… I wish you allowed me to pay for your night, not her,” he brought up. “I know we didn’t agree to you giving me that, but I’m a little disappointed in knowing someone else could do something for you that I was refused.”

“‘Disappointed’?” He repeated playfully, trying to shift the heaviness in the air. “Or jealous?”

He didn't even need to answer. It was the lack of response that said more than his words ever could.

“My master’s cute when he’s jealous,” Phainon teased him, and a scoff followed. “I won’t let her do it again. It was a one time thing, so don’t think too much about it, okay?”

“Good.”

One weighty hand dropped on top of his head, and he couldn't help his smile when it ruffled the ivory strands. They fanned over his face messily, slightly stiff from him meticulously styling it earlier in the night.

“I don’t want someone’s mistress looking after my prince.”

“I… told Hysilens about us too,” he added after, unable to open his eyes and meet Mydei’s in fear he’d be upset. “Well, I didn’t tell her about us. She saw the lock on my collar, and she put it together herself. She knows that I’m someone’s collared submissive now, just not whose.”

“Does she? How does that make you feel?” Mydei asked gently, turning his body so he was face first into his collar rather than his arm. “Are you okay?”

He shrugged weakly, pushing deeper into him as a pair of arms wrapped around his shoulders. “It’s really scary, and I feel really exposed when she looks at me, but… maybe you and her are right. Maybe it’ll be good for me, but I just won’t realize it until later.”

It could be similar to how he enjoyed exploring this now but was so sure he’d hate it when he first thought about it, or when he used to call him ‘master’ as a way to ridicule him but now he used it as a way to address him.

Maybe now it felt intimidating to be so open, but later he’ll look back and realize he needed this. He just needed to trust the judgement of people who knew more than him about it.

“She gave me her page. She said to look at it sometime if I can’t bring myself to talk to her directly about it. Will you… look at it with me sometime?” A tilt of hope laced his words, but it didn’t encompass the desperation he felt inside for him to agree. “I’m scared to look at these things online by myself. I don’t want to see the bad parts all over again.”

“An important thing to realize is that both sides can co-exist together, Phainon. There is no ‘good’ side or ‘bad’ side, just what’s ‘comfortable’ to you and what’s not,” he said softly. “You can be uncomfortable or repulsed with what some people practice and take part in, but that doesn't necessarily make it ‘bad’. They’re not bad people for wanting heavier plays or dynamics.”

He didn’t even consider the possibility.

“Is… her page heavy?” He forced himself to ask, unsure if he even wanted to know.

Could he stomach seeing Hysilens, someone he considered his friend now, in that same position of the girls he saw before? Would he be able to look at her the same if he somehow saw pictures or videos of her body in an explicit kind of way? Should he actually look at that page?

“Her mistress is much, much more strict than I am, and her punishments are heavier than the ones I deliver. Their dynamic has been sharpened and developed over years of trust, experimenting, and love,” he explained carefully. Phainon’s stomach dropped at what was, essentially, a warning. “You might read some entries of hers and get squeamish, but you might also find some things helpful. I don’t want you on it without me.”

“I won’t,” he promised, and Mydei rubbed his stiffened shoulders soothingly. “Can we go to bed? I’m really, really tired. The day has been physically and emotionally draining.”

On top of work and being up later than he has in a long time, it felt like his emotions were on a rollercoaster. He had been anxious and afraid. He had been jealous and upset. He had been so blissed out he couldn’t think, then so deep in his head that time completely escaped him.

Now, he just wanted to go to bed with Mydei cuddled up behind him, his fist on his neck and their heads on the same pillow.

“I need to clean up my mess, and you need to go change before we can prepare for bed,” he reminded him. “We have to be up early to work out, then we need to pack these cinnamon rolls up after breakfast.”

His eyebrows furrowed in confusion.

‘Package’?

“I told Cyrene you came over to help me make some sweets for everyone,” Mydei chuckled over his confused silence. “She sounded happy. So, I want to spend some time tomorrow handing them out to our friends. Don’t worry, you and her can have most of them, but only if you promise not to eat them all at once.”

Oh.

Mydei made that towering stack of cinnamon rolls a little funny looking to make it look done by his unskilled hand, and he did it to protect him from Cyrene’s interrogation of why he didn't come home after work. When he said he would take care of it for him, he actually did. He meant it.

Phainon’s chest fluttered as he looked down at his tank-top, but guilt pooled into his stomach the more he thought about it.

“You… lied?”

For him?

“If you package them, it’s not lying,” he reasoned. “I didn’t say what you did, just that you’re helping me. If you don’t correct their assumptions, it’s not lying. It’s protecting your business.”

He guessed that made sense. Mydei did that often with most things to keep his privacy, or maybe to avoid an unnecessary confrontation, but it still didn’t make him feel any better that he was still, essentially, lying.

“Go change. I’ll join you in a second,” Mydei said to him finally, patting his shoulder firmly to symbolize their hug was over. “Come on, prince.”

Phainon pulled away from him, and he let his fingers trace over the muscle on Mydei’s arm slowly. They lined from his bicep to his inner elbow, and he curled them gently when they met his outstretched hand. In doing so, their fingers linked together for a second, holding each other by the knuckles.

“I better have my pajamas ready and my things out, master,” he taunted him, referencing their usual routine.

Mydei always had his clothes tucked neatly away from him, and if he wasn’t tasked with grabbing them himself, his skin care was the same way. The bottles and tubes were left out to be easily grabbed by him, and it was his job to put them right where they belonged after he used them.

“Your things are where they always are, ready for you to use them.”

Their fingers broke apart when he took another step away from him, and while his arm dropped, Mydei’s own lingered for a moment. His fingers stayed bent at the knuckles, then curled into his palm before raising towards his chest.

"Don't take too long.” Phainon pointed at him, then turned around while feeling Mydei’s eyes on his retreating body.

“You forgot to drink water!” He called after him. “I’ll bring you some, but now you owe me two bottles before bed.”

“Yes, master!” He returned, laughing to himself over how protective he could be. It was cute. It was sweet.

With rules like that, why was he ever nervous of them again?
