“Phainon.”

He hummed, licking his fingers of sticky and sweet icing while plastic clicked lightly beside him. As Mydei gently and delicately closed the small packaging around a trio of cinnamon rolls, his elbow came poking into his ribs.

“Stop eating and start helping me.”

Phainon laughed, leaning into his shoulder. “But, master, they’re so yummy.”

Mydei shook his head, snipping a strip of red ribbon before tying it around the small, black tray. His fingers carefully lined the box, keeping the decoration straight and pretty. Around a nice little bow, he knotted a name tag’s glittering gold string. With a click of his pen, he carefully and swiftly wrote the name ‘Castorice’ in a beautiful, practiced cursive. At the end, he drew a couple of butterflies.

A proud smile lit up his face as he examined the tray, and he set it off to the side before looking at the one he was meant to do—the one meant for him and Cyrene.

“She’ll definitely be able to tell you did it.”

“Hey!”

It was true, but he could have been nicer about it. Maybe his didn’t look as polished as his, but the ribbons were still pretty and his penmanship wasn’t terrible. He even drew a little flower in the corner for her!

What flower was it? He didn’t know. This ‘flower’ was essentially just a bunch of oddly shaped circles grouped around each other, but it was close enough to resemble one. Maybe.

Possibly.

It had character, and that had to count for something, right?

“I told you to stop,” Mydei scolded him, watching when he dragged his finger across the messy glass dish. “Get your damn finger out of your mouth.”

“Why? Does my master wanna put his in there instead?” Phainon teased, and Mydei also watched when he popped his clean finger inside his mouth to clean it off.

Those hot, amber eyes raked over his face, focusing on his shining lips before meeting his playful wink.

“You’re asking for it.”

“No, ‘asking for it’ would sound like this.” He then cleared his throat. “Can you please put your fingers in my mouth, master?”

Mydei made two movements, both swift and firm. One hand cupped his jaw, fingertips pinching into either cheek to hold him still. His other hand dragged two fingers through what was left on the dish, then planted them right against his steady tongue.

“Work.”

Ivory eyebrows furrowed as he looked at him, unsure what that meant.

“Wash your hands, and work,” Mydei repeated, nodding towards the sink right beside him. “No one wants dirty fingers on their gift. Go on. Wash your hands.”

He pushed his fingers deeper with his command. They hooked over his tongue and settled heavily against it, giving him no room to talk back.

Phainon reached for the sink, dropped a pearl of soap into his palm and lathered them until Mydei told him to stop. He scrubbed his hands and cleaned beneath his nails until the other man said it was enough.

“Dry them.”

He swallowed the best he could, spit pooling in his mouth as he picked a hand towel up.

“Good,” he encouraged him. “You can listen. You simply choose not to.”

A twitch sent his lip upwards, but the flex of a grin made Mydei dig his fingers deeper. He repositioned himself behind him, moving out of the way but not removing his presence or power altogether. Those fingers pressed to the back of his tongue, teasing his body’s limits.

“Package Cifera’s,” he instructed him. “You know she’s the hardest critique. She’ll point out the icing on the lid, the mismatched size, and whether or not the bow is straight. Make it pretty.”

Of course he would leave the most vocal of their friends to him…

Phainon looked down at the counter, and he grabbed the black bottom to the plastic tray before picking up the sticky tongs. Of the laid out rolls, he picked three of the same relative size, then tried to fit them inside nicely without smashing them. Icing dripped over the edges of the tray, and he stared at the mess.

“Clean it without sticking your fingers in your mouth, unless you think there’s some room beside mine,” Mydei taunted him, speaking directly into his ear.

A spark of arousal popped inside of his stomach, and he quickly ripped a napkin before gently and carefully cleaning up the edges. Once clean, he fit the lid on slowly, trying not to let it touch the tops and smear. They needed to be pretty. The cover needed to stay clean and transparent so as to admire the treats inside.

But then Mydei pushed deeper, and his hands slipped, smashing the top into one and smearing icing all over it.

“Oh,” he feigned in mock disappointment. “Try again. Clean it off, then put it on.”

Phainon choked. Heat pooled inside of his cheeks, and one hand grappled around Mydei’s wrist before pulling weakly. Not that it budged.

“You’re supposed to be assisting me. Come on, my little helper,” he urged. “Stop trying to fight me. Relax.”

Upon being told to, he dropped his hold on his wrist. Shaking fingers grabbed the lid and rinsed it underneath the sink, drying it off with a towel before shaking it to air dry it the rest of the way. A flex of his knuckles made him choke again, but Mydei only shushed him gently.

“You asked for this. You buckled down, opened your mouth, and asked me to do this,” he taunted him, and how could he argue? He did do that. “I’m beginning to think my naughty prince loves having his mouth filled with the way he drops this jaw so freely.”

Phainon hesitated, then nodded weakly.

“If you mess up again, I’m going deeper,” he warned him while gently sliding them out to relieve the pressure. “Package them, Phainon. Do the task I assigned you with—properly.”

Once again, he took the lid and gently rested it on top. Two fingers pinched it closed all the way around, securing them within the tray.

“Halfway done. Cut the ribbon.”

Mydei eased his fingers back more. He stilled them and steadied himself as Phainon took the ribbon, measured it around the box, and then snipped off the right length. As he tied the bow, a mouth pressed against the back of his neck towards the left. Judging by the press of metal into his body, he assumed that was directly over the lock of his collar.

“Even out the tails,” he nitpicked, using his other hand to point out how one was longer than the other. “Good boy. Write her name on a card now, nice and pretty.”

He took the pen, raised it to write their friend’s name on it as neatly as possible, and then tied the string around the bow. With it finished, he placed it beside the other box meant for Castorice, then raised the pen woven between his fingers higher. Its butt clicked to Mydei’s hand once, twice, then three times before dropping it, and he felt them slip deeper over the signal.

“You did good,” Mydei praised him, and he slipped his fingers around his wrist again when he choked. “That one’s much prettier than the one you’re taking home.”

Phainon’s eyes shut as he leaned back into his body. Breathing heavily, he guided the tips of Mydei’s fingers deeper by pushing his hand, allowing them to pass what he was comfortable with.

“Easy,” he whispered, stilling his hand as his throat tightened and eyes watered.

When he flexed them with a curl, the sound of his muffled gag filled the room, and his hand gripped his wrist tighter. There wasn’t another movement after, just the weight and pressure of his touch mixed with anticipation.

“Two more. Give me two more and we’ll be done.”

He nodded weakly, spit rolling down his bottom lip and eyes full of water. The slots between Mydei’s fingers pushed to the corners of his mouth, and he flexed them again to tickle his gag reflex again. As he did, Phainon’s shoulders raised and his chest lurched.

“Shh… You’ve got it.”

They were held there, forcing him to take them even after he gagged. It left him on the edge, slightly panicked as his throat flexed repeatedly.

He could feel it. He could feel himself silently gagging, his body buckling and trembling underneath the presence of his too-deep fingers. More heat ticked his face. More tears filled his eyes.

Shaking fingers rubbed over his wrist, the index and middle lifting high so he could see them both.

“One,” Mydei said, speaking firmly. “One more, and you’re done. You can do it for me.”

Phainon felt them slide down his tongue, tucking as deep as possible again to drag another gag from him. This one came with sticky, copious amounts of spit, and it spilled down his chin messily. It also caused his fingers to curl, desperate to claw at his hand and peel it away before they made an even bigger mess. But it was his only job to keep this safety signal up.

He just didn’t want to throw up. He didn’t want to throw up. He didn’t want to—

Soon, just as he was going to drop one of his fingers, they reeled back slowly, and he gasped loudly through his opened mouth after forcing down the pool of his saliva. Swallow by swallow, he gulped the air down to try and soothe the tickle in his throat from having something so deep in there.

Those two fingers were pulled free completely. Drenched down to the bone, he held them out for him to see, to look at how the wrinkled skin was connected by ropes of saliva. Even when he scissored them apart, there were translucent strings stretching wide between them.

“We’re done here,” Mydei said with an air of finality. With it, he balled his fist and headed towards the sink in an attempt not to drip his spit everywhere.

That… was it?

Mydei wasn't going to touch his body? He wasn’t going to make him do the same?

All he wanted to do was stick his fingers in his mouth and mess with him? Rile him up and then just… what? Leave him like this? Like a mess?

He exhaled deeply, watching him wash his hands before he grabbed the nearby towel. When he did, he looked over to him and beckoned him closer with the sopping wet fingers that were in his throat less than a minute ago.

Phainon walked towards him anyway.

“Messy boy,” he murmured, taking the towel to wipe his slick chin.

“You’re not… gonna make me suck you off for being bratty?” He rasped out, still trying to catch his breath, and Mydei shook his head. “You won’t do it for me either?”

“No.” The answer was so short, so clean cut and simple that it was obvious whatever happened wouldn’t be continued. “But if you keep doing that, I’m going to give you less enjoyable things to fill your mouth with.”

He hummed quietly, then closed one eye when the towel dipped beneath it. “One of your gags, right?”

“Yes,” he said, leaving no room for doubt. “I feel like you enjoy talking back too much. Maybe some time tasting rubber will teach you how to be more reserved.”

“But my master likes when I’m bratty,” he accused him, and Mydei lifted an eyebrow as he went to wipe his other eye. He quickly switched which one was close to accommodate.

“I like that you feel as though you can have fun with me,” he corrected. “I enjoy seeing you enjoy what we do together, so much so that you’re not scared of being punished by me. It brings me comfort that I’m not forcing you to like this or behave a certain way."

Phainon nodded, but he knew there was something else coming.

“However, had you been more experienced in this and more confident in your interests, I would not allow you to be this mouthy,” he told him while holding his jaw again. “Sometimes you make me feel like a pushover because I’m not used to being this forgiving.”

“What would you do otherwise…?”

Mydei’s hand squeezed his jaw tighter. The juncture between his thumb and index finger pressed beneath his bottom lip, and his fingers climbed to sprawl across his heated cheek. Slowly, they raised until just his thumb was touching his skin, then they dropped with a light and painless tap.

A breath caught in his throat over the implication.

“I won’t,” he promised, holding his face again. “You are safe, and I won’t hurt you. But if you make me feel like a pushover, I’m going to push you back. Harder.”

He held his gaze as Mydei loosened his grasp, nodding softly. “Yes, master,” he forced himself to say.

“Clean this mess up, and keep your fingers out of your fucking mouth before I stick a gag in it,” he demanded, keeping his voice quiet but firm. “Whatever’s left from the batch can be tucked into a tupperware and put in the refrigerator. I’ll eat it myself throughout the week.”

His eyes darted down to the front of his sweatpants, then back up at Mydei who didn’t seem concerned at all.

“I won’t repeat myself,” he warned him, tapping his fingers to his cheek lightly again. “I’m going to text our friends and see who’s home so I can drop them off. When you finish up here, shower. Make it cold if you need to because I’m not touching you even if you get on your knees and beg. Got it?”

“Yeah. I-I got it.”

He walked off, and Phainon took a deep breath before looking at the last two cinnamon rolls left. They were smaller than the rest, had the least amount of icing, and had been at the very top of the tower if his memory served him correctly.

His eyes darted to the large tray packed with his and Cyrene’s, and he carefully unraveled the packaging he did before swapping them out. After all, Mydei spent so much time baking these. It wouldn’t be fair for him to get the least appetizing ones of the bunch.

This time, he carefully tied it up like he had Cifera’s, making the ribbon pretty and writing his best friend’s name just as neatly. It was placed beside the rest of the boxes, and he took the glass dish before setting it in the sink.

As he looked down once again, his feet shifted.

Mydei said he wasn’t, but he could be so mean sometimes. Leaving him pent up like this was just cruel.

—

If he was being honest, he didn’t have to accompany Mydei to deliver the treats. That wasn’t necessary in ‘helping’ him, and he knew if he turned the offer down then there wouldn’t be any hard feelings. But he wanted to see his friends real quick, and he didn’t mind tagging along after dropping his car and tray off at his apartment.

Cyrene wasn’t there, but that was fine by him. She said she was with Castorice going shopping for a little ‘date’ before they hung out with Hyacine, that she might stay over and spend the night for a little bit of extra ‘girl time’, and he understood that. If he wanted his own space to be with Mydei, then it was only reasonable that she needed her space with the girls.

The only one to be home at the time was Cifera, and that meant the giant wooden door they were standing outside was hers. Well, her older sister, Aglaea’s, but what belonged to Aglaea belonged to her too. That was how they worked.

Holding the plastic tray he had packaged himself, Phainon smiled brightly at his friend when she opened the door. Her hair was a mess, the clothes she wore were crinkled up with a slightly stretched collar, there was a slight darkness beneath her tired eyes that he wasn’t used to seeing, and she looked surprised to see him, but that melted away quickly.

“Well… Goldilocks said he’d be comin’ with treats, but I didn’t expect him to bring company,” her mocking voice purred, looking up between him and Mydei. “What? Feelin’ like a couple of strangers? Come in already! It’s hot out here.”

That tone didn’t quite meet her tired eyes, and his smile faltered over the sight.

“Thank you.” Mydei nodded, planting a hand on the small of his back as a gesture at him to walk first. “Aglaea isn’t here, right?”

“Big sis’ is out God knows where for the next few weeks.” She waved carelessly, then readjusted her shirt. “Make yourselves at home. Or don’t. I don’t reckon you're stayin’ long, are ya’?”

Phainon followed her towards the kitchen as he chuckled, hearing the front door close and lock behind Mydei. It was odd hearing their shoes against the tiled floors as he was so used to taking them off at this point.

“Awh, are you kicking us out so soon? I thought we were friends,” he pouted, and she giggled.

“I’m just here for the goods, whatever else you need to talk about can hit the curb.” She flashed a toothy grin at them before holding her hand out. “Mm… Thank you, kid. My sweet tooth appreciates it.”

“Don’t eat them all at once,” he warned her.

“And what’re ya’ gonna do? Tattle to Aglaea on me? Don’t be so immature,” she mused. “When did you start tellin’ people what to do?”

“I don’t, but it’s not good to eat so much sweets at once,” he insisted. “Your teeth won’t come back if you rot them with sugar, Cifera.”

“My teeth are fine, thank you very much!” She hissed. But even with the sharp words, she licked over her top teeth slowly before rolling her eyes. “Tch. You’re just like she is— condescending. I’m not a child.”

“I’m only looking out for you,” Phainon said back. “De? Help me out here.”

He hummed, then looked between them both as if he had zoned out while looking at her. “When was the last time you saw a dentist?” He asked.

“Oh how I hate when you two muscleheads get your last little brain cells together to form an impenetrable wall of lame,” she grumbled, then looked down at the box in her hands. “Hey… these are kinda ugly this time. What gives?”

Mydei snorted quietly from behind him, and Phainon felt his lips wobble as she rotated the tray and examined them. With one eye shut and the other wide open, it was as if she were searching for clues in a murder scene, not flaws inside of baked goods.

An elbow poked into his side, and he jumped before shooting a look over at Mydei, who had his hand over his mouth. With a subtle nod towards their friend, he could hear the words loud and clear even if they were unspoken.

‘I told you so.’

“This one is caved in on the edge like you dropped something on it! And that one is smaller than the other ones! Oh, and the writing is different from usual—this doesn’t look refined at all! Finally, goldilocks always puts a sneaky little cat face on mine, but I don’t see that either,” she pointed out, just as Mydei said she would. “This ain’t the work of my usual baker, so spill. Did you tamper with it, snowy?”

Phainon turned to face her, watching as her eyes narrowed skeptically at him.

“I tried my best in helping him,” he settled with, not wanting to get too in depth about it. Specifically, he didn’t want to think too much about how he helped him this morning. “They taste good though. There was meant to be four in there, but…—”

“Hey!”

He laughed as she pointed one sharpened nail at him, slowly walking up as if to be menacing. But between her being eye-level with his chest and the childish pout on her lips, he couldn’t find it in himself to be intimidated. Especially when she was slowly starting to grin up at him the longer she tried to hold that pose.

“You’re fired,” she said to him, and he lifted one hand to flick against her forehead lightly. “First, you come into my home and bully me. Now, you take my desserts and deprive me of my little cat face doodles. What are you taking from me next, kid?”

“What do you have left to take?” He asked, and she pushed his chest before turning away from him.

“Did’ja have to get a pet dog, goldilocks?” Cifera taunted, looking behind him with a pointed look. “What? Are ya’ scared of a lil’ cat now?”

“I don’t have a pet,” he said simply, shortly. An edge lined his voice, and it was one Phainon knew well. “Do you like the gift or not? He tried his best.”

Phainon really did try, but truthfully, it was a little bit difficult to make things look perfect when he had two fingers ticking his gag reflex the whole time.

It wasn’t as if he could just say that, though…

She laughed, the sound light and airy. “Don’t get your lil’ red panties in a twist, kitten. You may eat with your eyes too, but my tastebuds will surely love it anyway. Thank you two muscleheads for the goods, but don’t forget my cat face next time, ‘kay? It’s the little things.”

He nodded silently, storing that in his memory for next time.

Mydei hummed, pleased by the show of gratitude. “Had Aglaea been here, I would have brought more.”

“Please, that woman doesn’t eat junk like this,” she scoffed. “The fashion industry is a killer. She’d barely take a bite! Guess that’s what I’m here for though, to finish up what she can’t and give her a little mouse-y nibble of things. Oh well.”

“So I’ve heard,” Mydei agreed. “I wouldn't want to be tangled up in that business.”

“Being reduced down to your body ain’t for the weak.” Cifera sighed deeply after that. “But, Aglaea’s never been one to back down from a challenge. She’s gotta keep a sharp eye to deal with that kinda pressure, but I worry sometimes about her gettin’ lost in it all. Those fancy camera lights can be real blindin’, ya’ know.”

“She has you in her corner,” Mydei reminded her. “I’m sure that motivates her plenty to get through her day.”

Cifera smiled wide at that, one of sincerity rather than mockery. Her eyes glittered brightly too, like she was glad to have her efforts acknowledged by someone else.

“Yeah, huh?” She said thoughtfully. “Heh. See? This is why you’re my favorite behind princess homebody and pinky-pie. You sure know how to make a girl feel good about herself, don’t’cha?”

Phainon then pouted. “What about me?”

“You’re after him,” she said, moving her finger to motion him being behind Mydei in her list. “But you’re there. Promise.”

“I’m last!”

“Oh, the specifics! Who really cares about those?” She waved her hand after. “You know I love ya’, snowy. Don’t make me spell it out for ya’.”

“Yeah yeah,” he sulked, dropping his shoulders and rolling his eyes. “Love you too…”

“D’ya want some water?”

“I’m okay.”

“Please,” Mydei requested, and she pulled the fridge open before tossing him a bottle. “Thank you.”

“Where are you two headed after this?” She wondered. “Pinky-pie is out with the princess, so they’re not home. Don’t tell me you two are gonna loiter around here until then. Ya’ know how long they take and how bad I am at entertainin’. What do I look like? A circus lion?”

“Glorified house cat,” Phainon corrected her, and she pointed a warning finger at him while using the other to unravel the bow on her gift.

“Can it, dog. No one asked you.”

His lip curled into a grin over the sassy remark, and she laughed before looking down to pop the tray open.

“Got a taste for somethin’ sweet?” She offered them both. “I’m askin’ to be nice, by the way. Say ‘no’ for me.”

“For you?” He asked, pointing at her before looking at Mydei as if he heard the same thing. “For her? After she keeps calling me a ‘dog’?”

He shrugged, keeping a neutral expression as he cracked his bottle of water open.

“You know what? Give me half—”

“Oh, come on! Don’t you have a green smoothie to gulp down?” She groaned, and he rolled his eyes.

“Actually, I had fresh pressed juice,” he said proudly, ignoring her deadpan expression. “It was ginger flavored because ginger helps with your metabolism.”

Her lip curled upwards as she ripped a piece of cinnamon roll off and placed it in her mouth. “Oh, yeah…” Cifera dragged out as she chewed slowly. “That sounds so delicious… You must be so satisfied with yourself…”

Mydei chuckled lightly. “Don’t mind this fool. He has his own at home.”

Phainon gasped in betrayal over him siding with her, then jumped again when he felt the toe of his ankle boot tap his leg. It wasn’t rough, nor was it loud, but it was sudden. He didn’t expect it.

“You good?” Cifera asked, eyeing him. “What? Upset goldilocks prefers cats over dogs?”

“Hardly,” he protested. “Mydei likes both cats and dogs.”

Mydei liked cats over dogs. He liked that they were independent, that they came and went as they pleased. If they wanted attention, they’d come. If they wanted to be left alone, they’d walk away. He liked that they cleaned themselves, used the bathroom by themselves, and they could be happy just sitting in a warm spot by the window.

Phainon knew that. But he wasn't going to give her the satisfaction of winning this argument.

“Someone’s in de-ni-al,” she sang, amused.

“Someone thinks she knows my best friend better than me,” he mouthed off.

“Mydei likes quiet,” the man in question huffed, and they both turned to look at him. “That being said, I believe it’s time we take our leave.”

Phainon nodded, and Mydei walked around the counter before reaching his hand out.

“One more bottle of water, please. For the road.”

Cifera walked over to the refrigerator, grabbed another, and then handed it to him as he thanked her. Both bottles were then shifted over to one stretched hand.

“Thanks for the treats, Mydei,” she said after, raising two fingers to her forehead before saluting him casually. “Me and my stomach will be here when you decide to visit again. Try not to make it so soon. I don’t like visitors.”

He nodded, and Phainon watched him plant his hand on top of her head before ruffling her already messy hair. The ashy locks fanned over her forehead, causing one eye to shut while looking up at him.

“Be good while Aglaea’s gone, or you won’t be getting any treats the next time I make them.”

Her jaw dropped.

“Well… I suppose I could be a little nicer to snowy…” She caved, flicking her gaze over to him briefly before looking back up at Mydei. “Let’s not be rash, now…”

“No. I mean brush your hair,” he scolded her, and she winced. “And brush your teeth. Every morning. Every night. If you don’t, Aglaea will be very disappointed when she finds out you’ve been neglecting yourself again.”

Phainon’s head tilted as he watched them, unaware they were that close to one another.

It was sweet though, like watching an older brother with his younger sister when their parents weren’t around. Not that she was younger than them, but she definitely behaved more youthfully than Mydei did. Most people did, though.

“Yeah yeah…”

Mydei pulled away, and she turned her head before looking away from them both.

“And schedule a dentist appointment, Cifera.”

“Tch. Scram before I kick you out,” she hissed, pushing him weakly away from her. “I’m fine, got it? It ain’t time for one yet anyway, so stop naggin’ me.”

“Good,” he said before turning around. “Phainon, please hold this for me.”

He took the unopened bottle, then followed him towards the front door. As he did so, he watched the way he peeked into the living room briefly before looking away, almost like he wanted to check on something.

“Don’t let the door hit you!” She called after them, and Phainon glanced over his shoulder to see her arms crossed over her chest. “Especially you, dog.”

He laughed, and Mydei held the door open for him to walk through first—as he always did.

“I’ll see you around. If you’re free sometime, let’s get you out of the house,” he said after.

“I’m never free. You’ll have to plan up somethin’ real fun to get me to go out with you two buzzkills,” she scoffed, but a smile was on her lips anyway. “Buh-bye now!”

The door shut behind them quickly, and Mydei took a deep breath as they made their way to his car.

“You two are close,” he noticed, earning a nod in return. “It’s pretty cute. You talk to her like some kind of older brother.”

“That girl acts like she’s got it all figured out, that no one needs to worry about her, but it’s obviously a front,” he scoffed quietly. “Simply waiting for someone to reach out isn't enough. Sometimes you need to check in yourself.”

Phainon never really noticed. In his memory, she’s always that same kind of energetic and playful. No matter what occasion, she was loud, mocking, and quick to chase someone around or jump on their back. His back was victim to it plenty of times as he was supposedly ‘more fun to surprise’. By her standards, he was the most fun to bully.

He never really looked at her beneath her makeup or their friend group, but he guessed those were things Mydei saw when he dropped by randomly to give desserts away. Those bags beneath her eyes and the messy state she was in at home, that was something he never really thought could be hiding behind someone like her.

“You think a lot of other people.”

“A good friend does,” he brushed off casually.

Phainon grabbed his arm gently, and Mydei stopped to look at him as they stood in front of his car. When his grip tightened, one golden eyebrow raised as if to warn him of his next move.

“Be honest. Do you do this so you have a reason to check up on everyone individually?” He wondered, and Mydei nodded curtly. No other words needed to be said.

It wasn’t just ‘leftovers’ that he couldn’t finish. It wasn’t just ‘my submissive misbehaved, take his treat’ to dump on them.

This was calculated. Mydei did these visits for a reason, only he didn’t tell anyone why. If he did, he would have been the first to be told.

His eyes raked over Mydei’s face, over his slowly relaxing expression and the sunlight beating over his fluffed bangs. It bathed him in warm, summer gold, in a brightness that he knew was there but had never really seen before. Not in its entirety, anyway.

Mydei really was good at taking care of people, wasn’t he?

“Cifera’s always been a… ‘fake it until you make it’ kind of person. As you can see, she tries very hard,” he decided to share, even if he wasn’t one to speak on other people’s business. “Sometimes she doesn't see the point in anything, especially in simple things like brushing her teeth or changing her clothes. Aglaea takes care of her, but when she’s gone, I like to give her a little push. That’s all.”

Phainon thought back to his rules, to Mydei mentioning that if he was ever too tired, too sick, or just flat out didn't see the point in taking care of himself, he would step in. He would tackle any problem with him, from dish washing and laundry to reminding him to brush his teeth or wash his hair. As long as it was done, that was all that mattered to him, since living in filth was not a healthy way for anyone to live.

If he wasn’t feeling up to bathing, he had no doubt that Mydei would dump him into a tub and wash him down himself. Especially now that he’s seen him pretty much naked.

Maybe he wouldn’t do that for her. That was a line he wouldn’t dare cross for someone else not inside of his bed. But he also knew if it was that bad for one of their friends, he’d probably push them in the bathroom and guard the door until he heard the shower running from the other side. Because that was just who he was.

Mydei was so full of love and care that it burst from him in every way, and he showed it to everyone—stray cats, strangers on the internet, his close friends, and even his father, as he still pushed himself to be the man he needed to one day accept his company. He could ‘complain’ until his face was cherry red, or he could act as unbothered as he wanted, but it was obvious that he did nothing but care. He did nothing but try.

While staring at his still face lit up beneath the sun, Phainon’s stomach lightly fluttered. It was airy and gentle in a way he wasn’t quite used to, and sudden.

Anxiety was common as he slowly opened himself up completely to him. Arousal was new, but it was slowly becoming just as normal the deeper they dove into their dynamic. Admiration had lived inside of him since they met and Mydei was the only person who could run their high school mile just as fast as him.

But this felt… different… from all three of those.

It was lighter than that old competitive gaze he set over him, innocent in a way that their lust wasn’t, and not nearly as scary as his nerves could be. In fact, it felt warm.

His stomach was full of that same sun-kissed warmth as he slowly discovered more about the man he thought he knew.

“Phainon, are you okay?” Mydei asked him, setting the back of his hand over his forehead. Afterwards, he touched his cheek. “Mm… your face is hot.”

Was it? He couldn't tell.

He had grown so used to being flustered and nervous that his body just felt hot all the time at this point. Like a perpetual flame burned inside of his body.

That was all it was, right? A flame. A spark. He was flustered as he always was, and there was nothing deeper to it than that.

“I’m fine,” he murmured. “I should… uh… call Cyrene and tell the girls to meet us at Cassie’s. We can drop her tray off then head back to mine.”

“Is that what you want?”

“Yes please, master,” he agreed quietly and politely, making Mydei softly smile. “I want to spend another night with you. If she’s going to be with Cassie, then who cares if you’re with me?”

“I have to visit my mother tomorrow morning around ten. I promised to take her to her doctor's appointment, then pick some groceries up with her,” Mydei brought up, and Phainon nodded understandingly. “But we can have another repeat of feeding those cats and going on a run. I’d like that a lot too.”

“Do you like the fat orange one?”

“I love him,” he said. At that, he laughed while remembering the two together. “I want to see him again. What if he’s starving to death without us there?”

Phainon highly doubted that, as they stayed by that bush and that family’s apartment for a reason, but he let his worry linger. He cared, and that was all that mattered.

“Let’s go then. The faster we finish this up, the faster you can see him,” he reminded him.

Mydei nodded, pulling his hand away to reach for his keys. As he did so, Phainon cracked open the water bottle in his hand.

“I didn’t even need to tell you to drink it. You just knew it was yours,” he said, watching him gulp down the still-cool water. “Good boy.”

Plastic crunched underneath his fist from the praise, and he looked over to him one last time as a breath fell from his lips. With it, a few droplets of water followed.

The back of Mydei’s knuckle wiped under his lip, then he silently nodded towards his car for him to get in. Without so much as a word, Phainon followed, allowing him to open his door and shut it for him.

—

Both he and Mydei sat in his car while waiting for the girls to show up. With the engine off, they spent their few minutes of their downtime talking about what they planned to do when they finished up here. Dinner plans, lounging plans, and things alike were tossed back and forth between them, giving him a choice even if the decision ultimately landed on Mydei’s shoulders.

But he liked that. It was nice.

He didn’t need to worry about what to buy for dinner unless Mydei wasn’t there, and getting to share it with him was always a treat.

When Castorice and Cyrene finally made it, Mydei was quick to offer his arms to carry Castorice’s shopping bags. He did too, but Cyrene only looked at him before throwing them over her shoulder. As she lifted her nose, he grumbled playfully.

“I’m trying to help.”

“I don’t need your help. You left me all alone,” she told him, and he rolled his eyes before following her to the front door. “You know what I need instead? A sweet treat! We skipped out on one to come here since Mydei said he was bringing some!”

“These aren’t for you,” he hushed, following her through the front door while yanking the tray away from her. “Ours are at home, and you can have whatever’s left tomorrow when you come back.”

Cyrene whined loudly at that, and he tapped her head with the tray before turning to face his other friend.

“Cassie, these are for you.” Phainon emphasized his words by holding it out for her to take. “Please enjoy them.”

She smiled, taking the gift before smiling sweetly up at him. “Thank you so much. Would you guys like to share them with me? I can’t possibly eat them all by myself.”

“No thank you,” Mydei denied. “I have some at home.”

“Yeah, I have a few at the house calling my name,” he chuckled, then felt as two hands held on to his arm. A quick glance revealed a head of pink hair, and he let her lean her head into his shoulder.

“We can’t stay for long. Hyacine finally has a night off from the hospital and us three are going to hang out,” Castorice said happily. “It’s been so long since I got to see her in person.”

“Tell her we said ‘hello’,” Mydei spoke when he joined them, having just gotten back from placing the shopping bags neatly by the coffee table.

In his right arm was a small gray cat, and he had his left hand outstretched so she could claw and bite at his wiggling fingers. Though he kept his eyes on them, he continued playing with Castorice’s pet absentmindedly.

“Why not invite Cifera?” Phainon asked after, and Cyrene’s shoulders sunk over the mention. “I don’t believe she’s up to anything today. Save her from sleeping and playing video games all day.

“She hasn’t texted me back! But, watch, I bet she will at some obscure hour when it’s too late,” she told them, then quieted down slightly. “Should we just drop by and pick her up? No warning?”

“Warn her first,” he decided, then reached his opposite hand around to cup over her mouth. “Cassie, you should text her and tell her that you wanna take her out. I’m sure she’ll enjoy being surrounded by her friends.”

She nodded curtly in response. “Very well. I will send her many texts. So many that she can’t possibly sleep through them all.”

“Good idea,” Mydei agreed.

One smaller hand pried his off of Cyrene’s mouth, and she huffed as he laughed. “This is why you’re not allowed to join. All you do is bully people,” she accused him.

“I’m also not a girl. You can’t have a girl’s night with a guy hanging around,” he reminded her. That caused her eyes to roll. “However, the next time we can all get our schedules aligned, I have someone I’d like you both to meet. She’s sweet. Maybe a little bit timid, but I promise she’s very kind.”

That made both girls gasp, eyes wide as they looked up at him.

“Oh, Phainon… Is it your girlfriend?” Castorice’s voice held an edge of excitement to it. “Do you have one already? We haven’t even seen what she looks like!”

His stomach dropped.

“And you never told me?” Cyrene’s fist punched into his upper arm lightly. “Is it your coworker? The one you said you’ve become friends with? Phainon, it’s so soon!”

“No! No, no, no! You’ve got it all wrong!"

Mydei watched, a slight grin on his face while watching him fumble over his words and wave his hands frantically. Soft growls rumbled from the cat gnawing on his fingers, but her green eyes were on him as if she were also trying to find out if he had a girlfriend or not.

“Is she pretty?” Cyrene asked. “I wanna see! Show me!”

“There’s no need to be nervous,” Castorice tried to reassure him. “It’s… really refreshing to see a guy act this shyly, though. When you read romance novels, the men tend to act indifferent and suave. Sometimes I forget guys can be cute too. Phainon, your flustered reaction is quite cute.”

Phanon groaned quietly, feeling as if someone was watching him. “What I’m trying to say is that she has a wife! What makes you think I’m seeing someone?”

Her gentle, amethyst eyes raked over his outfit, lingering on his neck before dropping.

“Not only did what you sound as if you were announcing a secret partner, but you dress like you have one,” she reasoned with him. Now standing beside her, Cyrene also looked at his clothes with one hand holding her chin. “You have that… touch. You’re wearing jewelry suddenly, and you carry yourself with a higher regard. Guys with girlfriends always tend to act more confidently, and they look better taken care of too. They have someone to show off to.”

“Perhaps he discovered what matching colors could do for a person’s look,” Mydei added, noticing the way he froze underneath their analytical gazes. “I also gave him a new facial cleanser and moisturizer. Has he been using it, Cyrene? You see him most.”

Did she?

At this point, did his own roommate really see him more than Mydei did?

“Yeah! We both have,” she beamed, obviously not thinking as much as he was about that. Maybe to her, she was still the person closest to him. “It’s pretty nice. That could be where the ‘touch’ is coming from, Cassie. You know how much a person’s skin can change how they look and feel about themselves.”

“Maybe,” she agreed, and he exhaled quietly as Cyrene looked away from him. “Your necklace is very pretty, by the way. The blue really matches your eyes.”

One finger reached to touch the chain, and Phainon touched the diamond shaped gem before pressing over its pointed face. He remembered seeing it glisten in the golden sunlight, and he remembered the light reflecting off of it under the bar lights in his selfies.

It did match his eyes nicely.

“Thank you, Cassie.” She only nodded kindly in return. “And, for the record, I’m not in some secret relationship. I’ve just been… experimenting with some things.”

That wasn’t technically a lie, but he knew it also wasn’t the full truth either.

“Maybe this will work. You know, I’ve been trying to help this guy get a date forever,” Cyrene dragged out, holding on to Castorice while leaning into her. “But he’s so picky. He needs a golden somebody to descend from the sky—guy, girl, both, neither, whatever. They need to be bathed in sunlight and holier than thou to catch his eye.”

Her exaggeration made him curl into himself, just a little insecure.

“Someone kind and respectful who likes to talk about more than themselves is good enough for me, okay?” He mouthed off.

“You’re asking for so much in this day and age!”

“I don’t think that’s unreasonable,” Castorice sided with him, and he thanked her for her solidarity in this. “People become much more attractive when you enjoy their personality too. Just as people become less attractive when you don’t. What are good looks worth without a kind heart behind them?”

Thank you.

Phainon could grab her by the face and kiss her forehead for being one of the few people to understand why he wasn’t into hooking up. It wasn’t enough to be attractive. It wasn’t enough to simply make him turn his head.

She got that, and it made him feel better about himself.

“At this rate, we’ll be best friends who get married because they've been single too long and gave up. Mom would like that,” Cyrene sniffled dramatically, and his eyebrows furrowed while glancing over at her.

Cyrene liked girls, and he loved her deeply, just not like that.

She was always there in his life. Even if she liked to come and go from his apartment to run around, gather inspiration, then work on her books, he could count on her. If not a door away, she was always a call or text away, and he knew she’d come if he ever needed her badly enough. The same could be said about him too. He’d run to her without question if she needed him.

They grew up together as children, split when his family moved to the city, and he opened his door for her when she came to live with him to go to college. She was family. Not in the way a wife was with her husband, but in the way a sister was to her brother—free to hold if times got tough, to leave without remorse, to find what she wanted in the world, then to come back like they were never apart to begin with.

What did she mean her mom wanted them together in any other way?

“My mom was asking if you asked me out yet when I visited,” she confessed to him in front of their two closest friends. “A boy and a girl are best friends growing up together then move in together as adults… it’s romantic. She thought we were already dating for years now. She asked me when her grandchildren are coming to see her.”

Oh.

Grandchildren, huh?

Not once has he ever seriously contemplated dating her. Besides a random joke here or there, or a stray thought that felt more intrusive than ever while growing up, it never really crossed his mind. Not in anyway that could leave up to grandchildren.

Castorice also looked down at her, one hand holding the one on her arm. “You don’t like guys,” she said as if they all didn’t know that.

“I know. Phainon knows. But she doesn’t know that! I’m scared it’ll break my mom’s heart. She’s fragile, you know.”

“That would be an unfulfilling relationship,” Castorice tagged on immediately, glancing between them both slowly. “If Phainon ever felt any kind of romantic way, it isn’t as if you can return it.”

“Well… even if I could, this guy is the densest brick there is!” He was too amused by her ability to stay so upbeat after what she just said than offended by the jab. “Cassie, someone could smack him in the face with an ‘I love you’, and he’d say it back thinking they meant it to be nice!”

Their friend giggled at the thought. One hand covered her mouth, and a soft rosy hue dusted over her plush cheeks.

“Be nice to him. Phainon has love for everybody around him. Whoever can break through that and force him to see them in a special way has to be someone very special,” she teased. “Or, maybe, someone very strong. They might need to hit him pretty hard with that brick.”

“But who is stronger than he is? Look at his arm!” Cyrene pointed at him, and he grinned before flexing for them. “Oh, stop showing off! We get it!”

“Not to interrupt your… romance talk, but I texted Cifera for you,” another voice spoke up, and he shifted his attention to Mydei. As he talked, his eyes were glued to his phone, and the cat was draped over his bent figure to stand on the back of his neck. “She’s getting dressed now.”

“Thank you, Mydei. And if Pollux becomes a nuisance, please just bat her away,” Castorice mused, but Phainon wasn’t sure if she recognized just how unbothered Mydei seemed by it. “You’ve been very quiet. As Phainon’s second best friend, what do you believe? Is he simply being picky? Or does he just need someone extra special?”

‘Second’ best friend.

Cyrene grinned proudly at that, but Mydei only looked up before giving each of them a once over. When he finished, his gaze lingered on him for a moment.

“Phainon’s entitled to his own standards and expectations,” he offered his opinion. “We all have them.”

“Mydei’s probably got the highest of us all,” Cyrene teased him. “Mr. Big-Shot over here has never even had a relationship, right? I’ve never seen him with someone.”

“Mydei’s a private person,” Castorice defended him. “He does not kiss and tell, so to speak.”

“Ugh… Boys are no fun,” she whined. “One can’t find a date to save his life, and the other wouldn’t tell us even if he had one. What do we tease them about if not girls?”

“You could not tease us,” he suggested, but the deadpan expression on her face made him sigh. “Girls are mean…”

“Boys are lame.”

“Cats are better than both,” Castorice giggled, slowly approaching Mydei to pick her pet off of his shoulder. “Come, Pollux. Please leave Mydei alone now. You’re going to hurt him.”

She really must not have noticed that the expression Mydei wore wasn’t one of annoyance, but peace. He didn’t mind being walked on by the slender animal. In fact, he was even watching as she pulled her away from him and set Pollux on her way, slightly disappointed by the missing presence.

“She’s clingy. I apologize.”

“She’s very much welcomed,” Mydei said as he straightened himself out. “By the way, how is your sister doing?”

“She’s doing very well, thank you,” Castorice returned. “I plan to visit her tomorrow. I’m going to take her through the new flower garden they opened up a few cities over, then possibly grab lunch.”

He hummed thoughtfully. “That’s wonderful. It sounds like a very nice day. If you need a recommendation for a nice restaurant, I can send you links to a few places my mother and I have visited in that area.”

“Oh, I’d love that. How is your mother?” She asked him just as kindly. “Is she doing better these days?”

“She’s exactly the same as she always is.”

“We should get going,” Cyrene told them, cutting their conversation short. “Hyacine texted me, and she’s asking when we’re leaving so she can leave too.”

Castorice’s eyes widened as she seemed to remember their plans. “Oh, right! We still need to pick up Cifera too!”

Phainon stumbled lightly when Cyrene’s hands pushed on his back, and he laughed over her attempt to shove him to the door. It didn’t move him much, but it was funny that she thought she could.

“We won’t keep you,” Mydei promised. “Come on, Phainon. Let’s call it.”

He followed towards the front door, then pulled it open for the girls before Mydei could get his hands on the doorknob. As he held it, a pair of amber eyes shot him a sideways glance, one their friends didn’t see when passing through.

“Thank you, Phai,” Cyrene gave him a smile, then a wave. “I’m gonna start the car, Cassie!”

“Yes, I’ll be right there!” She rushed out, and he closed the door behind himself. “It was nice seeing you both. Let’s please hang out soon.”

“I could never say ‘no’ to something like that,” he chuckled as she locked the door. “Have a nice night. Take it easy.”

Mydei reached for her, and he watched as the two shared a hug. Her arms wrapped around his shoulders, and he settled his own just above her waist.

“Be safe. Tell your sister I said ‘hello’,” he told her, and she nodded. “I’ll see you around.”

“Yes, I’ll see you around, Mydei.”

When they finished, Phainon offered her a hug as well. His hand patted over her shoulder, and she rubbed his own lightly before letting go.

“Tell Hyacine to stop being a stranger. I never see her anymore,” he said, which made her promise to relay his message. “All that girl does is work and sleep. Nurses need to take breaks too.”

After their hug, she waved to them both, running to catch up to Cyrene before making their friends wait any longer. Once more, it was just him and Mydei standing outside of their friend’s place, and he turned to look at him.

“You don’t bake Hyacine anything?”

“Sometimes. Hyacine is hard for me to meet up with so freely,” he explained. “She works the night shift, and I work all day. Our schedules hardly ever align like this, but had I known, I would have made more.”

Phainon nodded, then felt a hand lightly thump against the back of his head before pulling him in close. The sudden proximity made his heart skip as his body shifted to face him completely.

“While we’re here, I’ll say this once—let me open doors for you,” he told him, holding his gaze now that they were alone. Thanks to Castorice having a bottom floor and corner apartment, they were tucked deep enough to be completely hidden as well.

“I can’t be chivalrous too?”

“You can be,” he allowed. “But practice it in other ways. I open the doors for you, and I close them behind me. That’s my job.”

“Why don’t you just lay out the red carpet for me?” He mocked, then felt his breathing hitch when he pulled him closer.

Mydei dropped his attention to his mouth briefly before meeting his gaze again. While there, he narrowed his eyes.

“Your tongue,” he warned him. “I said that’s my job. Your response should be something along the lines of ‘yes, master’ or ‘I understand, master’. Nothing more.”

Oh.

Mydei was in that kind of mood, but he probably should have known after this morning. That was his fault for getting a little too comfortable around their friends.

“Y-Yes, master,” he repeated, and Mydei nodded before letting him go. “Are we… done? Can we head back to my place?”

“Yes,” he answered. “Mind your manners for the rest of the day, Phainon. If I have to say this again, you’re going to upset me.”

“Yeah, I-I got it,” he promised, not wanting to do that. “I’ll be good, master.”

As much as he liked toeing the edge of his nerves, he also liked being good. He wanted to be good.

Maybe he was right. Maybe he had been too bratty recently, and he needed to tone it down before he started to make Mydei second doubt his commitment to their arrangement. There was a balance, right? A fine line between playful and disrespectful, but it was one that he was trying to comfortably find.

One thing was for sure though, he was going to be good for the rest of the day. If not to save himself from another punishment, to give Mydei the control he wanted from this.

Chapter End Notes

mydei wants to spank his ass red and raw so bad that it makes him look stupid. i wonder if phainon realizes just how much he’s holding himself back.

i also wonder if this next chapter is gonna have a little more of mydei letting loose/opening up and some more limit pushing like this one did. hm.

With the rest of the day to themselves, the first thing Mydei did when they got to his apartment was take a lid to some old food container and rinse it off. He dumped two tins of cat food into it, poured some water into its accompanying bowl, then walked it out to the cats by his mailbox.

Phainon was going to join him. He wanted to join him. Only to be instructed to put the groceries away and start marinating their chicken for dinner. Which was what he did, swiftly and efficiently, even if he pouted at his retreating figure and gave him a light glare when he came back inside.

After washing his hands, Mydei then ruffled his hair lightly just to further toy with his attitude.

“Good boy,” he coo’ed. “Cheer up. I’ll pick up the mess once I’m sure they have eaten their fill. That garbage won’t be there overnight. We can wash it and reuse it in the morning.”

Nodding, he looked to where his glass of water was leaving a slick ring of condensation over his counter.

“Master, would you like a drink?” He asked, realizing he had yet to get him anything since they got here. “I’ll pour you one.”

Amber eyes rolled playfully. “It’s far too early for that. I’ll wait until dinner later. Thank you for the offer though, prince.”

But now? The only person he wanted to impress was Mydei, his dominant.

“You know who you dress like actually?” She brought up casually, and he hummed curiously. “Mydei.”

His stomach dropped.

“Mydei’s usually wearing darker colors like that. Were you inspired by his closet?” The joke made his breathing hitch. “You two hang out so much, it’s like he’s rubbing off on you! Soon, will we even be able to tell you apart?”

“Yeah…” Phainon laughed awkwardly after. His grip on the bag tightened. “Maybe. If it works for him, it should work on me, right?"

Her eyes raked over his clothes. Those warm, blush-colored eyes stared as if trying to dissect every piece of him, to pull him apart and examine every single fragment closely. His black boots, his black jeans, his black leather watch, and his golden necklace. All of it was taken in by her, and she hummed a low, drawn out sound.

A spotlight was cast over his head, and a jury surrounded him, waiting to declare him guilty of deceit.

Could she see right through him?

Cyrene then shrugged casually and exaggeratedly, hands lifting into the air as she turned her attention away. While facing her back, he exhaled, glad to be released from the choking hold.

“It looks fine. I like how much confidence you’ve been radiating recently, and Cassie was right when she said you have a kinda ‘glow’ to you. But honestly? As long as you continue to be the same genuine and kindhearted guy inside, I’ll love you through any identity crisis you have,” she told him, then waved her hand dismissively. “Just… don’t try too hard for some attention, silly. People who are worth the time will like you for you, not an act you’re trying to put on.”

His lips sealed tightly together as he wondered what that was supposed to mean. After all, it wasn’t as if he was trying to be someone else. He wasn’t just letting Mydei take him and push whatever he liked onto him like some kind of blank canvas.

He was still him, just dressed up a bit more with a little bit more thought into the things he did.

There was a choice. There was always a choice even if he agreed to give up his control. Mydei held his cards and played them as he wished, but he was the one to deal the hand to him. Whatever his dominant ‘made’ him do was nothing more than a gentle push in a direction he wanted to walk down anyway.

That was fine, wasn’t it?

He was learning. He was experimenting. With both came changes, and he welcomed them as they came because they felt good. Physically and mentally, he felt better than he used to.

If Phainon looked past the shame that clawed at him when things got particularly heavy or foreign, Mydei never made him feel as though he wasn’t good enough. Even when he was being ignorant and unnecessarily cruel for no reason, Mydei did his best not to talk down to him but to explain why he was wrong. He didn’t shame his feelings, only supported them and their suffocating weight.

It was his own mind playing tricks on him that made him feel inadequate. Those were his own insecurities painting over the things that didn’t make sense. All Mydei ever did was tell him that he should have more respect for himself and those around him, he should dress to better accentuate his handsome features, and he should be more confident in his body and his interests. That didn’t mean he wasn't good enough, just that he could be better.

Was that bad for Mydei to do? Was it wrong for him to guide him in that way?

“You hear me, Phai?”

“Huh?” He asked, having zoned out completely. “Yeah. I heard you. Something about not changing myself for people, right?”

She nodded while giving him a smile. The gesture was so sweet and genuine that he couldn’t find it in him to defend himself or protest.

It wasn’t her intention to drag anyone, he knew that. She didn’t suspect Mydei was changing him in any kind of way, so she didn’t blame him. She didn’t insist that this newer version of him was bad for trying to change things up a little bit, just that he was different. Confident, but different from the guy she knew him as.

He couldn’t really fault her for a word that she said.

“I’m… gonna put this bag in my room,” Phainon settled on, wanting to remove himself from the subject completely. “I’ll drop it off at De’s some point this week.”

“Okay! I’ll get together a snack tray so we can binge some television,” she beamed happily. “I missed hanging out with my best friend.”

“Yeah. I missed you too.”

Phainon rushed to his bedroom, and as if Mydei had a sixth sense of when he was alone, his phone buzzed. Because he was the last person to text him, everything in him just knew it was his dominant finally responding to his messages.

The bag was placed neatly by his nightstand. With his phone in hand next, he checked the few messages that were sent.

One was a photo of Mydei and his mom inside of her kitchen, and she was leaning against his arm while smiling sweetly up at his camera. Behind them was a dainty vase of red, white, and burgundy flowers all wrapped up in gold ribbon. Beside that was a pink pill-container stocked full of medicine for the next week. Both him and his mom had a similar side braid, their cherry ends tucked into a golden cuff and amber eyes mimicking one another’s softened squint from their wide grins.

> [Mydei: My mother misses you. She said to tell your mother that they need to meet up for coffee soon.]

> [Mydei: Also, I look forward to watching you try to build that lego set, get upset when you mess up, then quit half way through. It’ll be amusing.]

Phainon laughed, rolling his eyes over the light jab and choosing to ignore it. They could bicker over it in person while building it together, as he never intended to do it on his own.

> [Phainon: You look more like your mom every day, you know. I hope she’s okay. That container looks pretty heavy.]

He didn’t remember her ever being sick. She was always so lively and bubbly when he saw her, diligently running her household while her husband did whatever he wanted outside of it. The only time she was ever upset were the handful of times he heard them arguing behind closed doors, but every family had their arguments. Even his own.

> [Mydei: They’re just to manage her glucose levels, blood pressure, and cholesterol. She’s fine otherwise.]

That sounded right to him. Their parents were getting older, and their bodies needed the extra help. His dad took medicine for his blood pressure too, and that wasn’t anything to worry too much about. He lived as he pleased and ate whatever he wanted, just within moderation.

Maybe that was why Mydei was so strict with his body, diet, and work out routine, to stave off having to eat several pills every single morning like his mother did. It didn’t sound fun. It didn’t look fun, either.

> [Mydei: Thank you for the concern though.]

> [Mydei: I’m going to put my phone on silent and spend some more time with her. I’ll text you later. Feel free to spam me with messages if you'd like.]

Phainon smiled to himself, grateful that Mydei was always so clear with him. It wasn’t as if he’d just stop texting and disappear for hours, then respond when he remembered to. If he planned to leave, he said as much. If he planned to not check his phone, he warned him of that.

> [Phainon: I’m home with Cyrene. I’ll be around if you need me. My phone’s always on.]

Mydei reacted to that with a thumbs up and a red heart, and Phainon shut his screen off before curling a finger into his day collar. Pulling, he lined the front and then sighed happily while feeling on the golden links.

“Phai!”

His head turned to the door.

“Are you actually gonna eat peach rings with me this time, or is it a waste to put that many in a bowl?” Cyrene called out to him through the wood. “Same with the sour watermelon!”

“Just a little bit!”

“‘kay!”

He heard her footsteps leave, and the hand not on his collar turned his phone back on just to see the picture Mydei sent again. The little crinkle by the corners of his eyes from genuine joy and the sparkle in his golden gaze made his heart kick a lot like it did in front of Aglaea’s home, warm like a kiss from the sun. It was both terrifying and comforting, foreign yet so familiar, because this was Mydei.

Everything they did together was tinged with those two emotions, though. It also wasn’t anything new to feel hot underneath his skin when looking at him, so he brushed it off just like he did back then.

Phainon’s finger pressed over it before he could even think and he saved it to his camera roll. It wasn’t often Mydei looked that happy these days, yet here that look was captured in a photo meant for only him and his mom to see. How could he not?

Mydei was just so handsome when he let that cool, collected exterior melt just a little bit, and he wanted as much of that version of him as possible—sexual or not.

Chapter End Notes
