chapters.html:
Chapter Notes

THIS TOOK ME FOREVER. I’M SOSOSOSOSO SORRY.

my bf visited for a week, my mom got sick (shes getting better tho), and i rewrote this FIVE ENTIRE times to try and get mydei where i wanted him because his character means a lot to me.

i love phainons character too. i think they both have their own specific way of caring for each other that sometimes it clashes because it’s not exactly the same. they crave similar things, but they also have different needs.

but mydei is so careful and as much as i wanna make him blow up and rant, hes just… not that guy. it makes it a lil difficult to write disagreements/arguments.

The next time Phainon found the time to visit Mydei, with his bag of activities in one hand and keys in the other, he actually happened to see the other man.

Mydei was walking into the lobby when he spotted that familiar two-toned hair. His hands were taking down a ponytail as he nodded curtly at the receptionist. That same flirtatious, finger wiggling wave she liked to give him was given to the other man, though his attention was already turned away from her.

It seemed the only thing he cared about was going home after a long day, and Phainon couldn't help but feel a little bit bad for the poor woman. He hoped she found someone else soon.

Mydei, who was typically well aware of his surroundings, not interested in looking her way for more than a second.

“Mydei!”

He paused midstep, then looked over his shoulder while dropping his hands. Surprise was written across his face, lifting his eyebrows and picking up his frown.

“What are the odds?” Phainon grinned at him as he wrapped an arm around his shoulders. “I don’t ever catch you here. You usually make it up before I do.”

“I had a lot of things to do, so I’m late coming home,” he sighed. “I must have missed your text, but I’m glad you’re here.”

“No worries,” he beamed happily. While speaking, they walked closer towards the elevator. “I hope work wasn’t too hard on you. You look a little bit beat…”

Mydei’s lips pursed. “I’m more annoyed than I am tired right now,” he admitted. “Please behave for me.”

His voice was tight, like he was trying to hold his composure together and was one wrong move away from snapping. That edge was familiar.

One of his hands was already reaching to undo his tie as the elevator doors opened for them. Its knot loosened, dragging lower so he could pop the button holding his collar together. The other gently brushed Phainon’s back, fingers settling just over his shirt but not quite his skin, to silently nudge him inside first.

Phainon walked forward with a quicker step to get in front of him.

“Was it really that bad of a day?”

“I work with grown ass children,” he grumbled crudely, following in behind him. But when he went to push his floor number, the button was already lit up thanks to Phainon’s quick touch. “How can someone be pushing thirty and still be breastfed by their mother?”

“Some people work just because they need something to do, not because they need the money,” Phainon added casually.

He opened his arms once the doors sealed shut. Upon opening them, Mydei filled them, leaning his head into the right side of his own and resting his back into his chest. It was silent and swift, almost like he was too exhausted to keep up his usual independence.

Another sigh left his lips. “I wish they’d bum a job off of someone else. My father works hard for this company, so watching him play nice guy to his friends at our expense really pisses me off.”

Phainon held him tighter. The stiffness in Mydei’s body didn’t ease, but he did stay within his arms.

“So you care about him.”

“I can acknowledge his hard work and his ability to provide for the people around him. He’s my father, of course I love him for what he’s done for me and my mother. But that doesn’t mean I like him as a person or a boss,” he reasoned. “It’s… complicated. It makes sense in my head, just not in the mouth.”

It sounded complicated. Phainon couldn’t imagine being in that kind of spot with his own dad.

“What’s in that bag?” Mydei asked suddenly, clearly wanting to change the subject, and Phainon raised it higher for him to look inside. “Mm. I remember now. Your games and toys.”

“The things you forced me to buy,” he reminded him, shaking the bag a few times for emphasis. “Never do that again, by the way. That was a dirty, dirty trick you pulled on me…”

“But it was a good day.”

“Don’t pull that card,” he huffed. With a lift of his shoulder, he nudged the other man just enough to disrupt his comfort. “It was a nice gesture, yeah. My parents loved it. But I’m not here to milk your wallet. I told you so many times that I don’t wanna be that person.”

Mydei was silent as the doors opened for them on his floor, and he guided him forward with the ghost of a touch while slipping away from him. Phainon walked ahead as he was silently instructed to, allowing his dominant to follow a step behind him.

“I got a little too trigger happy,” Mydei admitted, his voice softer than it had been when discussing his job and father. “With everything that happened, I was on a bit of a head rush. I thought about you and how I occupy a lot of your time now, and I wanted you to go see everyone else important to you. It’s important to make them feel special too.”

That was sweet. Phainon could agree with that. The gesture was clearly brought up from somewhere genuine, its intent pure of heart.

“Then I remembered someone you didn’t even know took care of your wants the night before, and it made me want to do that for you too. I just went for it,” he continued. As he spoke, his words grew slower. They grew heavier. “I… I wanted to do more. I wanted it so badly that I thought to myself, ‘I want to provide this’. That made me go for it.”

Phainon could kind of understand that.

That morning, it felt like all he wanted was more from him too—physically, at least. To touch his body while at its most peaceful. To hear him feel good without any kind of kinky rambles. To see him raw and real without any kind of walls up or clothes on.

He thought that he wanted to wake his dominant up with a blowjob, then he simply did it before his nerves could get the better of him. Mydei didn’t know he would try it. There wasn’t a clue to lead up to it. All that needed to be said was that he wanted it, and Phainon wanted to make it happen for him.

But this wasn’t like that, was it?

Mydei’s body was always open to him. He made that clear so many times. The only limit was if he specifically asked not to be touched, which was very, very rare.

Phainon did not like when Mydei bought him things more than he already did, but he knew that. Even if he let most of it go as if he didn’t notice, this was something entirely different. This was blatant spoiling. This was turning him into some kind of ‘sugar baby’.

Food for two didn’t just magically appear inside of his refrigerator, that was obvious. His collars didn’t just materialize out of thin air in his exact size and Mydei’s design. Skin care, toothbrushes, and soaps tailored for him didn’t walk from the store and sit themselves inside of his cabinets. All of it came from somewhere, slowly, and over the days he wasn’t around.

‘Spares’ are what Mydei called them, but he knew better than to believe that. Mydei did this when they were just friends too, like the night he ordered groceries to his house without asking because he knew he’d turn him down otherwise.

But never had he sent him a sum of money and told him to go spend it how he pleased. That was way too much to accept. That was precisely what he meant when he turned him down while making their rules. That could not happen again.

As their feet stopped at the front door, he turned to let Mydei open it for him.

“Look at me,” Phainon spoke up, stopping him when he tried to fit his key into the door. As a pair of amber eyes met his, he smiled softly. “There's a time and place for your generosity, De, but don’t make a habit out of sending me your hard earned cash. I can accept your gifts as rewards from a dom to his sub. I tolerate you buying me collars and gear on the excuse of experimenting. I turn a blind eye to the ‘spares’ you keep for me to use in your bathroom. But this act of straight up slapping money in my hand cannot happen again.”

“I… might have overstepped.”

“No. You did overstep,” he repeated. “Thank you for helping me make everyone’s day, but don’t do it again. We can figure something else out that doesn’t involve you transferring hundreds of dollars to me.”

They looked at each other, and Mydei nodded gently.

“I only wanted you to have a good day and feel closer to the people around you,” he tried to explain himself again. “I’m sorry, Phainon.”

“If you do it again, we’re gonna need more than a talk to fix it, okay?” Phainon’s free hand lightly pushed his shoulder to let him know that he wasn’t mad. “I carried it out because the damage was already done, and it did feel really good to see everyone around me smiling, but you do enough for me as is, okay? There’s no need for more.”

“I’ll do better,” he promised, voice quiet yet firm. “Someone who is given as much trust as I am shouldn’t misuse it like that…”

“I got these for us with that leftover money though.” Phainon jiggled the bag a few times again. “No matter how these came to be in my hand, just… promise me we’ll get to them sometime. They’ll be kept at your place, so it’s more like you bought them for yourself anyway. I just picked them up for you like some kinda delivery service.”

Mydei nodded. “I’ll happily join you no matter how childish it might be.”

‘Childish’.

There wasn’t an age restriction on lego-sets and video games. Just because they weren’t fifteen anymore didn’t mean they couldn’t still enjoy a colorful little puzzle or a nice story game.

“You really gotta let loose a little bit. Life’s more than work and sleep, you know.”

“I have no interest in games or toys for myself, but perhaps they’ll make for a cozy night in with you,” Mydei caved.

“You can open the door now, by the way. Standing out here and talking so seriously is awkward, isn’t it?” He chuckled, and Mydei slipped the key into the knob before twisting. “What do you wanna do tonight?”

The door was closed behind them, locked swiftly to protect their privacy, and Phainon threw a glance over his shoulder.

“How do you feel?” Mydei asked. “Are you mad at me?”

“I’m not angry,” he answered while kicking his shoes off. “I asked you to let go, so… if things like this happen once or twice, it’s because I asked for it, right? We’re allowed to mess up a few times before getting it right.”

“It’s not your fault that I overstepped your boundaries again. You can’t exactly ask for someone to trample over your security,” he shot his statement down. “We agreed that I didn’t have that authority, yet I coerced you into it anyway. That was your autonomy, and I infringed upon it. I… should have bit my tongue, kept it to myself, and let you do it on your own.”

A hand settled over Phainon’s shoulder, squeezing it tightly and reassuringly when he didn’t respond.

“It’s a part of me that wants to come out because I’m used to it,” he apologized again. “That doesn’t make what I did any better, I know. I crossed one of your limits like it was nothing, and that makes me no better than the fakes I was trying to protect you from.”

Phainon wasn’t really sure what to say to that. It felt like Mydei was more upset at himself than he was, like his guilt outweighed the crime somehow. But was it really a crime if he wasn’t hurt?

They did draw that line together, but he could have sent it back once it was transferred. He could have been more adamant against the transaction than he was, as his head was far from that foggy state of being by the time he was behind his wheel. Never would Mydei have allowed him to drive if his head wasn’t attached to his shoulders.

But he didn’t. He kept it, bought a pretty bouquet full of his mom’s favorite flowers in blue and white and ordered a nice barbecue lunch for her and his dad. Then he kept the leftover change to buy these activities for them to do together. After all, he liked spending time with Mydei too, and there were only so many nights they could waste on movies, shows, and funny online videos before it became repetitive and boring.

He backtracked on his own limit too. He accepted it the way he accepted the small things given to him behind his back—begrudgingly and ready to chew him out.

Was a simple action really worth calling himself a ‘fake’ over?

“I want to pour you a drink,” Phainon offered, holding Mydei’s hand when it didn’t lift. “And I want to move on from this already. It’s okay.”

“I don’t deserve to have you do that for me,” his dominant protested. “Would you like something to drink with me?”

“… Sure.”

“Go sit down for me then.”

Mydei was the first to walk away between them, and Phainon’s shoulders fell as he placed his sneakers down on the shoe rack.

It hurt inside his stomach as he stared at his back. Being rejected the opportunity to pour him a glass after their heavy conversation felt as if he were being punished for bringing it up, as if he wasn’t allowed to want what they normally did. This desire to take care of him in return didn’t simply disappear because Mydei felt guilty for something.

Phainon carried his bag to the kitchen counter before setting it down. Beside it, he dumped his phone and keys before avoiding the barstool completely.

“H-Hey…”

He grasped Mydei’s arm to turn him around gently.

“I don’t like when you brush me off like that,” he said, letting him in on the bitter feeling. “Just because you don’t feel you deserve it, doesn’t mean I don’t still want to do what I usually do.”

“Phainon, it’s okay.”

“If you feel guilty over it, then sit with it for a while until we figure out a way to fix it. That’s the natural consequence for doing something wrong, isn’t it?” He suggested.

It made him think back to the only uncomfortable punishment Mydei had ever given him. To kneel in quiet like a leashed dog and be stuck with his own thoughts while unable to speak or move was a terrible time. The things he thought of himself weren’t kind back then, and to physically feel like the things he said about himself was worse. But he hasn’t had a lot of those dark, depreciating feelings since that night. In a way, maybe it really did help.

If Mydei felt guilty, he could handle a little bit of time with his thoughts to sift through them too. But unlike a punishment, he wasn’t going to ask that he kneeled, bound and silent, like some kind of pet. Being serviced while harboring that inner negativity would be more than enough for a man like him.

The hand on the cabinet slipped, lowering bit by bit until it touched the counter.

“It is.”

“Can I get us both a drink, master?” Phainon asked softly, and Mydei exhaled shakily before looking away from him. With a hand on the lower half of his face, he nodded. “Can you use your words?”

“Yes,” he mumbled, walking around the counter to take the barstool. “I need to think. Please don't talk to me for a couple of minutes.”

Immediately, Mydei’s face was covered with both hands as he hung his head in silent shame. His elbows were pressed to the counter, and his fingers interlocked over his forehead. Heavy but steady breaths left his nose, lifting his shoulders slowly before sinking them at the same pace.

Silence fell between them as he turned to the cabinet and grabbed two glasses, careful not to knock them into each other. Heavy ice clinked to the bottom of them both once he cracked the freezer open, and those glasses clicked to the countertop after.

Phainon reached for the almost empty bottle left on a tray in the corner of his kitchen, eyeing what was left before pouring it. Warm, caramel-colored liquor filled them one by one slowly. The steady pour was almost completely silent if not for the crackle of ice when met with alcohol.

One glass was placed in front of Mydei, and the one meant for him was topped off with a splash of water to dilute the strong taste. Unlike the other man, he did not like to drink for the taste or to unwind after a long day. Whiskey, on its own, was gross. Alcohol of any kind, on its own, was gross.

But he carried the drink to where Mydei sat. His free hand then gently touched his shoulder, sliding towards his stiffened back to rub. The sound of his palm swiping back and forth against the smooth fabric of his button-up followed as he rubbed, coaxing him to calm down.

No words were spoken, and they didn’t need to be.

Mydei winced from the touch before he began to relax. His arms slowly lowered, elbows dropping and hands folding into his lap. Much like he always requested of him, he picked his chin up and straightened out his posture until he was upright.

Their eyes met, and Phainon tilted his glass towards him. A soft smile tugged on his lips, warm and inviting him to stop punishing himself with his guilt, to focus on him instead of his thoughts, and to pick the drink he made for him up.

With a soft, ringing clink, they were brought together. Afterwards, they both took a drink.

“You make cute faces when you try to drink like I do,” Mydei quietly teased him, watching as his nose crinkled from the bitter taste burning down the back of his tongue and throat.

Phainon rolled his eyes. “‘m not an alcoholic,” he defended himself.

“I’m not either.”

“Mhm.”

Mydei continued to look up at him, allowing him to trace along his spine and touch his body as freely as he wanted to. As he did, his own fingers reached to fully unravel his tie and unbutton his shirt.

“What do you want to do tonight, handsome?” He asked, and Phainon’s eyes dropped to his exposed skin. The neckline of his undershirt was low, showing off the divot between either collarbone.

"Do you feel any better, master?”

“I think I’ll be okay,” he told him. “Knowing you’re not hurt in any way will make the guilt go away over time.”

“Do you need anything from me?” He offered, then pulled him closer anyway. “Can you hug me?”

That’d help. It was what he wanted the last time he needed comfort, and it was something Phainon was more than willing to provide for him.

“Yes.” He felt him stand up before engulfing him within his arms like he was waiting to be asked that. “Always.”

His still figure stood there, tall and unwavering, allowing himself to be grappled onto tightly. Fists balled his work-shirt up within them. Breaths fanned over his skin as he hid inside of the crook of his neck.

“I’ve got you,” he promised while wrapping his arms around his waist to hold him just as firmly. “Mm… My master is as sensitive as I am, isn’t he? He’s just better at masking it.”

“I try.”

“Hm?”

“I try very hard to control myself,” Mydei confessed to him. “I try to keep my head as clear as possible, to shove the feelings away so I’m not acting out irrationally. I can’t be someone safe if I respond in anger or hurt.”

Phainon frowned.

What about him? Why was it that he was allowed to be as emotional and as sensitive as he wanted, and yet Mydei forced himself to always swallow his own down before speaking or reacting?

It wasn’t as if he didn’t see him grit his teeth or bite his tongue when he was upset. Whenever he was angry, he always covered his mouth and looked away, physically stopping himself from saying anything he might regret. Whenever he was too forward or excited with something, he back tracked himself and apologized for behaving out of line before settling down again. Phainon noticed that part of it too.

But he hated that. He hated knowing that for certain. He hated that Mydei was afraid to let himself feel because it could cloud his judgement, thus making it difficult to look after someone else. To him, that wasn’t fair at all.

One hand held the back of his head, fingers threading through the sunset locks to hold him closely. Cerulean eyes dropped down to the wine red shirt he wore, looking down his shoulders and back where his other arm was planted firmly around his waist.

“What do you do if you’re upset?”

“I brush it off until I can deal with it later,” Mydei said as if it were the simplest thing in the world. “I vent it while working out the next day, or I make myself rationalize it. Sometimes I don’t deserve to be upset. It’s pointless.”

Phainon held him tighter. His nose brushed the side of his head, and he took a deep breath.

Voicing his frustrations was the same as ‘complaining’, and feeling upset was something ‘pointless’. These things were nothing but a burden for him to have, but that couldn’t possibly be right.

Was that really the healthiest way to view negativity in his life? He wasn't a psychologist. He wasn’t a therapist. He didn’t take classes to study emotions, and he didn’t keep self-help books. Did Mydei know something he didn’t, or did he delude himself into thinking that was the best way to handle things?

“When you thought of me, or people like me, as ‘abusive’, I was angry and hurt,” he brought up, and the memory made his stomach drop painfully. It was sour, bitter, and full of chokingly thick regret. “I wanted to be mad so badly. I wanted to yell and ask how you could ever say that to me after knowing the kind of person I am. But when I broke it down, there was truly no reason for me to be angry. It made sense given what you saw, so how could I be?”

He did say that to him, didn’t he? He called him ‘violent’. He called him ‘abusive’. He told him that he was ‘crazy’ for wanting a life like this, that the things he did were ‘weird’ for a relationship.

While belittling himself, he dragged Mydei down by accusing him of wanting to treat him like a pet or an object. It happened even after Mydei said all he wanted to do was treat him kindly, spoil him however possible, and take care of him.

“I have to let it go and be realistic,” Mydei repeated, pulling him even closer until his leg stood in between his. “The best way to avoid unnecessary conflict is to drop it completely and focus on calming down.”

But with everything in his head, the sexual nature of bare breasts right in his face was probably the last thing in his mind. It was just nudity, and nudity was not inherently sexual.

Mydei twisted the ropes around one another between his chest, straightening out the rest of the length before tightening them. Pressure pulled on his neck, not uncomfortably but firmly, then around his ribs when either half was pulled beneath his chest and around his back. It made his breaths hitch to be hugged by the unrelenting and tight rope. Electricity tickled beneath his skin, burning even hotter when Mydei looked up at him rather than the phone.

Those warm, golden irises darted to his chest, to where he was slowly fixating the rope above either pec to highlight them. Framed in tight crimson, the color was stark and eye-catching against his white shirt, and it felt as if either were bulging even further thanks to the tie. When he took a breath, his expanding body pressed deeper into the stiff ropes from how firmly they gripped his body.

“Please don’t tighten them anymore, master.”

Mydei nodded, staring at him for a second before glancing back to his phone.

This wasn’t scary. If anything, it felt almost intimate the way Mydei raked his eyes over his body and began to carefully feed the ropes through the twist he made. He touched him gently despite the ropes being tight, flicking his eyes up to his every so often before focusing again.

Slowly, while raveling and unraveling his work when he wasn’t pleased with the way it turned out, Mydei stopped looking up at him. He stopped tentatively checking in, no longer conscious of being watched and doubtful of his participation in all of this. Not that he stopped caring, as Mydei would loosen the hold if he gasped too loud and slow down if he squirmed too much, but he stopped worrying about him not wanting this. He dropped the concern that he didn’t like it.

Instead, his attention sharpened on his work at hand, eyes shifting and moving as if imagining the next move. He wasn’t afraid to try it and then backtrack, look at the photo, then try again. He didn’t let a mistake stop him from taking a deep breath and doing it again. His fingers moved as if they couldn’t stop, tracing over the rope again and again to visualize where it needed to wrap and how he needed to knot it.

The look on his face reminded him of when they used to study together. Nose deep in a textbook for their shared class, he always used to get lost within the pages for hours on end. It was always easier for him to settle down and focus for long periods of time.

Phainon smiled softly, aware that he couldn’t even see him with how fixated he was on keeping this harness clean, pretty, and precise. Tunnel visioned into the task at hand, he was sure nothing could distract Mydei unless it went out of his way to do it. But he wouldn’t. He didn’t want to interrupt him in the middle of something that was both comforting him, distracting him, and important to him.

His head tilted back gently, resting on the edge of his collar as the sound of rope sliding against itself filled the room. He could feel the mass of delicate and careful knotting right against his sternum, and he was beginning to really like the way it held him closely. They weren’t suffocating. They weren’t panic-inducing, as not once throughout this whole thing did he feel a hint of anxiety the way he did when handcuffed.

On that same note, it wasn’t particularly arousing either. The sexiest thing about this all was Mydei’s determination to get this right for him. More than just an activity to calm himself, this was, essentially, what he wanted. He told him this looked nice, and he told him he’d wear it for him if he learned.

But it was supposed to take him days. It was supposed to be broken up into short segments, not done in a single sitting. Yet Mydei continued.

When the first yawn came from Phainon’s lips, he continued with that same diligent effort. When the low-battery notification flashed at the top of his phone screen, he simply swiped power-saving mode on and continued.

As exhaustion crept into his body, he hummed quietly, disrupting the comfortable silence that had been going on for what felt like an hour.

“Thank you, master.”

His eyes flicked upwards, slowly pulling rope free from beside his waist. That antsy and overstimulated expression had long since left his face, leaving behind only the cool, composed mask he frequented. There wasn’t a hit of desperation in his eyes, and his lips were safe from being bitten raw.

Phainon could still imagine the scratches he left in his own cheek, and he looked down at where they once lived—bright red and terrible against his soft, well-taken care of skin.

“Is this hard to learn?” He asked him softly, eyes half-lidded and lips wearing a kind smile.

Mydei, still not wanting to talk, shook his head before looking back down.

“Do you like doing this?”

He nodded, bringing the rope around his back to double up on the structure.

“I like it too,” he whispered, and the hand on his body paused. “I like how comforting it feels. It’s like a tight hug or a weighted blanket on top of me. The pressure is kind of nice.”

Mydei nodded again, leaning closer in order to look over his back. His hands fumbled around, tucking and tying the tail ends of his scarlet ropes.

“Thank you for practicing this for me.” Phainon yawned, leaning into his shoulder. “I… wanna do it again with other kinds of ties like this. No restraints, just being close to you.”

The ropes dug into his skin, bulging the fat around his stomach and waist slightly from his slouched posture. Each breath made them tighter. Every shift reminded him that he was bound in some way, even if his limbs were all free.

Hot palms touched his shoulders, gliding between his shoulder blades to hug him gently.

“Can you please touch me, master?”

They dropped immediately, needy for more. Mydei touched his lower back where the ropes weren't wrapped around him, and he pulled him closer to his body until their chests touched and stomachs brushed. Nose to his shoulder, Mydei inhaled deeply, holding his breath for a moment while squeezing him tightly.

“You look better,” he said, and Phainon felt a tickle of butterflies in his stomach from the sudden compliment. He remembered why immediately.

‘Make me look as good as she does.’

“Am I? You stared at that lady’s boobs pretty intensely for a while,” he teased him. “Maybe longer than any guy into women would.”

“I could look at you forever.” It was said so earnestly that he wondered if his joke even registered as a joke to him. “Thank you for letting me do this, Phainon. I’m sorry it took so long.”

His shoulders shrugged, uncaring. There was something else he cared more about.

“How are you feeling?”

“Better,” he answered. “So much better because of you. Thank you.”

“Then I don’t care how long it takes. As long as you’re feeling better, that’s all that matters to me,” he promised, allowing his eyes to close in comfort “Mm… I feel sleepy, master…”

“Can you wear this while washing your face and brushing your teeth?” Mydei requested. The softness of his voice betrayed just how confident and focused he was less than two minutes ago, as if he was afraid of asking for too much too soon.

It was cute.

“Can I wear this while getting ready for bed, master?” He repeated back to him, and a soft, amused breath followed from his attempt to turn Mydei’s question of comfort into permission to continue.

“Yes, you may.”

They left each other’s arms, and one guiding hand held him as he stood shakily in front of the couch. The first step made his knee buckle, only for a pair of arms to hold him up and keep him from stumbling.

“I’ve got you,” Mydei said almost instinctively, and he gulped while taking another step on his sleeping legs. “There you go. Can you take another?”

Did he have to say it like that? Warm, deep, and full of praise? Like he was genuinely concerned about his ability to walk?

His legs were asleep, not broken.

But Mydei didn’t care about specifics. He saw him struggle, then rushed to help him regardless. One hand held his own gently, and the other pressed to the small of his back to encourage him to keep walking.

There was a bit of a haze over his head as he was helped to the bathroom, still lost in that sensation of being handled so firmly but gently. It only deepened when he stopped and looked at himself in the mirror for the first time.

He gripped Mydei’s hand tighter, unable to look away from the ropes crossed over his torso. If a photo was taken of him right here and now, he’d look exactly like the men and women Mydei admired casually online when scrolling. The ropes pressed deep into his body, pressing in by his waist and emphasizing the shape of it. Even on top of his simple t-shirt, they made it obvious how wide his chest was and how slender his body dipped as it lowered towards his hips.

That red color looked good. It was brighter than his leather collar was, and the shock of color was vibrant as a rose. Twists, knots, and straightened lines curved to fit around him. The way the ropes were woven into each other looked so confusing at first glance, like those cereal box puzzles of a maze with the difficulty cranked up by a hundred.

Mydei figured it out though. He broke it down for himself silently, mentally, straightening the design into one long strand before fixing the rope into what it was now. Watching him slowly dip into that focused state from his previously antsy self, take hold of what he wanted to do, then not stop until he got it done, was amazing.

“Do you still like it, Phainon? Or is it too much for you?”

“It’s cool,” he accidentally said, and Mydei’s lips pursed over the nonchalant response. “No, like… sorry. I’m a bit out of it right now. I-I meant to say that it was really cool watching you up close and personally as you just… What am I saying?”

Words were difficult to think up and say as he just stared, allowing himself to continue being held.

“I just followed the natural shape of your body,” his dominant explained, brushing off the praise. “The basic shape of what we wanted to achieve was fairly simple. The trickiest part was keeping the ropes symmetrical and from twisting up on itself while trying to tuck and knot the design, as they need to sit a specific way. The whole point is to look beautiful.”

“Does it?”

“You do,” he answered, and Phainon watched him through the mirror as he admired him in the flesh. “I don’t have a long enough rope for anything intricate and show-stopping like other people. I don’t have hooks in my ceilings for suspension. But I’m sure you wouldn’t like to be restrained that heavily anyway. This is enough for you, and if it’s enough for you, it’s more than enough for me.”

“Yeah,” he agreed absentmindedly, feeling as his fingers brushed his side.

Mydei touched him like he was something precious, something delicate, and too firm of a press could break him. It didn’t matter if he had been tied up, handcuffed, and even slapped by his hand. It didn’t matter that he was built of strong bones and thick muscle. His fingertips knew the fibers of his rope, and they ventured over the wrinkled cotton of his t-shirt, but only the lightest touches met where skin bulged through both.

Even if his chest was bulged and popped from his ties, he didn’t grope his body or tease the little bumps where his nipples poked through his shirt. If he noticed it, then he must have pretended not to see it. If he didn’t notice it, then it was because all of his attention was elsewhere on his body. Arousal must not have been in orbit at all around his head.

As if he could read his mind, Mydei hummed quietly and traced along the very bottom of the harness.

“Leather ticks the dominant part of me better. I like the feel and the smell. But I have a soft spot for the rustic and raw look of ropes, then the marks they leave behind on the skin. They’re really beautiful,” he rambled without being asked, voice far away like he was deep in his own mind. “I like being able to weave them in nice designs too. A buckle is convenient, but this feels a lot more intimate to put on and take off. It makes me feel good inside too when it comes out as I hoped."

“Have you… done this before?”

“I practiced with my last submissive, but it wasn’t like this.” Mydei finally looked up to meet his gaze through the glass. “I tied him up for sex and sexual sessions. I’ve never done it just to admire it.”

It was there. The answer he wanted to hear was right there even if he didn’t say it explicitly.

No.

No, his dominant has not done this with someone before. He has not tied someone up just to watch them walk around innocently in his work, and that meant he was the first person to give him that.

Phainon felt a burst of pride pop inside of his chest. The revelation made him exhale shakily, heart racing even if he was simply standing there and listening. Each pulse was loud in his ears, rhythmic and familiar because of how often Mydei made it pound.

Another soft hum vibrated through the calm air, and the hand on his back gently nudged him forward. His feet stumbled just a bit, not expecting the sudden movement with how lost in his head he was.

“Someone meant it when he said he’s not all there. Come on, enough talking then,” he decided for them. “My prince needs to prepare for bed. Can you do that for me?”

“Yeah, I-I can do that,” he mumbled, walking forward until his body met the bathroom counter. Both hands held on to the marble top, and he closed his eyes for a second. “My head feels a little bit… weird.”

“Does it?”

“Mm…”

“I’ve got you,” he told him, rubbing his back. “Once we finish in here, I will take all of this off of you so we can rest.”

His head turned, but his eyes were still closed. “But my master just put it on…”

“I’ve had my fill, and I need to get this sleeping beauty to bed before he starts tripping over his own feet,” he hushed. “Thank you, again, for doing this for me, Phainon. You’re always so quick to indulge me, so I’ll work harder to be deserving of it too.”

If he could, he’d thank him for being so open and honest with him tonight, for giving him a longer and more intimate peek into all of the things he hid inside. But the hand rubbing his back made the words crumble and fall to dust. The warmth in his voice flooded in his head and replaced his own.

Mydei sounded so much better than he did earlier, and it made his heart beat even faster to know he was the one to cheer him up. Had it been any harder, it could have popped right into the hand pressing against his chest as it straightened his posture out.

But his head felt a little too hazy to really think about it. All that lived inside of it was Mydei’s sweet little tilt of the lip when he opened his eyes.

Happiness looked really good on him, better than any other mask he put on, and Phainon wanted to keep it there.

Upon learning more about how Mydei felt, Phainon realized that if he wanted to cheer him up when he felt down, there were certain things that helped.

One was that he did want to be reassured, but it didn’t count if it excused the mistakes he made in the past. Mydei liked affirmations when he did something well and to be told that he was doing good as he was. More often than not, he wanted encouragement to keep going instead. He wanted his efforts praised and his growth acknowledged, as that meant he was learning to be better. To him, progress was more important than being perfect.

The second was that sometimes he craved quiet and space. His head could be a loud place when he was upset. Rather than being smothered with attention and bombarded with extra noise, there came moments where he just needed everything turned off for a little while so he could try to drown his own thoughts into something manageable. Something smaller, quieter, and less daunting to approach. Though he allowed the occasional question or comment, if he didn’t feel like it, then he simply didn’t speak. Maybe a hug was needed for grounding too, but if he didn't want to be touched, then he was always sure to make it known.

Most importantly, he liked company. Even if he couldn’t handle speaking or touching sometimes, Mydei liked him being in the same general area as him. Whether they were doing the same thing, one by the stove while the other helping off to the side, or doing completely opposite activities, one on their phone with the other reading a book nearby, he liked Phainon there. It was comforting to simply be present, even if not active all the time. Though, bonus points were included if he asked permission for little things like leaving the room. More were rewarded if he offered to get him anything he might need for comfort's sake.

Phainon knew, to an extent, that he had some of these quirks. In school, he’d hide in his room when he wasn’t feeling like company or bury himself in whatever he could to keep busy. That ended up being his textbooks and other educational books from the library. Those were his little quirks. Those are what made him, him.

And he did his best to help.

A few days passed by with him trying to help Mydei feel better and work through his thoughts. Though he couldn’t spend every night by his side, he carried his duties through the occasional text message, photos, and audio messages.

Of course he didn’t need to. Mydei was incessant that this was not necessary as he could handle it. But he wanted to, and since he was putting in so much effort, he was allowed to.

The night Phainon did choose to visit was spent comfortably and casually as Mydei wasn’t yet feeling his best. He kept him busy by baking a honeyed tea cake with him, going as far as to join him in shopping for the ingredients after work. He asked for more things from him, like if he could have his phone when it was off charging in another room or if he could refill his glass of whiskey when it emptied. They felt so little for him to do, but Mydei looked so grateful for the attention, effort, and care.

And as always, pleasing Mydei brought him a gentle sense of fulfillment. So when he was happy, so was Phainon.

After dinner, while they were relaxing into a quieter part of their night, he was sitting at the dining table to put their flower set together. Beside him, Mydei was looking through the instructions and sipping on his God-knows glass of whiskey. Somewhere after the fifth or sixth pour, Phainon began to lose track of how many times he refilled it. At this point, he didn’t even ask if he could, he just did.

Soft music played lightly in the background, quiet enough to miss when they spoke but loud enough to hear during silent moments.

A thump of his glass to a coaster made him turn his head, and he reached for it instinctively.

“Are you sure you should keep going, master?”

“‘m fine,” he answered slowly, but doubt filled his gut as he hesitated pulling the cup any closer. “Please, Phainon.”

“Mm… I guess,” he caved, then grabbed the half empty bottle to give him another drink. “At least you don’t work tomorrow.”

Mydei nodded. His head was resting in his hand, elbow pressed to the table as he watched him with tired eyes. It was a gaze Phainon could feel even as he twisted the cap and set it back on to its tray.

“For my master.”

“Thank you,” he returned.

His hand wrapped around the glass, and he raised it to his lips before swinging half back at once.

Phainon didn’t like watching, but he did anyway.

Mydei wiped his mouth sloppily, then shifted his attention down to the opened box full of bags and pamphlets. He brought it closer, knocking the edge against his glass before pulling bag after bag out. They were numbered to make it easier, and each was placed in order.

“Please be careful,” he commented. “My master hates a mess.”

One arm stretched to move his drink out of the way, aware that shattered glass was the last thing that needed to happen tonight.

Mydei grabbed the guide before he could after, flipping it open to look over the pictures and details. Page after page was flipped, faster than anyone could realistically read, only to be brought back to the front.

“I buy my mother bouquets of roses in shades of red since she loves them,” he said casually, and Phainon chuckled softly over his openness.

“Red roses remind me of you when I see them,” Phainon admitted to him, looking over all of the bags before opening the first one. “You’re an awfully romantic guy, you know.”

To this day, he still had no clue how Mydei never had a boyfriend before he figured out the full extent of his desires.

“Me? A romantic?” He repeated as if he didn’t understand. “You’ve got the wrong guy, Phainon.”

“No. I’ve got the right one.”

The pieces clicked and clacked over the wooden table into a mess, one that made Mydei shift and look around as if anticipating them to be all over the floor. To help ease some of that worry, Phainon quickly stored them into grouped piles of the same pieces and tucked the bag into the box to minimize the mess. Its manuel was placed in front of him once Mydei decided he was done with it.

While looking between the toy and the instructions, he began to dig the pieces out to fit them together.

He wanted to build it first to make sure he did it right, then he’d take it apart to use the glue. In his head, it’d completely minimize the risk of it falling and shattering into pieces in the future that’d inconvenience Mydei. That was his game plan.

It definitely wouldn’t all get done tonight, but that was the fun. This would be an activity they could finish into tomorrow as well.

“You’ll find that my life is void of any and all romance,” Mydei insisted, watching his fingers work. “I’m quite an unromantic person.”

Phainon’s lip tilted downwards, slightly annoyed that he would think such a thing about himself when everything Mydei did was effortlessly charming. Even if his casual actions and care didn’t have any real feelings behind them for him, that didn’t suddenly make them any less romantic of a gesture.

“Who said that to you?”

“No one,” he rushed a little too fast to say. “I simply don’t find myself to be romantic. There’s a difference between chivalrous, responsible, and romantic.”

“Romantic people tend to be both chivalrous and responsible,” he reasoned. “What makes my master think he’s not a romantic person?”

Mydei hummed thoughtfully. “I’ve never even asked someone out on a date before,” he shared with him.

Truthfully, Phainon didn't expect an answer at all, let alone one that sounded so sincere.

He clicked two blocks together, then glanced over to his dominant.

“You’ve never been on a date?” He asked in quiet disbelief. “You’ve never agreed to one either?”

That didn’t sound right to him at all.

“No.” He said it so casually and surely that Phainon had to set the pieces down to give him his full attention. “I’ve never felt the need to formally ask someone out on a date.”

“But… you’ve had past submissives before. These guys you’ve met up with, did… did you not take them out? Or did you jump from a few text messages to sending them your address?”

There was no way.

Mydei wasn’t a guy who went around sleeping with just anybody who shared a kink with him, right? He didn’t match with someone then take them home a few days later, did he? That was far too reckless for such a calculated person. There was too little thought for someone with a head as loud as his.

“What? No,” he defended himself, and a quiet breath of relief left Phainon’s lips. “I meet them up somewhere public to see what they’re like, take them to a place more private, and if it feels right, then I’ll visit their place.”

Phainon, to save some of his sanity, prayed that it was a schedule made up over weeks. He hoped there was time and effort put into protecting himself from people who might want to hurt him or take advantage of his—painfully obvious—fixation on BDSM and innate generosity. Each stage should have weeks between them, especially the last one that had him going to a random stranger’s home to do whatever they did. Sex, probably.

But he did not want to think about his dominant with some nameless, faceless man in his arms and lap. He did not want to think about his husky voice moaning someone else’s name as he came undone, then praising them for being so good.

Fuck.

Now that he was, he felt sick to the stomach.

“Somewhere public is a date,” he argued instead, tuning back into the conversation they had in an attempt to drown the thought. If his voice came out a little bit rougher, he hoped Mydei didn’t notice in his drunken state.

That was his dominant. No one else’s.

Mydei shook his head. “You have to ask someone out on a date. We simply make a plan to go to a bar one night or out for lunch some afternoon. It’s not a date.”

“How do you think a date works?” Phainon mocked him, unable to overlook how serious he seemed about the qualifications of a ‘date’.

“First of all, I ask. That’s a responsibility I'd choose to take as a dominant,” he repeated, making him roll his eyes. “If they agree, I’d bring them something like flowers or sweets, and I’d pick them up to go somewhere nice or somewhere they’d like. Then, I’d take them home.”

“That’s romantic, master.”

“That’s a theory,” Mydei corrected him, then reached to grab his drink. “I’ve never done it. That’s just what they do in movies and books, so it must be proper dating etiquette. Therefore, that’s what I would do. But I don’t exactly date, so I’ll never know how it really goes.”

A twinge of something twisted inside of his chest, aching and uncomfortable at the thought of him not wanting to date.

“Why not?” He pressed. “Can’t you have a boyfriend who is also your submissive?”

“‘m sure I could, I just…” His words trailed off for a second as he seemed to think about his response for a second. “I never felt the need to ask because we agreed a dominant and submissive relationship was fulfilling enough for us.”

“People just agree to it? Like that?”

Mydei threw back the last of his drink. “Mhm… This’ just a different kind of relationship, after all.”

Phainon's nose crinkled slightly as he looked away from him, aware of Mydei setting his glass aside.

“‘m good. No more.”

He wasn’t sure how he felt about that. These men, these strangers, Mydei had gotten involved with, while he spoke highly of the few they talked briefly about, how could he let them in his life so easily? On the other hand, how could they let Mydei into their lives so freely?

How did Mydei trust them the way he trusted him? The ways in which he opened up to him, how could he do that with just anyone willing to be his submissive?

How did they trust Mydei the way he trusted him? This was intense, and it required so much reassurance to uphold, how could anyone give someone that commitment so casually?

“You’ve got a look on your face,” Mydei teased him playfully, and he hummed quietly. “Spit it out for me. What’s going on in that pretty head?”

“The way you treat me, you treated them despite not knowing them at all, right?” He accused. The words were even more uncomfortable to say out loud, as if they were a hammer coming to smash the untouchable image he saw in the mirror. “I’ve known you for so long, but what’s the difference between me and them if you can do this for anyone?”

Amber eyes looked up and down his face, taking in the lip between his teeth and the narrowed gaze being sharpened at him.

Mydei looked like he had too much to drink. His face was slightly rosy, tinted a cute shade of rose that matched the hair swept over his nose. The way he looked back at him was caught somewhere in between amusement, exhaustion, and kindness. His sudden openness tonight was the direct result of too many glasses, but Phainon didn’t care about specifics right now. He just wanted to know more.

For a moment, he was silent. It was the world’s longest moment and loudest silence as they stared at one another.

“You’re my best friend,” he said simply.

Phainon scoffed. “That’s not what I wanted to hear.”

Mydei was so good at pointing out the obvious and keeping things vague, wasn’t he?

It was, technically, still an answer, but he had to know that it wasn’t satisfying enough on its own. It wasn’t the right kind of answer he was looking for in response to a question that heavily handed.

“‘m not finished,” his dominant said firmly, making him purse his lips tightly to bite back what he wanted to say. “Can I continue?”

He nodded, waiting.

“The biggest difference is that this isn’t really sexual. It is, but also, not really,” he pointed out. “This is a lot more domestic than I thought it’d be.”

His jaw tightened over that, and a flare of hurt was lit inside of his chest.

“So, what? The second you nail me, I'm going to become the same as anyone else?” Phainon hissed, bitter at the thought of going from someone precious to someone disposable.

“Watch your mouth,” Mydei snapped while sitting up. “Who do you think I am, and who do you think you’re talking to like that?”

The restraint he usually practiced while completely sober was nowhere to be seen. His words were sharpened to a point, one they hardly ever took. Each pierced through skin, stitching his lips shut and leaving him only able to frown.

Phainon looked away from him as he physically bit his tongue harder, trying to calm himself down and remind himself Mydei wasn’t that kind of person. He wouldn’t do that. His heart was too big for his own chest, and if he ever got the chance to have sex with him, he’d never just use him.

He wasn’t a toy. He was someone special and dear to him, and that didn't just go away during their sexual encounters. If they went all the way, it’d still never go away.

Sometimes he hated the disconnect between his mouth and his head.

“I’m getting real tired of reminding you to keep your attitude in check,” Mydei warned him, and he nodded weakly. “I meant to say that I’ve never had a sub who enjoyed the casual side of this so much. I’m used to a lot of sex and sexually charged situations.”

His gaze dropped to the table as guilt seeped into his chest for accusing him of being someone so cruel.

“That’s just not how we are though,” he bit, still upset but not speaking as roughly as before. “The person I am around you is different from who I was with my past submissives. Everything’s different, and it’s frustrating.”

“Why?”

“I don’t know,” he answered.

“My master doesn’t usually like that answer,” he reminded him, then glanced back at him.

When their eyes met, Mydei took a deep breath and then shook his head as if trying to dispel the frustration. With eyes closed, he willed himself to relax his jaw and his pinched eyebrows.

“For once, I… I have someone personal to me catering to me,” Mydei clarified. Liquor stained his breath when he exhaled shakily, pungent and thick. “With strangers, if it didn’t work out, I never had to see them again. If I never saw them again, my life didn’t really change much. I might be sad for a while, but it won’t break me.”

Even if it might be terrible, Phainon’s heart throbbed at the thought that he was someone Mydei couldn’t risk losing.

No one else was as important as him. No one else who has been in this spot held a candle to him. It brought about a sickening sense of fulfillment, a horrible flood of pride and power, and the heat made his face rosy with a blush.

“You being someone close to me fills me with so much desire,” he confessed. “I wanna give you everything you ask of me, and I wanna share this with you so badly. It’s a bit… lonely… not feeling connected to the person I do this with, and now that I’ve got it, it feels like I’m learning all over again.”

Mydei’s fist then balled tightly over the table, shaking from the strength of his grip like he was trying to hold himself back. If Phainon didn’t know him as well as he did, he would have thought he’d slam it into the table from just how frustrated he was beginning to look.

Not at him, but at himself. Most of his grievances seemed to come from himself.

“But if I mess up, it’s all over. So I know I need to be stronger than I have been.” His voice then raised. “Tch… I know how to bite my tongue and move on too! I’ve done it so many times in the past that people called me robotic! But it’s so hard to do that with you during this… It makes me so fucking mad that I have so little control over myself when I’m usually so good at it.”

He watched his fist slowly and carefully open. His fingers curled and shook as if an invisible force were holding them down, as if it hurt to let the anger go. Crescent shapes were embedded into his palms, and Mydei sighed to himself before placing his hand flat to the table.

“I promised that you would be my… my best friend first and my submissive-in-training second,” he recalled carefully, voice weak. “I promised I wouldn’t become someone you didn’t recognize anymore. I promised.”

Another throb struck him in the chest, sharp and dangerous. Whatever air was left in his lungs was held tightly, leaving no room to escape or accept more in.

He remembered that? The little joke he made while they wrote up a bunch of rules and expectations in his living room, Mydei took it right to heart. He peeled back the forced and fake humor when he said it, noticed the insecurity and truth behind it, and internalized the plea. From the moment he said it, he ingrained it into himself.

“Every time I get too excited, every time I fuck up and step over your boundaries, I take a step closer into becoming someone we both don’t know. What’s… wrong with me?” He whispered while bringing his hands to his head. “If I can’t learn to bite this desire back, I don’t deserve to practice this. A selfish, out of control, liar has no place claiming responsibility over someone else…”

“You’re not,” Phainon protested. “The fact you try so hard for other people means that you’re not selfish. Everything you do, you do for someone else.”

Mydei sucked in a sharp breath as he held his head tightly, fingers curled into his hair to pull like those weren’t the words he needed to hear.

“If you make a mistake, you do your best to fix it. If you notice someone’s in distress, you step in right away. Would a selfish person do that every single day?” He asked him, but his shoulders only shrunk in on themselves.

“What kind of ‘supportive’ guy wants to see the person closest to him pushed to his limits? Especially ones he doesn't even know?” He choked out.

Sure, it was intimidating.

Sometimes when Mydei got fired up, it was hard not to feel nervous about all of the things he wanted to try with him because of how new they were. But it wasn’t selfish to want to share his passions with someone willing to listen, learn, or take part in. It wasn’t ‘bad’ to want him to enjoy this, to love this.

“The kind of guy who knows he’ll take care of his every need immediately after,” Phainon reasoned, trying to get through to him. “We made some mistakes, but we know better now. You know how to take care of me after we do something, and I realized that if I’m not clear with how I feel about things, both of us get hurt. A selfish person wouldn't care about those things. He’d take what he wanted and leave.”

He didn’t respond, but that was okay. It wasn’t necessary.

Phainon stood up out of his seat slowly, and he gently set a hand on Mydei’s shoulder before tapping.

“Can you sit up for me real quick, master?” He asked gently, and Mydei took a deep breath before sitting up.

He looked up at him, and Phainon looked down at his lap for a moment. The singular glance had the chair scooting back in silent invitation, encouraging him to take a seat and give him a place to calm down. Which he took slowly, cautious of overwhelming him, but happily, as he enjoyed being close to him.

Two hands held his face, and he looked down into his distracted gaze.

“Stop calling yourself something you’re not,” he scolded him. “By saying you’re this terrible person pushing your wants onto me, that implies you’re forcing me to do this for you.”

“Aren’t I?”

Phainon scoffed as a blossom of hurt and disbelief bloomed inside of his ribs.

“Was someone else in my apartment with you when we were making our rules? Was there a gun to my head when I woke up early and decided to suck you off?” He demanded. “How could you think I don’t want this after all that I’ve done for you? All that I’ve said I wanted to do? Are you stupid?”

Mydei’s eyes narrowed. “Attitude.”

“I’m sorry for my tone, but that was a stupid question to ask me, master,” he mocked him, holding his ground. “I don’t have to do anything, but I want to. Do you think I’d want to submit my effort and body to someone who didn’t give a damn about anyone but himself?”

Did he think he was that pathetic? That he was so desperate for it, anyone could fill his shoes?

“I give it to you because you deserve it,” Phainon said, glancing down at the way his hands were limp by his sides. “Look. You’re not even touching me because I haven’t asked you to. Because it matters to you even if it's as simple as a hug. Because you care about overstepping even if you know all you want is to be held right now. Isn’t that thoughtful of him?”

Those softening eyes looked over his body, over the black hoodie he borrowed and the way he sat comfortably over his lap.

Phainon knew he wanted it. He could see that he craved to burrow himself into his body and hold him so tightly that it was hard to breathe. It was written all over his face and his twitching hands.

A breath fell between them, and he willed his frustration to take a seat on the back burner. Instead, his lip twitched upward.

“Does my master want to hold me?” A nod followed. “Can you please hug me nice and tightly then?”

Mydei wrapped his arms around him the very moment he finished asking, fingers clutching the hood draped by his shoulder blades before tucking into his chest. His face nuzzled so deeply to the point he wondered if he could use his ribs to hide inside of.

“My master’s cute when he hides like this,” he chuckled, sliding his fingers into his hair before brushing through it slowly. Thick, two-toned locks cascaded over his knuckles, silky and well groomed when he fanned the ends out.

Had this been a few months ago, he never would have known Mydei bottled up so much responsibility inside of himself. He came across as so put together that it was so shocking to see him so pulled apart, and he didn’t let anyone get too deep into his personal affairs. Yet here he was, present through the days it was taking for him to feel better.

That Mydei worked endlessly, and he spent his free time at home unless someone called him to come out. Never did he offer first unless it was to drop something off, always waiting to be invited instead of just assuming it was okay to come around. He liked to drink with dinner, and he liked to talk about everyone else to keep the conversations away from him. If he did talk about himself, it was about looking after himself or being with his mother.

His best friend dressed semi-professionally wherever he went in case someone saw him, and he treated himself to luxuries like expensive jewelry and shoes. They made him look well-kept. They made him look like someone too busy to stop and have a conversation with, especially with his usually stoic demeanor. It protected his privacy to come off as better than anyone else, even if he didn’t feel that way inside.

Never would he have guessed that Mydei could also be the same one who was currently non-verbal inside of his chest.

Phainon brought his face closer. Soft lips pressed over the top of his golden head gently, ignoring the way his collar lightly pressed into his throat from the bend. But they didn’t pucker for a kiss. All he did was plant them there, breathing in the scent of Mydei’s fancy hair care mask mixed with his shampoo.

His fingers never stopped rubbing his scalp and playing with his hair, fixated on moving in a moment so still. His eyes closed in peace, unsure what to say to him next.

All of the things he wanted to say tonight were already laid out between them. If there was more, he couldn’t think it up. And if he couldn’t think it up, then they must not be that important.

But that was okay too. They didn’t need to talk anymore. Mydei just needed him to be there in his arms, and he could have him for as long as he needed.

—

That next morning, as they stood in his empty roof-top gym, rather than immediately working out like he usually did, Phainon took a seat on the ground and admired the soft, golden glow around them. His arms wrapped around his knees, pulling them to his chest. The cool, crisp breeze tickled his nose and brushed the hair from his face.

No one was typically here this early. They joined towards the end of their work out, when the morning matured a little bit more. They’d have their headphones on and hyper-focused on themselves, never giving them any attention.

It was just him and Mydei on top of his building, the sunrise they loved to watch, and whatever they wanted to do that particular morning.

“Feeling lazy?” Mydei teased him, standing beside him with one hand on top of his head.

“Can I ask you something?”

“Always,” he told him. “I encourage you to ask for whatever you need or want. What’s up?”

“Did you do this with anyone before?” He asked, leaning into his leg while admiring the sky. “Have you brought anyone up here to work out with? Anyone at all?”

Mydei chuckled softly. “No, Phainon. I like to wake up at the crack of dawn to work out for hours, and you’re the only person who would too. No sane person willingly does this.”

A smile tugged on his mouth over the answer.

“I like this,” he agreed, and Mydei squatted down beside him to be closer. “I also like that no one else has done this with you.”

“Do you?” He teased quietly as Phainon turned to look at him. “Possessive little prince.”

Maybe.

It brought him so much comfort to know that there were things exclusive to just him and Mydei. This was a privilege reserved for him, and it wasn’t some rinse-and-repeat scheme he pulled on people in the past. He wasn’t just anyone.

More than just casual bondage around his home and domestic service, the other things they did were theirs alone. That made them even more special to share.

“What else?” He wondered.

“I didn’t allow my other subs to take my clothes home,” he brought up, and Phainon nodded. “I didn’t let them come over as much as you do either. Typically, I went to their place.”

“… So, my key…?”

“Only you have a key to my home,” he shared with him, and that made him pull his knees closer to his body. “You are the only person in my life who needs that much access to me and my things.”

He smiled wider.

The hand on his head lowered, and he craned his neck when he felt it inch closer. He didn’t have his collar on because this was still a public space. He chose not to wear his choker since his collar would just be clicked on inside of Mydei’s home again. The palm curled around his throat, taking advantage of the underdressed skin to cup gently. Fingers pressed beneath his jaw, keeping his chin lifted.

Mydei’s eyes raked over his face, meeting his eyes before making their way down. He watched him, aware of their weight but pretending not to notice.

“Do you remember last night?”

“It’ll take more than that to get a man like me black-out drunk,” he mused. “I’ve never been drunk enough to forget what I did the night before.”

“Then, you remember what I said about us…” Phainon trailed off. “About if we ever… you know… had sex…”

Mydei gave a single nod of the head. “You need to stop thinking poorly of yourself and of me. I would never treat you with anything less than what you deserve.”

“That’s not it. I don’t think I’m lesser than anyone, actually,” he confessed. “It’s more like… I think I’m better than them.”

“You ‘think’?”

He rolled his eyes. “Yeah. I think I’m better than them, and that’s why I don’t like being compared to them. After all, you said so yourself, this is different with me because we were already close. This is different with me because you have something to lose.”

The hand on his neck gently pinched as if to warn him of his next choice words, and he twitched his shoulder briefly to combat it before relaxing it.

“You won’t lose me,” he reassured him. “I want to be here with you, master.”

“I’m glad.”

While those fingers loosened around his throat, they began dragging slowly against his skin to release him. He already missed the heat of his touch the very moment they broke apart, wishing they could’ve stayed like that for a little bit longer.

Mydei stood, then held that same hand out for him to take.

“But you shouldn’t go around thinking you’re better than anyone else around you,” he advised. “Confidence in yourself is a good trait to have. Arrogance is not.”

“Is that your way of telling me I’m not better than any of your exes?” He mused, reaching to grasp his hand. Palm to palm, thumb crossed over thumb, he squeezed down tightly for a pull.

“Not all relationships end poorly.”

“That’s not what I asked,” Phainon pointed out while lifting himself off of the ground. “Am I better? Is what we have better than what you had in the past?”

Mydei’s eyebrow lifted, staring at him as if he didn’t expect him to ask that so blatantly. But how could he not? This confidence and openness was something he instilled in him. He coaxed him into learning how to ask whatever was on his mind, so there was no point in him being surprised with what came out.

Standing eye to eye, Phainon tilted his head innocently as Mydei’s mouth tilted upwards slightly. Just the smallest lift of that grin underneath the gleaming morning sun made his stomach flutter terribly.

“They were good men at heart. If it ended nicely, it was mutual. If it went wrong, I was to blame for being so naive,” Mydei shared, still dodging his question. “Not all of them were necessarily bad, Phainon.”

“Am I better?”

The grip around his hand tightened for a second, and it looked almost as if Mydei didn’t want to answer that. A small ache burned a hole through his stomach at the thought of someone giving him what he couldn’t, of someone being better than him despite all that he was in Mydei’s eyes.

But then he nodded, and the humbling thought shattered right then and there. Pride burst throughout his chest.

“You’re better, Phainon,” he agreed softly, feeding into his ego.

“And you didn’t need a drop of alcohol to tell me how you feel,” he teased him. “Was that so hard, master?”

“I don’t like your condescending tone.”

He laughed, then felt his opposite hand grip his face. Fingertips dipped into his cheeks, pinching them firmly before tapping his cheek.

“Be good,” he chided. Phainon felt a tingle burn underneath his skin from both the slap, the early morning air, and his own interest. “Are you going to be good?”

“I can be.”

Another light handed smack clapped against his cheek, and he pushed his tongue to his cheek as the tingle became a buzz. Electricity burned through his nerves like a live wire, coursing through his body from cheek to chest to groin. Being underneath Mydei’s firm and narrowed gaze only made it burn hotter, as he liked when he held every ounce of his dominant’s attention.

“Are you going to be good?” Mydei repeated.

“Do you… know how hard it is waking up and being unable to relieve myself?” Phainon whispered, tucking into his hand. “If you keep this up, I won’t want to work out. You’re… This is putting me in a different kind of mood…”

“If you ask, I’m going to say ‘no’. I’m not in the mood for sex, just teasing you.”

A soft groan left his lips as he pulled away from his hand, hoping to save himself the frustration of getting worked up just to wait it out. It was torture every time.

“Ah ah.” Mydei snapped his fingers beside him, then held his palm in a cup shape. “Put your face back in my hand. Now.”

He tilted back into it, still looking up at him.

“Why don’t you ever ask me for relief?”

“My hands aren’t enough fun,” he murmured, then glanced at the door to make sure they were still alone. “If I’m going to go through the whole process of asking, I don’t want to do it by myself, master.”

The thumb on his chin lightly brushed his bottom lip, and he took a deep breath to try and calm himself down.

“Ask while you’re here so I may help you,” he said simply.

“You haven't been feeling good recently, and I usually get so caught up in everything else that it just doesn’t matter as much,” he admitted. “Most of the feeling comes when I remember that I can’t. I don’t have a choice even if I don’t want to, and it just gets me worked up even more.”

“Does it?” Mydei feigned sympathy. “Oh, my poor…” His palm tapped to his cheek. “… poor…” And again. “… little prince.”

Shaky breaths left his lips, and he glanced back to his eyes.

“Maybe if you were good last night and didn’t speak poorly of us both, I’d suck it up and get you off when we finished up.” Mydei then tsk’ed. “Maybe if you had some shame and humility in telling me how big that ego has grown, I’d have let you go about your day normally.”

Phainon immediately shot his gaze back to the door upon seeing it swing open from his peripheral vision. Vigilant. He pulled back slowly, and Mydei tucked his hand into his gym shorts before leaning in to whisper.

“You are what I allow you to be,” he reminded him quietly. “If I want a spoiled prince, I’ll cater to one. But if I want a denied slut, I’m going to make one.”

His eyes followed the stranger as she fixed her too-big glasses and checked a compact mirror. She was so far away that he knew she couldn’t hear them, and two guys just standing around wasn’t incriminating at all. They were just talking. But the twist of anxiety and arousal in his gut at the prospect of getting caught was too strong.

Just standing here and listening to Mydei’s casually cruel words was making his head feel fuzzy, and his pants were not going to hide the entirety of his boner if he kept thinking about it. But he couldn’t stop.

“Are you hitting your shoulders and chest today?” Mydei asked, pulling back to grin at him. “I’ll spot you.”

Laying on that bench with his dick in front of his face as he stood over him was going to be Hell. Especially since he really, really liked the scent of his skin, and working out only made it stronger.

“I’m not gonna be able to lift that bar,” he warned him. “Mas… —Mydei, I’m not… gonna be able to focus enough to be safe with weights like that.”

“Shame,” he said. “I was looking forward to it. Play it by ear then. Do what’s comfortable, and if you need my help, just let me know.”

Phainon nodded, then looked down at his body when he turned around. The leggings hugging his legs really highlighted his thick calves, and he almost wanted to curse his shorts for hiding the way they’d do the same for his thighs and ass. It was a curse.

One hand covered his face, and he groaned quietly before sneaking one more peak at the way his long sleeved compression shirt was glued to every inch of his upper body. He could make out his shoulders when he walked, each muscle in his arms, then the twist of his waist when he turned around to look back at him.

He was going to crush himself with a dumbbell. He was going to get distracted and get flung off of a treadmill. He was going to hit his shoe on the stair climb, then smack his head into the machine.

“Don’t be lazy, Phainon!” Mydei called to him, and he walked over to him. When close enough, he glanced between him briefly before looking right at him. “Good boy.”

An involuntary whine clawed its way up his throat.

He was going to die up here, and it’d be Mydei’s fault for being the biggest distraction known to man kind.
