Chapter Notes

dont ask how many times i rewrote this and drafted this. or how little sleep i got for this.

my heart strings were not just tugged, but yanked.

also, im certain i mentioned it, but cyrene and phainon were childhood friends before he moved around middle school/highschool where he met mydei and the others. then cyrene came to live with him/his family for college, and now she stays in his apartment. and has for awhile. but she comes and goes to travel back and forth

It was Monday morning when he woke up to a text from Mydei, one that told him that he was going to stay over that night. He wasn’t asking, either. That text was a demand, flat out and not even attempting to masquerade as anything else.

As if he planned to go against it anyway. Spending time with him was his favorite thing to do, and if he was given an order, he wanted to follow through with it.

“Hey, ‘rene?” He asked after coming back from his morning run, and she hummed sleepily while holding her pink toothbrush still. “I’m gonna be at De’s tonight again. Don’t wait up, ‘kay?”

“What’s over there?” she mumbled, eyes closed and toothpaste dripping down the corner of her lips. “Are you gonna be sleeping over again?”

“Yeah, I’ll be home tomorrow morning.”

“Hm…”

Phainon watched as her head tilted, as she moved her toothbrush and pushed the messy beadhead from her face. One eye peaked open, squinting to look up at him as it wasn't yet used to the brightness in their apartment.

“Can I ask you something, Phai?” She asked, the sound slurred and muffled by her full mouth. “What’s the deal?”

“It’s kinda rude to talk with a full mouth,” he mused, and she groaned before stomping to the bathroom to spit into the sink.

“I said, what’s the deal?” She repeated, then rubbed her eyes to better see him. “You’re up so early all the time now, even on days you work. It’s a little bit weird. Like just a smidge.”

Phainon forced a smile as she pinched her fingers together to emphasize a ‘smidge’.

Guilt struck him right in the depths of his stomach for the truths he was about to stretch. It wasn't as if he could tell her that he had rules to follow and expectations to meet, so he had to come up with something.

“Are they loud?” He deflected. “I can turn them down.”

Her head shook at that. “No, they’re not loud at all. I just hear the front door open and close sometimes when I’m in bed, then your shoes hitting the stairs way earlier than I’m used to."

“I’ve just been on top of my exercise recently,” he brushed off, keeping it short and simple. “It’s good to keep active. Since I’m too tired after work to commit, the morning is the best time to get it done.”

At least that wasn’t a lie. He really was tired after work, and that typically made him not want to do anything. Who wanted to go on a run or work out after a full shift of being on their feet?

But working out in the mornings with Mydei was refreshing and left him more energetic, so he changed it to match even when he was alone.

“It’s just weird. It feels like I left to visit my parents and came back to someone completely different than I remember,” she sighed dramatically, then eyed his outfit. While examining it, a soft smile tugged on her lips. “Well, you really do still wear this disaster of a hoodie… I guess you weren’t lying that time.”

One hand grabbed half of his zip-up hoodie, then closed it around half of his chest gently.

“All I did was try to change a few things that weren’t good for me, that’s all. I’m still me.”

Her eyebrows furrowed as she fisted his sweater tighter, visibly confused by that statement. “Like?” She pressed curiously.

Damn.

Phainon was really hoping she wouldn’t press too deep to keep him from lying too much, but she wouldn’t be his best friend if she didn’t. That was who she was, a curious little cat who liked to explore and paw at her surroundings no matter where it took her.

And it really wasn’t like him at all to be so vague with her. He could tell she noticed even if she didn’t say anything.

“Like…” Phainon struggled to word his thoughts without giving away too much information. “I don’t have to sleep at three in the morning, rush to get to work, then crash right when I get home. That’s not very healthy, you know? I could tackle my day in a better way than that, and I’m trying to learn.”

Cyrene eyed him closely while listening. Then, she nodded slowly.

“It’s not,” she agreed with him gently. “But it’s familiar. We used to stay up late watching dumb videos or old movies, now you’re in your room before I even remember to brush my teeth. It’s, honestly, a bit weird to see and get used to it.”

His hand cupped hers, and she met his eyes as he gave it a reassuring squeeze. The light touch made her grip loosen, sliding slowly down the length of the zipper as if too weak to hold on. He stopped it before it passed his waist, and he held them both there for a moment as a beat of silence passed.

“Do you hate it?” He wondered while watching her expression slowly shift from confusion to guilt. “The changes and all of that… Do you look at me and think it’s something bad?”

It didn’t feel bad to him as he took it day after day. It felt natural by now, like he couldn’t imagine a different way to live. If anything, Mydei often told him this whole arrangement was encouraging him to grow as a person, and their other friends threw words like ‘glowing’ and ‘confident’ around when they looked at him. Feelings became easier on the chest. Thoughts tasted better in his mouth.

But she said he shouldn’t change for anyone’s attention. He should stay true to himself, as someone who was worth his time would like him the way he was. It was cliche, but objectively true.

In his eyes, he didn’t change much inside, but it wasn’t as if he had a side-by-side comparison of himself from day one until now. Did she see him and hate the person he was slowly becoming? Was he really that much different from who he used to be?

Cyrene immediately shook her head, and he bit back his nerves to remind himself to stay calm. To stay cool.

He was okay. It would be okay.

This thing between him and Mydei was okay because he asked for it, pushed for it, and accepted it.

“Of course I don’t hate it. I’m just… not used to it,” she defended herself. “I can’t hate you for trying to live a healthier life, dummy. It’s not a bad thing to clean your act up and start looking out for yourself…”

Phainon couldn’t help but feel like there was something she wasn’t telling him, but it would be hypocritical of him to dig deeper, wouldn’t it? She wasn’t obligated to tell him everything she thought of, did, and felt. That was her business, and she could keep it as close and as dear as possible.

In return, he knew he wasn’t held to that same exact standard, yet it felt… wrong to hide things from her. Even if they were both allowed that privacy, it was natural to simply come clean and share everything with each other. The concept of ‘TMI’ was long forgotten after living together.

Cyrene noticed his expression, then glanced away briefly while biting on her bottom lip. Within seconds, she looked back up at him and held his sweater tighter.

“Mydei’s helping you do this, right…?”

He hummed in agreement, feeling a tickle of fear inch throughout his body from the mention of his name and involvement.

“That’s really nice of him.” She accepted that silent response with a soft giggle, but the sound wasn’t quite as sweet as it usually was. This was almost forced, like the way he laughed when things got too uncomfortable or too much for him to handle at once. “He’s been with you a lot recently too since I’ve come back. Did he talk you into some kinda health kick?”

Unlike the last time this conversation came up, now it sounded as if she was pointing her finger in Mydei’s direction. Cyrene wasn’t just comparing him to Mydei’s likeliness anymore. She was connecting the dots between them and accusing the man of trying to change him. This change wasn’t an influence as much as it was coercion.

In her eyes, did she think he was being forced into this?

“I should take better care of myself, that's all,” Phainon defended him, hoping to shift the narrative in her head. “He’s like that with everyone, you know. The wellbeing of his friends matters to him, and I care about how he feels.”

“That does sound like him,” Cyrene agreed simply. “He’s always telling everyone to look after themselves or checking in on them himself. Cifera said he’s like an annoying older brother who doesn't know when to back off.”

“Well, Cifera’s left alone often with Aglaea traveling for work,” he reminded her. “De makes sure she’s not missing her too much.”

Cifera probably didn’t want anyone to know about the closeness of their friendship, which was why she tried so hard to mask herself with makeup, humor, and teasing. If she wanted to share her problems with them, she would. If Cyrene didn’t know about them, then he didn’t want to be the one to tell her.

“Cassie said he’s a very mature person who appreciates quiet things in life,” she added, but he didn’t quite understand why that mattered. “They talk a lot about things other people might find boring, like flowers, art, and cats. Apparently he doesn't go out much though, just when he takes his mom out.”

His shoulders shrugged weakly. “Mydei’s the kinda guy who likes being at home. If he isn’t invited out or bearing gifts for someone, he won’t just show up uninvited.”

He was never the overly social type. Though he didn’t outright reject people’s advances, once a civil or polite exchange ended, he didn’t care to continue it if it didn't interest him. If asked, he showed up on time and as present as can be. If not, he kept completely to himself. That was it. Was that suddenly wrong?

“Hyacine said he used to dig into her medical knowledge with all kinds of questions. Apparently the human body is interesting to him,” she shared.

“You’re a writer, and he picks your brain to talk about what you do as well. What’s that supposed to mean?” He asked, still not grasping what she was trying prove.

Of course Mydei was interested in her area of expertise. When pushing people to their limits and looking after them, there were certain things he needed to know. The parts of the body that were overly delicate, the most common ailments and how to treat them, and how to keep both himself and his partner healthy were key factors in what he practiced. There were anatomy books in his bookshelf too that proved his dedication, but it must have been nicer to consult a friend than a piece of paper.

“The girls all agreed he’s this perfect person—”

Mydei was gold like the collar around his neck and the sun tucked into the sky. It was wrapped around him like a reminder that he’d never be alone and someone was always in his corner. It bright over all of the dark feelings he tried to hide inside of him and warm over his skin like a school girl’s blush. If Mydei tried to touch him again, if he mocked him and pushed his buttons to see him squirm even more, there was no doubt in his mind that he’d let him. This body was his, and so long as he loved him, took care of him, and treated him well, he could continue to have it in any way he liked.

Love and submission was proving to be a dangerous combination, wasn’t it?

—

His grievances didn’t last for long, however.

Between listening to fun, upbeat music with the windows down, sending Mydei as many selfies as he asked for, and picking a few things up for himself, Cyrene, and the apartment, it was easy to push aside that clawing desire. Mydei texted him sweetly too. Instead of teasing him even more like he sometimes did, he told him that the sun made his eyes look even prettier when it hit them and the sweet, taro and pudding drink he picked up looked pretty— even if the lavender and gold colors were atrocious together. But that was his Phainon, a weirdo.

Phainon also grabbed a drink for Cyrene, one that was strawberry and peach flavored. He was tempted to take a sip of it, but ultimately refrained no matter how sweet and delicious it looked. If he could hardly hold himself back, surely his best friend with an even worse sweet tooth than his would love it.

When going home, with his arms full of grocery bags for dinner and both drinks carefully balanced in one hand, the first thing he heard was clicking from a laptop keyboard. The first thing he thought of was that she was here as she usually was and doing what she usually did like nothing was wrong in the world. Each key was pressed in rapid speed, and the scent of toasted blueberry bagels filled his nose meaning she ate already.

As the door shut, he took a deep breath and looked at the woman curled into the couch.

Her too-long hair was clipped up into a balled mess, and her slim glasses dropped to the tip of her nose when she tilted her head down to look up at him. The yellow shirt she had on was one she had stolen from him at some point in their lifetime, and it was old judging by the crackled, black smiley design on the chest.

One brief look was all it took before she immediately shifted her attention back to the screen of her laptop. It lasted no more than half a second.

“Hey…” Phainon greeted her, but her lips pursed tightly as her clicking grew louder. “I… uh… called into work today. We were running low on some things, and I had to put gas, clean out my car, and… Well, I wanted to talk to you…”

Her eyes stayed focused where they were, on her book.

“My co-worker might be mad. She tells me I’m the highlight of that job.” His chuckle felt more forced than anything, and it died just as quickly as it started. “Hysilens might toss me into the sea at some point. So, if you don’t hear from me… glub glub.”

There was no response. Not even a smile.

“How’s auntie and uncle?” He asked suddenly, then heard her spam a button repeatedly. “Have you talked to them recently?”

“They’re fine.”

“Good… That’s good…”

Awkwardness like none other settled between them, and he nodded before walking towards where she sat. Not even his approaching figure made her look away from the screen.

“I bought you this while I was out. You love sweet tea,” Phainon told her as both plastic cups touched the glass coffee table. “Peach with extra strawberry pearls. You like the popping ones, right?”

“You didn’t have to.”

“I wanted to.”

The clicking and clacking continued, making him sigh quietly to himself before walking towards the kitchen with his bags. While setting them down, he began to unpack the items and fold the paper bags away to throw out later. And since he was already there, he also placed the unopened bottle of soda left on the counter in the fridge, as he was sure she probably just forgot to do it herself.

Sometimes she did that. She grabbed things from the pantry, got distracted, and left them on the counter. If they were ever completely cleared off, that meant she was back at home with her parents.

“I’m making dinner tonight too! Are you gonna be here, or did you have plans?” He called out, looking at the ingredients. “If you’re gonna be with the girls, I don’t need to cook as much.”

“Don’t make me anything,” she called back, and he turned his head slightly in the direction of their living room. “I’m not hungry.”

“This is for dinner. That’s hours from now.”

“I’m not gonna be hungry then either.”

That was wrong. Cyrene was always hungry, and she never passed up an opportunity for him to cook her dinner. Especially since they both knew she’d just snack the night away or have a simple sandwich if he didn’t. Because she’d forget to eat, or tell herself she’ll eat later, only for ‘later’ to never come.

“You’re lying.”

She didn’t respond after that, and he took a deep breath before covering his face with his hands. They rubbed slowly, lining the sides of his nose before dragging down his cheeks.

If Mydei were here, what would he say to get someone to respond to him? He controlled the room so effortlessly all the time, and while he didn’t want to control her, he wanted her to talk to him. This cold shoulder treatment was both aching and annoying when he just wanted to fix things.

“Skipping meals is bad for you, ‘rene. You shouldn’t be so neglectful.”

Nothing.

“I’m going to make you food later anyway, and you better eat it. Don't let your stubbornness affect your health.”

Silence.

Frustrated, Phainon left the kitchen to stand by the wall separating them. His arms crossed over his chest, and he bit down on his tongue while watching her type away. Unbothered.

“What are you writing about that’s so interesting right now?” He asked, trying to calm himself down. “Is it the story about the guy lost in time waiting for his lover to come back? Or the one about the lady who seized a king’s crown and fell for her knight?”

Her clicking stopped.

“The first love story is pretty sad. Imagine waiting thousands of years just for your partner to come back…” He trailed off in an attempt to get her to speak. “Or imagine falling in love with someone you can’t have because you’re in the middle of governing a war.”

“What are you doing, Phainon?” She finally said, not even looking at him. “You asked me to mind my business, and I am. I’m leaving you alone like you told me to, yet you’re the one trying to pry now.”

His stomach dropped as she clicked her laptop closed.

“I… didn't mean it like that,” he tried to explain himself, guilty from making her feel as if she needed to ignore him. “Cyrene, I never meant to yell at you or make you feel bad about yourself. And I never meant to compare you and Mydei because that’s just… not possible.”

“I don’t wanna hear this,” she mumbled. “Save it.”

He watched as she tucked the device to her chest and stood up, ignoring the phone that fell, the tea he had bought for her, and the blankets her legs were wrapped up in. All she did was keep her head down and then walk, hoping to make it past him quickly and quietly. But how could he just let her run and leave this unresolved?

“Cyrene, come on.” One hand reached to grab her by the oversized sleeve, and she stopped. “Please. I don’t wanna argue with you. I don’t want you to… to ignore me, and I don’t wannna feel like I’m begging for attention. Can’t we just talk like adults?”

But she was just as stubborn as he could be sometimes.

“I’m minding my own business,” she repeated. “I’m not gonna b-be nosy or pretend like I own you anymore. I get it, Phainon, okay? Just… let me do my thing, and you can do your thing, and we don’t have to be in each other’s business like that anymore.”

He groaned loudly. “That’s not what I meant!”

“That’s what you said.”

“I was angry! You know I say stupid things when I’m upset, and what you did really pissed me off, Cyrene,” he tried to explain, exasperated. “You went snooping around behind our backs!”

“I really don’t wanna talk about—”

“And you stood here accusing Mydei and I of being people we aren’t. It felt like you were rejecting us both when we did nothing wrong," Phainon confessed, cutting her off. “You made it sound so bad, like Mydei’s some kind of puppeteer and he’s got me by the strings. But it’s not like that! I’m not… weak, Cyrene! I’m not going to roll over and just let someone walk all over me—even if I love Mydei.”

At one point, Mydei explained to him that his submission was not to be confused with weakness. Following rules and completing the tasks asked of him didn’t mean he was less than the one who set them up. Kneeling and allowing himself to be small, vulnerable, and powerless didn’t make him any less strong or capable of a man. It was a conversation that stuck with him since the moment they had it, and it changed the way he saw their dynamic completely.

Being told that adhering to these routines made him someone weak, someone being taken advantage of, felt a lot like a slap in the face to everything he’s learned and tried to let go of. Telling him Mydei was someone he needed to be careful of just reminded him of how devastated he was over the idea of actually hurting him. And it hurt. It made him angry.

“Can you say something, ‘rene? I’m trying here, okay?”

With her back still to him and head hung low, a light twitch shook her small shoulders. The sound of her sniffling made his heart ache, and he eased the fist wrapped up in her shirt.

“I-I didn’t mean to make you cry…”

“Mydei’s s-so intimidating sometimes… He walks in and all eyes are on him like he controls the room just standing there—no need to even speak.” Her voice was small and quiet, like she had felt this way for a while but was never able to tell him that. “He’s so secretive, and he clearly keeps everyone at a certain distance besides you. He’s all over you, and it's been worse as of lately like he can’t be away from you. Now, he’s talking you into changing your life and your style to suit him better. It’s… scary, Phainon.”

“… Is it?” He asked gently, not wanting to shoot her feelings down even if he craved to just yell that she’s got it all wrong. “What can I do to make it less scary for you? I’ll explain it to you if you ask because I don’t wanna have to pick between my best friends. Don’t turn this into a-a battle between you and him—”

“I’m not!”

“Then why does it feel that way?” Phainon insisted. “How can I get you to drop the suspicions and just… believe in us?”

She shrugged quickly and violently. “I don't know, Phainon! Maybe start with… with… God. Why does he even want to change you so badly? What does that do for him when he has it all already?”

The fingers on the shirt dropped when he realized she wasn’t going to walk away anymore.

“Mydei’s not changing me. I’m choosing to do things a little bit differently,” Phainon answered firmly, sick of the idea that he was helpless. “It’s my life, and I wanted to experiment with some new, healthier habits. He only gave me some tips from his own life, and they’re not anything someone like… like Hyacine wouldn't suggest anyways. If you asked her, or any nurse or doctor for some tips to feel healthier, she’d tell you the same thing Mydei told me—eat well, sleep well, and go outside to exercise. That’s it.”

“Why now? You’ve been friends for so long, but this all happened so fast,” she brought up, holding her laptop tighter. “What changed?”

Phainon hummed thoughtfully as he looked at her back, remembering all of their intimate moments from start to finish. From the tomato between his teeth to shut him up and to fact he had been underneath him while dressed in nothing but leather belts and cuffs, then everything in between. His growing comfort in his sexuality. Mydei’s journey into finding comfort in his own feelings. Their knowledge of each other at their most intimate and raw state of being, and their want to be what the other needed so no one else could ever fill it for them.

Everything changed.

Both of them went into it thinking they could come out the same people, but that was never in the cards. They would have always ended up right here with how possessive either of them were.

Last night, they stayed in each other’s arms as long as physically possible. From the rooftop hug as they gazed out over the city, to holding hands on top of the table during dinner, and finally cuddling in bed while watching funny videos on his phone until bedtime struck, they were wrapped up together. But he wasn’t complaining about being smothered in attention. In fact, he wanted it again, and again, and again.

He wanted Mydei here in his apartment with them so she could see them as they were. She could see there was no coercion between them, and things weren’t as one-sided as they looked.

Them being together shouldn’t scare her. Nothing felt ‘scary’ about being with him.

“We changed. We aren’t friends, ‘rene,” he shared with her, and she immediately turned around to face him.

“Wh-What are you talking about? Did you have a f…” Her words trailed off into silence as she looked at him, as she really looked at him since he walked through the door. Eyes to this throat, she gulped quietly. “You t-two didn’t fight, did you?”

Phainon shook his head as one of her hands gently touched her own neck, pressing against a spot where his choker opened up on his own. He knew of the reddish-purple lovebite left there. He knew others saw it too when he walked by, the bruise more possessive and straight forward than the collar he wore every day.

He was taken. He was someone’s.

He was Mydei’s, and the people closest to them were going to start figuring that out soon. Why not start right at home?

“I love him, ‘rene. I love him… so much more than ‘just a friend’,” he said, smiling at the mere thought of his handsome face and low voice. “He’s intimidating at first glance, sure, and he speaks pretty flatly and minimally. But he’s a good person who does his best for the people he’s close to, and he loves me too much to ever try and force me into anything I don’t wanna do. Trust me.”

She didn’t answer, too busy watching his face and the heat warming his cheeks.

“I never meant to compare the two of you or make you feel unimportant to me,” he repeated himself. “You could never be what Mydei is to me, but Mydei could never be what you are to me.”

Wide, misty eyes blinked up at him, and he took a deep breath as she sniffled.

“Really?”

“I was angry because you basically said that we weren’t good for each other, and that the person I’m becoming isn’t ‘me’,” Phainon told her, spilling everything he had told Mydei. “But it is. I’m trying to do better for myself, dress up nicer to make him look at me, and visit him more often to be around him. Isn't that normal things a guy in love does? You love love stories and romance, so tell me—is seeing me like this really something to be scared of?”

Cyrene shook her head, then looked away from him as silence washed over them. Her eyes focused on the wall, face turned but still completely visible.

“Th-That’s all…?”

“That’s all,” he promised. “I like this thing we have, and I’d like for you to be happy for me. My family liking my partner has always been really important to me.”

Her eyes glossed over even more, and he reached to take her laptop from her hands.

“Can I have a—mmph!” The impact of her body hitting his chest made him take a step back to stabilize them both. “Yeah, that… I wanted that.”

Both arms wrapped around his waist, and he curved an arm over Cyrene’s shoulders to hold her closer. The glasses she had on creaked from the pressure of her pushing her face into his chest, and her long nails scratched through the tank-top he was wearing, but he liked this. He liked pushing his nose to the top of her head and feeling her close.

“I’m sorry for what I said,” he apologized quietly. “I’m sorry for worrying you so much. I just wish you would have come to us instead of trying to go to our friends and fish for answers on your own. Being confused doesn't mean you should accuse people of being abusive or two-faced.”

“I’m sorry,” her muffled voice said back to him. He could feel her mouth moving against his body, and the heat of her breath through his top from how close she was. “Phainon, I’m so sorry.”

“I forgive you, but you should apologize to Mydei sometime too,” he suggested. “I… might have told him of our fight, so he knows.”

Cyrene nodded quickly, and he pulled his arm back briefly.

“Here. Give me your glasses before you break them,” he offered. After she pulled her face back just enough to slip them off, it went right back into his chest.

“I’m sorry,” she sniffled. “I didn’t… I-I know it was too far, but… I guess I thought… I mean… I just…—”

“Take it easy,” he coaxed, holding her tighter. “And try not to get too much snot on this shirt too. I kind of like the feel of this one.”

“Too l-late…”

Yeah. He could feel how damp it was with tears and more.

“Awh, come on…” He joked. “Mydei’s gonna kill me, and we just barely made it official. There’s no way I can take both him and Hysilens on my tail.”

Cyrene choked on a laugh, then unballed her fists to plant them flat to his shoulders. But she didn’t move.

“I was… a-a little jealous too,” she admitted. “You’ve known him for so long, and I-I know we grew up together as kids, but he was there, you know? I missed so many important years of growing up… gossiping about first crushes, high school dances, sports games, learning who we are… I moved here with you as your best friend from then, but he was your best friend now…”

Phainon stayed quiet, not wanting to interrupt her.

“I can get along with the girls. We’re girls. There’s this… thing we just h-have.” A hiccup broke her words up. “But Mydei’s harder. We aren’t close at all even though I've known them all the same amount of time. Lately, I’ve been wondering if I’m just… holding on to the past too hard and holding you back from doing your own thing. I’ve never been good at letting go.”

“You’re not,” he reassured her. “The spot next to me isn’t a competition or a game of tug-o-war, silly. I have my partner, I have my friends, and I have my family. All three co-exist, and all three are important to me.”

“Did uh… M-Mydei call me selfish when you told him?” She wondered quietly, and he shook his head. “Did he say that I’m a terrible friend? That he never wants to see me again?”

“He would never say that to you. He said to talk to him if you have an issue with him,” he shot the assumptions down. “If you know what to ask, you’ll find that he is a very honest person. If you don’t ask him the right questions, he’s not going to feel the need to correct you or answer personally… unless you’re me. For some reason, he likes being particularly nitpicky with me.”

Cyrene pulled away from him. With the added freedom, he readjusted her things into one arm as she used her own to wipe the mess beneath her nose.

“You’re just r-really e-easy to tease,” she giggled through her raspy voice and sniffling.

“That’s gross. Go find a tissue.” He then pretended to gag, causing her to laugh and push her arm closer to her nose. “What are you doing just leaving it all there? Shoo!”

She turned to run towards the bathroom, and he rolled her eyes over her squeal of being ‘so un-cute’ when the light turned on. After living together, he wasn’t sure if her face full of snot was the worst thing he had ever seen. But it was, undoubtedly, a little bit funny. The laugh he gave was a little too hard to bite back completely.

He could hear the water run, then the splash of her rinsing her arm off. As she cleaned up, he set her things down on the coffee table.

“Make sure you drink this tea, by the way! Don’t forget about it on the table!”

She probably will, so Phainon made a mental note to remind her again sometime later.

“So, you a-and Mydei are together,” he heard from the hallway, and he hummed positively. “Does that mean I-I should also apologize for insisting that he likes girls?”

His eyes rolled. “You think everyone likes girls,” he reasoned.

“Why wouldn’t they? I do,” she sniffled again, making him chuckle quietly. “I feel so bad… I want to hide in m-my room and never come out. I should j-just never see him again.”

“Sucks to suck. I was thinking of inviting him for dinner sometime this week. You two should talk a little more,” he tsk’ed, enjoying her worried groan. “Stop seeing him as this ‘too cool to talk to’ person. He’s just a guy.”

“He’s going to think I’m a-a terrible person!”

Phainon wasn't sure how many times he needed to say it to her, but Mydei was not going to think of her as anything less than a confused and worried friend. Not once did he even blame her for anything that she felt, did, or said. All of it was simply, ‘she’s doing her best to understand’. Like he was when he came at him similarly.

“He’s going to come over with some kind of offering, try to make dinner all by himself, then ask about your book,” he said confidently. “He’s going to ask you why you feel how you do, then tell you that you shouldn’t worry so much.”

“Mm…” She shrunk back into herself. “Are you sure he won’t be like… angry at me?”

“Positive. He wasn’t angry when I told him, and he won’t be when you apologize.”

Cyrene rubbed her nose with the tissue, then crossed one of her arms over her chest while looking at him up and down.

“So, you told him about our fight, and Mydei uh… haha… Mydei consoled you with sex?”

“Cyrene!” He gasped, and she laughed while holding the tissue over her face. “I’m not talking about—”

“Oh, come on! It’s all over your neck! You’re so guilty!” She cut him off, smiling so wide that her glossy eyes crinkled. “I wasn’t around to tease you for your ex-girlfriend, so… I wanna talk about you and him. Does he treat you well, Phainon?”

Phainon sighed, then slowly traced his tongue over his top row of teeth while contemplating the weight of gossiping with her. Their relationship just became official, and Mydei didn’t like too much of his business being aired out. Just the little things, casual things, like his interest in baking and cooking.

As long as they didn’t talk about his sex life, it should be okay. Certain things everyone could notice about him and innocent acts people in love did normally should be fine to share.

“He’s very… romantic,” he said carefully, and she nodded in encouragement for him to keep going. “He likes to hold doors open for me, and he always calls me handsome… even if I’m all gross from work.”

Saying that out loud felt so… good. There had been a weight settled on top of his chest since he swore himself to secrecy, then again when she told him something was wrong with them. But she looked at him like she was actually interested in hearing about their relationship, like what they had was something she could now fawn over.

“That’s sweet,” Cyrene coo’ed.

“And… And the lego sets you saw me buy that day, we built one together,” Phainon added. “It’s in his house right now. We glued it together so it never falls apart.”

“Awh! He’s that sentimental?”

“And he cooks for me all the time.” He grinned, thinking about the breakfast they shared that morning and dinner from the night before. “Like… De will ask what I feel like having, and sometimes he cooks it just like I ask if I’m extra tired from work. Then we work out every morning, and he’ll make us a big breakfast while I clean up so it’s almost finished when I’m all dressed.”

Cyrene didn’t respond, too busy watching as he reached to touch his neck and hold the pendant closely. His fingers pinched, circling the ring shape slowly with his index while embedding the stone into his thumb.

“He’s so handsome too. I mean, he always has been, but it’s just so much more now than it was before. His body, his personality, and the way he carries himself is just so… attractive…” He struggled to word as a rush filled into his chest, familiar and warm like sunlight. “Oh, ‘rene… He’s everything someone could want.”

“Mydei better take good care of you,” she warned him despite her softened gaze. “If he doesn’t, I’m going to beat him up.”

All he could do was laugh at the mental image of her battering her smaller fists into his chest. If he somehow did hurt him, Phainon had no doubt that Mydei would try to duck just so it was easier to reach his face. It’d be just like him.

“I should shut up now. It’ll get annoying if you let me drone on about him. Do you wanna watch a show, or—”

“I wanna hear you sing more praise about him,” Cyrene egged him on, waving her hand for more emphasis. “Keep going. This is going to be great for the story I’m working on.”

“The real storybook lover is Mydei,” he protested. “You should talk to him about it when we have dinner together. He’ll inspire you so much more than me just rambling on about how gorgeous he is.”

“Maybe I will if he accepts my apology,” she agreed, then turned to look at her laptop. “But the look on your face is so much more expressive. Keep talking. Maybe I can get through the chapter I was stuck on.”

Well, if she insisted… He could talk about how much he loved Mydei all day.

“Have a good rest of your night too, my love.”

Once it was sent, within seconds, it was read. But it wasn’t nearly as quickly responded to. Seconds turned to minutes, and it made his stomach knot nervously.

Did he decide that he didn’t like it?

Phainon set his phone down, opting to clean himself up with his already soiled clothes and toss his filthied outfit into the hamper. He stripped his sheets, replaced them with a second pair, and prayed he wouldn’t step out of his room to another confrontation with Cyrene.

His prayers were answered when he peeked out his door and saw hers still cracked, soft ocean noises and clicking followed.

“Cyrene, dinner,” he tried to remind her while turning into the bathroom.

“After this chapter!” Her muffled voice called back once he shut the door. “Wait! Phainon, I need the word that’s like… like… when you… when…”

She screamed into her pillow in sheer agony immediately after, and he laughed as his phone buzzed inside of his hand. There was nothing he could really do to help her until she calmed down, so he gave it a second. She’d sober up soon enough.

> [Mydei: I could listen to you say that all day.]

Oh, so it took him that long to respond because he liked it? He liked being referred to as his ‘love’?

That was cute. In fact, that was more than cute. It was so adorable that Phainon couldn’t help but grin as he pushed his back to the bathroom door.

> [Phainon: My love really is a hopeless romantic.]

> [Mydei: But on second thought, that name might not be the most appropriate for other people to hear. Not when it makes my chest feel like this.]

That was too bad, wasn’t it? He asked for it, and Phainon was always ready to do as he asked. Even if it meant pushing into brat territory and risking a punishment.

> [Phainon: My master told me to say it, so I HAVE to. That’s how this works.]

> [Phainon: Sorry, my love. Orders are orders.]

Mydei was surely going to scold him for being so mouthy and toying with his emotions like this. But it was worth it to imagine him red-faced and flustered as he read over their texts, or as he replayed the audio message in his spare time for comfort or reassurance.

He wanted to see it in person already.

Chapter Notes

When Phainon asked what night Mydei would want to come over for dinner, the answer was none. He didn’t really want to come over this time.

Instead, Mydei wanted them to come over to his place. He wanted to be the host this time around, and Phainon didn’t mind that at all as he really liked being there.

That was what led to Cyrene pacing back and forth inside of her room, hands on her head as she asked him repeatedly, ‘is this okay?’

She opened and closed the door for him, showing him outfit after outfit to see if it was ‘nice enough’ for a dinner with his ‘boyfriend’. Because Mydei at their place meant he was a guest who needed to be on his best behavior. But they were going to be guests at his place now, and she couldn’t just look or act as she pleased in another person's home.

“It’s not like you to be so nervous.”

“It’s intimidating going to his place,” she defended herself, making him chuckle softly. “Plus, he’s kinda… high-class, isn’t he? Like… he didn’t grow up picking vegetables from the garden, de-scaling fish for dinner, and—”

“That doesn’t matter,” Phainon cut her off. “Mydei’s not like that. He’s not going to stick his nose up if you dress comfortably rather than to the nines. All you need to do is dress clean. Don’t go over with dirty sneakers or paint-stained clothes.”

She held herself, looking around her closet as if his words hadn’t curbed some of her anxiety.

“I think you see him as someone better than he is,” he mused. “Mydei’s in a different tax bracket, sure. He was raised with different standards of living than we were, but he’s still just a guy. He’s not this untouchable entity to hold at a distance, Cyrene.”

“He makes himself out to be someone high standard and unapproachable sometimes,” she mumbled. “He’s civil, but it’s also like he’s too good to get close to. You just don’t see it as much because you’ve been friends for over ten years.”

He couldn’t deny that. Mydei did hide behind his carefully curated mask in public, letting it slip only when he was indoors with his friends. Even then, sometimes he still allowed everyone else to talk over him or without him, choosing to silently observe from afar or fade into the background to do something else.

‘Supporting character’ was what he saw himself as, and it did make him seem a little aloof to keep to himself so much.

“Just… wear what’s comfortable for you,” he suggested. “Here. Put a pretty dress on. You look really nice in white.”

“White is a terrible idea! What if I spill something on myself?” She gasped, offended by the choice “He loves his alcohol. What if I get wine on my dress? It’ll be ruined!”

Phainon sighed, staring at her mess of a closet. “Red?” He offered next, seeing a peek of that color.

“That’s way too sexy for a dinner with your man! The only red dress I have is for going out with the girls, not showing him my girls!” Cyrene shot down, and his nose crinkled.

Oh. It was that dress, her clubbing dress she swore wasn’t too short even if he swore that it was.

“Cyrene, it’s not a black tie event. Wear something cute! Put a little skirt on or something!” Her eyes squinted while rubbing her chin, staring at the railing packed full of hangers and boxes of shoes. “Just please don’t make us late. You still need to do your makeup.”

“It does not take that long.”

It did.

Her hair took even longer too considering she had this thing about growing it out as long as possible after having it so short as kids. At this point, the colored tips touched her thighs.

“Please,” he repeated, and she sighed dramatically before pushing him out of her bedroom. “We agreed on a certain time. Mydei values a well kept schedule and punctuality, so let’s keep to it.”

“Yes! Yes, I will! Now get out so I can change!” She huffed.

The door slammed in his face, and he raised one eyebrow before turning back around to his own room. With her dressers ripping open loud enough to thump on their rails, it made him wonder if he now needed to put a little bit more thought into his clothes. Originally, he was going to just wear some of the clothes left in his closet from Mydei’s place. Black jeans, a simple shirt, maybe some ankle boots. This wasn’t a dinner that would combust if he didn’t wear the right pants or put on an ironed out button-up. He didn’t really care to try any more than he usually did.

Staring at his drawer full of folded jeans, he eyed the blue pair he wore only a couple of times —the gift he was given in the past.

Well, reward. Mydei had bought these blue ones for him as a reward, and the black pair he wore more often as a gift for himself. These were meant to be enjoyed on his own, but he found little use for them these days.

One hand reached for them, touching the nice denim before deciding that Mydei would like to see him wear them since he hasn’t yet. After all, even if he liked him in dark colors, he liked him being comfortable and confident in himself too. Maybe even more.

Maybe Cyrene wouldn’t tease him for trying too hard either, which made it a win-win in his book as he pulled it free.

—

In all the time they’ve been friends, for the life of him, Phainon couldn’t remember if Cyrene had ever been to Mydei’s place.

Maybe when Mydei first hosted a housewarming dinner years ago. That night had been special even if he had to be talked into it by Castorice and Hyacine, but was that it? Once? In years?

She was tapping her nails to the bottom of the porcelain plate they wrapped up with plastic and ribbon. Cubed brownies were stacked into a neat pyramid, meticulously balanced to keep pretty. Though the edges were messy from being cut with a knife they forgot to keep wiping off, they tasted great. Snacking on what was left caked to said knife proved as much.

Showing up empty handed to dinner was bad manners, and while he knew that, this was Mydei. He didn’t need to bring anything, but Cyrene insisted this was standard. It was respectful.

Phainon chose to knock rather than unlock the door on his own, and he stuffed his hands into his pockets while waiting.

“Smells good already,” he hummed, and she hummed simply. “You need to calm down. If you cry, you’ll ruin the makeup that took you forty minutes to do.”

“I just couldn’t decide what eyeshadow looked best with this! Should I have worn something classier?” Cyrene asked, and his eyes dropped to her pale blue blouse and matching skirt. “Oh… I should’ve just worn black and white. It’s somewhat formal and classy. Watch him come to the door in a button-up and slacks…”

“Mydei dresses like that casually. He always has,” he reminded her, then heard the lock twist. “It’s kinda hot.”

She scoffed over his attempt to change the topic. “Well, yeah! But—!”

Mydei, as expected, was in a buttoned, collared shirt with a pair of dark pants. His hair was pulled up into a ponytail with his bangs clipped back with a few bobby pins. Sweat lightly glistened on his forehead, a result of working hard in the kitchen, no doubt.

“Hey, you two actually made it on time for once. Come in,” he greeted them. “You look beautiful, Cyrene. It’s nice to see you again.”

Both men let Cyrene walk in first, and Mydei opened the door wider while stepping to the side.

“Oh, this? I just looked in the closet and threw on what I found!” She laughed nervously, lying right to his face. “But thank you, Mydei. You always look nice.”

He nodded curtly. “Of course.”

“Oh! And we baked these for tonight!” She showed him the dish while he silently held a hand out. “Where do you want me to put them? They’re not that pretty, but Phai ate all the chunks off the knife, so they must be yummy!”

“I’m sure they’re delicious. The counter is fine for now,” he answered. When she didn’t notice him reaching for the plate, he retracted it back to settle on his hip. “How are you?”

“I’m okay,” she returned. “How are you? You look like you’ve been working hard in the kitchen.”

“I’m doing fine, thank you. Please help yourself to anything in the refrigerator. If you’d like something, Phainon can get it for you,” he offered, but she shook her head before walking deeper into his home.

Upon hearing her heels click to the wooden floors, Phainon reached an arm out.

“Cy—“

Mydei’s hand rested over his arm gently, and he shook his head to cut him off. Seeing it, Phainon dropped his arm as he lifted an eyebrow.

“It’s a bit irrational to ask your dinner guests to take their shoes off at the door, no?” Mydei reasoned. “I’m sure she tried really hard to put together something nice, so no need. Just come in.”

Phainon allowed the door to close behind his body, and he tilted his head slightly while admiring his face.

“Hi, De.”

Mydei glanced towards where their third party disappeared briefly. When he was sure she couldn’t see, his curled index finger tilted his chin up and met his eyes.

“Hey, handsome.” His voice lowered in both pitch and volume. “You look good tonight too. Let me take your jacket.”

Phainon pulled his black jacket off sleeve by sleeve, revealing the fitted sleeves of his white henley shirt.

“I wore this jacket for you. You know, to meet your expectations.”

“Then take it off for me too.”

He handed it over to his awaiting hand, and Mydei draped it over one arm before leaning in to kiss his cheek. The soft brush made his smile widen, warmed by his chivalrous touch.

“I like the way those sleeves hug your arms and chest,” he praised him quietly, and Phainon had hoped he’d say that when he put it on to begin with. “And those jeans always make your ass look good—black or blue. Go on, walk in front of me and show off for me.”

Phainon laughed, then set a hand on his chest to gently push him away. In doing so, he made sure to sneak a press against his own chest and feel his body for himself. But it wasn’t as unnoticeable as he hoped when the muscles stiffened underneath his fingertips.

“Try not to get too excited,” he whispered just for them both, but turned to walk away from him anyway.

“Pour us all some drinks, and let Cyrene snack on the sliced bread if she’d like.”

‘Yes, master,’ was on the very top of his tongue just begging to leap free from his lips, but he swallowed it down to nod instead. Harmless flirting was one thing, but that was something he didn’t want to slip at all around her.

“And show me some more respect,” Mydei ‘suggested’ from behind him. “Call me something less casual than ‘De’. That’s not going to be acceptable tonight.”

“Yes, my love,” he obeyed, listening to his breathing hitch. “Can I go now?”

“Y-You may…”

He made his way over to the kitchen, finding Cyrene there on a barstool with her purse on her lap. To make things less awkward, his elbow brushed her shoulder while passing by. The little bump made her gasp.

“Hey! Watch out, Phainon!”

“Sorry, you were in my way,” he teased her, finding the cutting board full of cleanly sliced bread and a shallow dish full of a tomato and garlic filled dipping oil. “Here. Help yourself to this while we get everything ready.”

Cyrene looked down at the offering, and when Phainon noticed her hesitation to be the first to ruin the display, he picked a piece right from the middle for himself. The crisp bread scooped some of the chunky dip, and he took a bite right in front of her before turning around.

“Mm… He worked hard for it, so don't let it go to waste, ‘kay?” He said, then finished his slice before wiping his hands on a kitchen towel. “Eat. Talk. Enjoy getting to be here and feel closer to us, that’s what we’re here for.”

That was when he heard her fingers pinch a piece as well, then the crunch of her biting into its crisp crust.

“Mydei’s also got a whole cart full of stuff for a nice cocktail to take the edge off. Would you like a glass?” He offered. “Or do you want some soda? Maybe water?”

“Soda, please,” she answered, then swallowed. “Mydei, this bread is really good. Did you bake it yourself? I know you typically do things like that.”

“I bought it,” he admitted.

“From where?”

Phainon smiled, glad she realized if she wanted answers then she had to be prepared to keep asking questions.

“It’s a bakery my mother likes to visit. I’ll give you the address,” Mydei explained simply.

“Mm-mm! Please do!”

While grabbing the two of them a pair of glasses, he also brought down three plates to set down neatly besides the finished food. Mydei joined him in the kitchen after their conversation, one hand brushing the small of his back when walking by.

“Behind you,” he warned him gently, and a shiver inched down his spine from the casual touch. “How was your guys’ days? Did anything interesting happen?”

“Couch rotted most of it,” Cyrene answered honestly this time. “Well, I did. Phainon’s much more active than I am. I tried to go on a run with him, but he’s too fast and stays out too long for me.”

“She gave up.”

“I strategically acknowledged the extent of my own abilities,” she said stubbornly, and Mydei picked a plate up while he poured two glasses of soda. “In other words, I… gave up…”

“If you start something new by trying to keep up with someone whose made it a regular routine, you’re bound to give up,” Mydei advised. “Everyone moves at their own pace. Start slow, and build your way towards keeping up.”

“I know,” she sighed as Phainon placed a glass closer towards her. “I just wanted to try, but I don’t like it. My hair is so heavy, so it drags on my head when I put it up to start running.

Then my shorts ride up to make my thighs chafe, and people look at you weirdly when you pass by.”

A low, unbothered hum followed. “Sounds like excuses,” he brushed off. “Those are superficial at best.”

“They are,” Phainon joked, sticking his tongue back out at Cyrene when she glared at him. “Mydei, water or a refill?”

“Both.”

“Greedy,” he mused over the immediate response, but his fingers stretched to reach for his empty glass anyway. “Please move so I can get to the cupboard for another glass.”

With the added space, he quickly reached for a tall drinking glass like the ones he and Cyrene had. It was filled with ice water. The other carried Mydei’s usual whiskey. While closing the bottle to put back on its tray, a hand settled gently over his shoulder.

Phainon turned his head.

“Thank you for being so helpful, handsome,” Mydei told him.

Cyrene grinned from her spot in front of them, and his hands gripped the bottle harder.

“Please help me move everything to the table. I’d like us to eat comfortably rather than crowd around the counter,” he instructed him. Phainon nodded in understanding. “Cyrene, I’m sorry to interrupt you. Do you mind moving?”

“No! No, that's fine! Anything I can do?” She asked kindly. “I’m not useless. I can do more than let you both do everything.”

“I won’t let my guest help. It’s my job as a host to take care of these things,” he shot down. “Phainon helps because he doesn’t count as a guest anymore. He half-lives here by now.”

“Mydei, but you do this when you visit too,” she pointed out. “You take control of things like we can’t help you. Please. Let me do something too instead of making you both do it all.”

Mydei hummed, letting go of his shoulder while looking at her.

“You’ll find I don’t like splitting my responsibilities. The things that I feel are my duty, are simply my duty. No one else’s,” he shared with her, his voice holding an air of firmness. “If I’m a guest, I need to lighten the burden of my presence. If I host, I need to take care of my guests by allowing them to rest comfortably.”

“It’s a little… um… how do I put this…?”

Phainon butted in, speaking carefully while looking at his partner. “Sometimes your desire to do it all by yourself makes it hard for other people to feel close to you. You and I are doing all the work, and Cyrene just… doesn’t want to feel left out right now.”

His eyes dropped. “That’s not my intention.”

“It’s not, but it’s how it feels sometimes. By doing it all, you close off the opportunity to make a deeper connection with others,” he explained. “So, surely there's something she can do to feel included with her friends…?”

Mydei was silent for a second, then nodded in understanding. “Please help Phainon get the table ready, and I’ll bring our plates.”

Cyrene smiled as she got up from her seat, picking up the cutting board to bring it to the table for them.

“Thank you, my love,” he whispered as he leaned closer to kiss beside his ear. Mydei tucked closer to him as if he craved to be skin to skin. “Please allow us to take care of this, okay? Go sit down. I’ll bring out all of the plates.”

“Are you staying the night?” He asked him hopefully. “Pease tell me you are.”

“I can,” he agreed quietly. Every bone in his body wanted to stay the night too. “Cyrene can drive my car home, and you can drop me off tomorrow.”

“If she’d like the guest bed, she can take it. No need to send her home by herself,” he offered, but deep down, Phainon knew neither of them really wanted to dance around extra company later. “I’d feel terrible taking you from her like that. Especially after everything that has happened so far, I fear that’d make her feel more isolated.”

“I’ll bring it up later.”

“Thank you.”

Phainon then set the bottle down, and he picked up both of Mydei’s glasses to bring them to the dinner table.

“Hey, Mydei? Wait a sec’,” Cyrene spoke up, catching him when he passed her. “I… know Phainon told you about what I said before…”

Deciding that was their conversation to have, Phainon turned around to head right back into the kitchen to grab three small bowls of salad. Stacking them carefully, he carried the nice dishes to the dinner table, placing one by each seat.

When he finished, his quick feet walked him right back to the kitchen, and he grabbed three full plates to place them by either salad bowl.

“I’m working even on my day off,” he joked to himself while setting them down.

This time, when he was going back to grab the appropriate silverware, a strong hand grasped his arm and pulled him closer. It forced him to stay and listen, standing in between Mydei and Cyrene.

“I want to apologize,” she said, and her eyes glanced between them both before settling on Mydei. “I should have been upfront with you instead of trying to go behind your back, and I shouldn’t have doubted you. You’re not a bad person. I know that. I guess… I don’t know… I guess I was just…—”

“I forgave you the moment Phainon told me. If there’s something you need me to do to reassure you, tell me,” Mydei said calmly.

As he spoke, he linked their arms together like he needed him there, and Phainon looked down at their touching bodies. He curved his wrist to hold his hand better, and Mydei’s fingers slotted in between his own.

“No! No, it’s… fine. I mean, I don’t know why I even said those things…” She muttered. “It was stupid of me, Mydei..”

Mydei shook his head, not accepting the self-deprecating words. “You didn’t understand, and you shouldn’t punish yourself for that. It isn’t your fault we didn’t clue you in.”

“You really are so understanding, Mydei… It makes a person feel a bit… immature.”

His eyes shifted to his partner, and Mydei’s lip inched downwards as he shrugged weakly.

“Misunderstandings happen,” he reasoned. “Moving forward, please bring your worries to me directly. Don’t burden someone else if it's my motives being questioned or my mistake to correct. I am Phainon’s partner, and I should speak for myself.”

“I… also want to apologize for insisting that you get a girlfriend. I didn’t know you uh… liked guys,” she apologized again as one hand held her arm shyly. “You never corrected me, so I thought it was right to say.”

“I didn’t see the need to correct you because it isn’t anyone’s business who I’m attracted to,” he brushed off. “It doesn’t upset me to hear from you. I don’t care.”

“Still. It’s just as bad as my parents telling me to get a boyfriend, isn’t it?”

Cyrene looked away from them, and Phainon smiled widely to himself before setting a hand on her head. Ruffling her hair, she gasped in betrayal as Mydei immediately batted his arm aside for her. Both looked at him as if he had done something unspeakable.

“I spent so long doing my hair, Phainon!”

“You shouldn’t do that to a woman dressed nicely, Phainon.”

“You’re both being so serious,” he whined, wondering if he was the only one who felt as if anything more than ‘I’m sorry’ was unnecessary. “Come on. Let's cut the formalities and just relax a little bit. Why don’t you two just talk and become better friends to put this behind us all?”

Mydei’s lips pursed, and Cyrene carefully patted her hair down while looking up.

“Talk about romance, books, sweets, and flowers,” he listed the similar interests they shared. “The food is getting cold, so let’s not let it go to waste.”

Because Mydei loved him, and he wanted to solidify that their relationship wasn’t something to worry about, Phainon knew his partner would try endlessly to clear his name. The same way he was there to greet her with him when she came back from their hometown, gifted her a plush toy of a character she liked to make up for messing with her things, and baked the cinnamon rolls she enjoyed so much—he knew he’d try. It was the one thing he always did.

And Cyrene was no different. She liked being liked just as much as he did, and she felt just as deeply as him too. There was no need to be redundant when everyone knew that moving forward, they’d all try to clear up any misunderstandings before they happened again.

“I’m currently reading a book about a prince and a hero,” Mydei shared. “Perhaps you might like it. When I finish, you’re free to borrow it.”

“Tell me about it,” Cyrene beamed happily, meeting his eyes. “I wanna hear about it. Is it a love story?”

“Like one I’ve never read before.”

“My favorite!”

Phainon unraveled their arms so they could split, and Mydei followed his best friend to the table. While they spoke, he rushed to grab all of their silverware so they could actually eat. No one was going to stick their fingers into the mashed potatoes or salad bowl.

Cyrene thanked him as he handed her a set, and Mydei looked up at him when he handed him both his utensils.

“Thank you, baby.”

“You’re welcome, my love,” he returned, and those amber eyes followed him as he sat down. “This looks good. Thank you so much. Cyrene, say—”

“—yeah yeah,” she huffed. “Thank you for dinner tonight, Mydei. We’re always so lucky when you cook for us.”

“Please uh… e-enjoy," was all he said back, rose tinting his cheeks. “Anyway, about that book…”

—

After they had their dinner and dessert, after Phainon was finished washing their dishes and putting them away, Cyrene decided that she wanted to go home. She told him that he could stay if he liked, but she didn’t want to intrude on their alone time or sleep in these uncomfortable clothes. It'd be too awkward for her, and it’d be even worse if she actually accepted Mydei’s offer of pajamas to sleep in.

Phainon handed her his keys without hesitation, made her promise to unlock the front door for him tomorrow and not sleep through the whole morning, then gave her a hug goodbye. Mydei too, just before thrusting several containers full of leftovers into her hands.

With the door locked, Phainon gasped as his back thumped against it suddenly, not expecting it.

Mydei’s hands took his own, and he threaded their fingers together while lifting them over head. Pinned to the front door, Phainon gulped quietly over their close proximity and the display of power.

“Hi, master,” he greeted him while smiling sweetly at him despite the vulnerable position. “Can I do anything for you?”

“I spent the last hour on the couch listening to Cyrene ramble on and on about all of the things you said about me,” he shared with him. “Someone has a big mouth.”

Damn. Cyrene really didn’t want him going home tomorrow, did she?

Phainon shrunk back, attempting to make himself look smaller as he flicked his gaze up at him through his lashes. When he did, Mydei’s left hand brought both of his into the right. Lowering his hold from his palm to his wrist, he gripped them inside of one stretched fist.

“Do you have a big mouth?” Mydei asked, pinching his jaw.

“Maybe,” he played along. “Or maybe I just love you and am proud to brag about you to others. Has my master thought of that?”

“That’s not what I asked you. Let’s listen when I speak,” he chastised, and butterflies filled his stomach as his legs shifted involuntarily. “Do you have a big mouth, Phainon?”

“Yes, master,” he answered. After, he dropped his attention to the lips across from him. “I have a big mouth, and I… I told her all about the cute things we do—legos, dinners, movies, stuff like that.”

“There you go, that’s what I wanted to hear,” he told him, lowering his fingers from his jaw to his neck. While there, they stretched to either side.

Phainon gulped quietly. “Am I in trouble for that, master?”

His head shook.

Instead of speaking again, Mydei leaned forward and pressed a kiss against his lips. Soft, sweet, and short, he didn’t give him the time to do more than push back. Once he did, he pulled away.

“How are you feeling? Not too full anymore, right?”

Oh.

His body squirmed beneath him when he stepped closer, pinning not just his arms but his restless feet too. Dressy shoes stood between his old boots, forcing his legs apart.

“T-Tingly, and I’m not really full anymore. It’s been awhile since we all ate,” he whispered back, feeling the buckles of their belts click together from how close they were. “Why? What did you wanna do to me, master?”

“Fill that mouth, of course,” he said as if he should have already known. “The kitchen is clean and the living room is organized, we have nothing left to do tonight but get ready for bed. Do you want to play with me for a little bit before we do, handsome?”

He nodded quickly.

“Can I please play with you, master?” He asked, and Mydei’s lip tilted higher. “Do I need to do anything?”

“Undress.”

A short tug attempted to pull his arms free, but Mydei tightened his hold.

“Undress here,” he finished.

“H-Huh?”

Here? By the front door? A decent walk away from the comfort of his bedroom?

No one was going to see. No one was here to see—just him, Mydei, and all the empty space in his house. But…

“Y-Your curtains are open.” He couldn’t help but notice the darkened sky behind him. “We usually close them in the room, but the living room ones are usually wide open, master. What if someone happens to peek in?”

“Are you saying ‘red’? Or are you saying you’re nervous?” He hummed, eyeing him up and down. “Be specific. We’ve done some pretty intimate things with my curtains opened, Phainon, like making out on my couch and me collaring you in my bedroom. Did you think of someone peeking at us then?”

“But… this is being naked, master…” Phainon reasoned. “And… the lights were off when you collared me. It’s harder to see anything then.”

“What are you saying, Phainon?”

His eyes glanced towards the tall, wide windows in the living room behind him. They were beautiful for letting in the morning light or showing off this sky-high view of the city, yet terrifying to consider the lack of privacy with the buildings across from them. Because all the lights were on, he was sure once glance would expose all of him if he were to walk around undressed.

Maybe no one was actively peeking into Mydei’s home. Maybe he didn’t think of it as a big deal because someone else might have been okay with doing that in the past, but the possibility of being seen by anyone other than him was uncomfortable. It made the rosy-hued veil of arousal lift over his senses, freeing them for a moment to feel discomfort and shame.
