“—oh, don’t give me that lip!” Cifera hissed while leaning over the table. “I’ll have you know, I’ve had more girls than you’ve ever had with their mouth—”

“That’s not hard,” he deadpanned, aware all his friends knew he’s only ever had one sexual partner before. “But what about men?”

“Please, I don’t even want to deal with you and Mydei sometimes! I’m not about to deal with another dog around here,” she scoffed. “And does that imply you’ve slept with a man before, snowy?”

“I never said that.”

Cyrene shook her head while looking at him, and Cifera’s eyes widened as she rushed to sit next to him. Batting her eyes with her hands crossed over her lap, she stared innocently as if she wanted him to share every-juicy detail of his intimate life. Not that he would after all of that teasing.

“Twenty if he tells us he’s this pathetic top that begs for a shot,” she told Cyrene, who lifted an eyebrow at her skeptically.

But because his best friend was also a traitor, she grinned along with her. “Twenty says he’s not.”

It was almost offensive how, after knowing what they were like together, she would rush to bet in him being a bottom. Did he really come off that obviously?

“Two-hundred says he doesn’t open his mouth about his personal affairs,” Mydei joined in with a huff, and Phainon reached for an iced bottle while sealing his lips shut. “That’s not your business, and I’m not drunk enough for this conversation.”

“Oh my—what’s the point?” Cifera groaned. She slumped into the leather couch, whining over how unfun he was being by cutting them off. “It’s not like you’re fucking him, De. Why does it matter if he tells us? Twenty buys me my next battle pass!”

Cyrene giggled as he began to pour another drink. “Oh, Cifera… How nice of you to turn your video games off to join us here tonight. Did you ever hit that rank you wanted?”

“Of course not! I swear that ‘999’ person is personally staying in my rank to destroy my hopes and dreams!” She whined, and Phainon turned to his partner. “They always target me too! They see my gamer tag and just know!”

He handed him his glass as Mydei leaned in closer, his voice dropped to a stern whisper. “If you let that happen again, I’m going to punish you. Watch your mouth.”

A buzz made him jump from his seat, and he set the bottle back down before rushing to reach for his phone. Two sets of curious eyes glanced down on either side of him, and all he needed to see what the name before he moved his clicked the screen off.

“Who’s that?” Cifera asked. “Girlfriend? Boyfriend? Mom?”

“She’s my friend, and she’s married,” he hushed, placing a hand to her shoulder and pushing her away.

“… Girlfriend?” Cifera repeated, and he rolled his eyes before standing up. “I want to go meet your mistress.”

Phainon cringed at both the idea of dating Hysilens and having a ‘mistress’ in his life. Though he knew she meant it in a different way, both senses of the word felt so wrong to hear and think about.

Mydei grumbled quietly before taking a drink, upset by it as well.

“That makes me really uncomfortable, actually. Don’t say it like that,” he requested, and she sighed dramatically. “Stay here. I’ll bring them up.”

“Fine! Mydei, you should pour out some shots for them since you bought them. It’s only right.”

“I bought the bottles, but I’m not here to be your play bartender,” he brushed off as he leaned back. “Phainon can pour them their first shots when he comes back up.”

Damn. Mydei said that so casually, yet behind his almost bored tone, Phainon could feel the weight of his silent expectation. This wasn’t to be argued. It wasn’t a suggestion.

Mydei wanted him to do it, so he was going to do it.

“Awh, me?” He tried desperately to mask the immediate rush inside of his gut from the order to be good. “Why do I have to do it?”

This was right in front of their friends too, as if he knew they wouldn’t say anything about it —and they didn’t. All they did was accept that Mydei was telling him what to do, like he typically told everyone what to do.

“Yes, you. Those are your friends you invited, so make them feel welcomed.”

“I guess…” Phainon sulked, brushing off Cifera’s teasing of what a ‘good dog’ he was. Cyrene laughed at her, telling her to stop bullying him so much.

For once, he didn't care about saying anything back. Mydei was making him do something, and it wasn’t just for him now. It was for other people. Was he trying to silently show off how good he could be to people who had their own dynamic?

Sure, he could deny him. He could insist that he only wanted to serve him drinks, as it felt like something special between them both, but why was it so exciting to think about? Why was it making his body tingle so much to think that this would please him?

Mydei might even reward him for listening.

“Just one round out of courtesy. Everyone has their own hands,” his partner added after, reassuring him that he wasn’t expected to perform this way all night. “Well? What are you waiting for? Go get them.”

“Yeah! Phainon, you can’t let them just wait!” Cyrene agreed while waving her hands at him. “Go, go, go! Shoo!”

Phainon nodded in agreement. His feet rushed down the stairs and through the crowd, weaving through the bodies carefully. He soon found both women by the bar, and he slowed down while taking in their outfits from afar.

It was one thing to see them online or to see Hysilens in their work uniform, but seeing her dressed up like this was always so surprising. Sometimes he forgot that she liked to look like that—wearing skirts shorter than the length of her straightened hair. From behind, he almost wouldn’t have known she had anything on until her hair split to reveal the short hem when she turned.

Granted, he had seen her without clothes on, but he tried very hard not to think about it when together. Especially since he would rather forget the image of her bruised ass completely.

She was standing right beside her wife, who had on an equally short skirt as well. Instead of wearing black, she had on white, and her top covered much more than Hysilens’ did despite being backless and sleeveless. One hand was on her hip, short nails tapping against the fabric as she then looked over her shoulder from his staring.

“Can I help you?” Attitude was the first thing he noticed about her aside from her height, then a bored expression when she faced him fully. Her other hand touched around her wife’s hip after, wedding ring flashing under the lights. “You may go. Neither of us are interested.”

Hysilens turned around from the exchange, then smiled kindly at him. “Oh, that’s not… That’s Phainon, not just some random guy.”

“Hm… Is it?” She asked, looking him up and down before crossing her arms. “Maybe it is. I don’t quite remember his face.”

“Nice to meet you.” He waved awkwardly. “I promise I wasn’t checking you out. It’s just so strange seeing Hysilens out of uniform.”

“You’re telling me. Where’s your button up? Why are we showing off our bodies like this?” She mused, then held her cup close. “We looked around and didn’t find you, so I got a drink and decided to wait for your reply. Maybe you were caught up somewhere.”

“Everyone’s up top.”

“‘Up top’?” Cerydra repeated, and he pointed to the loft area above them. Upon looking over there with her, he noticed Cyrene standing there with Mydei to peek at them. While his best friend waved enthusiastically, his partner only stared. “I see.”

“My uh… friend…” One pale eyebrow raised at him, and Hysilens grinned at him. “… reserved a table for tonight, and they bought a bunch of bottles for everyone to take shots. So, if you feel like it, help yourselves.”

“Are they here?” Hysilens asked while following him, and he hummed. “You-know-who?”

“Well…”

Would Mydei mind if he came clean? He did say to leave it at just her, and he didn’t mind that she knew because of her own relationship. Cerydra being here meant little when they both knew these women told everything to each other.

“Yes, they are,” he answered shyly. “But, please don’t bring it up around the others. No one knows they’re that for me, just my best friend and potential partner. We haven’t admitted to anything, but I’m sure they all kind of suspect it.”

Mydei had this thing about him. While he would never lie about them being in a relationship, he also wasn’t going to come out and tell them out of nowhere. If they found out from how he acted, then they did. But if they didn’t ask or point out their behavior, he would never feel the need to announce it to the world.

That was fine. Phainon didn’t need to have a sign over his head that told the world he was Mydei’s, he just didn’t want to outright play pretend.

“I won’t, but I’ll have fun guessing,” she joked. “Hm… Man or woman? Sweet or shy? I’m excited to meet them.”

Phainon only laughed as they climbed the stairs, finding that all his friends were laughing while Castorice had her face scrunched up in distaste. She coughed into her arm, eyes full of water and betrayal.

“That’s terrible!”

“Come on, princess, you’ve gotta toughen up,” Cifera snickered. “It’s just a shot of tequila.”

“It tastes so bad!”

“That’s the difference between a ‘shot’ and a ‘cocktail’, Cassie,” Hyacine giggled. “Oh! Phainon’s back with his friends! Cyrene told us you were down there!”

He turned to face Hysilens and Cerydra, hands clapping together while they stood awkwardly behind him.

“Let me pour your first shots since you’re our guests tonight,” he offered kindly.

Hysilens glanced at her wife, who then nodded curtly. “I’d like that,” she agreed. “She’ll drink whatever you pour. Only one though, as she’s driving.”

“Great! I’m only doing one round, so if you want another, you’ll have to do it yourself,” he mused, earning a gasp of ‘don’t be rude’ from Cyrene. “I don’t wanna work on my day off.”

“Tell me about it! It’s so nice being on the other side of the bar,” she laughed, walking closer towards his friends with Cerydra.

“Guys, this is Hysilens and Cerydra,” he introduced them while swiping a bottle off of the table. “They’re married, so don’t even think about it, Cyrene, Cifera.”

“Hey!”

Phainon clicked two glasses together before pointing at each person.

“Hysilens and Cerydra, these are my friends—Cyrene, Cifera, Hyacine, Castorice, and Mydei,” he listed them all in the order of how they were sitting. “Sit wherever you want, drink whatever you want, and don’t worry about anything but having a good time.”

“I like those boots,” Cifera commented, staring at Hysilens’ shoes. “Where did you get them from?”

Once full, Phainon slid both glasses towards either woman, then took a seat beside where Mydei’s arm lined the couch. He sat close, leg to leg, aware of the way Mydei pushed up against his own.

“It would be rude not to drink with them,” Mydei brought up as he leaned forward. “Here. Pour everyone else one too—even you.”

“Ah, I have to—”

“One is okay if we’re going to be here for a while,” Cyrene reasoned, and he sighed. “Who’s going to tell?”

“You can’t say that in front of the nurse and the lawyer!” He hinted, and he looked to where Cerydra was while the others glanced at Hyacine.

“You guys are so…” Hyacine trailed off exasperatedly. “Do you know how many accidents happen?”

Beside him, Cerydra crossed her arms. “Hmph.”

When she looked away, Cifera grinned and then slammed her empty shot glass to the table. Cyrene followed. Then Hyacine. Then Castorice.

“I like these ladies! Go on, be a good boy, Phainon,” she taunted him, and he cringed as Hysilens gasped in surprise.

Mydei huffed quietly, nudging his leg again.

“You know, you can go back to calling me a ‘dog’ if that’s the alternative,” he mouthed off, then grabbed the bottle again. “I’m only doing this once for you guys! You’re just lucky I feel nice today!”

“I’m sure Mydei will give you a tip later for playing bartender for us.” One eye dropped into a wink, and Mydei choked over his drink before putting his glass down on the table too.

Phainon was no better as he shot her a look.

“I’m kidding!” She waved her hands, though Castorice was giggling quietly over it. “Come on!”

“That’s completely inappropriate in front of new people,” Mydei muttered, wiping his mouth with a paper towel. “Please ignore her. She gets—”

“—annoying,” Phainon finished, cheeks burning from her comment. “She’s annoying.”

“—hyper,” he said instead after he shot him a look. “Cifera is a very eccentric person, and she gets even more bold when drinking. Let’s not take her too seriously. She just wants to joke and make others laugh all the time.”

Hysilens nodded, setting her cup down before handing a shot to her wife with a nudge.

“Let’s all have a good time! It’s not often we can come out like this! Especially when Hyacine and Mydei are always so busy,” Cyrene beamed happily, changing the subject.

One by one, Phainon gave them back their glasses, then poured himself half of one. When finished, he looked at the shot as Mydei shifted his abandoned jacket over either of their legs.

The hand not holding his own drink touched his thigh, holding it firmly by the leather strap. Though he didn’t look his way, it was nice to know Mydei was both thinking about him and wanting to touch him.

“Let’s keep making nice memories together, even if we might not remember them all,” Castorice added kindly. “And let's hope Mydei doesn’t go bankrupt from spoiling us all so much…”

“I’ll pay you back on my next paycheck,” Hyacine promised.

“Phainon orchestrated this whole thing because he thought we all needed to unwind,” he admitted to them, turning to face him. “Thank him. I wouldn’t have done this otherwise.”

“Yeah! Snowy!” Cifera cheered, jumping from her seat. “You know I love you!”

His eyes rolled.

He loved her too, but sometimes he wanted to hide all her favorite things on the top shelves of her house, then not tell her where they were. Then he wanted to laugh as she was forced to climb all the furniture for them.

“Yeah yeah…” Phainon taunted her, raising his glass too. “Just get me drunk and let's all sleep in the bathroom stalls.”

“Ew…” Hyacine mumbled as they all raised their shots and clicked it to whoever was closest to them. For her, it was Castorice. For him, it was Mydei.

While looking at him so closely, Phainon could smell the liquor on his breath and feel the slip of his usual restraint. Even just the way he looked at him, eyes softened and focused on his lips, was different. Though he didn’t kiss him or say anything, he gave a tight squeeze of his thigh.

Fingers lingered under the belt, teasing him, and he smiled back at him. But it only lasted for a second before they looked back to their friends. With them, he took his drink and Mydei did the same.

“Mm…” Mydei hummed once he set his glass down. “You’ve drank with us now, so tell us more about yourselves. What do you do for a living, Cerydra? How were your days?”

Phainon’s nose scrunched as a burn tickled down his tongue and throat, and he coughed to himself lightly. Even with friends, it was still miserable to swallow down.

“I serve as a district attorney,” she answered, and Mydei nodded. “And you?”

“Your average, cookie-cutter office worker,” he brushed off, only for Hyacine to shake her head.

“He’s being humble,” she corrected him. “His father runs Kremnos Enterprises, and he’s climbing the ladder to get experience before taking over the company as CEO. How long does that take again, Mydei?”

He shrugged weakly as Cerydra looked at him. “It just takes time, and a lot of it.”

“To think, he used to intern there,” Castorice commented. “Now you’re… what? Director?”

“I babysit grown men, play middle man between the staff and the higher-ups, and sit in a chair all day on my computer.” Mydei sounded finished with this conversation already, like he was tired of having to talk about himself already. “Don’t make it sound like I’m more important than I am.”

“You don’t seem to like—”

“Was it hard?” Phainon asked suddenly, and they looked at him as he looked at Cerydra, who looked offended by him cutting her off. “The uh… schooling, tests, and all that. How long have you been an active attorney? You’re still so young, right?”

“Asking a lady about her age should be a crime,” she scoffed, and Cyrene nodded in agreement as Hysilens giggled. “It wasn’t easy, but I’m nothing if not ambitious.”

“I’d like to hear how that went,” Castorice requested, interested in her story. “Where did you go to school?”

With the conversation steered away from Mydei, he felt another squeeze on his thigh as if to thank him. Nails scratched against his jeans, gripping him tightly.

Phainon lowered his hand towards it, slipping beneath the jacket as well in hopes the table covered enough of them to hide. His fingers dragged over the backs of his knuckles and traced along the skin and rings slowly. Once over, they shifted. The slots between Mydei’s were filled with his own, holding the both of them.

“How did you know you wanted to become an attorney?" Mydei added, hoping to keep the conversation there for a while.

“Easy.” Hysilens’ head shook as if she already knew the answer, but she stared lovingly at her wife. “I like to argue with people, and I’m always right. I should get paid for it.”

“Oh, dear… Here we go.”

Phainon laughed, then leaned back into the couch, listening to her talk while holding Mydei’s hand.

—

After the girls had gotten bored of simply talking about each other, Cyrene decided they should go dance. In tow, she took Hyacine and Castorice, not wanting to go alone. With two heads of bright pink hair and Castorice’s glittery, butterfly-shaped hair clips, it was hard not to see them even if it was dark.

Phainon, Hysilens, and Cifera were together, watching from the upstairs railing. Those two were nursing their drinks from the bar rather than shots, and he had a cup of soda in hand as he was dead set on not drinking anymore.

“That looks fun…” Cifera murmured to them, watching with sparkling eyes. “Should I…?”

“You should join them,” he encouraged her, bumping her shoulder gently. “Go on. I bet Cyrene’s hands miss you. You’re the only one confident enough to dance on her, you know.”

She drank from her straw until it had nothing left to pick them, then thrust both her cup and strapless purse into his chest. A soft grunt left his lips on impact, and he rushed to catch them before they fell.

“I’m gonna go join my girls! Watch my stuff, snowy!”

Before he could say anything back, her feet rushed down the steps with loud, thumping steps. Phainon chuckled while watching to make sure she made it there. Only when her smaller body managed to sift through the sea of people to meet up with them did he allow himself to look away.

“Is she always bullying you?”

“Yeah… It’s kinda mutual,” he sighed dramatically. “She calls me a ‘dog’. I call her a ‘cat’. She likes to scratch me with her too-long nails, and I hold her phone over her head because she can’t reach it.”

Hysilens laughed at that. “Sounds eventful.”

“Mydei hates it,” he joked, and she tilted her head curiously over the mention of his name. “We can go back and forth all day, and we somehow always bring him into our bickering. We give him a headache.”

“Is he not the argumentative type too?” She wondered. “He seems quiet so far.”

“He doesn’t talk much until you get some liquor in him. It helps him open up a bit.” Phainon then looked over his shoulder, finding that Mydei was still listening to Cerydra talk to him. “Those two seem to be hitting it off though…”

“Like me, my wife doesn’t go out often. It’s good she’s making new friends with me.” Hysilens looked so happy watching them together. “She made a few, but she has… quite the personality. Sometimes, she talks too much, speaks too bluntly, and it makes people uncomfortable.”

Well, that must have been nice for Mydei, who also spoke without restraint yet preferred other people to drive the conversation.

“She can be a bit intense,” he confessed to her, focusing on how relaxed his partner looked right now. “But… she’s uh… she’s a cool… person…”

Mydei was leaning back on the leather couch with an arm spanning over the back again. One ankle laid crossed over the other knee comfortably, and he had decided to actually wear the jacket instead of keeping it folded over his lap. All of his attention was on Cerydra, lips pulled into a polite and courteous smile and eyes tired but still aware.

Whatever was being said from both Hysilens right beside him and Cerydra right across from him fell on Phainon’s deaf ears, as the club music was loud and he felt a twinge of something in his chest. It flickered for a moment, hot and demanding attention.

“We should go talk to them again,” he blurted out, and Hysilens’ hand reached to hold his arm. “I wonder what they’re talking about.”

“Absolutely not,” he managed to make out over the music. “My wife doesn’t like stuff like that, if you get what I mean. I’ll get in trouble if I disrupt her when she’s talking to someone else.”

Right. He and Hysilens were in the same ocean but not the same boat. As much as he could poke and prod at his partner to get on his nerves, she was probably heavily reprimanded for being a ‘spoiled brat’.

Mydei actually liked his neediness and attitude more often than not, as he liked teasing, bullying, and playing around with him back. Though he had his moments when he wanted the games to stop, they weren’t as ‘normal’ as the two of them messing around.

From what he remembered, Cerydra didn’t accept such behavior from Hysilens. They had two completely different kinds of dynamics.

“Then I’ll go alone,” he decided, not wanting her to be punished for his bratty behavior. “If you like, you can go dance with them. The girls would love that.”

“Maybe I will,” she agreed. “I must tell my wife, however. So, I guess I’m going over anyway…”

Hysilens followed him back to the table despite her apprehension, and he set Cifera’s purse beside Cyrene’s. Upon hearing a glass click beside him, Phainon noticed Mydei had set his own down.

“My love, do you—”

One hand raised to signal that he was busy, attention still fixated on Cerydra. But then he brought his palm down to touch the table, and his index finger tapped three times from behind his glass. The gesture was both quiet and discreet to their party, yet because he was looking, it was loud and obvious.

“You really shouldn’t interrupt them while they’re speaking,” Hysilens insisted, taking her seat beside her wife. Rather than asking for her attention like he did, she placed her things down, pulled her phone out, and waited.

Phainon grabbed the bottle in the middle of their table, tingling inside of his belly from Mydei’s wordless command, and began to pour him another drink. It was exciting to be told what to do so blatantly. The other two could see them, but it wasn’t as if they knew why he was suddenly popping the cap off.

When full, he slid it towards Mydei and watched as he reached for it and brought it towards his mouth.

“This is quite the purchase. I understand things like this are not cheap,” Cerydra commented while looking around. That was when Mydei actually took his sip. “How much do I owe you for tonight?”

“Nothing,” he brushed off. “I needed something to do tonight, and my friends happened to really like this club. It all aligned.”

Her eyebrow raised. “You don’t appear to be having fun yourself.”

“I am,” Mydei reassured her, and Phainon slid closer to his partner despite them still talking. “Are you?”

“I don’t do things like this. It’s loud and hot,” she criticized, a tinge of annoyance in her voice. “But… My wife is making good friends. Seeing her enjoy herself is making this bearable, and it’s rude to refuse a gift. So, thank you for tonight. Whatever you feel I owe you, I will give to you on behalf of my wife and I.”

Hysilens smiled to herself, keeping her distance while still waiting for her turn to join in.

“You should learn to relax a little bit like Hysilens,” his partner advised. “Every now and then, things like this are nice to indulge in.”

Cerydra didn’t seem to like his unsolicited advice and criticism.

“Well. You should tell your submissive to be more considerate of two people having a conversation,” she chided, then glanced at him as he sat thigh to thigh with Mydei once again. “We’re talking, and you’re being rude by attempting to take his attention away from what he’s doing.”

He froze underneath her firm gaze. “Y-You uh… came to that conclusion already?”

She rolled her eyes from his shock. “It’s fairly obvious from how close you’ve been sitting, and how neither of you have left each other’s presence. He was watching you with us downstairs, and he was watching you while beside my wife. This man is your dominant, and yet he doesn’t discipline your poor behaviors at all. You’re awfully mouthy and cut people off when they’re speaking. How disrespectful.”

Phainon leaned back, surprised by the casual scolding from someone he had barely met tonight. Though, he already knew it was kind of rude to interrupt, and Hysilens had warned him multiple times that she didn't like that.

They were always with their friends. It had been a long time since he and Mydei were with anyone they hadn’t known for a few years or more. The things they did so casually probably felt a little bit invasive to strangers just getting to know them.

Before he could apologize, Mydei set his glass down and pulled the leg crossed over his knee onto the floor. With them apart and his body sat up straighter than it had been, he looked back at Cerydra.

“I’m sure your wife has told you some aspects of our relationship already,” he started, and Hysilens cringed lightly from the mention of her name. “I’m not shaming you. In fact, I understand. That being said, it only feels appropriate to let you both know he also told me some things about you—as he shares everything with me too.”

Phainon winced next, catching the glance his friend gave him when she realized they were both guilty of over-sharing.

Judging by his approach, he assumed Mydei wasn’t going to let them know that he had followed their secret love life and sexual experiences online for years. This was their first time meeting, and it seemed he wanted to keep it that way to refrain from making anything awkward.

“You clearly know the kind of relationship we have.” Cerydra nodded again as her hand reached to rest under her chin. “While I appreciate you looking out for him that night he and Hysilens went out, it is not your place to scold him or question how we treat each other.”

Warmth tickled inside of his face from the firmness of his voice. Very rarely did he ever sound like that unless he was purposely trying to be demanding.

“Oh?” Her head tilted as she leaned forward to straighten herself out as well. “Then what will you do? You should be teaching him better.”

“I like him the way he is,” Mydei said simply. “Swing all you want if that’s what you like to do, but do it in another direction. He meets my expectations, consents to my rules, and behaves how I allow him to. Don’t push yourself on to him just because you know a little bit about us. This isn’t a playdate. I’m not sharing him.”

Phainon’s stomach also fluttered over how protective he was being. That tone mixed with his body language and unfiltered speech was… well, doing inexplicable things to his insides. Never had he heard him sound so quietly pissed before.

There wasn’t any sugar-coating or beating around the bush, as he didn’t typically care to lighten the weight of his words—especially around new people. Mydei didn’t like the way she spoke to him, and he wasn’t going to tolerate another word of it. There was no discussion to be had past that.

It was so attractive when he took control of a situation like that.

“I don’t ‘swing’,” Cerydra said simply, unbothered by his words. “I have no interest in your man other than allowing him to be my wife’s friend. You can relax. I was simply letting him know it’s disrespectful.”

“I also don’t talk about these things carelessly.” Mydei looked around to see if anyone else could hear them. But with the loud music, secluded table, and their friends all downstairs dancing, the coast was clear. “You may discuss your relationship, but separate words like ‘submissive’ and ‘dominant’ from Phainon and I in public. That’s my best friend and my lover.”

“This is getting a little intense…” Phainon mumbled as he shifted in his seat. “I guess… I wanted to be next to him, so I just sat down next to him like I usually do.”

Cerydra took a deep breath when Hysilens gently touched her elbow. “Hm… I suppose I should apologize for overstepping. My wife told me about you, so I assumed this was a comfortable topic to approach since we’re all alone.”

“Phainon?” His partner reached to touch his knee, but he didn’t yet look at him. “What do you say to that?”

“That was kind of rude of me,” he apologized next, still holding on to her gaze. “But please find another way to tell us next time.”

“We accept your apology,” Mydei decided after. “Hysilens, please don’t look so nervous. No one is mad here.”

“Sorry, I just… worry…” She murmured.

“He’s right, this was just a misunderstanding,” Cerydra added soon after, then looked beside her. “Ground yourself.”

Hysilens nodded, taking a deep breath while fidgeting with her rings and nails.

“Yes,” she answered, and Mydei looked away from them to focus on him instead. “I’m okay. One second.”

It was different from him and his dominant. Had he been in that place, there would be hands holding him, soft hushes to relax, and plenty of kisses. Mydei would tell him to breathe, give him the exact timing on when to inhale and exhale, then reassure him that he’d be okay.

Watching them made him realize Mydei didn’t expect Cerydra to do any of that. Maybe he knew them better from watching them from afar, or maybe he simply knew he was much more handsy and gentle of a partner, but he didn’t scold her for approaching it in another way. Not like Cerydra did to them.

That worked for their relationship.

“Phainon.”

His attention shifted to Mydei.

“You aren’t in trouble either for wanting to be next to me,” he promised him quietly. “Did her scolding you make you uncomfortable?”

“No, my love. It just took me by surprise. I… think she thought you were stricter than you are, so… Does that mean we do it wrong?” He wondered, and Mydei shook his head. “Are you too nice to me?”

“Do you think I’m too nice to you?”

“No…”

“Then no,” he hushed, bringing him closer. “We do things the way we like it, and that’s all that matters. Don’t worry so senselessly about things like that.”

Phainon smiled softly to himself, then leaned into his shoulder comfortably. Across from them, he heard Hysilens ask if Cerydra would like to dance with her downstairs. Within seconds, the two stood up out of their seats.

“We will be back.” There was no time to respond to Cerydra, just to glance their way and watch them head towards the stairs.

Could he and Mydei also do that? Mydei didn’t really dance, and he didn’t like the pushiness and lack of personal space from being down there, but… would he agree to it anyway?

As soon as he was going to ask, right behind the couple that left, Hyacine limped up the stairs towards them. It caused them to both pull away, and for Mydei to reach a hand out.

“Here. Come sit with us,” he encouraged her, immediately knowing what was wrong. “Don’t overdo it.”

“Mydei, did you know I really hate wearing these? I miss my sneakers…” She huffed, slumping down next to him and carefully pulling the white shoe off. “Oh, and Phainon, Cassie wants you down there.”

But he wanted to ask his partner to go down there.

“Go ahead,” Mydei encouraged him. “I’ll keep Hyacine company up here. No one wants to be alone.”

“But…”

He really wanted to spend some time with him too. Not just with their friends, but with him.

Maybe it was uncomfortable to be so close in public, but they didn’t have to grind or hold on to each other. They didn’t need to touch and pull. The same way Castorice and Hyacine swayed side to side with each other, they could do that too, right?

“Please?” Hyacine asked. “Cassie might have had too much, so it looks like I’m staying the night with them both to take care of them. I feel a little tired, so… I was hoping you could help me sober up a bit.”

“Of course.”

Well, how could Phainon be upset that they couldn’t? Mydei was just being his helpful self by taking care of their friends. He knew his partner was like this, so of course expecting him to just up and disregard it all was selfish.

“I’m going to join them if it’s not serious.” Both of them nodded in return. “Take care of her, De.”

Mydei’s lip pursed over the nickname.

“Okay. Have fun.”

Phainon stood up, walking away as Hyacine began to talk to him about how Cyrene and Castorice dressed her up for tonight. Though he loved her, and he wanted to listen to her pout, part of him felt a little… disappointed  that Mydei just wanted to sit, drink, and talk all night. They talked all the time, every day, maybe even more than the average couple did.

They talked about their days every day. They discussed new things to try out, the newest movies they watched together, and flirted until it ended up with them kissing and touching each other. Talking wasn’t bad, but… it would have just been nice to do club-like things at a club.

When he found them, Cyrene grinned widely and held his hand in her own, lifting them up high.

“Phai! I missed you!” She yelled over the music, and he forced a smile while looking down at her.

“Does it make me look weird to dance around three girls?” He joked.

Cifera stuck her tongue out. “You’re always weird!”

He had set himself up for that one, so he accepted it and laughed. Castorice held on to his sleeve while stumbling, then her other one touched Cifera’s shoulder.

“Careful.” One hand brushed her back to support her. “Cassie, are you okay?”

How much did they make her drink?

“‘m so good!” She slurred loudly, and he let her keep holding on to him as they all danced around each other. “Where’s M-Mydei?”

He shrugged, ignoring the prick of disappointment inside of him. “At the table with Hyacine!”

Castorice seemed to accept that answer, and the other two girls looked at each other before agreeing that was fair enough. They continued to dance beside him without pouting over his missing company, giggling and drunkenly yelling along to the music. Because it was normal. It was to be expected.

He didn’t drink more than a shot, but it was nice to let go for a bit too.

Soon, more people joined them. More girls squeezed in by Castorice and Cifera, and a few guys tried to do the same with Cyrene. Not that Phainon let them stay long. He was quick to push them away, step behind her, and nudge her closer to her friends instead. Watching them walk away in shame and anger made him proud.

It was always a little bit weird when people felt entitled to join. Grabbing someone like that and pulling them close was so uncomfortable when all they wanted to do was just have fun.

While thinking of that, someone’s hand touched his shoulder, and he turned to find a tall but slender man there. Dressed in red with a pair of designer sunglasses perched on his head, he smiled back at him kindly. Rose tinted his cheeks from liquor, and a light flush glistened over his forehead.

Objectively, he was handsome, and he had a nice smile. Not as handsome or nice as Mydei’s, but one that would definitely make someone else swoon.

“Mind if I join? Or will you kick me out too?”

Because he asked him, surely it meant he wouldn’t make his friends uncomfortable. This guy had at least a little bit of shame in him, and he could be someone nice. There were good people just looking to hang out and dance, and Phainon knew that.

He shook his head, then turned away to focus his attention elsewhere. But this person didn’t approach the girls like he thought he would. He didn’t talk to them at all.

And that was good… Until that same hand snuck forward, sliding over Phainon's shoulders to pull him closer. Fingers squeezed into his bicep, holding him as that man’s body slipped in front of his own. He looked up at him, shorter by a handful of inches, eyes tracing over his face.

“Are these your friends?” Phainon nodded, silent, because he had no clue what was happening right now. “A man who takes care of others is attractive. I like that.”

… Huh?

“Can I get you a drink?” This stranger wondered, and if his flashy gold chain and wrist watch said anything, then he had more than enough money to blow. “What do you like? I’m a long island kind of guy.”

Was he hitting on him?

“I uh… I don’t,” he answered awkwardly. “Can you actually—”

“Awh, come on. Handsome men like yourself all have a favorite drink,” he cut him off, making it more obvious. “Whiskey on the rocks?”

That was more Mydei’s style. The only time he ever chose to throw back glasses like that was when he was sitting beside him at home. Otherwise, he preferred not to taste the alcohol in his glass.

“No. I don’t drink,” he repeated, pushing on his chest lightly while stepping away. “I’m actually—”

“Surely there’s something I can do for you then…” Phainon felt a twist in his gut from how pushy this person was being. “You know, I really like guys who look like you… A tall and muscular man is always so attractive.”

“I’m not really… interested…” He trailed off while pushing on his chest again. “Please go if that’s what you want. I’m not looking for that.”

Cyrene turned around from where she was holding Castorice, eyebrows pinched while noticing their fifth.

“You can get to know me and become interested,” he hinted. “I think we could be good—”

“He has a boyfriend!” Cyrene drunkenly shouted at the man, and both of their friends gasped loudly as they looked at him directly instead. “He was just being nice to you!”

“Is it serious?” The stranger had the audacity to ask, and Phainon pushed harder to get in between him and his friends again. “Because I don’t see him here. Why would he let you go out without him when you look this good? Does he care?”

What did not seeing Mydei have to do with anything? That didn’t mean his partner was suddenly nonexistent, and it didn’t mean he didn’t care.

Of course Mydei cared. He cared, so he was keeping Hyacine company while her feet hurt too much to stand on. He cared, so he took everyone out and didn’t expect them to pay him back—even if he knew everyone was going to give him what they could from their next pay checks. He cared, so he dressed him up in a way that was handsome to him, watched him even when he was away, and let him sit as close as possible to him all night

Just because he wasn’t standing right by his side didn’t mean he didn’t care.

“I’ll get Mydei!” Castorice yelled for him, and the stranger’s eyes widened over the name as if he knew it.

“No, don’t get Mydei, I’ll handle it,” Phainon promised her. “He’s taking care of Hyacine, so leave them for now.”

What was that about? Did they think he couldn’t handle himself? That he needed another man to come play hero for him as if he wasn’t just as strong?

“Heh… ‘Mydei’?” This stranger asked, speaking the name slowly as if he missed the way it tasted in his mouth. “Tall, blond, rich, and never leaves his damn house?”

Phainon froze over the description.

How did he know who Mydei was? Were they colleagues at work? Was this one of his dad’s friends’ sons—the rich guys who liked to cause trouble for Eurypon?

Or… was this someone more personal than that? Was he one of Mydei’s exes?

“Oh! That’s why you’re alone!” He laughed, taking his silence as an answer. “That guy’s not even grown enough to be here! He throws his little tantrums, hides in his little office, and thinks he's too good to be around people. He’d probably prefer to watch you with another man than come down to a place like this!”

Phainon looked up to the railing where their table was, where Mydei actually was staring directly at them. Distance and his usual stoic expression made it hard to tell what he was thinking, and it made his blood run even colder.

“You won’t be happy for long. He’s not going to change.” That was confirmation enough to tell who this was, and Phainon took a deep breath over the revelation. “He’s going to leave you alone when you want to go out, hide you like a filthy secret, and then try to act like the good guy by sending you on your way for no reason.”

Oh.

The last part hurt because it was true.

To an extent, Mydei did try to do that to him. If he had any less courage when confessing to him, then they probably would’ve fallen apart right there. No more playing as a dominant and submissive, no more hanging out alone together, and maybe even no more friendship between them. And it would have ended because Mydei decided to kick him right out the door on his own, believing he was right in how he felt and doing the right thing by letting him go.

Phainon couldn’t even be mad as he stared at him, silent.

“Are you still talking?” Cifera groaned, reminding him that his friends were still there. “Unskippable NPC dialogues are the worst. I have to deal with them in games and real life now? This blows!”

Not seeming to care, Mydei’s ex continued. “The most that guy is good for is nice gifts and a good lay. Squeeze what you can out of him, and then go find someone who can actually give you what you need.”

What… was that? Did he want him to use Mydei for his money, body, and experience as if he didn’t have a heart?

That made him mad.

Thinking about this person potentially wearing the expensive gifts he conned out of Mydei made him want to rip the designer brands off of his body and smash them beneath his boot. How dare he do that to his best friend, his dominant, his partner?

So what if sometimes Mydei got in his head? That made it okay to hurt him?

“Are you upset that I’m making sense?” He asked while reaching for his arm again, but Phainon jerked away from him. “It feels so good at first, but then you come to realize all he’s good at is sex and drinking. He has no hobbies, no interests, and no life outside of his job and his liquor cart.”

Phainon’s skin crawled.

Everything inside of him wanted to cock his fist back and punch this stranger so badly. He wanted to hit him in his mouth for talking badly about him and for hurting Mydei in the past when they were together, but that would probably get him kicked out. It would cause an even bigger scene for them all, and his friends all deserved better than him ruining their night out.

On top of that, Mydei deserved better than a partner who went around hitting people just because he got a little angry. Being violent wasn’t something to be proud of. Being cruel and hurtful weren’t traits that made a good person worth showing off.

What did Mydei see in this person besides his handsome face and body? His personality was terrible.

“I can be nicer to you than daddy is,” he said suggestively, and Phainon glanced back up at the railing to find that Mydei wasn’t there. Mydei wasn't watching him.

And if Mydei wasn’t watching…

Phainon’s arm pulled back, and just as he heard the girls cry that he shouldn’t do it, his fist balled tightly.

“Phai!”

He wanted to wipe the smug look off of his face. But he also wanted to be good, and he wanted to be nice. He liked to think he was both most days, and that he was getting better at managing his emotions when angry.

“No, Phainon! Come on!” Cifera urged him, pulling on his shirt. “It’s not worth it, idiot!”

He hated that she was right.

His arm lowered, and he looked down before shaking his head.

This guy was interrupting his time with his friends, bad-mouthing the man he loved, and airing out business that didn't need to be known. Several times they asked him to leave, but he didn’t. To him, he deserved to be punched in the mouth.

A ringed fist grabbed the stranger’s shoulder, and Phainon looked behind him to find his partner’s heavy glare.

“Get the hell away from him,” Mydei snapped, pulling him back roughly to pry him out of the way. Even Phainon hadn’t thought to shove him like that.

Phainon watched him grab him by his shirt next, and he stumbled into him from the sudden force. It was rougher than he ever handled him and shocking in every way.

“One of you go back to Hyacine. Don’t let some creep get close to her while she’s napping,” he ordered them, making his eyebrows furrow over how demanding he was being with them. Never did he speak to them that way either. “I need to… talk… to Phainon…”

Mydei then began to pull him away from the crowd. His knuckles were white from his tightened fist and feet slightly stumbling with each step. He took him away from their rushing friends, away from his stunned ex-boyfriend, and away from where anyone could see them completely. The music became quieter as they walked further away from the dance floor, then muffled completely when he brought him into a bathroom.

They looked at the poor guy washing his hands when the door was slammed open, but upon seeing them both staring at him, he rushed to shake them dry. He bolted out the door Mydei was holding open, nothing more than a blur of yellow. After, it was pushed shut.

“H-Hey, are you okay?” Phainon asked, nearly tripping over his feet when he was shoved into the bathroom. “Mydei, how much did you drink?”

“A lot,” he answered bluntly. “Why were you so damn close to that guy?”

His head shook as he backed away from his slowly approaching figure. Each step tapped loudly to the floor, and they were much more careful than when he dragged him away.

Anger was written across his face. Pinched between his golden brows and drawn across his curved lips, Mydei looked as if he wanted to punch someone too.

The only time he ever looked that upset was when criticizing himself and his own flaws.

“No. Wait. Did you know him?” Phainon needed to know. “That guy called you ‘daddy’ to my face. I should be the angry one for having to deal with your ex.”

“I stopped caring about those guys after it ended. If I knew him or not doesn’t matter,” he brushed off, completely unbothered. “Whichever one that was—fuck him. The ones who called me that name were the most entitled men I ever met.”

That was so unlike him too. Mydei rarely ever spoke poorly about someone, always believing that good could be taken out of everyone. Even those who could have hurt him, he simply said that he wasn’t what they were looking for and never blamed them for what they could have done. In this case, Phainon assumed it was cheating their way into expensive gifts and using him for sex.

What was it Mydei once said? He was ‘naive’?

Sober Mydei viewed it as his fault for being taken advantage of, yet this drunken version of him was calling them ‘entitled’.

“He told me uh… some things about you.”

“Yeah?” His voice was low and goading. “Was that the one that said I’m fuckin’ boring? Or one of the ones that thought I’m only worth sex and people only wanna be around me because I’m loaded?”

Phainon flinched from the venom. Each of those things made him cringe into himself, feeling hurt for him. And when Mydei exhaled shakily, now close enough to feel, his breath was so full of whiskey that it hurt to breathe in.

“I don’t care who that was. I have no feelings for anyone from back then,” he bit. “But what did he do to you? Did he touch you?”

Phainon felt a wall bump against his back, and Mydei slammed his hands down on the tiled surface.

“I think you drank a little too much tonight,” he noticed, shifting beneath his intense gaze. “You’re being way more aggressive than usual, Mydei.”

“Did you feel him grind against you? Did you want to?”

“Of course I didn’t want that. You don’t need to sound so jealous,” Phainon defended himself. “That was your ex. Not only do I not want him, but he was being a-a dick.”

Mydei scoffed, briefly looking away from him to glance at the mirrors to their right. With a tightened jaw, he glared harder at their reflections.

“I’m not jealous. You keep getting it confused,” he accused him while turning back to him. “‘Jealous’ implies that I want to be them. I don’t need to be someone else to make you want me, Phainon.”

A quiet gulp filled the quiet as his words hung heavy in the air.

“It’s possession. You’re mine, and they can look all they want, but they don’t get to touch you and they don’t get to talk to you the way I do,” he hissed. “Do you see this collar?”

One of his fists grabbed the golden chain and pulled his shoulders off of the wall with it. Nose to nose, Mydei looked him in the eyes as he pulled harder, testing its strength.

“Don’t break it because you're upset at someone else!” He rushed to say, immediately grasping his fist in his hands to try and ease his grasp.

“I own you,” he whispered, and Phainon bit on the inside of his bottom lip as a spark tingled inside of his gut. “No other dominant is telling my sub how to behave for me in public. No other man is touching my man like my hands were cut off at the wrist. All night people have been testing my restraint with that, and I’ve had it up to here with being nice for the sake of good graces and pleasantries. You are mine.”

What was the feeling inside of him right now?

“Y-Yeah?”

“Say it.” Mydei’s voice held little room to protest or deny the command. “Who do you belong to?”

It was so… hot. So overwhelming.

“I… I belong to you,” he breathed out, tingling inside of his gut from his brutal honesty. “Mydei,—”

“Try again.”

“Master,” Phainon corrected himself immediately, eyes flicking to the door behind him before looking back at him. “I’m yours. No one else can have me.”

“There you go.” He let go of his necklace to instead grip around his collar. Fingers wrapped around his neck, holding but not squeezing. “For the rest of the night, you don’t get to leave my sight. If you want to dance, we dance. If you want to sit and talk, we’ll talk. But you don’t go anywhere without me until I say you can, do you understand?”

This rough and domineering version of Mydei so… damn… attractive…

“Yes, master,” he promised as one hand dropped around his wrist to hold him. “You know, I… really actually did want to dance with you earlier… Can you please join me before we go?”

“You already know I’ll do anything for you,” he reminded him, and that made him feel silly for being too nervous to ask earlier. “Now, kiss me. I miss your lips.”

Phainon leaned forward, eyes shutting as he felt the warmth of Mydei’s lips touch his. They tasted like whiskey too, and never had he wanted to get more drunk off of it in his life.

Was Mydei even going to remember this when he woke up? Was he taking advantage of him right now?

The last thing he wanted was for him to wake up tomorrow and not remember a thing, but have all these photos of them all laughing, joking, and dancing together. It’d seem as if he completely disregarded his desire to be private and used his drunken state as an excuse to touch him in public. Then, kissing him and making out with him in the bathroom where anyone could walk in was probably just as bad.

Oh. He hoped the girls didn’t remember Mydei’s ex saying all those things about him, especially the ‘daddy’ part. How embarrassing would it be for them to bring it up while sober and have to explain it all? He’d probably go into hiding. He might even look at him and ask if he happened to let that slip.

As if Phainon would ever call him by that name knowing he didn’t like it anymore.

Deciding this was probably too much, he turned his head to break their kiss, causing a quiet grumble to leave Mydei’s lips.

“When we get back home, I guess…” He caved, letting go of his neck to instead smooth the wrinkles of his shirt out. “You are coming home with me, right?"

Phainon chuckled over his hopeful tone. “Yeah, and so is Cifera, remember? We picked her up, so we’re responsible for her. She can have the guest bedroom.”

“Okay. I-I’ll be good. I’ll calm down.”

“Promise?” Mydei nodded lightly. “Come on, let’s dance for a little bit before we head back.”

“Can you dance on me like you used to with those other people?” He asked, and heat immediately stretched across his cheeks. “‘m not jealous. I just wanna experience it too.”

Phainon was almost certain that was the textbook definition of jealousy, but he let it slide because of how cute Mydei looked asking for it.

“You want me behind you?”

“No. Put your ass on my dick then push back on it,” Mydei said bluntly. With it, that very cuteness dissipated. “I want to feel it and see it.”

“I can’t. People are going to see us, and you don’t want that,” he reasoned. “You don’t want people to know that about you, so let’s just do it normally like… friends.”

Mydei’s nose scrunched. “‘Friends’… Yet I want you to grind on me, Phai.”

His lip curled downward over the nickname Cyrene and their friends called him, hating the very sound of it in his partner’s mouth.

“Stop that. It’s not ‘Phai’,” he said stubbornly. “It’s ‘handsome’ or ‘baby’ for you, especially if we’re alone.”

“It’s ‘my love’ not ‘De’,” he shot back, and they looked at one another for a moment. “Tch… I don’t  wanna pretend you’re not mine… makes people think you can be theirs instead.”

“Then don’t.”

Mydei grabbed him by the shirt and pulled the second those words left his mouth, backing slowly towards the door while dragging him.

“Come dance on me, baby.”

Phainon sighed, aware he might be getting yelled at when they both woke up because of this. But if they didn’t go any further, maybe it’d be okay. It wasn’t as if he was going to have sex with him while he was slurring and stumbling, just a little bit of fun on the dancefloor before they went home. They wouldn’t visit a place like this again for months, so why not indulge just a little bit?

“I’ve been waiting all night for this, my love,” he admitted, catching his tilted and drunken grin as they chased each other out the bathroom.

Mydei was so handsy after that.

Belt to belt, his partner slotted himself behind Phainon so closely that his buckle sometimes got in the way with the back of his own belt. Those desperate hands touched his waist and gripped his hips tightly, holding him flush against his body so they were never too far apart. Wandering fingers untucked his shirt to slip over his lower stomach and feel up on his skin, nails dragging through the tickle of hair beneath his navel.

He liked to kiss him where his choker split too. Lips touched the skin in between the leather bands, and his tongue lapped at the sweat before biting. If he left marks, Phainon wouldn't be surprised.

The club was so dark except for the flashing lights, and everyone around them were probably too drunk to really notice them in a sea of people. It was so late at night that the only people sober were the ones driving home, but even then, didn’t most people just call a cab or an Uber anyways? He had his own fair share of stumbling into random cars with Cyrene when they were younger and freshly legal to drink.

But because of the darkness, he didn’t even realize when his friends came back down to join him. Phainon was too engrossed in the way Mydei was rolling his hips into him and practically humping him back.

Too drunk to realize they were about four articles of clothing away from having sex on the dance floor, Mydei only kept going as the girls giggled and joined them. Even a sleepy looking Hyacine with half of a chicken tender in hand and a surprised look in her eyes.

“This is surprising,” she teased, looking at him instead of Mydei. “You two are a thing?”

“Uh…” A nervous laugh bubbled from his lips when Mydei pulled him even closer. “Y-Yeah. Kinda?”

“‘Kinda’?” Her attention dropped to their moving bodies briefly. “Uh-huh…”

Mydei grumbled in his ear while clawing at his body. “We are,” he corrected him.

Phainon gulped nervously over the confession. Part of him knew he should’ve stopped Mydei from continuing, especially since their friends had found them. He could’ve pulled himself away from the situation or pushed Mydei away and saved him from exposing too much about himself. A good partner would’ve never put him in a position like this.

But Cyrene cheered Cifera on as she danced in front of her, both girls laughing loudly. Castorice was swaying side to side, one arm on Hyacine’s shoulders and the other raised to move with the beat.

Everyone was having so much fun, and Hyacine was looking at him like she was happy for them. All of it egged him to let it happen.

“We are,” he agreed, and she nodded simply before offering Castorice the rest of her chicken tender.

Within no time, Hysilens and Cerydra found them too, opting to simply hold each other and encourage them to have fun. Specifically Hysilens, who watched him with a smile, proud that he and Mydei finally had their hands on each other after being so reserved all night. That egged him on too, wanting to show off that Mydei was his, he was Mydei’s, and no one should forget that.

Empowered, he turned around and faced Mydei, both arms locking around his neck as he looked at him. Under the neon lights, he could see that he had an almost arrogant grin stretched over his lips.

“Lemme do that,” he slurred, and Phainon turned around to see Cifera tapping Castorice’s ass as Hyacine and Cyrene pushed closer together.

Both hands slipped down his body before he could ask, pulling him buckle to buckle before leaning in closer. Hot breaths fanned over his ear, then his mouth touched just below his earlobe.

“Lemme spank this fine ass.”

But before his hands could touch any part of his bottom, Phainon grabbed them tightly. Their fingers interlocked over his hips, holding either still.

“C’mon…” Mydei pushed. “I wanna…”

“I can’t let you do that,” he finally put his foot down, aware that would be way too far. “Just hold me, okay? None of that… kink… stuff here.”

“Ugh…” He seemed disappointed by that, but listened nonetheless. “You ‘n Cifera dance the s-same, ya’know… You move these a lot…”

“If there’s a few things she’s good at, it’s being annoying and moving her body like she’s made of water. You learn a little bit of how to dance from just watching her let go,” he mused, feeling him squeeze his hips. “But don’t look at her, look at me.”

Mydei snorted quietly, amused by his pout. “She keeps lookin’ at me… ‘s not like that.”

That made him laugh next, reminded of the silly bet she made with Cyrene. “She might be trying to see who owes who twenty.”

After hearing that, Mydei slipped both of their hands to the back of his jeans, and he gasped loudly when he curled into his left back pocket. Fingers dug into the cheek, holding him tightly before they slid lower and deeper down the middle seam. They pushed, groping him in front of all their friends.

It would have been somewhat okay, but Mydei’s middle finger was lining right over his crack and pushing in between. Just that touch alone must have made them realize who did what between them both.

“No!” He vaguely heard, then a series of laughter. Somewhere in the chorus, he even heard a surprised scoff from Cerydra over how childish it was to bet on who was a ‘top’ and who was a ‘bottom’.

“Mydei!” He scolded sharply, pulling away to find him grinning. It was as if he were proud of himself for having the guts to set the record straight. “You can’t just do that in front of everyone!”

“Snowy!” It was Cifera who was crying, and Mydei’s eyes shifted to look behind him. “You let me down!”

“Oops…” Mydei chuckled, moving his hand back to his belt. “I’ll be good now.”

“Right…”

Heat tickled over his cheeks, and he puffed them out over the thought that everyone had seen him grab his body like that. Realistically, only a few would remember, but for right now, they knew.

“You’re never drinking like this again,” he mumbled, and Mydei laughed as he tried to pull away from him. “No more grinding for you until you learn how to control your hands.”

“Tough shit,” he said, still sounding lighthearted. “You’re not leavin’ me ‘til we all take off, so get comfortable. Like Hell am I lettin’ someone else put moves on my man.”

His eyes widened over the veiled command.

Mydei’s smile never fell, and his eyes stayed locked onto him as he dragged his hands up his body. Some space was put between their bodies, enough to not feel the tent behind his zipper press up against his jeans but still keep their chests brushing.

“If you won’t dance on me, dance for me.” Phainon could hardly hear it over the music, but the way he gripped his collar made it hard not to focus. “Be a good boy, ‘n don’t try to leave my sight, okay?”

Phainon was pulled in for a kiss, and he exhaled shakily while pulled back into him by the necklace. His own hands hung limply at the wrists, arms crossed above and behind Mydei’s head with his elbows on his shoulders.

“Wha—Mydei?” Hyacine gasped loudly as they stumbled backwards and closer to them all. “What are you doing?”

“‘kay…”

Mydei finally made it into his side of the bed, and Phainon emptied all his pockets onto the nightstand. Keys, wallet, phones, everything was dumped hastily down so he could comfortably, at the very least, unbuckle his own belt and unzip his own boots.

Everything was everywhere, and Mydei was going to be a bit annoyed picking it all up, but that was his punishment for getting so drunk he couldn’t even stand. Phainon hoped he had fun doing it with his hangover, even if he knew he’d probably cave and help.

Beside him, Mydei turned and draped one arm over his back, weakly pulling him closer by the waist even if he was on his stomach. A slurred and muffled sound suspiciously close to ‘goodnight’ left his lips.

Face first in the pillows with both arms above it to hold it close, he mumbled back the same as Mydei threw one leg over his. His nose touched beside his arm, mouth close to his rolled up sleeve and underarm, too drunk to be bothered with spooning the way they usually did.

Throughout the night, Phainon was woken up to take care of them as they rushed and stumbled to the bathroom to throw up the liquor in their systems. Cifera was first, and the bathroom door slamming into the mounted door-stop had flinched him from his sleep like a gunshot. Whereas Mydei was snoring in his ear like he could sleep through the end of the world.

Holding her bangs from her face and gently rubbing her back took up a decent chuck of the remaining darkness in the night. Helping her wipe her mouth with a damp rag and getting her water to drink wasn’t quite a drag—as he would never leave his best friend suffer alone—but he was tired. Undeniably.

Then, just when he thought he could sleep again before the sky shifted too much away from pitch black, Mydei stirred to shift onto his other side. The snoring stopped. The steady, sleeping breaths stopped. Cool, early morning light streamed through the sheer curtains, brightening the room with a gentle hue.

And he felt the bed shift. He heard Mydei rolling out of his place to rush to the toilet, gagging from the liquor he swore up and down he could handle.

Rinse and repeat, Phainon held his hair back in a makeshift ponytail, whispering soothing words while patting his back to help him. Damp towels wiped the bile from his lips, and he cupped water into his mouth so he could wash the taste out. His nightstand was too full of things for a glass of water to rest on, so he fed it to him and left the empty cup in the bathroom before guiding him back to bed.

By then, the sky was pale and bright. The sun wasn’t quite up, but it would be soon no doubt. Ten minutes, maybe. Twenty minutes top.

Deciding they were not going to work out today, he grabbed Mydei’s phone and turned all his alarms off. None at sunrise for working out. None at eight-in-the-morning to have breakfast. They’d wake up whenever they did, eat whenever they could, then go about their days after that.

Oh, he was so ready to lay down and pass out after setting the dying device down quietly…

Just for his own to buzz steadily, for Hyacine’s contact picture to pop up, and he sighed, resigned to his fate. For today, he was going to just deal with it. It was fine.

They never had time to see each other like that, and they never were able to go out and let go. The last time he could remember everyone in the same room was maybe at a holiday dinner party at Cifera and Aglaea’s house. Maybe.

Phainon wasn’t mad, just tired, as he answered his phone and walked out of the bedroom to not disturb Mydei.

“Hello?”

“Is your morning as rough as mine?” She asked hopefully. In the background, their coffee maker chimed. “Cassie has been whining all night. I’ve been in your bed with her watching just in case.”

“Did any of you try to get food in her stomach?”

“Hyacine, do you have an espresso machine at home by chance?” He asked, looking at the machine.

“Huh? Yeah.”

He made a mental note to ask Mydei if they could bake a coffee cake or muffins sometime, something she could enjoy with her latte before a long night at the hospital.

“I believe in you, Phainon.”

They said their goodbyes, and he peeked into the pantry and refrigerator. As long as it didn’t have yeast, he should be okay.

Back to the counter, mug in hand, he scrolled through the internet until he settled on something called an ‘old-fashioned donut bar’. It sounded easy. He learned to make espresso, and was going to cook breakfast later, so why not also fry some donuts?

And in that sense, why not also turn the television on for some music, push the curtains open to let in the sunlight, and have fun with it?

With his phone hooked up to the T.V. and the bright sunrise now brightening Mydei’s home, he grabbed a bag of cake flour from the pantry. His softer playlist lightly filled the silence, accompanied by the occasional tap of pans, soft humming, and the drizzle of the espresso machine working again. Eggs cracked. Vanilla being poured over creamed sugar splashed. A whisk crunched to the bowl beneath when mixing it all, and the bowl clicked to the refrigerator shelf when going to rest.

Time escaped him completely. Reality seemed to have a tear within it, and he was tucked into that space where the sun didn’t move from bathing golden light over the room. Phainon kept moving. He kept busy. If he stopped now, the energy rush would leave his bones, and he really wanted to finish this.

Frying donuts, glazing them with a thick maple icing, and starting a large skillet of chopped veggies, potatoes, and breakfast sausage, all of it felt like autopilot. If someone asked him what he did five minutes ago, of course it was rinsing potatoes off, but he didn’t really remember that. It had to have happened though, as he was frying them now.

Somewhere between cracking eggs into the skillet and dancing around the kitchen, he heard the heavy, uneven footsteps of Mydei stumbling through the hallway. “…—‘non?”

Phainon was screwed.

Sober Mydei often told him his body was his at all times, hinting that he was okay with being approached for sexual favors. If he wanted to touch him, he was free to. Grinding would probably fall underneath ‘sexual favors’.

Drunken Mydei wanted him with no objections or apprehension. He didn’t give him a chance to deny them both like he usually did, as he took the initiative with approaching him rather than waiting for it.

Was it bad of him to give in to his demand? Was it wrong to have indulged in it?
