“Tomorrow…” Mydei said, then gulped. There was a hint of nervousness in his hesitation, one he didn't usually exude. “Tomorrow at exactly three in the afternoon, I’m going to pick you up. We’re going on a date.”

Cyrene leaned in closer to sneak a listen, and he pushed her shoulder gently before looking up at the television. Not that it stopped her from trying to eavesdrop.

“Three?”

“Yes. Wear something casual—shorts, preferably, but anything you feel good in,” he instructed him firmly as Phainon pushed Cyrene away again before she could hear something she didn’t need to. “Bring a jacket though, or don’t if you want to borrow mine. You know I’ll give it to you if you ask politely.”

His lips curled into a smile at how his partner even had something like that mapped out in his plans. The cliche ‘take my jacket if you’re cold’ was the sweetest, cheesiest, and oldest move in the book, and Mydei just told him not to bring a jacket if he wanted his.

He was crossing a jacket off of tomorrow’s outfit. Mydei’s would be his by the end of the night.

“Do I get to know what we’re doing?” Phainon wondered, and Cyrene set her laptop while leaning back in.

Mydei hummed curiously. “We’re going on a date. Wasn’t that already clear?”

“Where on this date, my love? What are we doing?” He specified, causing Cyrene to wave her hand frantically while looking at him. “Can’t you tell me? Or is it a huge surprise?”

“Oh. I’m going to make it a surprise.” Phainon mentally groaned, disappointed he didn’t get to know. “You’ll know when we get there. There’s only so much we can do, and my man’s not that dumb.”

“Anything with you is perfect.”

They could go sit at the park to feed ducks, count clouds, eat hot dogs from the corner vendor, and crunch on ice pops from the ice cream truck for all he cared. As long as Mydei was the one he did it with, nothing would be boring.

But Mydei didn’t share that sentiment.

“That makes me feel like all this effort I’m putting in isn’t worth it,” he commented, and his eyes widened over the brutal honesty. “If anything will be perfect, then why try so hard to get it right? What’s the use if you’re satisfied with the bare minimum?”

Phainon couldn't help but realize he was right. Mydei was putting so much effort in because that was the kind of guy his lover was. He put his all into the things he did, and he liked to know his efforts were both well received and worth the attention to detail.

Instead of brushing it off as unnecessary, he should be grateful for how much he cared to get it right.

“You’re right. I’m sorry,” he apologized gently. “What I meant to say is that I’m excited to see what you have planned for us, and I trust you for whatever it is. I’m sure you came up with an amazing plan.”

“I hope it isn’t too boring or simple. It feels… like I could be doing more.”

“I’m sure it’s going to be everything we want it to be and more,” he insisted, already mulling over possible date ideas in his head. “Is there anything I can do to help? Should I bring anything?”

“I’ve got it. You just need to be ready on time and tell Cyrene you’ll be back on Sunday,” he brushed off, and Phainon flicked his gaze up to his best friend who was still cheesing over the word ‘date’. “Understand?”

“Yes, my love.”

Mydei hummed quietly. “I love you, handsome. I’ll see you tomorrow.”

“I love you too. I’ll see you tomorrow,” he returned, listening as Mydei hung up. Once he pulled the phone away, Cyrene bounced up and down on their couch hard enough to creak its wooden frame.

“Phainon’s got a date! Phainon’s got a date!”

“Shut up,” he laughed, and Cyrene poked his red hot and rounded cheek with her long nail. “C’mon… He and I have been seeing each other for so long, why are you making a big deal about it?”

“Because you’re as red as a strawberry right now!” She pointed out, and he lifted his shirt collar over his face while rolling his eyes. “It’s so cute! Phainon, I’ve never seen you blush this badly before!”

“Stop!”

But he knew she was right. He even felt hot in his face right now, like his skin was melting off of his bones.

“Where are you going? What are you doing?” She pressed, and he glanced away from her. “I bet you Mydei’s going to go all out if he’s making it a big deal to call you beforehand. He seems like the type to do all these grand gestures for the person he loves. You know, roses, chocolates, candles, everything!”

Oh, he was. Even if he didn’t plan dates like that, Mydei was still the kind of guy to worry if he had enough lit candles or if a patch on the floor had too little flower petals on them. Phainon could imagine him contemplating heavily over what time would be appropriate for them to go out, or whether it was too soon to buy him another bouquet of flowers when the ones he had were currently sitting pretty on his coffee table. Maybe he’d even pace a store aisle trying to decide what sweets to get him as a gift for simply showing up to open the door —as if things like that even mattered to him.

Mydei was an idiot. He was a confident yet nervous, proud yet shy, handsome and bumbling idiot who wanted him not to worry about a single thing. In turn, that then met he had to do the worrying and planning.

Phainon loved him. He loved him so much that this could be the worst date he ever went on and it’d still be better than any one he’s ever been on because Mydei was trying so hard. They could blow a tire, get caught in the worst traffic imaginable, trip and fall and end up in the hospital, but it’d still be worth every moment.

Even an injured Mydei would still look at him and ask if he was okay first. He would still do all he could to keep him calm first and foremost.

Phainon really loved him so much.

“What do I even wear? I don’t know where I’m going,” he mumbled. Immediately, the eyes beside him lit up as Cyrene jumped onto her feet. “No! That’s not an invitation to—!”

Their bowl of peach rings was picked up and set on the table, and he cringed from the loud clang of porcelain meeting glass. But before he could scold her for being so reckless, she hit the power button on the television. One thumb jabbed into her own chest.

“And this is what totally awesome best friends like me are for!”

He was pulled off of his couch and rushed to his bedroom before he could even laugh. The lights were flipped on with a harder thump than necessary. His bottom bounced over the bed from the force in which he was pushed, and Cyrene threw the closet door open with an excited ‘bang’.

“Why is your closet cleaner than mine?” She demanded immediately, both hands on her hips. “Mydei did this when he was over, didn’t he?”

“No, I’m just not as messy as you are,” he corrected her. “I also know how to donate clothes to make room for ones that actually fit—”

“I’m not listening!” Her hand waved at him dismissively. “I’ll lose weight, and those dresses are going to be super cute again.”

“Uh-huh…” He didn’t believe that one bit. “We aren’t twenty-one anymore. Put them to rest, ‘rene.”

An offended scoff follower. “You’re not twenty-one anymore.”

Phainon rolled his eyes, watching as she sifted through the hangers, examined different clothing items, then tossed things his way. They collected beside him, filling his bed with smaller options to choose from.

“I’m not trying all these on. I’m not a Ken doll.”

A look was thrown over her shoulder, one that read, ‘are you testing me?’

“Dress up, and I’ll bake that cake my mother always did when we were growing up,” she bribed him. “The one with all the hidden veggies, and nuts, and chocolate—”

“Deal,” he said instantly, not needing any more incentive. “But you have to make it the way auntie did where the edges got a little burned to the paper—”

“—so we can pick it off—”

“—and eat the crunchy parts.”

Cyrene laughed with him at the memory, and she threw a flannel at his face while smiling sweetly.

“Go on. Shoo,” she waved him off, and he looked down at the blue and black shirt in his arms. “I expect pictures for the future wedding montage. I want to see it all—including you two being sickeningly in love.”

“He likes when I wear black, so let’s respect that.”

“Ugh.” That groan came from the depths of her chest. “Fine! I guess!”

She was so stupid sometimes, but it was so nice of her to chill the thrumming anticipation and nerves he had for tomorrow.

—

That next morning, Phainon did his little stretches, ate his pre-run snack with a cup of tea to wash it down, then went on his usual morning run. With his earbuds turned up and his mind focused on later tonight, he was more pumped than usual. He even went for another mile just because he felt great.

The sun felt brighter overhead, but not overbearingly so. The park looked more green and full of life as squirrels skittered about, ducks swam in a line down the large fountain honking at each other, and birds chirped happily. Some people were doing the same as him with their dogs on leashes, and they waved kindly or chatted at the street lights before moving on.

Everything suddenly felt more alive, as if today was meant to be wonderful for everyone around.

When he was coming back, he shared the experience with Mydei. His fingers typed quickly over his screen, telling him all about the kind girl he met with her adorable pet, the squirrel with fat cheeks that looked at him when he paused to skip a song, and how good he felt both physically and mentally.

Like Mydei always did, he told him he was happy to hear him having such a good day. He mentioned that he was proud he ran longer than usual, but to take it easy and not push himself too hard.

Phainon noticed three little redheaded girls standing around the mailbox once he got past the gates, then texted Mydei to give him a second. They all looked worried, and he had plenty of time to help someone out before needing to prepare for his date. Maybe they needed assistance in mailing a little letter, or they lost a toy somewhere in a bush or down the street.

It wasn’t as if he didn’t know these girls. He saw them every now and then on his runs as their family was the ones who helped him take care of the stray cats around.

“Oh! Mr. Snowy’s back!”

He nodded, watching as one with a little braid in her hair ran up to him with a familiar looking orange cat. The poor then was being held by the ribs, arms up and belly wobbling side to side with her rushed steps.

“M-Mama said they’re gonna get rid of them!” She cried loudly, and he tilted his head curiously. “‘cause they have no home, they’re taking them all away! They’re stealing them!”

… Huh?

“They’re going to a ‘shelter’,” another one wearing a flower crown corrected her, holding the smallest one like a baby in her arms. “They started collecting the stray kitties and putting them in a big truck.”

Phainon frowned, bending over to give the cat Mydei had taken a liking to a pet. His ‘meow’ sounded low and slightly annoyed as he squirmed.

“Are they?”

There were a lot of stray cats around. All of them hid in bushes, under cars, and even on the balcony of the first floor tenants. He could see how it’d be annoying after a while, especially since he started hearing cats crying outside of his window most nights. No doubt, they just kept having kittens too.

“We stayed next to them so they didn’t pick them up! These are ours! They can’t just do that!” The last triplet insisted, her little fist on her hip as the mother cat stood by her side proudly. “So we need your help!”

“Me?” Phainon asked, pointing to himself. “What can I do?”

How much more a month was it to add a pet to his lease again? Would Cyrene even want a cat around?

“Mama said we can only have two of them because Trinnon already has a puppy!” One said accusingly.

“Yeah, and you’re the only one who helps us take care of them! No one else feeds them or even cares!” Another insisted, stomping her little shoe to the pavement. “You have to help us, Mr. Snowy! We even told mama that we’d wait until after your run!”

“Please take one! That way we can keep them together forever and ever! If not, they’re gonna steal them and we’ll never see them again!”

All three of them couldn’t be any older than seven or eight years old, and they looked so cute staring up at him side by side. Their big, doe-y eyes as blue as the sky and rosy cheeks made them look like little dolls in the flesh, and the determination to save the little feline family made his heart swell.

When he looked up, there was a woman staring outside the nearest apartment windows. She held a steaming coffee mug in her hands, and there was a fond yet tired smile on her lips. Yesterday’s makeup was smeared around her sleepy eyes.

How could he crush her daughters’ attempt at taking care of the animals? How could he send them crying back to her when she looked as if she needed a little break?

Caving, he looked back at the girls in front of him.

“Okay. Let me see this one… Come here, little guy.”

Phainon reached for the male one, carefully holding him up and looking into his eyes. He was chubby, smelled like both freshly cut grass and wet cat food, and stared back at him dumbly with its bright green eyes. Somehow, the way it looked at him reminded him of Mydei.

Mydei liked to look at him like that, as if he said something in a different language and was trying to decipher it. Or he did something that made so little sense that his partner needed to take a second to rationalize it in his head.

“Tribbie and Trianne really want the girls, so do you want the boy?”

“Awh man,” he mumbled, deciding he was now going to have to buy all the things a cat would need before he started getting ready. “We can’t let the bad guys split them up, right? So we need to keep them together.”

“Yeah!” The three girls cheered, bouncing up and down as their mother giggled off to the side from the sight. “We can have playdates out here in the grass so papa cat can see mama cat and the baby kitten! They don’t have to be away too long!”

“Girls, breakfast!”

“Coming, mama!”

“Thank you, Mr. Snowy! You’re the best!”

“Yeah! Thanks, Mr. Snowy! You’re awesome!”

They ran back into the apartment right next to them, and Phainon looked down at the cat in his hands before holding him to his chest with one hand. The other reached for his phone.

“Master is going to be so happy,” he murmured, then took a picture of them together while walking back to his own place. “Guess who just… became responsible… for this guy…”

The text was sent, and he watched as the ‘delivered’ receipt turned into ‘read’ quickly. There wasn’t a text back though, just an immediate notification hanging at the top of his screen. While dragging it down, he smiled.

“He’s yours?”

“The family that takes care of them with me said the property owner is going around collecting the stray cats to take to the shelter,” he explained casually as a series of ‘meow’s filled his opposite ear. “They can only take two, so they took the girls and offered me the boy because I’m the one that helps look after them.”

“… So, when I pick you up…”

“Yes, my love, he will be in my apartment probably hiding under the couch,” he hinted. “You’ll be able to see him.”

Mydei hummed negatively. “He’s way too fat to fit under there. Maybe the coffee table.”

“Cats are weirdly liquid-y and fit in the tightest places. I’m not sure how, but I bet he’d fit,” he mused, pushing the front door open. “‘rene! Kitty!”

“You did not just call me—kitty!” She gasped, running up to him to take the cat from his hands. “Oh my gosh, Phainon! Where did you find him?”

“If you ever went outside, you’d know,” he mocked her, only for her to roll her eyes. Inside of his ear, a scolding of ‘be nice to her’ sounded.

Her head shook as she gently petted the chubby animal’s head. “No thank you. What’s his name?”

“… Kitty?” He offered unsurely, and even Mydei grumbled that wasn’t a good enough name. “What? I don’t know! I didn’t know I was homing a cat today either, but three little girls kinda cornered me and begged with these big ol’ puppy eyes! And the cat looked like it wanted to come home with me too! And their mom looked so hopeful! Now I have a cat! We have a cat!”

“You’re such a bad dad!” Cyrene huffed, causing him to grasp in offense. “Here, mama ‘rene will give you a name, little one. What do you like? Fish? Chicken? Oh, we need to get you a litter box and take you to the vet. Can you walk-in for a vet? Or do we need an appointment?”

“Do I look like the internet, ‘rene?”

“You have Khas and Reaver!” She reminded him as if he were stupid. “Don’t you take them to the vet?”

“We were given them from our neighbor with too many puppies. We didn’t pick a couple of Samoyed puppies up from a bush,” he corrected, then shrugged. “My mom did all of that stuff when I was like… I don’t know… fifteen years old? All I had to do was feed them and take them out on runs.”

Again, Mydei scolded him to ‘be nice to her’.

“If you want, I can go—”

“I’ll do it,” she cut him off, turning around from her place in the hallway. “Go prepare for your little date! I’ll call Cassie, and she’ll help me get this guy situated in his new home. Won’t we, Mr. Kitty-Cat? Mrow… Hehe, that’s how Cifera always says it.”

Phainon didn’t even get a chance to deny her. He could only watch as she disappeared into her room and left him there.

“You’re mean to her.”

“She’s mean to me!”

Mydei laughed at that, and Phainon couldn’t help but chuckle with him as he relaxed against the door. With his head leaned back and eyes closed, a deep breath then filled his lungs.

“I’m really excited for later, by the way. I’ll see you soon,” he told him. “Try not to miss me too much.”

“You’re silly… I’ll see you all very soon, my prince,” Mydei returned as a clank of metal rang out on his end of the call. It was definitely the sound of a baking sheet hitting his counter top.

“Don’t hurt yourself.”

“I’m smarter than you give me credit for,” he scoffed playfully. After he hung up, Phainon pulled his earbuds off and pried his body off the door.

“I’m taking a shower now! If you have to use the bathroom, find a bush outside!”

“I will kick the door down,” she promised from her bedroom, and he stuck his tongue out at her when passing by. “Go wash your butt, stinky! Mydei isn’t going to want it if you smell like gym socks.”

He shut the bathroom door, locked it, then debated sending Mydei a pre-shower photo of him in the mirror all sweaty from his run. Or should he send one when he was soaking wet and in nothing but a towel?

Something like that would make him happy because his lover always wanted to see him, and getting to read his flustered messages was always nice. The best were the audio messages from when he was busy or particularly frustrated by them so he could listen to them again and again, but was it worth the possibility of being punished for being naughty?

“Mm… he’ll definitely punish me if I do that,” he murmured to himself, thinking of how he was currently cooking and baking. “Maybe another time.”

Phainon decided he should be good. There would be plenty of other times to tease him in the future, but how many ‘first dates’ were they going to have?

No doubt Mydei had a plan, and he didn’t really like to deviate from his plans. Cooking, baking, preparing for their date, and being sexually frustrated might be overstimulating all at once.

Yeah, Phainon would be good today.

—

Getting dressed for his date made him anxious, but not in a sense that he was worried whether Mydei would find his outfit attractive or not. His partner always did. But in the way that made him wish Cyrene were there so he could laugh and joke his way through the minutes.

Realistically, it would be very, very difficult for their evening to go bad. With the exception of crashing the car and dying, or choking on food and dying, the only way he could not enjoy himself would be Mydei going behind his back and picking out some luxurious, overpriced activity to go do. It’d be as if he told him he didn’t like fish, then was taken to a sushi restaurant anyway to try and convince him. There could be other things to order there, but it’d still feel like a punch to the chest that he simply didn’t care about his feelings.

Mydei wasn't really that kind of guy, thankfully, but he was still a little anxious about where they would go and what they would do. Was he dressed appropriately? Should he have bought something for when he came to the door like a flower or chocolates?

Phainon was never on this side of a date. Every date he had ever gone on in the past, he was picking the other person up. He was bringing flowers to the door, making sure his car was completely cleaned, and making all the plans so the other person could enjoy themselves. That was always his job.

But it was Mydei’s now, and being on the receiving end was both nerve-wracking and exciting. His leg couldn’t stop shaking. His tongue didn’t stop tracing over his teeth to make sure the chicken salad he ate three hours ago wasn’t still in between despite checking nearly four times.

He never expected a girl to give him anything at the door when he picked her up, but did that account for him being a guy and Mydei not being a stranger? Should he have got something for him because of that? Was it too late to run to the store?

When Cyrene came home with an entire store in the backseat, it just so happened that Mydei was right behind her too. His partner watched as he carried a sack of cat litter and a few boxes up the stairs, following behind with a bag that matched the one Cyrene had.

“Look at how his big belly hangs,” she teased after setting the cat down, and Phainon watched as he began to explore their apartment. “Oh! I left something in the car! Be right back.”

She pushed him into Mydei while zooming past. Thankfully, they didn’t topple over, but he still grumbled despite enjoying his partner’s swift catch.

“You look so handsome today.” Mydei took the moment to praise him, and Phainon met his eyes. “Such a pretty face.”

Lips pressed to his cheek next, causing him to grin widely before curling an arm around his neck.

“Only my face?” Phainon pouted. “I tried to look good for you, you know. Don’t you like my clothes?”

“I’m trying not to stare at your ass in those shorts too long. That’s not very respectful of me, is it?” Mydei asked, yet shot a glance over his shoulder and down his back.

“Oh? My master doesn’t have sex on the first date then?” He joked, then looked down between them. “You look good too. I really like this…”

Mydei skipped his button-ups and his henleys today. He skipped his sweaters and his turtlenecks for tonight. This white t-shirt was crisp and bright, and it hugged his waist nicely. His black jeans weren’t too tight, but they weren’t loose either, hugging his legs and showing off the thickness of his thighs. They were different from his usual slacks and dress pants, more reminiscent of how he used to dress back when they went out while still in school.

The leather jacket he had on was red rather than black, matching the dark sunglasses perched on top of his head and the tips of his sunset hair. It wasn’t overtly edgy or punk-ish. There were no unnecessary belts, buckles, and studs. There was only sleek red leather and the bronze looking zipper in the middle, a casual kind of edge to his usually clean attire.

Mydei looked so casual, like he wasn’t trying too hard to look professional or done up. It was so effortlessly attractive.

“This red leather reminds me of something,” he hinted, grabbing either half and looking up at him. “You know?”

“Don’t be naughty now,” Mydei whispered to him, and Phainon leaned forward. “Cyrene could come up any second. The last thing she needs to hear is you talking about our leather kink.”

It wasn’t his fault Mydei was dressed to kill. He looked so good that he didn’t want to stop admiring him, but it didn’t seem like Mydei was any better when his attention dropped to look him up and down.

A soft ‘meow’ then filled the room, and Mydei turned his head before tilting his lip up slightly. Bending over, he picked the cat up under its front legs and then looked at the stretched out animal.

“You really are so fat.”

“You and Cyrene need to stop calling him that,” Phainon scolded him, watching as the cat just allowed itself to hang there while looking around dumbly. “Leave him be.”

“He approached me…”

When he began to fuss at the sound of the door opening, Mydei let him go. Though, there was an almost saddened look from being left. His eyes even tailed him for a second before standing up straight and then pointing to the hallway.

“Let me wash my hands, and then we’ll go.”

Phainon nodded, then watched as Cyrene brought up two bags full of treats.

“People food. Cat food.” She bounced either bag in either hand.

“Please don’t eat a chicken flavored lollipop, Cyene. You’re going to get sick,” he pointed out, causing her to switch them around. “Better.”

Cyrene pushed him to the door while grumbling about him being a ‘smart ass’. And once Mydei left the bathroom, he too was ushered to hurry.

“Have fun on your date! Make sure he’s got some strength in him because there’s all these new boxes to take out tomorrow!” She winked at Mydei, who only tilted his head curiously.

“Why wouldn’t he?”

Phainon sighed at the response, pushing a hand to his own face. Heat burned in his cheeks, embarrassed by her shameless attitude now that the two had gotten closer.

“You know what I mean, Mydei.”

“Our date isn’t going to be particularly exertive, so he’ll be fine,” he reassured her, and Cyrene lifted an eyebrow. “I’ll get him home safely tomorrow.”

“You know what, forget I said anything,” she brushed off, sticking a leg out to keep their newest friend inside. “Have fun. Be safe.”

The door shut, and Mydei hummed while holding out a hand. He motioned him to walk forward, so Phainon did.

“You know what she meant.”

“I was contemplating going for a hike actually,” Mydei said thoughtfully, following behind him. “I spoke with Cerydra, and she mentioned there’s a nice mountain trail that leads to some pretty waterfalls a few hours up north.”

“Oh?”

So he took Cerydra’s number from when they all met up for drinks. How often did the two of them talk now? Did she help him come up with tonight?

“She sent me a video, but I think I'd get overstimulated being there too long. Do you know how loud waterfalls are? Or how many bugs there are?” He asked, and Phainon chuckled at the thought. “If we ever went, I’d only be able to handle it for a little bit. I’m not a fan of insects or having to speak loudly for casual conversations.”

“City boy,” he teased, stopping to then poke at Mydei’s arms and stomach. “Are you scared of a few bugs?”

“You are a bug.”

“Ha! But you are the one who bites like one.”

Mydei reached to poke him back on his side, and Phainon gasped before rushing to put a few extra steps in between them.

“You know I’m—!”

“Looks like you’re the one scared of a bug,” Mydei mocked him. He grabbed his wrist next, guiding him towards his car as the other dropped his sunglasses to his nose. “Come on.”

Grinning, he followed him towards the vehicle, eyeing the way the top was retracted back. As they got closer, Mydei pulled the door open and nodded towards the seat.

“Doesn’t it bother you when your hair gets crazy from the wind?”

“It’s going to be a long drive, and I think it’d be nice to drop it down for a bit,” he answered as he shut the door for him. “Here’s the plan.”

Phainon perked up as he looked at him, sitting up in his seat as Mydei crossed his arms to keep from touching the door. It was like he just got it cleaned earlier today. The paint was vibrant as if freshly shined, there wasn’t a hint of dust on the dash, and a faint citrus scent lingered around the air.

“The drive is going to take roughly two hours,” he told him. “Before we get on the road, you and I are going to stop to grab some snacks and drinks. Whatever you want, I’m buying.”

Mydei was letting him eat in his car too? Who was he and where was the real Mydei?

“What if I don’t want you to buy them for me?”

“What if you save that for a day where I’m not making all the plans?” Mydei shot back, and a tingle thrummed beneath his veins from his firm tone. “I have a set vision, and we’re going to follow it, okay? That’s it. End of discussion.”

Oh…

“Yes, my love,” he said sweetly, watching as his partner visibly shivered from the pet name. Not that his insides were any better after that firm tone of his. “Is that our date? A little road trip out?”

“No, it’s part of it.”

What was there around here that took a few hours to get to?

An amusement part? But Mydei didn’t like loud, crowded spaces. And getting him on a rollercoaster would probably involve a lot of begging, pleading, and bribing.

A concert? There was a big stadium a few hours out that always had sold-out shows, but with traffic, it might be even longer of a drive. Then again, Mydei wasn’t really a fan of those environments.

He said they weren’t hiking, so the mountains were impossible as well. There wasn’t much to do up there besides hiking and camping, but who was going camping for one night with their expensive car freshly detailed and an outfit like that on?

Maybe the aquarium by the bay as it wasn’t too far out. That sounded like something nice, and no doubt Cerydra and Hysilens would’ve recommended it. He knew his friend loved her little sea critters.

“Did you hear me?” Mydei asked, snapping him from his thoughts.

“Huh?”

Mydei uncrossed his arms, then grabbed the zipper of his jacket before leaning in.

“I said…” His voice was lowered both in volume and pitch. “You’re going to be a good little boy and wait patiently until the destination reveals itself to you, do you understand me?”

The hand not holding his zipper brushed under his chin, and Phainon flicked his gaze up to his.

“Yes, master,” he whispered for just them to hear. “No more questions about it.”

“If you want me to put the top back on, ask,” he was instructed. “Otherwise, sit back, enjoy this nice, sunny day we’re having, and try not to make an unnecessary mess in my car.”

“Can I please have a kiss before we take off?” Phainon asked before he could pull away.

Mydei leaned closer, and their lips lightly touched for a soft peck before he pulled away. It was just enough to smell his pomegranate chapstick, to feel his soft lips, and to miss them both before he could even close his eyes. But even his pout didn’t get him another.

“There’s an extra pair of sunglasses and a small bottle of sunscreen in the glove department for you. Put them on,” he ordered him instead. “I don’t want your pretty face getting burned or your eyes hurting.”

“Yes, master,” he said again, just a little bit louder this time.

That made Mydei to glance around them to survey their surroundings, hoping no one else felt like heading to their cars at that exact moment. And upon seeing the parking spaces completely void of anyone else, the fingers on his chin lifted to instead pinch his cheeks. They dug in deep, tilted his head back further, and kissed him again like he meant it this time.

Phainon grinned, already dubbing this the best date he’s ever been on without it even starting yet.

—

After picking up bottles of their preferred drinks, a packet of beef jerky, and a bag of chips to share, they took to the freeway to start their trip. Mydei had pinned his hair back into a ponytail during a minor traffic jam, and Phainon had to take a picture of him with his hair tie dangling from his mouth as he pulled it all together. Then another as he drove with one arm hanging out of the window and the other holding the steering wheel.

The music playing between them was a mix of Mydei’s favorites and his own, and he was told the playlist was made specifically for this trip. Each upbeat and catchy song was selected purposefully to keep him singing along and from growing bored. And Mydei always snuck a little glance as they cruised down the free way.

Phainon fed him beef jerky, teased him by pulling it away too soon, and earned himself several smacks on the back of his hand. But it was worth it. Seeing Mydei shoot him a warning glance always made his stomach tingle.

He watched from his place in the passenger seat as the big, bustling city they lived in shifted to the more rural outskirts, then as it all faded away completely. The air felt cleaner. The wind smelled nicer. Even if his hair was probably a mess from the wind, he enjoyed the rush of freshness from having the top down.

Half-way through the drive, Mydei’s arms shifted. He put his opposite hand in the wheel, leaned back in his seat, then rested his elbow on the center console. With his palm up and fingers light spread, Phainon already knew he was asking to hold hands. So he laced their fingers together and leaned back in his seat for a while to bask in how happy he was to get a version of Mydei that no one else ever had.

When he broke their hands apart to eat, Mydei stretched his arm out to wrap it around his thigh. The strong grip made him crush his chip in between his fingers, and the immediate smack against it made him press the back of his hand to his mouth. It was meant to be a warning about making a mess, but the spanking only served to kickstart a jolt of arousal out of him.

What movie or book had that move in it? Where did he learn to pull that?

Mydei held his thigh for a good chunk of the ride after, trusting him when he placed the larger chips in his mouth. Phainon snacked on the smaller ones, as those were harder to feed him without shoving a finger in his mouth and teeth from the bumps in the road.

The air grew crisper. The scent shifted from warm roads and dirt to a refreshing, salty breeze. Throughout the trip, he noticed as the temperature dropped degree by degree on the touchscreen, but he felt it most now. It was completely cooler here than it was at home.

Phainon had been driving for a while now. He got his license pretty early on, and when he did, he went exploring with his minimum wage checks. He knew where these freeways took him, what cities and towns were on the signs, and what that scent in the air was.

His eyes immediately shot to Mydei, to the scarily convincing poker face he wore. If he noticed him staring, he didn’t react at all.

“… Where are we going?” Phainon asked.

“I thought I told you to sit there and wait?” He called back, watching the road closely. “Be patient. You’ll get to see it soon.”

But Phainon had a tickle. He had an inkling of a thought that became more and more apparent as the moments passed.

“Mydei…”

“Ah ah.” That earned him another spank on the inner thigh, then the hand leaving all together to grab the wheel. His opposite rested on the car door, and he attempted to hide his mouth by placing a curled finger over his top lip. “I said to be patient. Don’t distract me while I'm driving.”

“Mydei!” He repeated with a bit more excitement, and the expressionless look cracked into one of blooming happiness. “Mydei, are we—”

Sure enough, driving around the hills for just a few more minutes revealed a glistening, endless sea of crystal blue in his peripheral vision, and he snapped his attention back towards the window. Staring at it, he felt a well of emotions flood inside of his chest.

He was reminded of his hometown, of growing up with Cyrene with dirt covered boots on, of chasing each other by the seaside when they were so bored they could die. The memory of being little, rolling up his baggy jeans, and casting a fishing pole out by the pier with his father made him wish he had a one-day license, a tackle box, and some poles. His mother liked to collect the pretty seashells he would find, and that jar of sand and shells was still on a shelf in their home.

Oh, he remembered his childhood home, the one his parents paid off and let Cyrene’s folks look after. They often told him they’d like to go back when they retired, and they were saving all the money they could put towards enjoying the small town they missed so much.

How long had it been since he last thought to come even close to the beach? It was such a long drive, and he wasn’t like Cyrene who could disappear for random weeks since his job was more demanding.

Phainon’s bottom lip gave a little shake, and he looked back at Mydei, who was juggling between him and the road in front of him.

“Pull over,” he demanded, turning the music down completely. “Pull over so I can give you a hug and kiss right now!”

“The only place this car can go right now is off the highway!” Mydei warned him, and ‘off the highway’ meant tumbling over the edge of the hill they were on. “Sit down, and don’t do anything funny.”

He sat, pulled his phone out, then snapped as many pictures and videos as possible. His finger didn’t stop until Mydei physically grabbed it from him, tucked it between his thighs, and took his hand into his own.

“Stay off of that for a bit,” he decided, and Phainon held him tighter. “Enjoy being here with me, not draining your phone battery.”

There were probably twenty more minutes of driving left before Mydei was able to pay for entry to this specific part of the beach. Because it was later in the day, there weren’t many people there as most of them were already preparing to go home. Parking was easy to find.

Once parked, Phainon rushed to unbuckle his seatbelt. The bags of snacks on his lap crunched as he shoved them aside, and his hand reached for the door handle before pausing.

“Hey. Look at me.”

Phainon obeyed just to find himself facing Mydei’s own phone as the shutter went off.

“You could have told me!”

“You haven’t stopped smiling since you saw the water. Don’t your cheeks hurt yet?” He teased him, eyes on the screen for a few more moments before dropping it into his jacket pocket. “You’re precious, you know.”

While looking eye to eye, Phainon couldn’t help but keep his grin up. “And you’re the best.”

“I’m so glad you think so,” he said gently, then reached for his face. “Come on, give this a little rest. You’re going to hurt yourself.”

He tried to calm his grin, but his heart was racing so quickly. His chest was so full and warm, stomach close to bursting with fluttering butterflies. They coaxed his lips to wobble from their pursed state, stretch upon seeing Mydei’s lifted eyebrow, then finish his grin with a laugh. All while Mydei’s thumb rubbed his heated skin.

“Come here.”

Phainon leaned forward, and Mydei pressed a kiss against his mouth to force him to draw the corners down. Closing his eyes, he kissed him back just as deeply, parting his lips briefly so they could be forced closed again. In focusing on the warmth of his partner’s lips and the feel of him cradling his cheek, the urge to grin slipped. All that stayed was a desire to keep kissing.

But then Mydei pulled back, and he pouted while meeting his gaze.

“Are you going to apologize for making a mess with all these crumbs when I took a lot of time to get my car cleaned for tonight?” He brought up suddenly, and Phainon nodded. “Go on.”

“I’m sorry for making a mess when you specifically told me not to, master.”

Wasn’t he just going to get sand all over the seats anyway?

“Thank you. Now be still.”

Mydei closed the top of his car, shut the engine off, then stepped out while dunking both the keys and their phones into his jacket pocket. The little jog he gave around the hood as he picked the bobby pins from his hair made him chuckle, and seeing his door open as he placed them between his lips made him reach for them. They filled an empty cup holder soon after.

Hand in hand, Mydei helped him out of his seat. Phainon took that as an opportunity to stretch both his arms and legs as the door closed behind him.

“The sun will set soon,” he commented, breathing in deep the scent of the ocean. “My love, aren’t you a romantic?”

“… For you,” he caved, then popped open his trunk as they walked towards it. “I came prepared.”

Phainon’s hand wrapped around his elbow, holding him while peeking at the items tucked inside the small space. A large black bag was pulled out to rest over Mydei’s opposite shoulder, the thing as big as an athlete’s gym bag, and a thick, woven blanket folded over that same arm. Beach towels followed.

All of it together looked like a hefty load to carry, but Mydei wrenched his arm back when he tried to help. Instead, he held his empty arm out expectantly, and Phainon took that as his command to put both of his arms on him. One held his elbow, and the other laced their fingers together.

“Are we going in the water?” He asked.

“I don’t plan to swim, no. But should you, I have clothes in the car.” Mydei dragged a pair of blue swimming shorts out. “I can roll my jeans up and walk in.”

“Is this why you wanted me in shorts? Not just to stare at my legs and thighs?” Phainon asked, and he nodded. “You should’ve too.”

“Not necessary. Do you want these?” His head shook. “Very well. If you change your mind, let me know.”

The trunk closed, and the things on his arm bounced to readjust one last time before they set out to find a comfortable spot—preferably one where the sand was packed tighter without being too close to the water. He knew Mydei wouldn’t like the possibility of loose grains blowing into his food or drinks. And Mydei’s own comfort was one thing he wouldn’t sacrifice for this night out.

They walked for a few minutes, surveying the beach together. Phainon pointed out nice places to settle down, but Mydei shot them down because people were already there. The beach was so big, why should they be close enough to hear other people’s intimate conversations? Or worse, for them to hear theirs?

When a nice spot they both agreed to came, they laid the blanket down with the towels folded on one corner. The bag was set on its opposite side.

“Did you make all of this?” Phainon marveled, eyes wide as Mydei began to lay containers out for them. There was a bag inside of the bag, insulated with a thick ice pack beneath, and everything was still cold despite the drive.

“Yes.”

One had neatly cut vegetable sticks lined by each other with a little divider between them. Another was full of raw berries and other small fruit. The smallest one with a screw lid had a creamy looking dip, something definitely made by him rather than store-bought as was. The largest looked as if some kind of pasta salad was inside of it, and the next on top was full with some kind of syrupy, orange-colored cake decorated with actual orange slices on top.

And there were still things wrapped up in foil, which he assumed might be sandwiches or wraps.

“Mydei…”

“Hm?” Upon noticing his stare, he paused. “Are these things okay?”

“This is so much,” he said, speaking lightly. While admiring it all, he even looked into the bag and found he had packed a little lantern, cans of sparkling water, and more.

Everything that they might need, he had. Everything that they might want, he had. There was even a battery pack for their phones in case they needed to charge them before they could get to the car.

“… Huh?” Mydei seemed confused by his amazement. “It’s not a lot though.”

“It is. It’s so much,” he gushed. “Everything you’ve done for me today is just so…”

What were the words to describe it besides for simply ‘romantic’?

‘Perfect’? ‘Wonderful’? ‘Dreamy’? A love-story that had come to life? A cheesy rom-com that escaped the television?

“I love you,” Phainon told him, unsure how to convey his feelings in any other way. “I love you so much. Master, really. L-Like… really. I’m so… fuck…”

His chest felt so full. His stomach ached with butterflies and tingles. Being here with him now with the sun closing in on the far edge of the sea and no one else around felt surreal. Like if he blinked, they’d be back at his condo just laying around together.

Not that it wasn’t nice to, but it sure wasn’t being on a picnic date at the beach.

Mydei’s eyes softened over his lightly choked up words. Their already glistening amber hue was brightened by the tangerine rays of the sky around them, complimenting his equally as golden hair. Rose bloomed in his cheeks, deepening their sun-kissed flush even more.

“You like it then?”

“I love it.”

A light squint made those eyes glitter. Smiling, Mydei let out a breathy chuckle as if he were relieved to hear that.

“I’m so happy to hear that,” he said through his laugh. “I was stress-baking last night while thinking about how you’ve probably had so many dates that were more exciting. There ended up being so many things for us to share. Please eat.”

Phainon leaned in closer, crossing his arm with Mydei. The ones they were leaning on touched at the elbow, cool leather touching his skin from where his plaid sleeve was rolled up. Their fingers overlapped, slipping in the spaces between one another’s.

“I labeled them,” Mydei told him, then grabbed one of the foil wrapped foods. “These are some garden pastries I baked with your favorite vegetables and some basil. These ones are spinach and artichoke. I also baked bread—”

“—you baked a whole loaf of bread for today too?”

Mydei nodded, then held something up while looking for the label. “Garlic and herb focaccia. It was easier than I expected.”

“Bragging much?”

“No. I’ve always wanted to bake fresh bread, but it’s very time consuming and requires yeast. A lot of the things I bake don’t have yeast in it,” he explained, and Phainon leaned against his shoulder as he listened to him ramble on about the science included in baking.

His free hand did the thing he usually did when explaining, moving as if his physical gestures could convey his words better than his mouth. Apparently yeast could die. Apparently the sourdough bread he loved was delicious but much more complicated because of the yeast.

Phainon knew these things, of course, but he listened anyway. He asked questions to keep Mydei going, shifting from the topic of focaccia to sourdough, then from sourdough to 7- grain bread that he could hopefully get his mother to eat to help with her blood sugar. The series of shifts made more sense as they were talking rather than taking them one by one without context.

“If I can get more comfortable baking bread, I can experiment in baking her something better for her body,” Mydei brought up, open in a way he usually didn’t allow himself to be. He couldn’t help but smile over his caring nature. “She doesn’t take her health seriously enough. That’s why I learned how to bake sweets in the first place—so she can have delicious treats that aren’t too full of sugar or fat.”

“I know,” he hummed. “You’re a good person and a good son, master.”

Mydei didn’t respond to that. He stayed silent as if mulling the response over, then leaned over to rest his head against his own. Temple to temple, they watched over the water as it climbed the shore and sparkled from the sun. Their hands slid further, reaching behind one another instead.

“I would’ve loved to take you back to your hometown, but that’s a pretty far drive,” he changed the subject instead. Phainon understood why, as that talk of his mom and being a good son was getting dangerously close to other topics. “I’d make it for you if we planned at least a whole weekend there.”

“It’s definitely better to fly than drive,” he agreed. “But this is perfect. There’s no need to think you could’ve done more when I’m so grateful you even did this much.”

“Let me take you someday,” Mydei insisted anyway. His heart skipped over the fact he wanted this. “Let me take you back home, then let’s take your parents back too.”

“You’ll even take my parents?”

Phainon wouldn’t agree so quickly, but Mydei seriously wanted that? He wanted to give his parents a short trip back to their hometown too?

“They left what they knew so you could come here and live in a big city. Without that sacrifice, we never would have met,” he reasoned, speaking softly. “They gave me my best friend and the man I love. I should thank them for it sometime. It’s courtesy.”

Water rippled, and in the faint distance, children giggling as parents called for them filled the silence beneath.

“Maybe I’ll let you one day,” he settled on, and Mydei nodded. “I’d really like for you to visit too. Maybe I can teach you how to catch the fish you cook.”

“Maybe I’ll be better than you at it,” he joked.

“No,” he denied immediately. “If you ever get better at fishing than me, I’m going into hiding and practicing my technique.”

“Is that a promise?”

“Are you trying to get rid of me?!”

Mydei laughed, and he grinned while leaning into him as well. “Tell me how fishing works. Is it really as easy as baiting a hook and flinging it into the water?

“No way! You have to know what you’re fishing for!” He started, and Mydei turned to watch him explain. “If your line or rod isn’t the right kind, they’ll snap!”

“Will they?”

“Mhm! So, you should research what kind of fish are where you’re going to be fishing first. Then understand you have to catch within certain weights. Too big? You’ll have to let it go. Too small? You have to let it go,” he explained to him. “Some fish are really well protected, so you can pull them up for a picture, but you have to let them go.”

“Tell me more,” Mydei said, giving him the chance to ramble as well. And because he seemed interested, Phainon was ready to talk his ear off about it.

—

Having got there so late, the sun was down quickly. Chills rolled in over the sea, and Mydei had given him his jacket to wear since he was in shorts and a flannel. The leather was warm inside, scented thickly with his cologne and deodorant, and more comfortable than ever.

And Mydei had his blue flannel on, having denied it originally but caved after seeing his puppy dog pout.

Their picnic set up was illuminated by the lantern, therefore easy to spot as they walked along the shore. With their shoes left by their belongings, cold waves tickled their ankles while they rolled in. Though Mydei chose to wear pants, he had them folded up the calf to keep them from getting wet.

Stopping, they stood in front of one another, lit up by the pale moon above.

“Phainon?”

“Yeah?”

“I want to remake our folder tomorrow,” he said suddenly, and his eyes widened in surprise. “It’s full of these ugly sticky notes and tabs, and it’s severely outdated with the things I wanted from this. Let us take some time, create new papers together, and detail everything our future should hold to better the both of us. Our future deserves some better thoughts.”

His eyebrows furrowed together. “Like what?”

“Romance,” he answered. “Let’s make a rule where I need to take you out on a date a certain amount of times in a month. You and I can make a list from game nights of your choosing to weekend trips out.”

“You know, that reminds me a lot of Hysilens and Cerydra,” he teased, but warmth bled into his cheeks anyways. “Is that what you’d like to have with me?”

“Is that what you’d like as well?”

‘Mandatory dates’, huh? It’d probably help Mydei a lot to be able to pencil them in on his calendar. Knowing he needed to plan one, two, three, or more dates in a month meant he’d never have to guess if he was doing it enough to keep him happy. It’d bring him the comfort he needed to know he was meeting his mark.

Phainon could deal with the uncertainties. He could handle the possibility so long as it did, eventually, come. Mydei was never that kind of person.

“I think a rule like that would be a good idea,” he agreed, watching as the man in front of him smiled. “Let’s also make a rule where we leave the house for a certain amount of time too. It can even be by ourselves like this, but let’s get out more. This is nice, isn't it?”

“If it’s like this, then I can do that,” Mydei promised. “Just us, no one else.”

“Who said this BDSM stuff can’t be romantic?” He joked.

“You did.” Phainon’s eyes rolled over his genuine response. “You are the person who said that.”

That was true.

Maybe he used to wonder how someone could smack their partner across the face and then have the audacity to say they loved them. But he kind of liked the little taps Mydei gave him so long as they stayed beneath a certain strength. And maybe he used to feel uncomfortable at the thought of needing to ask permission for things and behaving a certain way, not liking the idea of punishment. But the punishments Mydei dished out weren’t always bad. They could be fun, teasing, and even a little bit enjoyable.

It was kind of romantic how even if Mydei liked to rough him up, take his control, and tell him what to do, it was always done to make him feel good, give him better habits, and take care of him completely too. He was pampered like royalty, and he couldn’t imagine a relationship where someone didn’t give him as much as Mydei did.

For all he gave up, Mydei always gave back. And even if the version of him from before didn’t understand that, the one now did.

Mydei pulled him closer, and Phainon stepped towards him as water washed over them once more.

“I take it all back,” he murmured. “My master is the most romantic person in the world, and there’s no one I’d rather be with than him.”

“You know, my mother always told me there’s certain expectations for a man like me,” Mydei shared, taking his hands and holding them. “I should hold doors open for others. I should always pick up the bill because I can. I should always appear both clean and professional—no one wants to look at a slob.”

Phainon felt him rub over his knuckles.

“Certain things I do, I know you don’t like, like my daily drinking habits. Certain ways I feel, I know you don’t reciprocate, like my itch to spend money on others,” he listed, and he was right about that. “But the one thing I never want you to have to second-guess or worry about again, is the way I see you. You are everything to me, Phainon.”

A smile stretched across his lips, and he pulled their hands to his cool cheeks. The knuckles were cold, and Mydei gripped his hands tighter as he kissed them gently.

“If you want dates, I will take you wherever you want to go and do whatever activity you want to do,” he promised him. “If you want me to dress a certain way for you, I will fill my closet with whatever will keep you looking at me and only me.”

Mydei pulled him chest to chest next, moving their hands so he could hold his face and Phainon could grip his wrists.

“I never thought I’d ever be interested in going out, introducing myself as someone’s boyfriend, or planning trips with someone else’s family, but here I am.” Shaky breaths fell from his lips, orange scented like the cake they shared previously. “I’m so in love with you that I need to thank your parents for giving me you. I’ve never felt so strongly about anyone before.”

“You’re cheesy,” he accused, but it was definitely working on softening him up. “Would the Mydei from before have guessed that he’d be here?”

“No. The Mydei from before would have snuffed any feelings out until he forgot about them if you never admitted you loved him,” he admitted quietly. “Had you let me cut you off that night, I would have bit my tongue until it fell off. I would have moved on in my own quiet misery.”

“I know. Aren’t you glad you have a man like me with a little bit of attitude in him to talk back to you, master?” Phainon teased, and Mydei rolled his eyes. “Even if you gotta spank him a little bit for that?”

“I’d never want to change a thing about you.”

Phainon leaned in, pressing a kiss to his lips softly and wishing the night never had to end.

That Sunday morning after, as Phainon was washing dishes from their breakfast and the tupperwares from their picnic date, Mydei approached him. With his arms crossed and his hips pressed against the counter, he supervised his chores for a moment before speaking.

“When you're finished, come to my office.”

That was it. There was no added explanation, just his command.

“Yes, master.”

And Phainon followed it once he dried the dishes and tucked them away where they belonged. He didn’t need to know anything else because he could figure it out on his own.

Mydei mentioned that he wanted to work on their rules, omit some, create some, and most importantly, cater the folder completely to them rather than the generic things he had before. Now that he had his own grasp on what he liked, what he disliked, what he might enjoy, and what he wouldn’t ever want, it was time to put these findings together into a better, more coherent set of expectations, limits, and more. This was their folder, not a rinse and repeat process carried from person to person that belonged only to Mydei. It had been overdue.

Wiping his hands on his pants and fisting the hem of his borrowed t-shirt, Phainon walked towards Mydei’s office curiously. Immediately, he was greeted with a folded up blanket on the floor beside his rolling desk chair. Inside of the leather seat, his partner was holding up a familiar red folder full of sticky notes with different highlighter colors, colored tabs on various pages, and pen scratches.

“Kneel.”

His knees touched the pillowy blanket, and Mydei looked down at him once he was situated.

Back straight with his chin up confidently, legs folded beneath his bottom with his hands on his thighs, Phainon assumed the position Mydei liked him in when sitting like this. Confident. Attentive. He was ready for orders, and he was ready for whatever Mydei wanted to do with him.

“Aren’t you a good boy?”

A hand pinched his cheek, and he smiled while tilting into the touch.

“Thank you, master,” he said, still watching him. “What do you need me to do?”

“I’m going to ask you questions, and you’re going to answer me. We’ll discuss our views, our expectations, our necessities, and our limits,” he explained to him. As his hand pulled back, Phainon watched him bring it to his keyboard and begin to type. “Then, we sign it for appearance’s sake again. It makes our agreement feel a little bit more official, don’t you think?”

“It does,” he agreed, then looked up at the computer screen. “I can’t see much from down here though.”

“Do you trust me?”

“Of course.”

“Then sit there and be pretty.”

Phainon rolled his eyes playfully, and Mydei set a hand on his head when he was able to stop typing. The mouse clicked a few times, and a few keys were pressed, all done with one hand so he could keep petting his head.

“Who am I?” Mydei asked next, getting straight to the point. “Who are you?”

“You’re my master, and I’m your spoiled prince,” he said, mourning the weight of his hand when it left yet again.

“Why do you want a master? What does submission give you?” He wondered, and that wasn’t something Phainon was quite ready to hear this soon—or at all, really. That wasn’t something they discussed when opening the folder before, was it?

Why did he like it?

Phainon kind of just… did. But that wasn’t an acceptable answer, was it? Mydei wasn’t satisfied with anything other than the utmost clarity, and ‘I don’t know’ wasn’t something he accepted from him in moments where their dynamic shined the brightest.

He liked the tingle that shot through his stomach when Mydei’s voice lowered to be more stern and demanding. He liked the warmth that pumped from his racing heart when being told he was ‘good’ or ‘doing good’. It was exhilarating to give in to him sexually, as giving up control meant he could focus more on feeling good because he knew Mydei would take care of him. Being able to rely on him for the things he didn’t know or understand felt so safe, and he could explore as much as he wanted with someone who not only knew better than he did, but someone who truly cared about his comfort, enjoyment, and growth.

The satisfaction of Mydei being proud of him for completing his tasks or submitting to him made Phainon want to accept more and more. Pleasing him made him happy because to him, Mydei deserved to smile more and be taken care of in return. Being spoken of highly, held to a certain standard of self-care, and encouraged to embrace his sexuality made him feel more confident in himself, both mentally and physically. It pushed him to step out of his comfort zone more, and that made him try new things, befriend new people, and confront what he’d usually run away from.

Phainon liked to know his efforts were acknowledged, accepted, and rewarded. He liked to blanket himself under his guidance when the world felt too much, aware that he was safe from cruel judgment within his embrace. There was only moving forward with Mydei, never lingering in complacency and wallowing in the past.

How was he supposed to put those thoughts into words that made sense in a document? In his head, they were perfectly clear, yet his tongue was twisted over how to speak them into existence.

“Would it help if I told you why I want my prince?” Mydei asked gently, and he nodded as his chair turned to face him completely. “Are you ready?”

“I am.”

“I want a man who will accept my desire to have control by entrusting it to me in return for the safety, care, and comfort I provide,” he started, opening himself completely. “I take care of myself, my friends, my parents, and I will happily take care of my partner too. That’s the man I am. I may complain about my job, and I may sound ungrateful for this life at times, but I’m blessed with the opportunity to look after others completely.
