Sometimes she just wanted to talk about how Khas gets into her tomatoes sometimes or have him brush Reaver’s coat since he squirms too much with her. Sometimes his father liked to check in, ask how his job was going and if ever wanted to join him in getting his pretty hands dirty. A couple of callouses did a man good, supposedly.

Phainon was confused by the extra cars parked outside their home when he got there, by Cyrene’s parked in front of the mailbox and an older model of pick-up sitting in the driveway. His mom parked her little sedan in the garage and his father’s work truck was parked in front of the gate to the backyard. Whose car was that? And why was Cyrene here without telling him? She always told him if she was visiting his parents.

As he walked up to the door, hearing multiple voices before it finally opened, it became a little bit more clear.

“Cyrene, what are you doing at my mom and dad’s house?" He asked slowly, noticing she was slightly dressed up.

When she visited, she’d leave in leggings, messy hair, and a sweater. They were family. She didn’t need to impress anyone. Yet she had a plaid dress on, make-up to match the baby blue color, and her hair pulled back neatly.

“Phai,” she laughed fakely, then shot a look over her shoulder. “So, um… guess who came down for a night…”

His eyes widened over her nerves.

“And guess who thinks we’re…” Her fake smile widened even further as she opened the door for him even more. Then, her voice raised. “Hey! How was work!”

“Surprise!” His mom beamed, hands up and cheeks rosy from the glass of wine in her hand. “Oh, Phainon! Look who came down for the night!”

“Yeah…” He chuckled awkwardly while stepping inside. “Hey, auntie… uncle…”

Great.

“Oh my—you’re so big!” Cyrene’s mother beamed, and he watched as she climbed off of the couch and then rushed over to him. Her hands then flattened out her own dress. “What a man you’ve grown to be! Look at you, Phainon!”

“Gets it from his father, eh?” Her father teased, elbowing the man sitting beside him.

“You bet’cha,” his dad chucked back. One hand raised to greet him. “The apple doesn’t fall far from the tree around here, huh, son?”

Phainon was not ready for this. He wasn’t prepared to put on an act for the sake of pleasantries.

“Look at you two,” she coo’ed, glancing between him and Cyrene as they stood side by side. Either of her slender, freckled hands held his and her wrists. “Where are the rings? Where are my grand babies, huh? You should be all over my daughter, young man. She’s the most beautiful girl in the world, and you’re so lucky to have her.”

“Oh.” His eyes darted aside for a second, then looked back down at her. “No, it’s… not like that. We’re not…—”

“Huh?”

“Mom, please,” Cyrene sighed, then turned her around gently. “You had too much wine… Don’t bother Phainon when he just got off work.”

“But you two have been living together for so long! You were begging for years to go live with auntie Audata from the second they left! You clearly had a crush on him!” She reasoned. “It doesn’t take this long to get together and decide you want to have a baby.”

“Stop it,” his mom cut in, pushing her shoulder playfully while giggling. “These two might not even want kids right now! They’re still in that apartment, you know. You don’t have kids until you can take care of them!”

“Oh, go back and fix up your old home!”

“That’s my house!” His dad called back, eyes on the television before he titled a beer bottle back. With a loud sigh of pleasure, he then glanced their way. “While I don’t mind a-a little baby or two crawling around, a man needs his own place to grow his future family! That’s our job as men, son.”

This was so awkward.

Was this what Cyrene faced every time she went back home to see her parents? Constant jokes and pressure to come back, to bring home a child, and give up on her writing dreams to be a wife and mother?

Not just any wife and mother—his wife and his baby’s mother. Because boys and girls couldn’t just be friends or roommates with one another, it seemed. Because boys had to jump the girls they were around like dogs, and girls had to deal with it, right?

He felt a little sick at the thought of having that kind of life when he loved his own so much.

“My son is smart. He’ll know when the right time to start a family is,” Audata insisted, then looked back at them both to wink. “Cyrene, darling, don’t let him get you pregnant until he can give you a nice big ring and a good home. Hold him accountable.”

“Right…” she dragged on uncomfortably. “Phai, don’t worry about it, ‘kay? It’s no rush. Take all the time you need.”

Mydei would not be happy to hear the things that were being said tonight. Just one second of this conversation would probably have him walking right out the door or on the edge of his seat, biting back his tongue for the sake of being kind.

“You guys are… what? Twenty-five? Twenty-six?” Cyrene’s mom asked them curiously. “You guys need to get on it. The older you get, the less fun you can have with your little one. Your bodies aren’t getting any younger.”

“Look at them! They can be on a magazine cover!” Cyrene’s dad waved his hand dismissively. “They’re fine! They have some time before they start feeling the age creep in. Oh! And Phainon, your dad says you haven’t left that fancy ol’ restaurant yet. What’s with that?”

“Um… No, sir,” he confirmed, walking into the kitchen before glancing at them through the window above the sink. He wanted to be as far away from them all as possible. “Why? Do you wanna make a reservation for a special occasion?”

Please say ‘no’.

“When are you going to be like your old man and get a man’s job? Or are the muscles just for looks?”

Phainon glanced away while reaching for a glass from the cabinet, not wanting to let his expression be seen.

There was another big reason why he didn’t go back home sometimes, and it was this. Cyrene’s parents were terribly and unapologetically old-fashioned. It was a side effect of having generations after generations of family that lived in a small farming town all their lives. The men worked hard with little breaks. The women stayed home to watch the kids. Everyone started families before they were twenty-five, and no one ever ventured too far away from the nest.

It was too much to listen to sometimes.

What if he didn’t want to do hard labor all his life? What if lifting sacks of wheat and shooting nails into rooftops in the middle of summer wasn’t something that appealed to him?

There was nothing wrong with it, but why did he have to do work like that to be considered a ‘man’? Why did he have to have rough, calloused hands and an aching back to be considered ‘hard working’?

Phainon grabbed some ice, hoping their chatter amongst themselves could push the question back far enough to where he didn’t need to answer it. But while filling his cup with tea from the refrigerator pitcher, Cyrene’s dad’s voice came back.

“Well?”

Damn.

“It pays decently, and it’s not too much trouble,” he answered back simply. “I like it there. I have a close friend who works there too, and she makes it even more rewarding.”

“What about that degree you made your folks come all the way down here for?” He asked casually, like he didn’t see how rude it could be considered. “It doin’ anything for ya’?”

“Mm…”

Phainon deflated, not wanting to answer that.

“He has his bachelor’s in art,” his mom said proudly, swishing her wine around in her glass when he glanced her way. “Humanities. He’s such a good person, and he just loves to help others and be there for them. He’s been that way since he was a boy, but you guys know that!”

His lip curled upwards over her praise, warm from the idea that she was proud of him for it even if it didn’t really help him in life yet. Maybe one day he could figure out what good it could be used for, but until then, it just sat in his closet.

“Does it pay? What can you do with a degree for something like that?” Cyrene’s mom asked curiously.

Cyrene, herself, tried desperately to talk about how yummy the chocolate cake she took a bite of was. She was moaning while chewing, begging to know what made it so moist, what chocolate his mom used, and if she could give her the recipe sometime. Not that anyone but him seemed to notice, as they were too busy discussing him and his degree.

She went to college too. She had her degree in art as well, choosing to study all things literature. Why wasn’t her degree as important as his?

“Whatever my son wants,” Hieronymus brushed off. “Phainon, you can do whatever and be whoever you want. You’re still so young. Don’t mind this old fart. He never even went to college.”

“I didn’t need college to have a nice home, a beautiful family, and a decent job,” he bragged. “Did you, Hieronymus? Audata?”

That wasn’t fair to ask. He knew his parents were in the same boat as him—born and raised in a small town where most people went right to work and families after high school.

“Oh, don’t be like that… The kids these days wanna keep going to school and meet new people! They wanna learn all they can when they’re young so they can relax when they’re old like us!” His mom stood up for them. “When the time is right, he’ll have his family. I trust him.”

“This cake is really good, auntie!”

He stifled a laugh.

“Oh, ‘rene, be a dear and get Phainon a slice,” her mom said to her, but Phainon shook his head.

“I’m not really—”

“My son can get his own slice. Look how grown he is, and his limbs aren’t broken,” his dad mocked them. “Girl, sit back down and enjoy yourself. He can cut a piece of—actually, his mom already pre-cut it! He just needs to pick it up! If he can drive a car and go to work, he can get a slice of cake. C’mon now.”

At least his parents weren’t going to force her to keep up the ‘good future wife’ act.

“I… I wanna say ‘hi’ to Reaver and Khas,” Phainon spoke up, then set his tea down. “Excuse me.”

“You’re excused, baby,” his mom said back.

“Me too!” Cyrene rushed, and the both of them made their way to the sliding door. They couldn’t flip the lock fast enough.

Phainon held it open for her, ignoring the way her mom coo’ed over what a gentleman he grew up to be, then slid it shut to separate them. Once sealed, their voices were no more than severely muffled laughs, he sighed happily. He paid the laughter little mind.

Immediately, Cyrene walked away from the glass and smacked her hands over her forehead. The sound of skin hitting skin made him jump suddenly.

“This is so embarrassing,” she whimpered. “Phai, I want to disappear. I love them, but they’re so…”

“I know.”

“I’m so sorry you have to deal with it.”

He shrugged, getting down on one knee as a large, overactive ball of white fur ran up to him from his dedicated dog house. “It’s not your fault, ‘rene. It’s okay.”

“They told me not to tell you so it could be a surprise.”

“Well, I’m definitely surprised,” he laughed, rubbing Khas’ face before kissing his dark nose. “Oh, you’re so handsome. Look at you. My handsome boy.”

“I bet it’s so disgusting being told all that while you have a boyfriend. God, this blows so badly,” Cyrene continued to ramble. “And the worst part is it won’t stop. No matter what, they’re going to tell us to get married and have kids! They want me to be a pretty little housewife with all these babies! But I can’t break their hearts and tell them I wanna write, travel, and find a pretty girl! Th-They’re gonna be so sad…”

Phainon hummed in understanding as another dog walked up to him, and he smiled while looking at the moon-shaped charm on his collar.

“Hi, Reaver,” he greeted him softly. “You’re so big. Look how handsome you are too…”

They nudged him, licking at his face and pushing him back to get as close as possible. Phainon brought his hands to their collars, grabbing them as their sun and moon shaped charms jingled and clicked.

It really did sound like his own.

“I should tell them I have a boyfriend, huh?” He thought out loud, watching as she then looked over at him. “That way they stop pestering you about me.”

“Do you know how traditional they are?” She whispered. “I mean, they’re going to be…—”

That was true. The last thing he wanted was to hear a spiel about how he and Cyrene would make a better couple than him and the love of his life.

“I guess I’ll have to keep it in until they go to bed,” he sulked. “I planned on telling my parents when they asked me to come over.”

“Please don’t do it in front of mine. I don’t want to know how they’ll react until it’s my turn. It’s way too nerve-wracking,” she begged, and he nodded in understanding. “Thank you.”

“Anything for you.” He then ruffled Reaver’s fur. “Wanna say ‘hi’ to auntie ‘rene? Go! Go say ‘hi’!”

Cyrene gasped when he ran towards her, giggling when Reaver nuzzled into her stomach. Watching Phainon smile softly, glad that she could let go for her lingering discomfort and nerves for a second.

“Also, my mom’s chocolate cake recipe comes from a box. She added milk instead of water, butter instead of oil, and chopped up semi-sweet dark chocolate into it,” he spilled. “A little bit of coffee too. It brings out the chocolate.”

“Does it?”

“Mhm. Mydei told me that trick one night, so I told her, now it’s her little secret,” he mused, holding on to Khas. “The more you know.”

“Mydei would make a really good housewife,” she teased and Phainon raised an eyebrow. “But don’t tell him I said that!”

He could laugh.

Mydei may like cooking, baking, and cleaning, but it was him who enjoyed dressing handsomely for his boyfriend and being there for him to come home to. While Phainon would never want to give up working to live in Mydei’s home as a spoiled partner, their little domestic roleplay was fun. Cooking for him, cleaning up for him, and waiting around for him didn’t hurt if it was every once in a while.

“I should buy him a little dress,” he played along.

“He might hit you on the head.”

“Maybe,” he brushed off, aware that Mydei would probably give him a confused little look before laughing that he would never wear that. “I think I’ll stick to seeing him in leather then.”

“Kinky.” His eyes widened, and she laughed over his flushed expression. “I’m kidding! I bet he’s too sweet to be like that.”

Phainon laughed awkwardly, reaching to pull on his choker lightly.  “Mm… Yeah. Mydei’s a real sweetheart…” He agreed.

This was getting dangerous…

“Let’s go back inside before the mosquitos get to you. They always liked your blood more,” he changed the subject, and Cyrene smacked her arm. “Or before you make them extinct…”

She only smiled back at him, then bid Reaver a goodbye before following him to the sliding took. They both took a deep breath before joining their parents again.

It was going to be a long night…

—

Once Cyrene’s parents went to the guest bedroom to rest, Cyrene took off to go home. But Phainon decided to stay a little bit longer to help clean up. He dusted the table cloth off, pulled all of the chairs back to sweep the floor, and picked up the empty bottles of beer and wine. The clean dishes left in the rack were tucked neatly away, and he folded foil over the containers without lids before placing them into the refrigerator.

“I should buy you guys new tupperware,” he commented, and his mother wrapped her arms around his before leaning into him. “Where are all of your lids?”

“It’s fine. They all have clear bottoms, so we can see what it is,” she pointed out as if that made it any better.

“Mom, this is stained orange.”

“Tomato sauce will do that,” she brushed off nonchalantly, making him roll his eyes. “The lids are… somewhere. They didn’t just grow legs, ya’know.”

His next paycheck, he was buying them some new sets. Their refusal mattered little when it pained him to see such an unorganized kitchen.

“Son, who were you on the phone with earlier?” She asked, and he hummed curiously. “At eight. You went to our room and made a call.”

”Well…”

“First, what time is it, Phainon?” His father asked next as he took the garbage bag out from the can and tied the handles together.

He reached for his pocket, then clicked the screen on. While he read the time, his mother gasped quietly. His father hummed as if he had seen it but just wanted to confirm his suspicions.

“What is that?” She asked, taking his phone. “Phainon, who is… oh my… Is that Mydei?”

He felt a presence behind him, then a hand rested on his shoulder as they stared at his phone screen. When it faded, Audata clicked it back on to stare at Mydei’s sleeping body. It was impossible not to notice the two-toned hair spilling over his pillows as he had it since they first met.

“Son?”

His heart pounded, and Phainon took a deep breath while trying to steel himself to confess that Mydei was his boyfriend, he loved him deeply, and he would not be giving them grandchildren in the foreseeable future.

“That’s Mydei,” he confirmed, and his mom clicked the screen back on. “That day, we baked, packaged, and drove around to give cinnamon rolls to all of our friends. We got back to my apartment, watched movies, had dinner, and fell asleep together. I took this when I woke up.”

“O-Oh…”

“See that little guy? He bought me and Cyrene matching teddy bears when she came back from her trip to her parents’,” he chuckled, pointing to the puppy plush with his thumb. “He said it was ‘courtesy’.”

“You’re… not into girls anymore?” Hieronymus asked slowly as if trying to make sense of it.

“I am, but… I’m into Mydei the most. I only look at my partner that way,” Phainon answered, and the word, ‘boyfriend’, made him take a deep breath. “Um, being with him makes me happy. He and I want to be together for a long time, so… I’m sorry. I won’t be marrying Cyrene, and I never planned on it. She’s just my best friend, nothing more.”

They were silent, and as the screen shut off again, all three pairs of eyes were on the reflections staring back.

“How long?” Audata wondered quietly.

“Months.”

“Are you happy with that boy?” His dad added soon after, and Phainon nodded. “You see yourself marrying him one day?”

“I see us being together for a long time,” Phainon settled on, knowing marriage wasn’t something they wanted now. Maybe it’d change over the years. Maybe it wouldn’t. But regardless of what happened, he only wanted Mydei. “He makes me really happy, and he treats me so well that I couldn’t imagine being with someone else.”

His mom didn’t respond. She just held his hand and his phone, taking in the information that was just unloaded onto her. No pretty wife. No darling kids. No traditional little family with a few dogs scurrying around.

Maybe Mydei would open up to having a pet around once he got a house, maybe his own cat as he seemed to love them. But big, messy dogs who loved to roll in dirt? Most likely not.

“How does it work? Do you treat him well? Or does he treat you well? Are you the gentleman, or is Mydei?” She wondered, and he laughed quietly over her confusion.

“Both of us are, mom. We both treat each other well,” Phainon settled on. “That’s the point. We’re both gentlemen.”

“What she’s asking is if you’re the one who gives—”

“Love!” Audata scolded her husband immediately, and Phainon rolled his eyes as a hearty chuckle came from behind him. “I don’t need to know all of that! Stop it!”

He definitely didn’t want to tell them that either.

“Mydei is very sweet, you know. Just last week, we went on a date to the beach. He set up a beautiful picnic,” he told them, switching the topic from whether he was a bottom or not to something more family-friendly. “Want to see the pictures we took there?”

“Oh, he drove all the way out there? Of course,” she said sweetly, holding his arm again so he could look through his gallery on his own. Her head leaned into the muscle, using him to rest on.

It was a good thing he made a habit out of deleting the sexy pictures he sent to Mydei. Once in their messages, they were removed from his camera roll completely just in case moments like this happened. Family and friends would always want to see pictures or videos, but no one needed to see their private texts.

“Oh, and he bought me the most beautiful flowers one night,” he brought up, swiping to show them the bouquet. “Look. Aren’t they pretty?”

Both of them nodded and hummed in agreement, and Phainon went back to show them the photos he took on their date. From the candids he took of Mydei driving them, to the ocean over the edge of the highway, to their picnic set up once fully spread out, then the distant horizon as the sun began to set—he didn’t skip out on a moment of letting them into his life. Some photos had them kissing in them. A few hand their handprints in the sand with a heart drawn into it. One or two involved just him or just Mydei, and as the pictures shifted through the day, so did the clothes they wore as they switched outer layers.

He took so many, and he saved the ones Mydei took too. How could he not? It was their first date.

“What about this?” She asked, squinting her eyes as she clicked on one he saved from Mydei’s phone.

It was him. His blue eyes were glittering with fresh tears, and his face lit up a bright shade of rose as he smiled uncontrollably. The sun was behind him, casting a golden glow over his body since the roof of his car was dropped.

“Mydei took that.”

“Look how happy our son is,” Hieronymus commented, zooming in. “My boy looks just like he did when he was a kid, only ya’ have more teeth now. I remember when you were just up to my hip, asking if you could go to a big school with a lot of books and people to meet—like in those little teenage movies and shows. When we said we’d do our best to take you, you looked at us all smiley and teary too.”

Phainon felt a pair of lips touch his arm from where his mom was still holding him.

“If he treats you right and makes you happy, I have no problem with you seeing that boy. I always liked that kid and his mother,” she admitted to him.

His heart skipped, and he exhaled shakily as he realized they were happy for him. They were going to accept this part of him.

Warmth bled into his chest, and he reached to touch the chain around his neck before nodding. His thumb rubbed over the circular ring, pushed against the stone, and made him smile gently.

He always wanted his parents to love his partner. The idea that he’d ever have a relationship where he had it hide it from them or have holidays apart made him uneasy. He wanted his mom to be excited to see them, and his dad to be proud of the person he chose.

To hear they were happy for him being with the man he loved so much made tears prick in the corners of his eyes. While he didn’t think they’d hate him, he didn’t expect them to come around so fast or so easily. And he didn’t expect this weight off his chest to make him feel so light.

A finger shut his phone off, then reached to swipe the moisture away before anything could fall. The gesture made Audata look up, Hieronymus look down, and he sniffled as he looked away.

“Are you crying?” His mom asked gently, shifting to stand in front of him instead of wrapping herself on his arm. “Phainon, why are you crying?”

A choked laugh left his lips.

“Oh, you didn’t think we’d stand here and tell ya’ something like ‘you’re not our son anymore’, did’ja?” His dad scoffed. “We spent too long being your parents to suddenly stop. You’re gonna be our little boy until the end no matter who you bring back home to us.”

“The rules these days are always changin’,” Audata agreed, waving her hand dismissively. “Boys love boys. Girls love girls. Boys are becomin’ girls. Girls look like boys but are still girls. It’s all so much! It’s hard to keep up with! I just go, ‘yeah yeah yeah, whatever you want. Whatever makes you happy. It doesn’t change my life any’.”

He nodded, then felt her hand hold his cheek.

“But you tell that boy he better greet us properly as your boyfriend,” she scolded, and he laughed again. “He better come over and not be a stranger if he’s gonna be kissing and cuddling on my son. I wanna know what he does these days and what he plans to do with you.”

“Mydei’s old man is that big-shot company guy, dear, remember? That’s what his mom used to say, always too busy to ever come meet anybody,” he dad reminded her. “No doubt that kid’s got a job there too. What I wanna know is how he spends that money and treats the people around him. No spoiled brat who only thinks of himself is gonna be good enough for you.”

“Mydei does everything for everyone all the time,” he told them. “Just recently, Cyrene and I adopted this cat he used to feed at my apartment complex. He came over with food, toys, and treats for him.”

“Yeah?”

He nodded before sniffling again.

“He’s a really good guy. He’s spoiled, but he’s not a brat at all,” he promised. “I’ll bring him over sometime, or we can all go out to dinner.”

“I’d like that,” his mom agreed, dropping her hand from his cheek. “I’m guessing the reason you told us now and not when auntie and uncle were awake is because they’re a little more closed minded?”

“Little bit, so… if they drone on about Cyrene and I, just laugh along,” he requested, and she rolled her eyes. “I don’t wanna put Cyrene in a spot where they have to tell her bad things about me.”

“Alright, son. That’s your business, and we won’t tell it,” she promised. “But you tell that boy to be good to you.”

“He knows.”

“I gotta take that trash out,” his dad sighed. “If only I had a son with a better back to—”

“I got it.” His eyes then rolled. “I’ll take it out. You two go lay down and get ready for bed.”

Audata sighed. “You leavin’?”

“Yeah, I should check on Cyrene and head to bed myself. It’s late,” he answered, and she nodded despite pouting. “Awh, don’t do that…”

“Come back soon. I miss you.”

“I will,” he promised, then leaned down to kiss her cheek. “I’ll see you later, dad.”

“Just know, we are proud of you every day,” he swore, spinning him around to grip his shoulders. “You are smart, kind, and loved. That’s what matters most in this world.”

He nodded, then leaned into him when he pulled his body in for a hug.

“I love you, boy.”

“I love you and mom too,” he said back, eyes closing for a moment to melt into his touch. “So much…”

He couldn’t wait to tell Mydei the news.

—

Because Cyrene admitted that she stole Cifera from her bed to stay over at theirs for a night, Phainon decided that he could, safely, go visit Mydei’s. As much as he loved both girls, and as much as he wanted to be there for Cyrene, he didn’t want to listen to their giggling all night. He didn’t want to hear their gossip through the walls over celebrities Aglaea has bad mouthed in their phone calls together.

So he texted his boyfriend that he was coming over, walked through the silent lobby with a foiled plate of leftover chocolate cake, rode the empty elevator up to his floor, and unlocked his door as quietly as possible. His shoes were set on the rack. He double checked the door to make sure he locked it, then tucked the cake in the refrigerator for Mydei to taste tomorrow.

And because he knew Mydei would want him to, he also took a bottle of water, drank it quickly, and tossed it into the recycling. There was hardly any noise as he didn’t want to alert him.

Not a single light was turned on. He used his phone screen to navigate through the hallway, to the bedroom, and towards the closet.

Mydei was in bed on his side, back facing him when he walked past. He snored away as if an invisible body was taking up the other half, as if he had left it open for him to come back to. And Phainon planned to take it.

He changed into some pajamas, folded his work clothes neatly to carry them to the bathroom, and he set them in the dirty laundry since they were not only sweaty, but full of invisible grass stains, dog hair, and a little bit stinky from the dogs rubbing against him. With the door closed to block the bathroom light, he began to wash his face, brush his teeth, floss, and prepare for bed. It didn’t take him too long.

By the time he was shutting the lights off and making his way to the bed, Mydei had turned over to face the door since he last saw him. One arm was beneath his pillow to rest his head, and his other arm was curled tightly around a body pillow. Even his leg was thrown over it, pulling it close to his body.

Phainon wished he was that pillow.

He set his phone and choker down on Mydei’s dresser, then tucked his messy hair back from his face. Gently, he brushed over his warm cheek patterned with the indents of his hair.

“Master?” He whispered, admiring his sleeping expression. “I wanna let you know it’s me. I’m not any kind of intruder for you to start wailing on.”

Mydei hummed, low and rumbling, turning deeper into his pillow.

“And can you cuddle me instead? I feel a little left out.”

How dare a pillow get cuddled when he was right here? He should brat about it tomorrow, huff and puff that Mydei didn’t want to hold him, and see where it got him.

“… Mm?”

Phainon chuckled at both the thought and Mydei’s confusion, watching as his eyebrows pinched and his breaths kicked up for a second. He inhaled deeply until his lungs couldn’t hold anymore oxygen. Once it paused, he cracked an eye open to peek. Upon seeing him there, he exhaled slowly.

“Mm… Welcome back, sweet prince,” he rasped, pulling his pillow away almost instantly. “C’mere… What are you doin’ just standing over me like a little creep, huh?”

“Watching you sleep, duh.”

”Stop that. Sleep with me.”

Grinning, he climbed into bed on his side and then turned his back to Mydei happily. They shifted, and a warm blanket wrapped around him when his partner’s heavy, heated arm did. Mydei’s nose touched his neck. His legs tangled with his own.

Immediately, his body relaxed.

“Mas—”

The hand tucked under him lifted, sliding up his body, under his arm, and towards his neck before he could even finish the word. There, fingers stretched to wrap around it, resting beneath his jaw and tucking under his weight. With them in place, Phainon tilted his head and closed his eyes comfortably when he gently pulled back.

Lips touched the top of his spine, kissing him lightly before just lingering there. Warm. Gentle.

This was how he liked to sleep. This was how he wanted to fall asleep every night.

“That’s better…” He sighed happily. But before he could relax enough to join him in falling asleep, Phainon hummed softly. “I told them, by the way.”
